## 0. How to read this document

### 0.1 What this is

D1 says **what the business needs and why**. This says **what the software does, field by field**. A developer should be able to build a screen from the tables here without asking a question that has a business answer; a tester should be able to write a test case from them without inventing an expected result.

Everything here is downstream. **If this document and D1 disagree, D1 wins and this document has a defect** — with one exception, stated in §0.5: where an annex owns the fact, the annex wins over both.

### 0.2 What this is not

- **Not a business requirements document.** No rule is invented here. Every behaviour traces to a `BR-` rule in D1, a term in A1, a message in A2, a permission in A3, a field in A4, a product term in A5 or a contract in D3. Part IX is the traceability matrix that proves it.
- **Not a visual design.** Layout, spacing, colour, iconography and component library are the designer's and the developer's. This document fixes **what is on a screen, where the value comes from, when it is valid and what happens on each action** — not what it looks like.
- **Not an API specification for the interfaces.** The sixteen interface contracts are D3's. Where a screen calls one, this document names the interface (`I-05`) and says what the screen does with the answer, including with each error the contract defines.
- **Not a specification of the vendor platforms.** See §1.

### 0.3 Scope — thirty-seven of the fifty-three features

Framework **v2.5** §7.1 carries 53 features in six groups — Group B is deleted. **We build 38 of them and this document specifies 37**, and it deliberately omits the 15 that belong to a vendor:

| Group | Owner | Features | In D2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| A — InsureMO services | InsureMO | F01–F07 (7) | **No** — InsureMO's product, specified by InsureMO. **But two of them, F05 and F07, are what Part III now states requirements against**, because every claim reads them. Our side of the boundary is D3 §I-01…I-06 |
| ~~B — Policy Data Store~~ | — | ~~F11–F14~~ | **Deleted.** The store is not built (Framework v2.0 §2.1). The codes are retired and never reused |
| C — Mobile application | Us | F21–F30 (10) | **Yes** — Part IV |
| D — BnK IDP | IDP team | F31–F38 (8) | **No** — IDP's product, specified by IDP. Our side of the boundary is D3 §I-07…I-10 and §I-15/I-16, and the field catalogue is A4 |
| E — Claim web console | Us | F41–F60 (20) | **Yes** — Part V, **and §3.6 for F59** |
| F — Cross-cutting | Us | F61–F64 (4) | **Yes** — Part VI |
| **G — Term layer** | **Us** | **F65–F68 (4)** | **Three of the four** — **F65** at **§5.28**, **F66** at **§5.9.1a** and **§5.9.7**, **F67** at **§5.29**. **F68**, the term test mode, is *not* specified in this pass and is recorded as outstanding — **D2-158** |

**The arithmetic, because it is the kind of number that goes wrong quietly.** Group C 10 + Group E 20 + Group F 4 + Group G 3 = **37**, against a catalogue of 7 + 10 + 8 + 20 + 4 + 4 = **53**. **The count moved twice in one day and both moves are stated rather than absorbed.** v0.2 specified 33 of 48. **F60** (policy and cover enquiry, §5.27) took Group E to 20 and the catalogue to 49 without §0.3 being re-checked — a defect of v0.4's, corrected here rather than left. **v0.5 adds Group G**, four features from the *Solution Paper* §10, of which **F65, F66 and F67 are specified here** and **F68 is not**. 33 + 1 + 3 = **37 of 53**, and 38 of the 53 are ours to build.

> **The one feature we build and do not specify, named so that it is a decision rather than a gap.** **F68 — term test mode**, running a candidate term set against a sample of historical claims and showing what would have changed. It is Priority 2 (Framework §7.1, decision **D-10**), it has no screen in §5.1 and no section here, and **D2-158** carries it. §5.28.4 says plainly what its absence costs: an approver signs a term whose effect on real claims nobody has been able to see.

**Where Part III sits, and it sits on both sides of the line.** This is the one place where the count is not obvious, so it is stated rather than left to be inferred:

| Sections | Which side of the line |
|---|---|
| §3.1 … §3.5, §3.7 | **Not a feature we build.** They specify the **read model the claim engine needs** — the entities, the fields, the sentinels, the as-at-a-date semantics — as **requirements on InsureMO**, covering **F05** and **F07** from the consumer's side. Nothing in them is in the 37 |
| **§3.6** | **F59**, the group policy and member bulk load. **Ours**, and one of the 19 in Group E. It is in Part III rather than Part V because it is where policy and member data enters, not because of who builds it |
| §3.8 | Serves both — **twelve rules**: seven the import enforces, five the adapter enforces on the tree InsureMO returns |

**Why the vendor groups are out.** Specifying someone else's screens would produce fiction: we would be writing what we imagine InsureMO's product configuration UI does, and it would be wrong in ways nobody could check. The boundary is specified where it matters — as sixteen interface contracts with payloads, errors and retry behaviour. **What we need from the vendors is an answer, not a specification from us.**

> **A consequence that v0.1 stated the other way round, and it is the most important change on this page.** v0.1 said: *"Because Groups A and D are out, this document does not depend on the InsureMO or IDP confirmations."* **That is no longer true of InsureMO.** The confirmations came in, and one of them removed a system. Every screen in Parts IV and V that reads cover, benefits or limits now reads them from a platform we do not build, with **no fallback if it cannot serve the contract as demonstrated** — Framework **RK-14**. The 37 features here are still specified independently of InsureMO's *schemas*, which is what contract-first buys (P-06); they are **not** independent of its *capability*, which is what P-06 no longer promises. **§10.7 restates the exposure feature by feature.**

### 0.4 Structure

| Part | Content |
|---|---|
| **0** | How to read this document |
| **I** | Actors, surfaces and the shape of the system |
| **II** | **Specification conventions** — the field table format, data types, the validation vocabulary, how errors are referenced. *Read this before any screen section.* |
| **III** | **Policy and member data** — what InsureMO holds, and what we hold. The read model every claim depends on, plus **F59** |
| **IV** | Mobile application — F21…F30 |
| **V** | Claim web console — F41…F59 |
| **VI** | Cross-cutting — F61…F64 |
| **VII** | The claim state machine as an action matrix — every action, from every state, by every role |
| **VIII** | Validation catalogue — every rule in one list, by identifier |
| **IX** | Traceability — feature → section → business rule → message → permission |
| **X** | Open items and the vendor-answer exposure |
| **XI** | Change control |

### 0.5 Precedence

When two documents state the same fact differently, this order settles it:

| Fact | Owner |
|---|---|
| A business rule, a decision, the adjudication chain | **D1** |
| A term, an enum code, a Vietnamese label for a concept | **A1** |
| The wording of any message shown to a person | **A2** |
| Who may perform an action, and on which data | **A3** |
| A document type, an extraction field, a checklist requirement level | **A4** |
| The pilot product's benefits, limits, rates and rule-step switches | **A5** |
| An interface payload, error code or retry rule | **D3** |
| **Everything else about a screen** — layout of fields, order, control type, on-action behaviour, client-side validation | **This document** |

**A field that appears on a screen here and carries a business rule not present in D1 is a defect in this document**, not a new requirement. D1 §Part XII already says so from the other direction.

#### 0.5a The realignment landed — the precedence table needs no exception

An earlier draft of this section carried a temporary rule, because Framework v2.0 was baselined while its companions still described four systems. **That is no longer the case.** D1 v0.3, A1 v1.1, A3 v1.1, A5 v1.3 and D3 v2.0 were all reissued on 21 August 2026 against Framework v2.0, and the precedence table above holds without qualification.

**Worth recording, because it is the substantive point:** deleting the Policy Data Store changed the system boundary and nothing else. **No business rule moved.** The adjudication chain, the claim lifecycle, the permission model, the message catalogue and the product are exactly what they were — which is why D1's authority over this document was never in question, and why the realignment was a day's work rather than a rewrite.

### 0.6 What changed in v0.6

**One change, and it is a correction pass rather than a capability.** On 25 August 2026 the whole document set was reviewed against itself, and this document took **twenty-two findings — seven of them severity 1**. **No screen is added, no feature enters or leaves scope, and the feature count is unchanged at 37 of 53.** What moved is the difference between what this document said and what the annexes that own the facts actually say — plus four defects that were internal to it, of which three would have shipped as working code that did the wrong thing.

**The three that would have shipped, named first, because they are the reason this is a reissue rather than a correction in place.**

1. **A closed enum that was closed at the wrong number.** This document fixed `serviceCategory` at **sixteen** in five places; **A5 has twenty** since v1.4. An adapter built to v0.5 would have **rejected the four new codes**, two of the pilot's ten exclusions would **never have selected**, and §5.11.4's mapping precondition would have **failed every claim carrying one** — which routes the claim to a human with the gate recorded as *not evaluated*, silently, on a growing share of traffic.
2. **A control that was specified nowhere.** §5.28.3 F13 and F14 both said *"entered through the expression builder, never as free text, validated against the vocabulary on save"* — and **no expression builder existed in this document**: no field table, no fact list, no operators, no nesting rule, no states, and both fields typed `textarea(2000)`. A developer builds a text box and a regular expression, which is exactly what §5.28.2 argues against.
3. **A gate that promised a re-evaluation the state machine forbids.** §5.11.4 opened *"Evaluated **once**, by `SYSTEM`"* and closed *"a claim on which every checkpoint has been cleared auto-approves on the next evaluation."* **There is no next evaluation** — the claim has already moved to `UNDER_ASSESSMENT` and Part VII carries no `SYSTEM` transition out of it, which by §7.2's own rule means the transition does not exist.

That is a business blocker with a screen consequence, not a screen defect, and §5.29.5 removes the control rather than disabling it.

### 0.6d What changed in v0.5

**One change, and it is a capability rather than a consistency pass.** On 24 August 2026 the client approved **all ten decisions** of the *Solution Paper — Policy Terms, Rule Engine and Limit Management v1.1*. The paper answers three linked questions — bring the policy's terms into the claim system, give the engine something to evaluate them with, and close the gaps in limit management — and it opens by naming the defect underneath all three: **step 4 of the adjudication chain, *general exclusions*, was a rule with no data behind it.** A5 §7 is ten sentences of prose; the seed's `product_exclusion` row carried a product code, a sequence and a text. **Nothing in the system could evaluate step 4**, and a developer handed the v0.4 specification would have hard-coded ten `if` statements or quietly skipped the step.

**This reissue is what that costs on the screens.** Two new screens, one new service with no screen, one new step in the chain, one new condition on the auto-approval gate, and one new dimension on the limit ledger. **Nothing here is a business rule this document invented** — with one exception, which is §5.28.2 and which is declared at the point of change, in Part XI and as **`D2-173`**. **D1 ratified it as `BR-TERM-7` the same day, and `D2-173` is closed — §0.6c.**

### 0.6c Corrected on 24 August 2026 — same day, same version

**Two modelling conflicts were found while the prototype was built against v0.5, and both were real: two live documents said different things.** They are corrected in place. **The version is deliberately not bumped** — both are defects in what was issued this morning, neither changes a decision, and a version bump would imply a pass that has not happened.

| # | The conflict | Settled | What moved here |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **May a class-`D` term raise a checkpoint?** **§5.29.2 F5** said a class-D term never raises one and that such a row is **refused rather than rendered**. **A5 v1.4 §7.1** says a class-D term **may** carry `CHECKPOINT`, and two of the ten pilot exclusions do — `TBC-02` health checks and screening, `TBC-03` supplements | **A5 is right and this document yields** (§0.5). `termClass` and `effect` are **orthogonal**: `termClass` answers *can the system decide this?* and governs the auto-decline; `effect` answers *what happens when the term is in play*. `TBC-03` is the case that proves it — `serviceCategory = SUPPLEMENT` selects deterministically, and the proviso *"not prescribed as treatment for the diagnosed condition"* means a prescribed supplement is covered, so declining it automatically would be wrong | **§5.28.1a is new** and carries the reasoning · **§5.28.3 F11** restated one-directionally and **F14** conditioned on the effect · **`V-734`** reworded · **`V-742` allocated** — *a class `J` or `E` term may never carry `DECLINE_EVENT` or `DECLINE_LINE`* · **§5.29's purpose, F5 and the empty state** rewritten · **§8.1: 152 → 153** · `D2-155` corrected |
| 2 | **The `selector` / `predicate` split** — specified at §5.28.2, owed upstream as **`D2-173`** | **Upstream adopted it the same day.** D1 §5.3.1 carries both fields and states the rule as **`BR-TERM-7`**; A5 §7.1 and §7.2 give all ten terms a `selector`; `A5_seed_v1.4.json` carries a non-null `selector` on every `policy_term` row | **`D2-173` closes** (§10.3, §10.5) · §5.28.2's *"owed upstream"* note becomes a record of the adoption · §5.28.2 gains the reason **`V-734` has no exception**: a null selector does not mean *not selected*, it means *in play for every claim*, and A5 §7.3 settles the two irreducibly judgemental terms rather than carving them out |

**Nothing else moved.** No screen was added, no field removed, no message re-proposed, no step of the chain and no gate condition touched. **Both corrections are about how a term is described as data**, and the pilot product's ten terms are unchanged in meaning by either.

### 0.6a What changed in v0.4

**One change, and it is a set of answers rather than another pass over the document.** On 24 August 2026 the client answered eight of the questions in *`_Cau_hoi_Vendor_v1.0`* — seven of them vendor or scope facts, one of them a decision about a principle. **Nothing below is a new requirement.** Six of the eight close a question this document had already written the specification for and could not build; one removes a field; one adds two fields to the customer's form and re-points every customer email in the product at them.

**The one that reopened a principle is `A1`, and it closes reopened.** `P-02` freezes everything a settlement is reproducible from. **The answer is: snapshot the renewal status by default, and add a controlled re-read** — available only while the claim is before `PENDING_APPROVAL`, logged on every use with the value before and the value after, and **marking the calculation stale**, so that no figure can survive a change to the input it was computed from. That is a **bounded exception to `P-02`, and §5.4.5 is written to read as one rather than as a loophole.** **`D2-13` closes.**

### 0.6b What changed in v0.3

**One change, and it is a content pass rather than an architecture change.** The client approved every recommendation in *D2 Bảng đánh giá khác biệt v1.0* — the difference register written on 23 August 2026 against Reference System A. **This reissue applies the register in two passes and both are now in.** The Part V pass came first — rows 1 to 16 below. The Part II, III, IV, VI and VII pass followed — rows 17 to 28 — and it is what made the register's application complete rather than half of a document set.

**A third pass followed and it applies no register row.** Rows 29 to 31 close the two contradictions the second pass left standing and knew it had left — **`D2-44`** and **`D2-127`** — after the annexes that own those facts settled them. **The version does not move for it and that is the point of §0.5**: a document that yields to its annexes on a fact the annex owns has not changed its own requirements, it has stopped disagreeing with itself, and the changelog carries it as a third block rather than as a new version.

**Nothing here changes the architecture or touches the rule chain or the auto-approval gate.** *(The chain was thirteen steps when this was written and is fourteen from v0.5 — §0.6d.)* The register says so in its own §9.1 and this reissue holds to it: every change below adds a field, a column, a rule, a view, an entity or an action to something that already existed. **One item does reopen a settled business decision and it is named as such** — `D2-13`, whether renewal status is snapshotted or re-read, which challenges `P-02` (§3.3.3).

Until they are answered the platform behaves as it does today, and §5.25 states what that costs.

### 0.7 What changed in v0.2

**One change, and it is a change of architecture rather than a consistency pass.** On 21 August 2026 InsureMO confirmed — demonstrated against A5 v1.2 — that it can carry the adjudicable benefit schedule and the policy, member and coverage register. **The Policy Data Store is not built. Three systems, not four.** The client decided separately that InsureMO is used for the **policy side only**, and that the claim platform is built **entirely by us**.

## Part I — Actors, surfaces and shape

### 1.1 The two surfaces we build

| Surface | Users | Features | Language |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Mobile application** | Insured customer | F21–F30 | Vietnamese only |
| **Claim web console** | Claim assessor, approver, administrator | F41–F59 | Vietnamese UI, English identifiers and codes |

**Two, not three — and the one that went was ours.** v0.1 listed a third surface: the Policy Data Store's thin administration UI, where an administrator corrected a policy period, a member's coverage dates or a benefit schedule line. **The store is not built, so that UI is not built** (§3.5). Policy and member maintenance is **InsureMO's own UI**, outside our scope and not specified here.

**Two things that UI did are still ours, and both live on the console.** Member search at registration is **S-04** (§5.2.5), reading I-05. The group Excel import — its upload, its validation report and its two-phase commit — is **F59**, an administration area screen on **S-09**, specified at §3.6 because that is where policy and member data enters the solution.

There is no third surface. The **finance system is stubbed** (D3 §I-11, §I-12) and has no UI in MVP 1; IDP's review UI is reached by deep link (D3 §I-10) and is IDP's screen, not ours; **InsureMO's screens are InsureMO's.**

### 1.2 Actors

A1 §3 is the canonical list. Restated here because every action in Part VII is attributed to one of them:

| Code | Actor | Where | What they can do, in one line |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CUST` | Insured customer | Mobile | Buy, claim, respond, watch. Sees only their own claims (A3 §4.3) |
| `ASSESSOR` | Claim assessor | Console | Review extraction, decide cover, calculate, submit a settlement plan |
| `APPROVER` | Claim approver | Console | Approve or reject a submitted plan. Never on a claim they assessed (A3 §4.1) |
| `ADMIN` | Claim administrator | Console | Users, roles, thresholds, master data, the group import (F59) and the payee master (F58). **Takes no claim decision** — no assessment, no calculation, no approval, no payment (A3 §4.11). The one operational exception A3 §3.3 grants is resubmitting a package for extraction, which decides nothing. **They no longer administer policy data**: A3 §3.2's write grants over policy holder, period, member identity and coverage dates had a screen in v0.1 and have none now, because the records are InsureMO's (§3.5, D2-112) |
| `SYSTEM` | The platform itself | — | Auto-approval, ledger posting, notification dispatch, scheduled polling. Appears in the audit trail as an actor in its own right (F63) |
| `IDP` | BnK IDP | — | Returns extraction results and clinical recommendations. Appears in the audit trail; **never changes a claim's state** (D1 §1.4 AR-2) |
| `IMO` | InsureMO | — | **Holds the product, the benefit schedule, and the policy, member and coverage register**; issues policies; answers the as-at-a-date reads every claim registration depends on (I-05); records claim registration. Appears in the audit trail. **Takes no claim action and never changes a claim's state** — §7.4 |

### 1.3 The rule this document exists to make concrete

D1 §1.4 states the architectural difference in four lines. Two of them determine almost every screen in Part V:

> **AR-1 — IDP proposes; the Claim Platform decides.** Nothing IDP returns is a decision. Every extracted value is editable on the claim, every clinical recommendation is confirmed or overridden by a person, and the claim record — not IDP's — is what the settlement is computed from.
>
> **AR-4 — every assessor action happens on the claim.** There is no second system an assessor works in and no state to synchronise back. The deep link to IDP (F36) is for *looking*, never for *editing*.

**In screen terms:** every field that came from IDP is editable, shows its origin and its confidence, and keeps the original value visibly beside the corrected one (F46). This is specified once, in §5.6, and referenced everywhere else.

## Part II — Specification conventions

**Every screen section in Parts III to VI follows the same shape.** Read this part once and the rest is mechanical.

### 2.1 The shape of a screen section

```
§n.m  Screen name                                     [feature code]
      Purpose            one sentence
      Entered from       which screen or event
      Who may open it    roles, per A3
      Field table        the table specified in §2.2
      Actions            the table specified in §2.5
      Rules              behaviours that are not a single field's validation
      Empty and error    what the screen shows when there is no data, or a call fails
```

### 2.2 The field table

Every field on every screen is one row:

| Column | Meaning | Allowed values |
|---|---|---|
| **#** | Field identifier, unique within the screen | `F1`, `F2`, … |
| **Label (VI)** | The Vietnamese label shown | Text. **Must exist in A1** if it names a domain concept |
| **Type** | Control and data type | §2.3 |
| **Source** | Where the value comes from | §2.4 |
| **Req** | Requirement | `M` mandatory · `O` optional · `C` conditional, with the condition stated |
| **Validation** | Client-side and server-side rules | A `V-` identifier from Part VIII, or an inline rule |
| **On error** | The message shown when validation fails | An **A2 code** (`CLM-VAL-003`), `*(new A2 item needed — D2-nn)*` where none exists yet, or **`inline`** where the control prevents the error rather than reporting it — a date picker that cannot return a future date needs no message. Never free text in this document |

**No field table row is complete without a Source and an On error.** A row with an empty *On error* and a non-empty *Validation* is a defect — it means a rule exists with no way to tell the user it fired.

**Two declared exceptions, and both are record schemas rather than screens.** **Part VI** specifies the notification template, the user and grant records and the audit log entry; their fields are written by the platform and never validated against a person, so *On error* is empty by nature and §6.0 declares it. **Part III §3.2** specifies the ten entities the claim engine reads, in a four-column form — `Field | Type | Req | Constraint / note` — because a table with no screen behind it has no *Source* to name and nobody to raise an *On error* against; §3.2's opening declares it. **No screen section anywhere else may use either exception**, and a table that has a screen may not use them at all.

### 2.3 Types

| Type | Meaning | Format and constraints |
|---|---|---|
| `text(n)` | Free text, maximum n characters | Trimmed on save; internal whitespace collapsed |
| `textarea(n)` | Multi-line free text | Newlines preserved |
| `int` | Whole number | No thousands separator on input; grouped on display |
| `money` | Vietnamese dong | **Integer dong. No decimals.** Displayed grouped by three, e.g. `1.920.000`. Stored as an integer. Rounding is D1 §5.3 — nearest whole dong, half away from zero, at each chain step |
| `pct` | Percentage | Entered as a percentage to one decimal; **stored as integer basis points** (D3 §1.2). `20%` is stored `2000` |
| `date` | Calendar date | Displayed `dd/mm/yyyy`. Stored ISO-8601 date. **No time component** |
| `datetime` | Instant | Displayed `dd/mm/yyyy HH:mm`. Stored ISO-8601 with offset, **Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh (+07:00)** |
| `enum(X)`, `enum(X) multi` | One of a fixed set, or several from it | The set is named, and lives in **A1 §4, A5, or the annex that owns the concept** — A2 §0.3 for channels, A3 §0.1 and §0.3 for grant levels and data scopes. Never a free-text list defined here. Where this document had to name a set with no home, it is listed in Part X as an item for A1 |
| `lookup(X)` | A reference to a record in X | Displayed as a human label, submitted as a code or id |
| `bool` | Yes / no | Displayed as a switch or checkbox; never a nullable tri-state |
| `file` | An uploaded document or image | Constraints in §2.7 |
| `derived` | Computed, never entered | The formula or its source is stated in the row |

**`money` never accepts a decimal separator, and `pct` never stores a float.** Both were chosen because a rounding difference between two implementations of the same chain is invisible until it reaches a customer.

### 2.4 Source values

| Source | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `user` | Typed or chosen by the person on the screen |
| `snapshot` | Read from the policy snapshot taken onto the claim (D1 §4.2). **Never re-read from InsureMO** |
| `imo:I-05` | Fetched live from **InsureMO** through the named interface — policy, member, coverage as at a date, and the benefit schedule as at a date. **On a claim screen this is legal only before the snapshot is taken**; on the mobile cover screens, on S-04's member search and on §5.20's insured panel it is the normal read path and the restriction does not apply |
| `idp:I-09` | Returned by IDP's extraction result. **Always editable** (AR-1) |
| `idp:I-16` | Returned by IDP's clinical assessment as a recommendation. **Never applied without confirmation** (D1 BR-TRACK-3) |
| `imo:I-02`, `imo:I-03` | Returned by InsureMO — a quote, or an issuance response |
| `system` | Computed or assigned by the platform — claim number, timestamps, ledger balances. **Also covers facts arriving on an inbound webhook** (`I-08` processing-complete, `I-12` payment status): the platform records them, so the platform is the source |
| `master` | Read from platform master data — providers (F57), document types (A4), decline reasons (A5 §6.3) |
| `config` | An administrator-set value — the auto-approval threshold, ageing targets |

> **`imo:I-05` replaces v0.1's `store:I-05`, and the rename is not cosmetic.** The old value read *"fetched live from the Policy Data Store"*, and there is no Policy Data Store. Every field-table cell that carried it now names the system that actually answers — which matters, because a reader of a *Source* column is deciding what a screen does when that system is unavailable, and §6.4.2's answer for InsureMO is not the answer v0.1 gave for the store. **`imo:I-01` is not a `Source` value**: I-01 is a product-publish pull into the adjudicable model (P-03) and no screen reads it directly.

### 2.5 The action table

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Action** | The control's label, in Vietnamese, matching A2 where A2 names it |
| **Who** | Roles permitted, per A3. A role not listed **does not see the control** — it is not merely disabled |
| **Precondition** | State and data conditions that must hold for the control to be enabled |
| **Effect** | What changes: state transition, records written, ledger postings, interfaces called |
| **Message** | The A2 code confirming success, and the A2 code on failure |

**Permission is enforced server-side on every action.** Hiding a control is a courtesy to the user, never the control itself (F62).

### 2.6 Vietnamese and English

- **Everything a customer or an assessor reads is Vietnamese.** A1 is the source for terms; A2 is the source for sentences. This document quotes labels in Vietnamese and reasons about them in English.
- **Identifiers, enum codes, field names in payloads and log entries are English and uppercase-snake** — `PENDING_INFO`, `NOTCOV`, `PROVIDER_OFF_NETWORK`. They are never translated, never shown raw to a customer, and A1 §4 maps each to its Vietnamese display text.
- **A screen never concatenates a Vietnamese sentence from fragments.** Every sentence is a complete A2 template with named parameters. This is A2 rule **M-8** and it exists because Vietnamese classifiers and word order do not survive fragment assembly.

### 2.7 Files, images and documents

| Constraint | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Accepted types | `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `application/pdf`, and `text/xml` for the e-invoice | A4 §1.5 — XML is the **only** path for the invoice; there is no OCR route |
| Maximum size per file | 10 MB | Above this, capture quality is not the constraint, the connection is |
| **Maximum documents in a package** | **20** | D3 §I-07 |
| **Maximum pages in a package** | **50** | D3 §I-07 |
| **Maximum package size** | **100 MB total** | D3 §I-07 |
| Client-side check at capture | Blur and edge detection (F27) | A bad photograph rejected at capture is not a failed extraction three minutes later |
| Storage | Object storage, referenced by URI. **The claim record holds a reference, never the bytes** | D1 §1.4 AR-2 — documents live in IDP; the claim refers to them |

### 2.8 How this document refers to other documents

| Written as | Means |
|---|---|
| `D1 §5.3` | Section 5.3 of the BRD |
| `BR-TREE-5` | A business rule identifier in D1 |
| `CLM-VAL-003` | A message in A2 |
| `A3 §4.1` | A permission rule in A3 |
| `T1-02` | A document type in A4 |
| `200.1` | A benefit code in A5 |
| `I-05` | An interface contract in D3 |
| `V-004` | A validation rule in this document, Part VIII |
| `D2-03` | An open item in this document, Part X |

### 2.9 Canonical field widths

The same value is held on several screens and in several records. **These widths are fixed here so that no screen truncates what another stores**, which is a defect that only shows up on a customer with a long name.

| Value | Width | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Claim number | `text(20)` | The format is `CLM-YY-NNNNNN` with an optional `/n` event suffix — 15 characters. The margin is for the suffix growing past one digit |
| Policy number | `text(20)` | |
| Member card number | `text(20)` | |
| Person's name — full | `text(200)` | Vietnamese names with full diacritics; §3.2.7's register and every snapshot use the same width |
| Provider name | `text(200)` | |
| Identity document number | `text(20)` | |
| Bank account number | `text(30)` | |
| Free-text reason or rationale **entered by staff** | `textarea(2000)` | Decline rationale, override reason, waiver reason, dismissal reason. A customer's covering note is a different thing and is narrower — Part IV §4.8 |
| Any code (benefit, decline reason, document type, ICD-10) | `text(20)` | |

**A snapshot never narrows the field it copies.** If Part III specifies a name at `text(200)`, Part V's snapshot of it is `text(200)` — anything else silently loses data at the moment the claim is registered, which is the one moment nobody is watching. **These widths are now also what we require of InsureMO's responses.** A register that holds a name at 100 characters truncates it upstream, and no width we specify downstream can recover it — the check belongs on the sandbox, benefit by benefit and field by field (C-IMO-06).

### 2.10 Two conventions that are easy to get wrong

**Nothing is silently corrected.** Where a value from IDP disagrees with a value from another document, the screen **shows both and flags the disagreement at the field**; it never picks one. This is D1 §5.4 and it applies to every reconciliation warning in Part V. The system's job is to notice, not to resolve.

**An operational failure is never expressed as a claim outcome.** A stalled extraction, an unreachable InsureMO, a failed payment — each produces an operational state with an operator queue, and each is worded per A2 rule M-6. **No screen in this document may show a customer a message that a system failure could be mistaken for a decision on their claim** (D1 §3.2, D3 G-3).

### 2.11 User-interface conventions

*(Register: **B-45** shared UI conventions table · **B-27** grid conventions · **B-26** the date-type selector · **B-39** customer-declared fields, reduced)*

**Parts II to II.10 say how to write a specification. This section says how a screen behaves when the specification does not mention it.** It exists because the reference system carries such a table and we do not, and the cost of not carrying one is not a missing feature — it is fifty screens each deciding for themselves what an empty list looks like, what happens to a name too long for its column, and whether a search matches `thang` against `Thắng`.

**Everything here applies to every screen in Parts III to VI unless that screen states otherwise, and a screen that states otherwise must say why.** Where a rule below and a field-table row disagree, the field-table row wins — it is the more specific statement — but the disagreement is a defect to be looked at, not a licence.

**This section adds no `Source` value and no type.** §2.3 and **§2.4 remain the only place a type or a `Source` is defined**; UI-27 below marks how a customer-declared value is *rendered*, and the two fields it names carry `system` in their field-table rows exactly as they did before. A convention about presentation is not a vocabulary extension, and treating it as one would put two lists of `Source` values in one document.

#### 2.11.1 Input and validation

| # | Convention | Statement |
|---|---|---|
| **UI-1** | **Whitespace** | Every `text` and `textarea` value is trimmed at both ends on save, and internal runs of whitespace in a `text` are collapsed to one space (§2.3). A name saved as `Nguyễn  Văn  Thắng` is stored `Nguyễn Văn Thắng`. **A `textarea` keeps its newlines** and is trimmed only at the ends |
| **UI-2** | **The mandatory marker** | A field with `Req = M` carries a red asterisk after its label. A field with `Req = C` carries the marker **only while its condition holds** — a marker that is always on teaches the user to ignore it |
| **UI-3** | **Empty on a mandatory field** | Reported at the field, on blur and again on submit, never only as a summary at the top. The message is the screen's A2 code; where no screen-specific code exists the generic mandatory-field message is used — **which does not exist in A2 and is `D2-25`** |
| **UI-4** | **Over-length** | The control **prevents** the excess rather than reporting it: the input's `maxlength` is the `text(n)` width, and paste is truncated to it with the count shown. This is `inline` in the *On error* column's sense (§2.2) and needs no message. **Nothing is silently truncated on save** — a value that reached the server over-width is a contract violation and is rejected, not clipped |
| **UI-5** | **Bad format** | Reported at the field after the field loses focus, never on each keystroke. Dates, money and account numbers are entered through controls that cannot produce a bad value where one exists (§2.3, §2.9), and where a control exists the error cannot arise |
| **UI-6** | **Duplicate record** | A uniqueness failure is reported at the field that carries the duplicate, naming what already holds the value only where the reader is entitled to see it. A card number in use is reported as in use; **which member holds it is not shown** unless the actor's data scope already reaches that member (A3 §0.3) |
| **UI-7** | **File limits** | §2.7's constraints are enforced at selection, before any byte is uploaded, and reported per file with the file's own name. A package that breaches a package-level limit is refused as a package, naming the limit |
| **UI-8** | **Default values** | A field with a default shows the default as a real value, never as placeholder text. **Placeholder text is never a value** and never survives a save |
| **UI-9** | **"Today"** | Every "today", every ageing clock and every `datetime` default is taken from **the server**, in `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh` (§2.3, V-004). No screen reads the device clock for a value that is stored or compared. A device whose clock is wrong must not be able to date a claim |

#### 2.11.2 Search and matching

| # | Convention | Statement |
|---|---|---|
| **UI-10** | **Case and diacritics** | Every free-text search on a person's name, a provider name or a document name is **case-insensitive and diacritic-insensitive**: `thang` matches `Nguyễn Văn Thắng`, and `THANG` matches it too. §3.3.1 states this as a requirement on I-05 and it is the same rule; here it is the rule for every search box in the product, including those served entirely from our own data |
| **UI-11** | **Contains, not starts-with** | A name search matches on a substring of any word in the name. A starts-with search on a Vietnamese full name finds the surname and nothing else, which is the least useful of the three name parts |
| **UI-12** | **Exact keys stay exact** | An identity number, a card number, a policy number, a claim number and a bank account number match **exactly**, with whitespace stripped. They are never partially matched — a partial match on an identifier returns the wrong person with no way for the reader to tell |
| **UI-13** | **A search with no criterion does not run** | The control is disabled until at least one criterion carries a value. §3.3.1 and V-501 carry the server side |

#### 2.11.3 Grids — sorting, paging, truncation and totals

**This is B-27, and it is here rather than on any one screen because it applies to all of them.** §5.3.2 lists the work list's columns and says nothing about their order; the same is true of every other list in the document. **Every table in Parts III to VI is governed by the rules below**, and a table that needs different behaviour states it in its own section with its reason.

> **Part V has already stated six of these for itself, at V-711, and the two statements agree.** §5.3.2's V-711 is B-27 reduced to the six conventions that change what a console user can do; the table below is the same reduction generalised to every surface, and where V-711 is the more specific statement it wins on a Part V list. **UI-14 to UI-22 are not a second rule set**, and a future edit that makes them differ is a defect in whichever was edited second.

| # | Convention | Statement |
|---|---|---|
| **UI-14** | **Default sort** | **Every grid declares its default sort in its own section, and the default is descending on the column that means "most recently touched"** — the ageing clock on the work list, the timestamp on a trail, the effective date on a master. A grid that does not declare one sorts by its own identifier descending, which is at least stable. **A grid with no declared and no implicit order is a defect**: two readers of the same data see two different screens |
| **UI-15** | **Header-click sorting** | Clicking a column header sorts ascending; clicking again sorts descending; clicking a third time **returns to the grid's default**, and the third click is the one most systems omit. The active sort is shown on the header with its direction. Sorting is server-side wherever the grid is paged — a client that sorts one page sorts a sample |
| **UI-16** | **Which columns sort** | Every column sorts except a column of controls, a column of images and a derived column whose value is not held (a computed remaining-limit bar). A column that cannot sort carries no sort affordance at all rather than an affordance that does nothing |
| **UI-17** | **Sticky header** | The header row stays visible when the body scrolls. Where a grid has a totals row (UI-20) that row is sticky at the foot |
| **UI-18** | **Page size and the result count** | Default page size **25**, selectable from 25 / 50 / 100, and **the selection persists per user per grid**. The **total count is always shown**, not only the count on the page — *"1–25 trong 212"*. A count that only counts the visible page is how a reader concludes a search found nothing when it found two hundred |
| **UI-19** | **Truncation** | A cell too narrow for its value truncates with an ellipsis at the end and shows the whole value on hover and on focus. **It never wraps to a second line** — a grid whose rows are different heights cannot be scanned. It never truncates in the middle, and it **never truncates an identifier**: a claim number, a card number and a policy number are given their §2.9 width and the column is sized to it. An audit entry that clipped a claim number's event suffix would attribute a decision to the wrong event (§6.3.3 A12), and a grid that clips it teaches the reader the wrong number to quote |
| **UI-20** | **Totals** | A grid whose columns include money carries a **totals row at the foot**, and the totals row totals **the whole result set, not the page**. It is labelled as such. Where a total over the result set is not meaningful — a mixed-currency or mixed-unit column — the cell is empty with a dash, never zero |
| **UI-21** | **Row activation** | A double-click on a row opens that row's detail where a detail exists, and it does exactly what the row's primary control does — never something else, and never something destructive. A single click selects. **A grid whose rows have no detail has no double-click behaviour** |
| **UI-22** | **Selection** | Where a grid supports multi-select, the header checkbox selects **the current page only** and says so; selecting across pages is offered as an explicit "select all *n*" affordance or not at all. A silent select-all-across-pages is how a bulk action reaches rows nobody looked at |

#### 2.11.4 Filtering by a date range

*(Register: **B-26**)*

| # | Convention | Statement |
|---|---|---|
| **UI-23** | **A date range is preceded by a date-type selector** | Where a list filters by *from date – to date*, the pair is preceded by a **date type** selector naming which date is being filtered, and the range applies to that date alone. A range with no named date is ambiguous the moment a record carries more than one date, and every claim carries at least six |
| **UI-24** | **The date type has a default and the default is stated** | Each list names its own default date type in its own section. Changing the type **does not clear** the range already entered |

> **The work list already carries this and names its own set.** §5.3.1 **F6a** is UI-23 and UI-24 applied — `enum(dateFilterType)`, four values, defaulting to *Ngày gửi* — and it deliberately carries four rather than the reference's six, because *ngày giao việc* and *ngày chấp thuận* are milestones our lifecycle does not record separately (**B-26**, **S-48**, **G-V-11**). **Registering `dateFilterType` in A1 §4 is `D2-124`**, not a new item; there is one set and one name for it.

#### 2.11.5 Empty, loading and error — the three states every list shows

**Every list, grid and card collection in this document renders four states, not one**, and §2.1's *Empty and error* line in a screen section is the place each screen says what its own wording is. The shapes are fixed here.

| State | What is shown | What is never shown |
|---|---|---|
| **Loading** | A skeleton of the grid — header, and placeholder rows at the row height the data will use. The controls above the grid stay enabled | A spinner over a blank area. A layout that jumps when the data lands |
| **Empty because nothing matches** | One sentence saying no record matched, **and the criteria that were applied**, and a control to clear them. This is a business answer, not a failure (§3.3.1) | An error colour. An error icon. The word *lỗi* |
| **Empty because nothing exists yet** | One sentence saying the list is empty and what causes a row to appear in it | The no-match wording. A reader who has never had a row and a reader whose filter is wrong need different sentences |
| **Error** | The A2 code the section names, the correlation id, and a **retry** control. The grid keeps its header and its filters so the reader can see what they asked for | A partially populated grid. **A grid that shows some rows and reports an error is the worst of the four states** — the reader cannot tell which rows are missing |

**No screen shows an empty frame with no sentence in it.** §5.14.5 already forbids it for the trail views; UI-25 makes it general.

| # | Convention | Statement |
|---|---|---|
| **UI-25** | **An empty region always carries a sentence** | Never a blank panel, never a bare zero, never a dash on its own. The sentence says which of the two empties it is |
| **UI-26** | **An operational failure is not a claim outcome, in a grid as well as on a screen** | §2.10 applies to a cell. A row whose data could not be read shows that the read failed, in the row, and does not render as a claim with a missing value |

#### 2.11.6 Customer-declared fields

*(Register: **B-39**, reduced)*

| # | Convention | Statement |
|---|---|---|
| **UI-27** | **A value the customer declared is read-only to staff, and says so** | **Two fields only in MVP 1**: the claim's **intake source** and the **customer-sent date** on a supplementary document (§4.8). Both are facts about how and when something arrived, not judgements about it, and a member of staff who can edit them can move the fifteen-day statutory clock's anchor without leaving a trace anybody would look for. They render with their provenance beside them and no edit control. **This is a rendering rule, not a `Source` value** — both fields are `system` in their field tables, and §2.4 is unchanged |

> **Reduced from the register's B-39, and here is what was left out.** The reference also locks the **episode type** the customer chose. We do not: our assessor must be able to correct an episode type, because the episode type drives the document checklist and the waiting-period class, and a customer who chose *ngoại trú* for an inpatient stay would otherwise be stuck behind a checklist that cannot be satisfied. What we take from B-39 is the half that concerns provenance of arrival; what we decline is the half that concerns clinical classification. **The distinction is stated so that it is a decision rather than an oversight.** Part V reaches the same answer from the console side at **V-715**, and **D2-124**'s question — whether §2.4 should gain a *customer-declared* `Source` value — **is answered here as no**: UI-27 carries it as a convention and §2.4 stays the single vocabulary.
