## Part III — Policy and member data: what InsureMO holds, and what we hold

**Read Part II first.** Every table below uses the type vocabulary of §2.3 without exception, and every screen field table in this Part — §3.6's import screens — uses the seven columns of §2.2 and the `Source` values of §2.4. Where a value is shown in Vietnamese it is a label from A1; where a message is cited it is an A2 code.

**One shape is declared rather than left looking broken, on the same ground Part VI §6.0 uses.** §3.2's ten entity tables are **record schemas, not screens** — `Field | Type | Req | Constraint / note` — because nothing on them is entered by a person on a screen this document specifies: seven are InsureMO's register and three are Claim Platform records written by the platform or captured on a Part IV or Part V screen that carries its own seven-column table. A *Source* column on a table with no screen behind it names nothing, and an *On error* column has nobody to tell. **§2.2's exception is Part VI's by its own words; this is the second and last place it applies**, and it is stated here so that a reader checking conformance finds a decision rather than a lapse.

**Two allocations this Part makes, so later Parts do not collide with it.** Validation identifiers in this Part occupy the **`V-1xx` block**. Open items occupy **`D2-01` … `D2-19`** — the block was `D2-01 … D2-09` in v0.1 and is extended here because this reissue retires five items and raises two new ones, and **a retired identifier is never reused** (§10.5).

**Field names.** The entity and column names below are those of **`A5_seed_v1.5.json`**, in `snake_case`, because that fixture is what the mock behind `I-05` is built from. **The seed carries 215 records over 16 collections at v1.5**, and three of the changes reach this Part: `policy` gains **`rule_set_ref`**, `member` gains **`continuous_cover_from`**, and a **`provider`** collection is added — the network list §5.17's `in_network` flag is read from. The wire names are D3's, in `lowerCamelCase` (D3 §1.1). Where they differ the constraint column states the wire name. There is no third naming scheme, and this document does not invent one.

---

### 3.1 What changed, and what it costs

**In v0.1 this Part specified a component we were going to build.** The Policy Data Store was a database of policy facts with a thin read API in front of it, standing where a policy administration system would stand, and existing because InsureMO's own published positioning said it was not one.

**That component is not built.** On 21 August 2026 InsureMO confirmed — demonstrated against A5 v1.2, benefit by benefit — that it can carry the **adjudicable** benefit schedule: a tree two to three levels deep, aggregation from child to parent, per-day and per-event sub-limits, limits in **count** as well as money with an explicit unlimited representation, waiting periods that differ across the six condition classes, inherited co-payment, and the deduction ratio together with its triggering condition. It also holds the policy, member and coverage register and answers an as-at-a-date query. **Three systems, not four** (Framework v2.0 §2.1). The client has separately decided that **InsureMO is used for the policy side only** and that the claim platform is built entirely by us (C-BUS-09).

**Most of what this Part said survives, because most of it was never a specification of the store.** It was a specification of the **read model the claim engine needs** — which entities exist, which fields are on them, what each sentinel means, and what a consumer may and may not infer. That requirement has not changed by one field. What has changed is who is obliged to satisfy it.

| §3.1 in v0.1 said | §3.1 says now |
|---|---|
| Here is a component we build, and here is the exhaustive list of what we are *not* building in it | Here is the data the claim engine reads, and here is who holds each entity |
| The control against scope creep is Framework RK-06 and an in-scope list we police | **RK-06 is closed** — there is no store to creep. Scope pressure now lands on InsureMO's configuration, where it is a change request rather than our build |
| If InsureMO cannot hold the benefit tree, the schedule is mastered here and the claim engine does not change (P-06) | **There is no second place for it to go.** P-06's contract-first half still holds; **its substitutability half is withdrawn** — Framework v2.0 §3, **RK-14** |

**A requirement on a vendor is a weaker thing than a component you own, and this document should say so plainly rather than let a reader discover it.** Three differences bite in this Part specifically:

1. **We cannot refuse bad data at entry.** In v0.1 the benefit-schedule editor at §3.5.4 rejected an `INHERIT` on a root line, an overlapping effective window and a limit amount that did not match its limit type — at the keystroke, before anything was stored. Those rules are all still in §3.8, but they can now only run **at the adapter boundary, on data that has already been configured** (D3 §1.6). A schedule error is discovered when a claim reads it, not when someone types it.
2. **We cannot fix it.** The correction path in v0.1 was an administrative edit on a screen we owned. It is now a change made by someone else, in someone else's system, on someone else's schedule.
3. **Framework P-06 lost its fallback.** Every earlier version could promise that a failed InsureMO confirmation cost an interface and not an outcome, because the schedule had a second home. **The benefit-schedule contract now has exactly one implementation.** If it is not served as demonstrated, the remedy is a build rather than a swap, and both SC-03 and SC-08 rest on it. The exposure is carried once, as **RK-14**, and the mitigation is not a document — it is getting hands on the sandbox early and evaluating it against A5 v1.2 (**C-IMO-06**, now on the critical path). §10.7 restates what that means for this document.

**What this Part is, therefore.** §3.2 to §3.5 and §3.7 are **requirements on InsureMO**, expressed as the read model the Claim Platform is built against — they specify **F05** and **F07** from the consumer's side, and no feature we build. §3.6 is different: it specifies **F59**, the group policy and member bulk load, which is **ours**. §3.8 serves both.

**The boundary stated as one sentence, and it has not moved.** The policy side answers *what does the contract say*; it never answers *what should happen next*. Every "next" in the solution — adjudicate, decline, pay, notify — belongs to the Claim Platform, and that is now a decision (D-B closes as *none*) as well as a design.

---

### 3.2 The data model — the entities the claim engine reads

**Ten entities.** **Each is marked with the system that masters it**, and the mark is the load-bearing part of this table: a field marked **InsureMO** is something we must ask for and verify we have received; a field marked **Claim Platform** is something we build.

```
InsureMO
  product ──< plan ──< benefit_schedule_line ──< benefit_waiting_period
                            (self-referencing on parent_benefit_code)
  policy ──< benefit_level ─── plan
     │
     └──< insured_member

Claim Platform  (F58 — §5.20;  claimant — §3.2.10)
  payout_account ─── insured_member (by member_id)
  beneficiary    ─── payout_account
  claimant       ─── insured_member (by member_id)   one per claim
```

| Entity | Master | Feature | Where it is specified |
|---|---|---|---|
| `product` | **InsureMO** | F01, F05 | §3.2.1 |
| `plan` | **InsureMO** | F01 | §3.2.2 |
| `benefit_schedule_line` | **InsureMO** | **F07** | §3.2.3 |
| `benefit_waiting_period` | **InsureMO** | **F07** | §3.2.4 |
| `policy` | **InsureMO** | **F05** | §3.2.5 |
| `benefit_level` | **InsureMO** | **F05** | §3.2.6 |
| `insured_member` | **InsureMO** | **F05** | §3.2.7 |
| **`payout_account`** | **Claim Platform** | **F58** | §3.2.8, and the screen at **§5.20** |
| **`beneficiary`** | **Claim Platform** | **F58** | §3.2.9, and the screen at **§5.20** |
| **`claimant`** | **Claim Platform** | **F41, F45** | **§3.2.10**, captured at Part IV §4.5, displayed at §5.4.2 |

> **Why the last three crossed the line, and why it is not arbitrary.** A payout account exists to reimburse a claim. It is created at claim time, verified at claim time by a person holding a claim-side permission, and it is not a term of the contract of insurance. The payee is a party to a **settlement**, not to a policy — and it differs from the insured precisely in the cases a claim raises, a parent claiming for a minor being the common one. The **claimant** is the same argument one step further: it is the party who *asks*, and a person's standing to ask is established at the moment of asking, against that claim, not at the moment the policy was written. Framework v2.0 §2.1 puts it as one rule: *policy business goes to InsureMO, claim business comes to us.* The first two are **F58**; the third is F41 and F45, because it is captured at registration and displayed on the claim.

> **Three parties, and the document has said so for two revisions without specifying one of them.** §5.20.1 and Framework §4.4 both assert that the insured, the claimant and the payee are modelled separately. Until this revision only two of the three had a field table, and the third existed only as `claim.claimantUserId` inside the `SELF` scope predicate at §6.2.3. **That is what `G-B-02` was**: A3 §4.12's automatic conflict-of-interest half compares a member of staff's identity number against the insured's, the claimant's and the payee's, and the claimant's did not exist anywhere, so the comparison could never do anything but pass. §3.2.10 is what makes A3 §4.12 executable. **Part V §5.4.2 F34 to F37 is the same record seen from the console**, added in the same reissue from the other side.

> **`benefit_waiting_period` is not an eleventh entity.** Waiting-period days by condition class is a **field** of the benefit schedule line; six condition classes cannot be a scalar column, so it is normalised and returned as the `waitingPeriodDays` **map** on one benefit node (D3 §I-05). It has no independent life. Whether InsureMO models it as a table, a map or six columns is InsureMO's business — **what we require is the map on the node**, and that is what §3.3.4 asks for.

#### 3.2.1 `product` — **InsureMO**

| Field | Type | Req | Constraint / note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | `text(16)` | M | Primary key. `HC` in the pilot. Wire: `productCode` |
| `name` | `text(120)` | M | `HealthCare Pilot` |
| `line` | `enum(productLine)` | M | `HEALTH_INDIVIDUAL` in the pilot. Set per A5 §1 |
| `currency` | `enum(currency)` | M | `VND` only. **See the note below on where currency lives** |
| `term_months` | `int` | M | `12`. Descriptive; nothing computes a period from it |
| `status` | `enum(productStatus)` | M | `ACTIVE` · `WITHDRAWN`. **The set is ours, not a source's — see the note below** |
| `effective_from` | `date` | M | Required for F07's as-at-a-date semantics |
| `effective_to` | `date` | O | `null` = open-ended |

> **Currency sits on the product, not the plan.** A5 §10 and `A5_seed_v1.5.json` put it on the product; the old Framework §4.3 put it on the plan. A5 owns the pilot product's facts (§0.5), so the product carries it. A plan of a different currency within one product is not a case MVP 1 has, and holding the column in two places would let them disagree. Carried to InsureMO as a modelling requirement — **D2-102**.

> **`status`, `effective_from` and `effective_to` are absent from `A5_seed_v1.5.json`**, still, and the `productStatus` set is this document's, because no source enumerates it. In v0.1 that was a gap in our own seeding script. **It is now a question for InsureMO:** what product statuses does its model expose, and how do they map onto `ACTIVE` / `WITHDRAWN`? The mock behind `I-05` continues to set `status = ACTIVE`, `effective_from` = the product's inception date and `effective_to = null`. **D2-01 is retired** — it asked which values *we* should define, and we no longer define them; the mapping question is part of **D2-03**.

#### 3.2.2 `plan` — **InsureMO**

| Field | Type | Req | Constraint / note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `product_code` | `lookup(product)` | M | Foreign key |
| `plan_code` | `text(16)` | M | Primary key with `product_code`. `HC-STD` · `HC-PLS` · `HC-PRM`. Wire: `planCode` |
| `name` | `text(60)` | M | `Standard` · `Plus` · `Premium`. Displayed to staff; the customer sees the Vietnamese label from A1 |

Three rows in MVP 1. **There must be no plan-level limit column**: every limit is a benefit schedule line. This was a rule we enforced in v0.1 by not building the column; it is now a rule we assert by refusing to read one — a plan-level limit that InsureMO carried and we ignored would be a limit that binds the contract and not the settlement.

#### 3.2.3 `benefit_schedule_line` — **InsureMO** (F07)

One row per plan per benefit. **51 rows** in the pilot — 17 benefits × 3 plans (A5 §10). This is the entity C-IMO-01 was confirmed against, and it is the single largest thing this document now requires of a third party.

| Field | Type | Req | Constraint / note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `plan_code` | `lookup(plan)` | M | Primary key part 1 |
| `benefit_code` | `text(16)` | M | Primary key part 2. Dotted notation `100`, `100.1`, `100.1.1`. **Never parsed for hierarchy** — the parent pointer is authoritative, the dots are a naming convention. Wire: `code` inside the tree, `benefitCode` everywhere else (A1 §3) |
| `parent_benefit_code` | `lookup(benefit_schedule_line)` | O | `null` at a root. Must reference a row **with the same `plan_code`**. Wire: `parentCode` |
| `level` | `int` | M | 1 at a root, 2 for a child, 3 for a grandchild. **Wire name is `depth`, not `level`** — D3 §I-05 renames it because *level* also means a plan-on-a-policy (`benefit_level_no`), and one payload carrying both senses is a defect waiting to happen |
| `name` | `text(120)` | M | English working name. The Vietnamese customer-facing name comes from A1 |
| `limit_type` | `enum(limitType)` | M | `annual` · `per_event` · `per_day`. States which cap column governs. Not on the wire — a consumer reads the caps directly |
| `annual_cap` | `money` | C | Mandatory when `limit_type = annual`, otherwise `null`. `null` means **`included`** in A5's sense: no cap of its own, capped by the nearest ancestor that has one. Wire: `annualSumInsured` |
| `per_event_cap` | `money` | C | Mandatory when `limit_type = per_event`. Wire: `perEventLimit` |
| `per_day_cap` | `money` | C | Mandatory when `limit_type = per_day`. Wire: `perDayLimit` |
| `count_limit` | `int` | M | **The second limit dimension, independent of money.** `0` means **unlimited** — see the sentinel note. Wire: `maxCount`. Confirmed representable by **C-IMO-01b** |
| `count_unit` | `enum(countUnit)` | C | `DAY` · `VISIT`. Mandatory when `count_limit > 0`; `null` is permitted when `count_limit = 0`. Wire: `countUnit` |
| `copay_pct` | `text(8)` | M | Either an integer basis-point value rendered as digits, or the literal `INHERIT`. **See the co-payment note.** Wire: `coPaymentBp` |
| `deduction_pct` | `pct` | O | Integer basis points. `null` where the benefit carries no deduction. Wire: `deductionRatioBp` |
| `deduction_condition` | `enum(deductionCondition)` | C | Mandatory when `deduction_pct` is not null, and `null` when it is. One member in MVP 1: `PROVIDER_OFF_NETWORK` (A5 §4.3). Wire: `deductionCondition` |
| `effective_from` | `date` | M | **The whole of F07 rests on this.** See the note below |
| `effective_to` | `date` | O | `null` = still in force |

**The `0 = unlimited` sentinel, and what it means to a consumer.** `count_limit = 0` does **not** mean the benefit allows zero days or zero visits — it means the count dimension is not limited at all. Both reference systems use the convention and it must be honoured explicitly rather than inferred. A consumer that treats `0` as a numeric ceiling declines every claim on `100.2` surgery, `200.1` consultation and `200.2` medication, which in this product is most of them. There is no way to express "zero permitted" and none is needed: a benefit that is not payable is not in the schedule. **This sentinel now has to be *asked for* rather than built**, and C-IMO-01b is the confirmation that it can be — a schedule that could hold money but not days would have forced the tree back to us (Framework §4.1.1).

**The `INHERIT` co-payment sentinel, and what it means to a consumer.** `copay_pct` is mandatory on **every** node. Where a child takes its parent's rate, the value is the literal string `INHERIT` — in the pilot, `200.1`, `200.2`, `200.3` and `300.1` all inherit. A consumer resolves `INHERIT` to the **nearest ancestor carrying an integer rate**, at snapshot time, and writes the resolved integer onto the claim; an `INHERIT` that reaches the root without finding one is a schedule error and fails at the adapter boundary (D3 §1.6). The three alternatives were each rejected for a stated reason: `null` already means *not known* (D3 §1.2), an omitted property means *no co-payment* under the ignore-unknown-fields rule and would silently pay a 20%-co-pay benefit in full, and a numeric flag value would be arithmetically valid and therefore silent. A benefit that genuinely carries **no** co-payment carries integer `0` — a rate of nothing, not an absence of a rate. The mock's mapping is exactly three cases: `20` → `2000`, `"inherit"` → `INHERIT`, `null` → `0`.

**Why `copay_pct` is `text(8)` and not `pct`.** It carries two kinds of value. Holding it as text is what makes arithmetic on an unresolved sentinel fail loudly instead of quietly producing zero, and it is the same reasoning D3 §I-05 gives for putting the string on the wire.

> **The sentinels are the sharpest thing this Part now asks of a vendor.** Each of the three is a value that is *arithmetically valid* if it is misread, and therefore fails silently rather than loudly. In v0.1 we guaranteed them by writing the store. We now guarantee them by **specifying them in the contract, checking them at the adapter, and exercising them on the sandbox against A5 v1.2 before we believe them** (C-IMO-06). That is a weaker guarantee, and it is the reason §3.8's V-111 … V-115 have moved from the screen to the adapter.

**Deduction ratio and its triggering condition.** The pair is the one mechanism in the product that depends on a fact about the **episode** rather than on the benefit alone. InsureMO holds both halves — the rate and the condition name — and evaluates neither. `PROVIDER_OFF_NETWORK` is answered by the Claim Platform against the `in_network` flag on the provider master (F57, §5.17), **per insured event, not per claim**, because one claim can carry a network visit and a non-network visit. In the pilot the pair is carried by `200` and `300` only, at 20% (A5 §4.3), and it inherits nowhere: a child with `deduction_pct = null` carries no deduction of its own, and the ancestor's applies to the amounts that reach the ancestor.

> **Effective dating is where a confirmed capability is thinnest.** `effective_from` / `effective_to` are required on every line, are returned by D3 §I-05, and are what makes the as-at-a-date query mean anything. **C-IMO-05 — product versioning and effective-dating behaviour — is confirmed as a capability and open on its detail**, and the Framework names it as the one contract-detail item where a surprise costs design rather than a mock. They are also absent from `A5_seed_v1.2.json`, so the mock cannot exercise `422 NO_SCHEDULE_AT_DATE` and `CLM-CONSOLE-007` cannot be tested — open item **D2-02**, unchanged by this reissue except that it now has a second half: the seed must carry them *and* InsureMO must honour them.

#### 3.2.4 `benefit_waiting_period` — **InsureMO** (F07)

The normalised form of one field on `benefit_schedule_line`. Returned as the `waitingPeriodDays` map. Confirmed as **C-IMO-01** — waiting periods that differ across the six condition classes were part of the demonstration.

| Field | Type | Req | Constraint / note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `plan_code` | `lookup(plan)` | M | Primary key part 1 |
| `benefit_code` | `lookup(benefit_schedule_line)` | M | Primary key part 2. **Carried at benefit-group roots only** — `100`, `200`, `300`, `400`, `500`. A descendant takes its root's waiting periods |
| `condition_class` | `enum(conditionClass)` | M | Primary key part 3. **Exactly six**: `PRE` *Bệnh có sẵn* · `SPE` *Bệnh đặc biệt* · `GEN` *Bệnh thông thường* · `BIR` *Sinh đẻ* · `MAT` *Biến chứng thai sản* · `ACC` *Tai nạn*. A1 §4 is the normative list of codes; A5 §5 is the normative table of day counts |
| `days` | `int` | M | Days from the **member's coverage start date**, not the policy inception date |

**The absent combination is absent, not zero.** A5 §5 marks combinations that cannot arise as `n/a`, and A5 §10 requires that they are **not carried at all**. On the wire they appear as `null`, and `null` means *the combination cannot arise* — a claim that produces one is a **data error, not a zero-day waiting period** (A1 §4). The pilot carries 17 of the 30 root × class combinations per plan: `400` maternity carries only `BIR` 270 and `MAT` 90; `300` dental carries no `SPE`; `500` accident carries all four at 0.

**Nobody upstream performs waiting-period arithmetic.** InsureMO returns `days` and returns `coveragePeriod.from`. The comparison against the service date is the Claim Platform's, at A5 §6.1, and the assessor sees `CLM-CONSOLE-004` when it fails. **Two facts and no subtraction — that division is the whole design**, and it survives the change of who holds the facts.

#### 3.2.5 `policy` — **InsureMO** (F05)

| Field | Type | Req | Constraint / note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `policy_no` | `text(20)` | M | Primary key. Format `POL-YY-NNNNNN`. **Never parsed for meaning.** Wire: `policyNo` |
| `type` | `enum(policyType)` | M | `INDIVIDUAL` · `GROUP` |
| `holder_name` | `text(200)` | M | A person for `INDIVIDUAL`, a company for `GROUP`. *Bên mua bảo hiểm* — **not necessarily an insured member** (A1 §2) |
| `holder_id_number` | `text(20)` | M | CCCD for a person, tax code for a company |
| `period_from` | `date` | M | Inclusive. Wire: `policyPeriod.from` |
| `period_to` | `date` | M | **Inclusive.** Must be ≥ `period_from`. Wire: `policyPeriod.to` |
| `status` | `enum(policyStatus)` | M | `ACTIVE` · `CANCELLED`. **Two members only — see the note below** |
| `source` | `enum(policySource)` | M | `ISSUED_J1` (issued through InsureMO in J1) · `IMPORTED` (arrived through F59 / I-14). **See the note below** |
| **`rule_set_ref`** | `text(200)` | **M** | **The rule set or policy wording in force on this policy** — the reference the customer's own document carries. Wire: `ruleSetRef`. **Confirmed returned — decision `B2`, 24/08/2026.** Snapshotted at registration and rendered at §5.4.2 F39. **Read by nothing**: no step of the chain consults it and A5 owns every benefit term. It exists so that a decline can quote the clause in the document the customer is holding |
| `premium_paid` | `bool` | M | Reported, **never tested by the policy side**. Set on payment in J1 or supplied by the import |

> **Two status values, and expiry is not one of them.** A policy past `period_to` is not `EXPIRED`; it fails the date test in §3.3.3's algorithm and answers `AFTER_POLICY_END`. An `EXPIRED` status would be a second source of truth for the same fact, and the two would drift the first time a batch job did not run. **This is now a requirement, and it is a real one:** if InsureMO's policy model carries a lifecycle status richer than two values — and a platform whose demonstrated strength is issuance almost certainly does — then **the mapping from its set to ours must be specified, agreed and pinned**, because every unmapped value silently becomes "not `ACTIVE`" and declines the claim. Open item **D2-03**, re-aimed at the vendor.

> **`source` was a question in v0.3 and it is a requirement in v0.4.** In v0.1 we set it, because both paths wrote to us. **`C-IMO-10` is answered yes** (decision `B7`, 24/08/2026): F59 writes into InsureMO through the bulk member load, so **`IMPORTED` is a value InsureMO must set and expose**, and it is what tells a reader that a group policy arrived through F59 rather than through J1 issuance. **The two-member-list branch that the `no` answer would have produced is withdrawn** — §3.6.7 states the single path and no longer states two.

#### 3.2.6 `benefit_level` — the plan on a policy — **InsureMO** (F05)

A policy may carry several. Each member points at exactly one. **Confirmed as C-IMO-01c**, and it is what group cover needs.

| Field | Type | Req | Constraint / note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `policy_no` | `lookup(policy)` | M | Primary key part 1 |
| `benefit_level_no` | `int` | M | Primary key part 2. Sequential from 1 within the policy. Wire: `benefitLevelNo` |
| `plan_code` | `lookup(plan)` | M | Which of the three tiers this level grants |
| `effective_from` | `date` | M | Must fall inside the policy period |
| `effective_to` | `date` | O | `null` = to the end of the policy period. Must fall inside the policy period |

**Never called "level" unqualified** (A1 §2). *Level* on a benefit schedule line is depth in the tree; *benefit level* is a plan attached to a policy. The two are different concepts, they are both integers, and D3 renamed the first to `depth` precisely so that one payload cannot carry both. **This rename is now a request rather than a decision**, and it is the sort of request that is cheap to make before the schemas are written and expensive afterwards — C-IMO-03.

#### 3.2.7 `insured_member` — **InsureMO** (F05)

| Field | Type | Req | Constraint / note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `member_id` | `text(20)` | M | Primary key. Format `MBR-NNNNNN`. Wire: `memberId` |
| `policy_no` | `lookup(policy)` | M | |
| `member_no` | `int` | M | Sequential from 1 within the policy. Unique with `policy_no` |
| `full_name` | `text(200)` | M | Vietnamese, with diacritics. Searched **diacritic-insensitively** (§3.3.1) |
| `date_of_birth` | `date` | M | Wire: `dateOfBirth` |
| `sex` | `enum(sex)` | M | `M` · `F` |
| `id_number` | `text(20)` | O | **Nullable, and this is load-bearing.** Children have no CCCD — `MBR-000912` and `MBR-000914` in the seed carry `null`. A search on `idNumber` therefore cannot find a child, which is why `card_no` exists |
| `card_no` | `text(20)` | M | *Số thẻ bảo hiểm.* Issued per member **including dependants**. Unique across the register. **A primary search key at claim intake** (A1 §2) |
| `relationship` | `enum(relationship)` | M | `SELF` · `SPOUSE` · `CHILD` · `PARENT` · `EMPLOYEE`. Relationship to the **policyholder**, not to another member |
| `benefit_level_no` | `lookup(benefit_level)` | M | With `policy_no`. Which level this member's cover is drawn from |
| `coverage_from` | `date` | M | Inclusive. **May be later than the policy's `period_from`** — the mid-term joiner. Wire: `coveragePeriod.from` |
| `coverage_to` | `date` | M | Inclusive. **May be earlier than the policy's `period_to`** — the leaver. Wire: `coveragePeriod.to` |
| **`continuous_cover_from`** | `date` | **M** | **The date this member's *uninterrupted* participation began**, which may be earlier than `coverage_from` and may lie in an earlier policy. **`null` where — and only where — `renewal_status` is `LẦN_ĐẦU`**: the member is a first-time entrant and there is no earlier participation to point at. Wire: `continuousCoverFrom`, beside `coveragePeriod.from`. **Confirmed returned at member-on-policy level — decision `B1`, 24/08/2026** |
| **`renewal_status`** | `enum(renewalStatus)` | **M** | **`LẦN_ĐẦU` · `TÁI_TỤC` · `KHÔNG_XÁC_ĐỊNH`** (A1 §4.6). Whether **this member's participation in this policy** is a first-time one or a continuation — an attribute of the participation, not of the policy and not of the person. Wire: `renewalStatus`. **Confirmed returned at member-on-policy level — decision `B1`.** `KHÔNG_XÁC_ĐỊNH` is a real answer and not an absence: it means InsureMO holds the member but cannot establish continuity, and §3.3.3's `V-119` is what runs then |
| `status` | `enum(memberStatus)` | M | `ACTIVE` · `ENDED`. **Descriptive only — see the note below** |

> **`status` must not be part of the coverage test.** D3 §I-05 fixes the test at exactly the five comparisons of §3.3.3 and member status is not among them. `MBR-001004` in the seed is `ENDED` with `coverage_to = 2026-09-30`, and a claim for a service date in August 2026 is **covered**. The dates carry the truth. A consumer that filtered on `status = ACTIVE` would decline every valid claim a leaver submits after they leave, which is most of the claims a leaver submits. **State it to InsureMO as a requirement on the response, not as an assumption about the store**: if `I-05`'s member search or coverage read filters on status anywhere in its own implementation, every leaver's late claim disappears and nothing in our system can tell that it did.

> **`card_no` uniqueness is now someone else's invariant.** It is the one search key that finds a dependant, and v0.1 enforced it with a unique constraint we owned. It is now an expectation of InsureMO's register — and the one thing we can still do about it is **detect a duplicate at registration and refuse to guess**, which is exactly what Part V's multi-match path already does (§5.2.3, S-04). The path was written for a data defect we were going to prevent; it is now the primary control.

> **This was the one field in Part III whose absence changed an outcome on the most ordinary claim there is, and it is answered.** *(Register: **B-15** renewal continuity. Decision **`B1`**, 24 August 2026.)* `G-B-01` recorded it as the strongest finding of the old Part III: A5 §5's waiting-period table had no data to run against, and v0.1's answer — *waiting periods run from the member's coverage start date* — is correct **only where every member is a first-time entrant**. On an annually renewed group policy, in the month after renewal, nobody is.
>
> Concretely, and this is the claim the answer unblocks: a member insured continuously for five years, whose policy renewed last month, attends an outpatient consultation this week. `coverage_from` is last month. The thirty-day general waiting period measured from `coverage_from` **declines the claim**. The opposite default was worse and cost more: assume every member is continuing and the two-hundred-and-seventy-day maternity waiting period never applies to anybody.
>
> **What changed.** **InsureMO returns both the renewal status and the continuous-cover start, at the level of a member on a policy** — not of the policy and not of the person, which was the whole of the question. Both fields are therefore **mandatory on this entity** rather than conditional, §3.3.3's anchor rule runs against real data, and **A5 §5's carry-over rule runs for the first time.** **`D2-11` and `D2-129` are closed** — one question with two consumers, and both consumers are served.
>
> **What is still owed, and it is a contract rather than a capability.** **D3 §I-05 carries neither field.** A capability confirmed in conversation and absent from the interface specification is a build nobody can start, and the correction is **`D2-113`**, now on the critical path rather than beside it. `renewalStatus`'s wire representation is raised with it as **`D2-171`**.

#### 3.2.8 `payout_account` — **Claim Platform (F58)**

Held by us. The screen is **§5.20**; the customer's capture of it is Part IV §4.5.

| Field | Type | Req | Constraint / note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `account_ref` | `text(20)` | M | Primary key. Format `ACC-NNNNNN-N`. Wire: `payoutAccountRef` |
| `member_id` | `text(20)` | M | The insured member the account belongs to. **A reference into InsureMO's register, not a foreign key** — see the note below. A member may hold more than one |
| `bank_code` | `text(10)` | M | Bank identifier. `999999` is the reserved test BIN throughout D3 |
| `account_no` | `text(30)` | M | Digits. **Masked in every display** except §5.20's detail panel |
| `account_name` | `text(140)` | M | **Unaccented uppercase Latin**, as banks hold it — `PHAM QUANG DUY`, not `Phạm Quang Duy`. **Never typed** — BR-PAY-1 |
| `verified` | `bool` | M | Name verification against the bank. Wire: `accountNameVerified`. **A payment instruction against an unverified account is refused `422 ACCOUNT_NOT_VERIFIED` at I-11** (A3 §4.6) |

> **`member_id` crosses a system boundary, and that is new.** In v0.1 this was a foreign key inside one database, and referential integrity was free. It is now a reference from our record to a record InsureMO holds, so **nothing prevents a payout account from outliving the member it names** — a member removed from InsureMO's register leaves an account pointing at nothing. The mitigations are the ones already in the design and they are enough for MVP 1: a member is **end-dated, never deleted** (§3.6.6), and the account is only ever read in the context of a claim that carries a policy snapshot. It is recorded here because it is the kind of thing that is obvious in the design and invisible in the code.

**Verification is performed by an assessor or an administrator** (A3 §3.2), on the console, after the claim is registered. **It is not performed by the customer** — the mobile app records the account as unverified and Part IV §4.5 says what the customer sees in the meantime. Changing the account **re-triggers verification** and, if a settlement is already approved, requires an approver to re-release the payment (A3 §4.5, `CLM-CONSOLE-010`). §5.20 is where all of this happens and §5.12 is where its absence bites.

#### 3.2.9 `beneficiary` — the payee — **Claim Platform (F58)**

Held **distinct from the insured member and from the claimant**, because the payee determines where money goes and reconciling that after the fact is the failure mode that matters most (Framework v2.0 §4.3).

| Field | Type | Req | Constraint / note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `policy_no` | `text(20)` | M | Primary key part 1. A reference into InsureMO's register |
| `member_id` | `text(20)` | M | Primary key part 2. **The insured whose cover is used**, not the payee |
| `payee_name` | `text(200)` | M | Defaults to the member's `full_name` |
| `relationship_to_insured` | `enum(relationship)` | M | Same set as `insured_member.relationship`. `SELF` in the common case |
| `id_number` | `text(20)` | M | **The payee's**, not the insured's. Mandatory even when the payee is a minor's parent — this is the identity the payment is made against |
| `payout_account_ref` | `lookup(payout_account)` | M | May reference an account belonging to a **different** member — §5.20 |

**One row per member, created automatically, defaulting to the insured.** The seed carries 12 members and 12 beneficiary rows. Two of them are the reason the entity exists: `MBR-000912` and `MBR-000914` are minors whose payee is `Phạm Quang Duy`, `PARENT`, paid to **his** account `ACC-000911-1`. Insured, claimant and payee do not coincide, and a design that held the payee as three columns on the member would have to be rebuilt the first time it happened.

> **The seed still models both entities under the deleted store's schema — unchanged at v1.5, and the seed's own `cross_system_reference_note` now says so.** The file was cut when all nine entities lived in one place. Both collections must be re-cut as Claim Platform records keyed by reference rather than by foreign key — a correction owed to A5, **D2-110**.

#### 3.2.10 `claimant` — the party who asks — **Claim Platform (F41, F45)**

*(Register: **B-07** · **B-08** · **B-09**)*

Held **distinct from the insured member and from the payee**, and carrying **two classifications that answer two different questions**. One row per claim.

| Field | Type | Req | Constraint / note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `claim_no` | `text(20)` | M | Primary key. One claimant per claim |
| `member_id` | `text(20)` | M | The insured member the claim is for. A reference into InsureMO's register, not a foreign key — the §3.2.8 note applies unchanged |
| `standing` | `enum(claimantStanding)` | M | **The legal question.** `SELF` *bản thân* · `GUARDIAN` *người giám hộ* · `HEIR` *người thừa kế* · `AUTHORISED` *người được uỷ quyền*. **Four values, and each pulls its own document requirement** — see the table below. Set to register in A1 §4 |
| `relationship` | `enum(claimantRelationship)` | C | **The family question.** `FATHER` · `MOTHER` · `SPOUSE` · `CHILD` · `GRANDFATHER` · `GRANDMOTHER` · `SIBLING` · `OTHER`. **Mandatory where `standing ≠ SELF`; must be empty where `standing = SELF`** (V-116). Set to register in A1 §4 |
| `full_name` | `text(200)` | M | §2.9's width. **Defaults to the insured member's `full_name` and is locked to it where `standing = SELF`** — V-117 |
| `id_number` | `text(20)` | M | **The claimant's.** Same lock as `full_name` under V-117. **This is the field that makes A3 §4.12's automatic half executable** |
| **`contact_email`** | `text(160)` | **M** | **The contact email for this claim** — typed by the customer on the claim form (§4.5 F15), not read from any party record. **This is the address every customer message about this claim is sent to** (§6.1.2a). Wire: `contactEmail` |
| **`contact_phone`** | `text(10)` | **M** | **The contact telephone for this claim.** 10 digits. Typed on the claim form (§4.5 F16). Wire: `contactPhone`. **Mandatory from v0.4** — decision `B4` |
| `claimant_user_id` | `text(20)` | C | The app account that submitted, where the claim came from the mobile app. **`null` for a claim registered by staff.** This is the value §6.2.3's `SELF` scope predicate reads, and it is now one field of a record rather than the whole of it |
| `created_by` / `created_at` | `lookup(User)` / `datetime` | M | `SYSTEM` where the app created it |

**Two dimensions, because they answer two questions, and one of them is not the other.**

*Standing* answers **on what legal footing does this person ask for money.** *Relationship* answers **who is this person to the patient.** A father claiming for his minor child is `GUARDIAN` + `FATHER`; a widow claiming under a death benefit is `HEIR` + `SPOUSE`; a colleague sent to the counter with a signed authority is `AUTHORISED` + `OTHER`. **Collapsing them loses the second one in every case where the first is not `SELF`**, and it is the second that a document requirement keys on.

**Standing drives the document requirement.**

| `standing` | What the claimant must additionally supply | Requirement level |
|---|---|---|
| `SELF` | Nothing beyond the identity document already on the checklist | — |
| `GUARDIAN` | Proof of the relationship to the insured — birth certificate, household record or equivalent | **`REQUIRED`** |
| `HEIR` | Proof of inheritance or of designation as beneficiary | **`REQUIRED`** |
| `AUTHORISED` | The written authority | **`REQUIRED`** |

> **A4 owes two new document types and the conditional rule that selects them** — *Giấy tờ chứng minh mối quan hệ* and *Giấy xác nhận quyền thừa kế / uỷ quyền*. A4 §6's checklist is keyed on episode type alone today; it needs a second key. **This document does not write A4's rows**, per §0.5. Carried as **D2-114**, a correction owed to A4.

> **These two fields were `email` and `phone` in v0.3 and they are renamed, because what they are changed.** *(Decision **`B4`**, 24 August 2026.)* In v0.3 they were **the claimant's** addresses, captured because `G-B-03` had recorded that `insured_member` carries no email column and that §6.1.2's `EMAIL` channel therefore delivered to a field the data model did not contain. **The decision is broader and simpler than the problem it was written for: the customer enters an email and a telephone when they submit a claim, and those are that claim's contact details.** Not the claimant's permanent address, not the account's, not the member register's — **the claim's**. Everything the platform sends a customer about this claim goes there.
>
> **`D2-14` closes as withdrawn, not as answered.** Whether InsureMO's member register holds an email address is still unknown and is now **a question with no consumer**: correspondence does not wait on it, and §6.1.2a no longer has a row that does.
>
> **Three consequences, and each is written down because each will otherwise be assumed the other way.**
>
> **1 — It is snapshot-safe by construction, and the construction is the one-row-per-claim key.** This entity has `claim_no` as its primary key, so a claim's contact details are captured *with* the claim and cannot be edited by anything that edits an account. **A customer who changes the email on their profile in March does not redirect the decline letter for a claim decided in February.** That is `P-02`'s property arrived at for free rather than enforced by a rule — there is no live read to forbid, because there is no second place the address lives.
>
> **2 — It splits J1 from J2, and a reader will otherwise assume one address.** **The certificate at purchase (J1, §4.3) goes to the account's registered address**, because at that moment there is no claim and no claim contact — the customer is buying, not claiming. **Everything about a claim (J2) goes to the claim contact.** The two are frequently the same string and are never the same *field*, and the case that separates them is ordinary: a father buys the family cover under his own address and his adult daughter, claiming on her own cover, gives hers. **A2 must carry the split**, because it owns which audience a message addresses — raised as **`D2-141`**.
>
> **3 — A customer can type any address, and the mitigation is confirmation rather than a control.** Nothing prevents a typo or a deliberately foreign address. **This is not the payment-redirection risk and it must not be treated as one**: correspondence is not money, BR-PAY-1 to BR-PAY-4 and A3 §4.6 stand between an address and a payment, and no letter moves a dong. **But a decline letter is a document about someone's health**, and one wrong character sends it to a stranger. **The address is therefore echoed back for confirmation before submission** — `V-407`, §4.5 — as a read-back of what was typed, not a second entry box. **Re-typing produces the same typo twice**; reading it back is what catches it, and it costs the customer one glance on a screen they were already on. What is deliberately *not* built is a verification loop: a code emailed to the address before the claim may be submitted would block a claim on a mail server, which is §2.10 exactly — an operational failure rendered as a claim outcome.

> **What this does not do.** It does not make the claimant an authenticated actor, it does not give them a permission, and it does not change §6.2.3's `SELF` scope — which still resolves through `claimant_user_id` and therefore still resolves to nothing for a claim registered at a counter, which is correct: a claim nobody submitted through the app has no app-side reader. §7.4 states it as a row of its own.

> **Two names for one set, and the collision is recorded rather than resolved here.** Part V §5.4.2 **F36** carries the same classification as `enum(claimantCapacity)` with the Vietnamese members `BẢN_THÂN` · `NGƯỜI_GIÁM_HỘ` · `NGƯỜI_THỪA_KẾ` · `NGƯỜI_ĐƯỢC_UỶ_QUYỀN`, and **F37** carries `claimantRelationship` with Vietnamese members. The two parts were written in the same week against the same register rows and neither is wrong about the *concept*. **§2.6 settles the form** — an enum code is English, uppercase-snake, and A1 §4 maps it to the Vietnamese display text — so the English set above is the conformant one and the Vietnamese members are display text that has been written into the code column. **A1 owns the set and neither part may define it** (§2.3): the reconciliation is one name, one member set, in A1, and it is folded into **D2-115** with the request **D2-124** already makes. Until A1 allocates, a reader should treat `claimantStanding` and `claimantCapacity` as the same set under two names, and **no new set is created by the pair**. Likewise **V-709** (§5.20.5) is Part V's enforcement, on the console, of the rule this Part allocates as **V-117** for the record and Part IV §4.11 cites on the app; **V-116** has no separate console identifier because §5.4.2 F37 states it inline in its *Req* cell. Each rule is defined once, on the surface where it first applies, and the correspondence is noted at §8.1 rather than duplicated.

---

### 3.3 The six reads we need InsureMO to expose (F05, F07)

Six operations, serving two D3 interfaces. In v0.1 these were endpoints we built; they are now **the shape of what we need back**, and D3 owns the contract. **I-01 and I-05 are re-pointed by Framework v2.0 §6 — both reverse direction**, because a store that was written to has become a system that is read from. D3 v1.1 still points them at the store; **until D3's realignment pass lands, Framework v2.0 wins** (Framework §8, and §0.5a) — carried as **D2-111**.

| # | Operation | Serves | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Member search | **I-05** | Find an insured member |
| 2 | Policy detail with members | **I-05** | Policy, its benefit levels, its members |
| 3 | Member coverage **as at a date** | **I-05** | The one derived read — §3.3.3 |
| 4 | Benefit schedule **as at a date, as a tree** | **I-05**, and **I-01** in the same shape | What the claim engine snapshots |
| 5 | Policy issued — policy, members, benefits | **I-04** | InsureMO → us, on issuance in J1 |
| 6 | Bulk member load — **create and end-date** | **I-14 onward write** | **Confirmed to exist — `C-IMO-10` answers yes** (decision `B7`, 24/08/2026). §3.6.7. **The contract is not written**, which is `D2-172` |

> **Operation 5 changed direction and operation 6 changed owner.** In v0.1, operation 5 was `POST /v1/policies` — an endpoint *we* exposed, that InsureMO called. It is now InsureMO's event or response and **we** are the receiver (I-04, style still open — C-IMO-04). Operation 6 was our group-import endpoint; the loader is now unambiguously ours (**F59**, §3.6), and **where it writes is no longer open** — `B7` confirms a bulk member load with both a create and an end-date operation, so it writes into InsureMO and §3.6.7 carries one path rather than two.

> **The paths, methods, payload schemas, error codes and retry behaviour are D3's, and they are not restated here.** v0.1 restated them because we were building both ends. We are building one end, so this Part specifies **what the answer must contain and what a consumer may infer from it**, and D3 specifies the wire. Six of the sixteen interfaces touch InsureMO (I-01 … I-06) and **D3 keeps every one of them marked *Provisional*** until C-IMO-03, C-IMO-04 and C-IMO-05 return the schemas.

#### 3.3.1 Member search

*(Register: **B-13** member search keys — **InsureMO-dependent** · **B-14** the result table, reduced)*

Parameters: name, date of birth, identity number, card number, **policy number and product code**.

> **`orgUnit` was a seventh parameter in v0.3 and it is removed.** **MVP 1 has exactly one organisational unit** — decision `B3`, 24 August 2026, and a client scope decision rather than a vendor answer. A search parameter that every record satisfies narrows nothing, and a **column that renders the same value on every row is worse than an absent one**: it teaches the reader that the column discriminates, which is the reading that costs an hour the first time somebody uses it to explain why a search returned two hundred rows. **The parameter, the result column and §5.2.5 F12 all go.** **`D2-12` closes as withdrawn** — the vendor question is real and no longer has a consumer, and it comes back with the second unit, not before.

| Parameter | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `text(200)` | C | **Diacritic-insensitive contains-match** (§2.11 UI-10, UI-11). `thang` must match `Nguyễn Văn Thắng` |
| `dob` | `date` | C | Exact. Narrows `name` |
| `idNumber` | `text(20)` | C | **Exact match** |
| `cardNo` | `text(20)` | C | **Exact match** |
| `policyNo` | `text(20)` | C | **Exact match. New in v0.3** — see the note below |
| `productCode` | `text(16)` | C | **Exact match. New in v0.3.** `HC` in the pilot, so it narrows nothing today and everything in year two |

**At least one parameter is required** (§2.11 UI-13).

> **Why three more keys, when four already work.** Because four do not. `G-B-08` recorded the failure and it is a failure of the commonest search there is: an assessor searching a common Vietnamese given name gets more than fifty hits and the search is **refused**, not truncated — correctly, per the outcome table below — and the assessor has no way to narrow it. Date of birth is often not on the document in front of them; the identity number is absent for a child; the card number is what they are trying to find. **The policy number is the one narrowing key an assessor reliably holds**, because it is on almost every document a customer sends, and it is the one key the search does not accept. Adding it turns a refused search into a single hit.
>
> **`policyNo` and `productCode` are cheap, and that is the whole argument for them.** Both are attributes of `policy` (§3.2.5) that I-05 already returns; asking it to filter on them is asking it to filter on its own columns.

**The result set.** The answer carries **one row per insured member × policy pair** — a member on two policies is two rows, not one — with:

| Column | Source | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `memberId` | I-05 | |
| `fullName` | I-05 | §2.9 width. Never truncated in the grid (§2.11 UI-19) |
| `dateOfBirth` | I-05 | |
| `cardNo` | I-05 | |
| `policyNo` | I-05 | **The pair's second half.** This is what makes the row a pair rather than a person |
| `policyType` | I-05 | `INDIVIDUAL` · `GROUP`. A group row and an individual row for the same person are the case this table exists to show |
| `policyStatus` | I-05 | |
| `productCode`, `planCode` | I-05 | |
| `benefitLevelNo` | I-05 | |
| `coveragePeriod` | I-05 | **This member's own window on this policy** (§3.2.7), not the policy period |
| `continuousCoverFrom` | I-05 | §3.2.7. **Always returned** from v0.4 (`B1`); empty only where `renewalStatus` is `LẦN_ĐẦU` |
| `renewalStatus` | I-05 | §3.2.7, A1 §4.6. **New in v0.4** (`B1`) |
| **`customerCode`** | I-05 | **New in v0.4** (`B6`). The policy holder's customer identifier as InsureMO holds it. Displayed and **filterable**; nothing computes from it |
| **`distributionChannel`** | I-05 | **New in v0.4** (`B6`). How the policy was sold. Displayed and **filterable**; nothing computes from it |

**No coverage decision is made here** — a search result is an identity, not an entitlement. **Nor is a benefit level a plan**: the row shows which level the member draws from, and what that level grants is §3.3.4's read.

> **`B-14`: four columns are available, two are taken and two are declined. The reasoning is stated here rather than left to be re-argued.** *(Decision **`B6`**, 24 August 2026.)* v0.3 dropped all four of the reference's extra result columns — **customer code**, **distribution channel**, the **agent who wrote the business** and an **insurance-group** classification — on the ground that we could not populate any of them. **InsureMO returns all four.** That answers *can we*, and it does not answer *should we*, and the two are different questions.
>
> **`customerCode` and `distributionChannel` are taken.** Both are cheap — they arrive in the ordinary policy payload and cost a column each — and both are **useful for filtering a pilot**: *which channel are these claims coming from* is one of the few questions a pilot exists to answer, and a customer code is the key an operations person uses to talk to somebody outside this system about the same policy. Neither is read by any rule, and neither is a benefit term.
>
> **`agent` and `customerGroup` are not taken, and availability is not a reason to add them.** **We have no CRM and no agent model** — which is precisely why these two were dropped in the first place, and the answer to `B6` did not change that. An agent column would render an identifier that resolves to nothing in this system: nobody can click it, no screen explains it, and no report groups by it, so it is a name that looks like a link and is not one. The insurance-group classification is a construct of the reference product model that ours does not have, so its values would be another system's vocabulary rendered as though it were ours. **A column nothing reads is not free** — it occupies width on the one grid where a reader is matching a name under time pressure (§2.11 UI-19), and it has to be redacted, exported, tested and explained like every other column. **The two are added when something reads them, and the sentence to look for is a screen or a report that names one.**

| Outcome | What we require |
|---|---|
| 0 … 50 hits | An empty result is an empty list, **not a not-found error**. Zero members matching a search is a business answer (§2.11 UI-25 — the no-match sentence, with the criteria) |
| More than 50 hits | **Refused, not truncated** — `422 TOO_BROAD`. A truncated list silently hides the right member (D3 §I-05). **This is the one item on this page most likely to be delivered differently**, because paging a large result set is the ordinary thing for a platform to do and it is exactly wrong here. If InsureMO pages instead of refusing, the console must refuse on its behalf: §5.2.5's **V-501** already says so, and it becomes the enforcement rather than a restatement. **Note that the three new keys reduce how often this is reached, and do not change the rule** |
| No parameter supplied | Rejected |

**Diacritic-insensitive matching is not a nicety.** An assessor typing `thang` who is shown nothing will conclude the member does not exist, and the claim goes down the *no member matched* path at §5.2.3 — which asks the customer to correct details that were already correct.

**Where the console renders this**: §5.2.5's S-04, whose field table carries the three new parameters and whose result grid carries the columns above, under §2.11's grid conventions.

#### 3.3.2 Policy detail

The policy row, its benefit levels, and its members with their coverage periods and benefit-level pointers. **No payout accounts and no beneficiaries** — those are ours now (§3.2.8, §3.2.9, F58), and the console assembles them from its own records against the `memberId`. **This is a change from v0.1, where one response carried everything**, and it is the visible cost of splitting the model across two systems: §5.20's panel is a second read, and the claim's snapshot (§5.2.4) takes both.

#### 3.3.3 Member coverage as at a date — the one derived read

**Every coverage check in J2 resolves to this**, and it is the one piece of logic on which every coverage decision in the system depends. It is stated as an algorithm because a re-derivation elsewhere is how two systems come to disagree about whether someone was insured — and there are now two systems.

```
coverage(memberId, asOfDate):

  1  m ← insured_member[memberId]
     if m is absent            → member not found
  2  p ← policy[m.policy_no]
  3  l ← benefit_level[m.policy_no, m.benefit_level_no]
  4  if asOfDate is absent     → asOfDate ← today (Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh)

  5  reasons ← []                                  -- every failing test, not the first
     if p.status ≠ ACTIVE            → reasons += POLICY_NOT_ACTIVE
     if asOfDate <  p.period_from    → reasons += BEFORE_POLICY_START
     if asOfDate >  p.period_to      → reasons += AFTER_POLICY_END
     if asOfDate <  m.coverage_from  → reasons += BEFORE_MEMBER_COVERAGE
     if asOfDate >  m.coverage_to    → reasons += AFTER_MEMBER_COVERAGE

  6  covered ← (reasons is empty)

  7  return { memberId, policyNo, policyStatus, asOfDate, covered, reasons,
              planCode: l.plan_code, benefitLevelNo: m.benefit_level_no,
              policyPeriod, coveragePeriod, premiumPaid: p.premium_paid, cardNo,
              continuousCoverFrom: m.continuous_cover_from,
              renewalStatus:       m.renewal_status,
              ruleSetRef:          p.rule_set_ref }
```

**Seven properties, each of which has a consequence if it is got wrong. They are unchanged, and each is now a requirement rather than an implementation.**

1. **All five tests run; `reasons` carries every failure.** A member whose policy has ended *and* whose own cover ended earlier returns both codes. A short-circuit on the first failure gives the assessor half the picture.
2. **Both boundaries are inclusive.** `asOfDate = coverage_to` is **covered**. A service on the last day of cover is a covered service.
3. **Comparison is date-only.** `asOfDate` is `YYYY-MM-DD` with no time and no timezone (D3 §1.2). Attaching a timezone to a service date produces off-by-one-day errors exactly at the policy-period boundary, which is exactly where they matter.
4. **`premium_paid` is returned and is deliberately not part of `covered`.** Whether an unpaid premium blocks a claim is an adjudication rule tested at A5 §6.1 step 1, in the Claim Platform. Folding it into `covered` moves a business rule out of the system that owns the decision.
5. **`insured_member.status` is not tested.** The dates are the truth (§3.2.7).
6. **The five reason codes are fixed**: `POLICY_NOT_ACTIVE`, `BEFORE_POLICY_START`, `AFTER_POLICY_END`, `BEFORE_MEMBER_COVERAGE`, `AFTER_MEMBER_COVERAGE`. **The claim engine maps these to decline reasons; it does not re-derive them** (D3 §I-05, §5.2.2).
7. **`covered` is a coverage test, not a payability decision.** Waiting periods, exclusions, limits, benefit mapping and the premium test are all downstream and all belong to the Claim Platform.
8. **`continuousCoverFrom` and `renewalStatus` are returned and are deliberately not part of `covered`.** Neither is a coverage test; together they are the anchor for a *payability* test that runs downstream, in the Claim Platform, at A5 §6.1. Folding either into `covered` would move a business rule out of the system that owns the decision — the same argument as `premium_paid` in property 4, and it has the same answer. **Both are confirmed returned at member-on-policy level** (decision `B1`), which is what makes property 8 a statement about live data rather than about a field we hoped for.
9. **`ruleSetRef` is returned and reads nothing at all.** The policy's rule-set or wording reference (decision `B2`) is carried on the response so that §5.4.2 F39 can render it and a decline can quote it. **No step of the chain reads it**, and A5 owns every benefit term; it is evidence for a letter, not an input to a calculation. It is listed here so that a reader of the return does not go looking for the rule that consumes it.

**The waiting-period anchor rule.** *(Register: **B-15**. Decision **`B1`**, 24 August 2026.)* A5 §5 gives a day count per benefit-group root per condition class; §3.2.4 gives it; nothing in either says which date the count runs from. **It runs from `continuousCoverFrom` where one is present, and from `coveragePeriod.from` where one is not.** Two facts and one subtraction, and the division of labour of §3.2.4 is unchanged: InsureMO returns both dates, the Claim Platform does the arithmetic and the comparison against the **occurrence date** (§5.7.2 F16, V-707), and the assessor sees `CLM-CONSOLE-004` when it fails.

**Three cases, and only one of them is now unresolved.** The rule is stated as a table rather than as a sentence, because *absent* used to mean one thing and now means three.

| `renewalStatus` | `continuousCoverFrom` | The anchor | What the assessor sees |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`TÁI_TỤC`** | Present | **`continuousCoverFrom`** | The count runs from the start of uninterrupted participation. **A5 §5's carry-over rule runs**, and a member who renewed last month is not blocked by a thirty-day wait |
| **`LẦN_ĐẦU`** | `null` | **`coveragePeriod.from`** | The ordinary first-time entrant. `null` here is **a fact, not a gap** — there is no earlier participation to point at |
| **`KHÔNG_XÁC_ĐỊNH`** | Either | **None** | **`V-119`**: the test is **inconclusive, never failed.** The claim is not blocked and the assessor is shown that the test could not run and why |

> **`V-119` narrows, and the narrowing is the point of the answer.** In v0.3 it fired whenever the anchor was missing, which was **every renewing member on every claim**, because the contract had no field. It now fires only on the third row — where InsureMO holds the member and cannot itself establish continuity. **That is a rare data condition rather than the ordinary case**, and it keeps the one posture that is safe in both directions: guessing *first-time entrant* declines every renewing member in the month after renewal, and guessing *continuing* removes the maternity waiting period from the product. §2.10 applied to a missing input — the system's job is to notice, not to resolve.
>
> **`D2-11` and `D2-129` are closed.** `I-05` returns a renewal attribute at member-on-policy level and returns the continuous-cover start beside it, which was the first of the three questions this note used to ask; the second and third do not arise. **What survives is a correction owed to D3 and it is sharper than it was** — §I-05's member and coverage contracts carry neither field, so the capability is confirmed and the wire is silent. **`D2-113`** carries `continuousCoverFrom` and **`D2-171`** carries `renewalStatus` and `ruleSetRef` with it.

> **The question this section put to the client is answered, and the answer is both halves of it.** *(Decision **`A1`**, 24 August 2026. **`D2-13` closes.**)* The reference system deliberately does not snapshot this attribute: it renders it on the claim with a **re-read control** beside it, so an assessor can pull the current value while the claim is open. v0.3 recorded that as a direct challenge to **`P-02`**, under which everything on a claim is frozen at registration so that a settlement is reproducible, and declined to settle it by assertion.
>
> **Both arguments were good and the answer keeps both.** Theirs: renewal status is a fact about the customer's **past**, and a change to it after the claim opens is usually a **correction**, not a change to the contract — freezing a wrong value freezes a wrong outcome. Ours: a settlement that cannot be re-derived from the record is a settlement nobody can defend.
>
> **What was decided.** **The value is snapshotted at registration and is the default in every case** — §5.2.4 is unchanged in substance, and no chain run reads anything but the snapshot. **A controlled re-read is added beside it**, and it is bounded on four sides: it is available **only while the claim is before `PENDING_APPROVAL`**; it is held by a **named grant** (A3 §4.21) and not by everyone who can open the claim; **every use writes the value before, the value after, the actor, the instant and a mandatory reason** to the claim and to the audit trail; and **it marks the calculation stale**, so the settlement is recomputed rather than left standing against an input that has since moved. **§5.4.5 specifies it in full**, and §5.4.2 F38 renders it.
>
> **Why that is a bounded exception to `P-02` and not a hole in it.** `P-02` exists so that a settlement can be re-derived from the record. **A re-read that records the value it replaced, and refuses to leave a figure computed from the old one standing, satisfies that requirement** — the record still answers *what was this settled against*, and it now also answers *what was it settled against before, and who changed it and why*. What would breach `P-02` is a re-read that silently updated the field, and that is precisely the version §5.4.5 does not build. **The state precondition is what keeps it bounded**: past `PENDING_APPROVAL` there is a settlement in front of an approver, and nothing an assessor can press may move under them (§5.2.4 reason 2).

> **Who runs this algorithm is answered: we do.** *(Decision **`B5`**, 24 August 2026. **`D2-10` closes.**)* Framework R-IMO-11 confirms that InsureMO can answer *"member coverage detail at a date"*, and v0.3 could not tell from any source whether that answer was a verdict or the facts. **It is the facts.** **Reading B below is the one the platform is built to**, and it is now a statement rather than a hedge: steps 5 and 6 run in the Claim Platform, against the snapshot, versioned with our code. The two readings are kept in the table because the *cost* of reading B is what a builder needs to know, and because reading A is what the compare rule below still guards against.
>
> | Reading | What InsureMO returns | What we do | What it costs |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | **A — InsureMO evaluates** | `covered`, `reasons[]`, and the dates | Read the verdict; never re-derive it (§5.2.2 already says exactly this) | The five reason codes and the two inclusive boundaries become **contract items on I-05** and must be agreed literally, code for code. A vendor's own coverage semantics that differ by one inclusive boundary would move the answer on every claim treated on a member's last covered day |
> | **B — InsureMO returns the facts** | Policy status, both periods, the member's coverage window, the level pointer | Run steps 5 and 6 ourselves, in the Claim Platform, from the facts on the snapshot | The algorithm above becomes **ours**, which is in some ways safer: it is versioned with our code and reproducible against the snapshot. What it costs is that a coverage answer is now computed from data read across a boundary, so a field InsureMO does not return is a test we cannot run |
>
> **The consequence of reading B, stated plainly.** The five reason codes at property 6 are **an internal enum, not a contract term**, so they may be extended without a vendor conversation — and the two inclusive boundaries at property 2 are **ours to guarantee**, which means they are ours to get wrong with nobody upstream to catch it. **The five tests are therefore a test case, not a comment**: §3.4's cases A to E are what proves them, and they run against the sandbox as well as against the mock (C-IMO-06). **A field InsureMO does not return is a test we cannot run**, which is the standing cost of computing a verdict from data read across a boundary.
>
> **The compare-don't-replace posture is kept, and keeping it is deliberate.** Where `I-05` returns a verdict of its own — today it does not, and a later release may — the console **compares rather than replaces**, and a disagreement between the two is an operational alert on S-03, never a silent choice (§2.10: the system's job is to notice, not to resolve). **Dropping the comparison because the answer came back *facts* would be the wrong lesson from a right answer**: the reason to compare was never uncertainty about today's payload, it was that a vendor which begins returning a verdict in a point release must not be able to change an outcome without anyone noticing. The rule costs one branch and it is the branch that would catch it.

#### 3.3.4 The benefit schedule as at a date — the tree

**Returned as a tree, not a flat list.** One object carrying `planCode`, `asOfDate`, `currency` and `benefits[]`, where each node is:

```jsonc
{ "code": "200", "name": "Outpatient treatment",
  "parentCode": null, "depth": 1,
  "annualSumInsured": 20000000, "perEventLimit": null, "perDayLimit": null,
  "maxCount": 0, "countUnit": "VISIT",            // 0 = unlimited
  "coPaymentBp": 2000,                            // or the literal "INHERIT"
  "deductionRatioBp": 2000, "deductionCondition": "PROVIDER_OFF_NETWORK",
  "waitingPeriodDays": { "PRE": 365, "SPE": 365, "GEN": 30, "ACC": 0,
                         "BIR": null, "MAT": null },
  "effectiveFrom": "2026-01-01", "effectiveTo": null,
  "children": [ … ] }
```

**Four properties that are contractual, not incidental** (D3 §I-05):

1. **`children` is always present**, as `[]` at a leaf. A consumer never tests for the property's existence before walking.
2. **`maxCount: 0` means unlimited.** Not zero, not null.
3. **The tree is complete in one response.** No lazy loading, no follow-up calls. The claim engine snapshots the whole thing in one operation (P-02), and **a partially loaded snapshot is a corrupt snapshot**. **This is the property most at risk from a general-purpose platform**, which will reasonably want to page a large collection — and the pilot's 17 nodes will not reveal the problem.
4. **`coPaymentBp` is on every node**, carrying `"INHERIT"` where the rate comes from an ancestor.

The tree is assembled from the lines for `planCode` whose effective window contains `asOfDate`, linked on `parent_benefit_code`. `waitingPeriodDays` appears on a node **only where rows exist for it** — in the pilot, on the five roots. A descendant's map is empty and it takes its root's periods.

**Where a plan exists but no line is effective on `asOfDate`, that is a real condition and must be answered as one** — `422 NO_SCHEDULE_AT_DATE`, when a claim arrives for a service date before the schedule was configured. It **must not be silently answered with today's schedule.** The assessor sees `CLM-CONSOLE-007`, which instructs them not to proceed (§5.2.7). **We can no longer guarantee this by writing the endpoint; it is C-IMO-05's most consequential detail.** An as-at-a-date query that quietly falls back to current is indistinguishable from a correct one until a claim is disputed.

#### 3.3.5 Policy issued (I-04)

InsureMO emits, or we poll for, the policy with its benefit levels, its members and its benefit data on issuance in J1. **The integration style is undetermined — webhook, event or polling — C-IMO-04**, and it affects I-04's design and J1's latency but nothing in this Part.

**Two rules from v0.1 survive with their reasons intact, and one is retired.**

| v0.1 rule | Now |
|---|---|
| A mandatory 15-minute polling reconciliation, because a policy that exists in InsureMO and not in the store is a policy whose claims are declined for no cover, invisible until a customer complains | **Retired as a data-integrity control** — there is no second copy to fall out of step. **It survives as a J1 screen behaviour only**: the certificate screen polls because the customer is waiting, not because two systems might diverge (Part IV §4.3) |
| An unknown `planCode` is an error, never an auto-create | **Survives, re-aimed.** The product catalogue mapping (P-03) is ours, and a policy issued against a plan our adjudicable model does not know is an operational alert, not a silently created plan |
| An inbound benefit schedule is accepted and discarded | **Retired.** It existed so that I-01 could be switched on later without a contract change. I-01 is on |

#### 3.3.6 Bulk member load

Specified at §3.6. **`C-IMO-10` is answered yes** and §3.6.7 states the single path.

### 3.4 Effective dating and the as-of-date query

Three questions the policy side must answer, worked against the actual records in **`A5_seed_v1.5.json`**. Every value below is read from the seed; none is illustrative. **The seed remains the fixture behind the mock (P-06), and these cases remain the acceptance tests — they are now tests we run against InsureMO's sandbox as well as against our own mock** (C-IMO-06).

**The records in play.**

| Policy | Type | Period | Status | Premium paid |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POL-26-004417` | `INDIVIDUAL` | 2026-01-01 → 2026-12-31 | `ACTIVE` | `true` |
| `POL-26-004503` | `GROUP` — *Công ty TNHH Cơ khí Đại Phong* | 2026-04-01 → 2027-03-31 | `ACTIVE` | **`false`** |

| Benefit level | Plan | Effective |
|---|---|---|
| `POL-26-004503` level 1 | `HC-STD` | 2026-04-01 → 2027-03-31 |
| `POL-26-004503` level 2 | `HC-PLS` | 2026-04-01 → 2027-03-31 |

#### Case A — a member whose coverage ends mid-year

`MBR-001004` **Vũ Thị Kim Oanh**, `POL-26-004503`, level 1 → `HC-STD`, coverage **2026-04-01 → 2026-09-30**, status `ENDED`. The seed's note is explicit: *"Leaver, end-dated mid-term rather than deleted."*

| `asOfDate` | `covered` | `reasons` | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `2026-08-14` | **`true`** | `[]` | Inside both windows, policy `ACTIVE`. `premiumPaid: false` is **returned and does not affect the answer** |
| `2026-09-30` | **`true`** | `[]` | **The boundary is inclusive.** A consultation on her last day of cover is covered |
| `2026-10-01` | **`false`** | `[AFTER_MEMBER_COVERAGE]` | The policy runs to 2027-03-31; only her own cover has ended. **One reason, not two** |
| `2027-04-01` | **`false`** | `[AFTER_POLICY_END, AFTER_MEMBER_COVERAGE]` | Both windows have closed. **Both reasons are returned** |

**What this case exists to prove.** A claim she submits in November 2026 for treatment in August 2026 is assessable, and settles against `HC-STD` as it stood in August. Deleting her row — the obvious thing to do when an employee leaves — would decline it. **This is why §3.6.6 requires end-dating and forbids deletion, and why `status = ENDED` is not part of the coverage test.** It is also the case to run first on the sandbox: it exercises the inclusive boundary, the two-reason response and the leaver in one query.

#### Case B — a mid-term joiner

`MBR-001008` **Trịnh Thị Hồng Nhung**, `POL-26-004503`, level **2** → `HC-PLS`, coverage **2026-07-01 → 2027-03-31**, status `ACTIVE`.

| `asOfDate` | `covered` | `reasons` | `planCode` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `2026-06-30` | **`false`** | `[BEFORE_MEMBER_COVERAGE]` | — |
| `2026-07-01` | **`true`** | `[]` | `HC-PLS`, `benefitLevelNo: 2` |

**Note what is *not* returned on 2026-06-30.** Not `BEFORE_POLICY_START` — the policy began 2026-04-01 and was perfectly in force; she was not yet on it. The two conditions are distinct and the assessor's next action differs: the first is a data question for the employer, the second is a coverage decline.

**And what the policy side does not do.** Her waiting period for a general illness on `100` is 30 days **from 2026-07-01**, not from the policy's 2026-04-01 (A5 §5). The answer carries `waitingPeriodDays.GEN = 30` and `coveragePeriod.from = 2026-07-01`; the Claim Platform does the arithmetic and reaches 2026-07-31.

#### Case C — a policy with more than one benefit level

`POL-26-004503` carries **two levels at the same time** — the case **C-IMO-01c** confirmed. `MBR-001001` … `MBR-001004` point at level 1 (`HC-STD`); `MBR-001005` … `MBR-001008` point at level 2 (`HC-PLS`).

| Query, `asOfDate = 2026-08-14` | Answer |
|---|---|
| Coverage for `MBR-001001` | `covered: true`, `planCode: HC-STD`, `benefitLevelNo: 1` |
| Coverage for `MBR-001005` | `covered: true`, `planCode: HC-PLS`, `benefitLevelNo: 2` |
| Schedule for `HC-STD` | `200` outpatient annual cap **20.000.000** |
| Schedule for `HC-PLS` | `200` outpatient annual cap **35.000.000** |

**The consequence for every consumer.** The benefit schedule is fetched **by plan, not by policy**. There is no schedule-by-policy read and there must not be, because the answer would depend on which member is asking. A caller resolves coverage first, takes `planCode` from the answer, and only then fetches the tree. A caller that fetched the schedule from the policy would pay one member's claim at another's limits. **Stated as a requirement: if InsureMO offers a schedule-by-policy read, we do not call it.**

#### Case D — a benefit level that changes mid-term

**The seed does not contain this case.** Both levels on `POL-26-004503` run the full policy period; the seed exercises *concurrent* levels, not a *change over time*. The mechanism is untested at both ends. Open item **D2-04** — the seed should carry it, and the sandbox should be asked it, because the alternative is discovering the behaviour in UAT.

What the mechanism is, stated so it can be asked for and so the seed can be extended:

```
benefit_level  POL-26-004503 / 1  HC-STD  2026-04-01 → 2026-09-30
benefit_level  POL-26-004503 / 3  HC-PLS  2026-10-01 → 2027-03-31
insured_member MBR-001001         benefit_level_no ← 3   (on the same change)
```

| `asOfDate` on `MBR-001001` | `planCode` | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `2026-08-14` | `HC-STD` | Level 3 is not yet effective; the pointer resolves to the level whose window contains the date |
| `2026-11-14` | `HC-PLS` | Level 3 is effective |

**The rule the resolution needs, and it is the one thing that must not be left to an implementer — at either end.** The member's `benefit_level_no` pointer is resolved **together with the effective window**: the level selected is the one for the policy whose `effective_from` … `effective_to` contains `asOfDate`, and the pointer disambiguates where more than one qualifies. Where **no** level's window contains the date and the member is otherwise covered, that is a data error, not an empty answer — `422 NO_BENEFIT_LEVEL_AT_DATE` rather than a coverage answer with a null plan. **A null `planCode` on a `covered: true` response would be snapshotted and would produce a claim with no schedule**, and there is no downstream check that catches it. Part V's registration path treats a null plan the same as `422 NO_SCHEDULE_AT_DATE` — hold, escalate, do not proceed (§5.2.7).

#### Case E — the schedule as at a date

The schedule read for `HC-STD` at `2026-07-14` returns the 17-node tree: five roots (`100`, `200`, `300`, `400`, `500`), `100.1.1` at depth 3, `maxCount: 0` on fourteen of the seventeen — the three exceptions are `100.1` at 60 `DAY`, `100.1.1` at 15 `DAY` and `200.3` at 20 `VISIT` — `coPaymentBp: "INHERIT"` on four, `deductionRatioBp: 2000` with `deductionCondition: "PROVIDER_OFF_NETWORK"` on `200` and `300` only.

Because the seed carries no effective dates on `benefit_schedule_line` (§3.2.3), **every `asOfDate` returns the same tree and `422 NO_SCHEDULE_AT_DATE` is unreachable in the mock.** That is a gap in the fixture, not in the specification — open item **D2-02**.

> **This is the paragraph to hand to whoever evaluates the sandbox.** Case E is not a description of a mock; it is a **checklist of seventeen nodes with their exact expected values**, and running it against InsureMO benefit by benefit is what turns C-IMO-01's *confirmed* into *proven*. Framework RK-14 has exactly one mitigation and this is it.
