### 3.5 Policy and member maintenance — not ours

**The administration UI specified at §3.5 of v0.1 is deleted.** It administered a store we do not build. Six screens go with it: policy and member search, policy detail, member detail, the benefit schedule viewer and editor, and the edit-permission table that governed them.

**What replaces it: InsureMO's own UI, outside our scope.** Policy holder and period corrections, member identity and card number, **member coverage dates**, the benefit-level pointer, benefit schedule lines and waiting periods — every one of those edits is now made in InsureMO by whoever administers it there, on InsureMO's screens, under InsureMO's own access control and audit. **This document does not specify them and must not**, for the reason §0.3 gives: specifying someone else's screens produces fiction that nobody can check.

**Four consequences, and none of them is neutral.**

| What v0.1 had | What we have now |
|---|---|
| Coverage dates editable only by `ADMIN`, at scope `MASTER`, with F63 recording actor, timestamp, old value and new value | **We have no record of the change at all.** The audit trail of a policy edit is InsureMO's, in InsureMO's format, and our audit log (F63) shows only that a later read returned a different answer. **P-02's snapshot is what makes this survivable**: a settled claim carries what the contract said when it was assessed, so a policy edit cannot retroactively move a settlement — but it can no longer be *attributed* on our side |
| `policy_no`, `member_id`, `account_ref` and `member_no` immutable, because they are referenced by claim snapshots, ledger counters and payment instructions | **`account_ref` is still ours and still immutable.** The other three are InsureMO's, and their immutability is now an assumption. A mutable member id is a dangling reference in our ledger, and we would find out on the second claim |
| `policy.premium_paid` read-only, because an administrator who could tick it would make an unpaid policy payable with no payment record behind it | **Not ours to make read-only.** The control is gone, and the flag is tested at A5 §6.1 step 1 on a value we do not govern. **D2-05 is retired** — it asked whether *our* administrator should be allowed a manual override, and we have no administrator here to grant it to |
| Verification of a payout account, performed on the member-detail screen at §3.5.3 | **Moved, not lost.** It is a claim-side action on a claim-side record and it is specified at **§5.20** (F58). Part IV §4.5 and Part V §5.12 both point there |

> **What still needs a screen on our side, and where it went.** Two things the deleted UI did are things the Claim Platform still needs. **Member search** — an assessor finding the right insured at registration — survives as **S-04** (§5.2.5), reading I-05. **Payout account and payee maintenance** survives as **§5.20**. Nothing else does, and the group import (§3.6) was never part of this UI.

> **A3 §3.2 now grants permissions over features that do not exist.** It gives `ASSESSOR` and `APPROVER` **R** on **F12** and **F14**, and `ADMIN` edit rights at scope `MASTER`, with the reasoning *"an assessor reads policy data and never writes it."* **The reasoning survives and the codes do not** — F11 … F14 are retired and never reused (Framework §7.1). A3 needs re-cutting: the read grants become reads of I-05 through the console, and the write grants have no target in our system. Correction owed — **D2-112**.

### 3.6 Group policy and member bulk load (F59) — ours

Serves **I-14**. **Ours end to end**, and it was ours before this reissue too — Framework v2.0 §2.1 moves it here explicitly, because the loader is ours whatever it writes into. This is how group business gets into the MVP without building group underwriting.

**The one thing that was open about it is answered: the imported members are written into InsureMO** (`C-IMO-10`, decision `B7`). §3.6.7 states the single path, and states what the withdrawn second path would have cost.

#### 3.6.1 The template

One workbook, two sheets. `.xlsx` only, **maximum 5 MB and 2,000 member rows** (D3 §I-14).

**Sheet 1 — `HopDong` (one row).**

| Column | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `policyNo` | `text(20)` | O | Blank on a first import — a number is allocated. **Populated means re-import** (§3.6.6) |
| `holderName` | `text(200)` | M | The company |
| `holderIdNumber` | `text(20)` | M | Tax code |
| `periodFrom` | `date` | M | |
| `periodTo` | `date` | M | ≥ `periodFrom` — V-104 |
| `planCode` | `text(16)` | M | **Must already exist in the product catalogue.** An unknown code is an **error**, never an auto-create — otherwise an importer invents plan codes and the benefit schedule silently does not exist. **This check now crosses a system boundary**: the catalogue is InsureMO's, so the validator resolves `planCode` through I-01's mapping (P-03) rather than against a local table, and an unreachable catalogue makes the file *unvalidatable*, not *invalid* — the run holds and retries, it does not fail the rows |
| `benefitLevelNo` | `int` | M | **One level per import run.** A policy with three levels is three runs, and the constraint is enforced, not documented (D3 §I-14) |

**Sheet 2 — `ThanhVien` (up to 2,000 rows).**

| Column | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `memberNo` | `int` | M | Unique in the file |
| `fullName` | `text(200)` | M | Vietnamese with diacritics |
| `dateOfBirth` | `date` | M | Not in the future — V-106 |
| `sex` | `enum(sex)` | M | `M` · `F` |
| `idNumber` | `text(20)` | O | Blank permitted — dependants |
| `cardNo` | `text(20)` | M | Unique in the file **and** across the member register — V-107 |
| `relationship` | `enum(relationship)` | M | |
| `coverageFrom` | `date` | M | Inside the policy period — V-109 |
| `coverageTo` | `date` | M | Inside the policy period; ≥ `coverageFrom` — V-109 |
| `bankCode` | `text(10)` | O | The three account columns are supplied together or not at all — V-110 |
| `accountNo` | `text(30)` | O | |
| `accountName` | `text(140)` | O | Unaccented uppercase |

**What the template deliberately does not carry.** No `planCode` per member — the run has one level. No payee columns — the beneficiary row is created automatically defaulting to the insured, and the case where the payee differs (a minor's parent) is an individual edit on **§5.20**, not a bulk field. No premium. No health declaration. Each absence is a decision.

**A payout account supplied in the file is created with `verified = false`**, without exception. Verification is an action a person takes (A3 §3.2); an import cannot assert it, and an import that could would defeat the control at I-11. **The three account columns and the beneficiary row are written to the Claim Platform (F58)**, and the member rows are written to InsureMO (§3.6.7) — they were never policy data, and the import is the one place where the two halves of this Part are written in one run, in the order §3.6.4 fixes.

#### 3.6.2 Validation performed on upload

Three passes, in order. **Nothing is written anywhere in any of them.**

| Pass | Checks | Produces |
|---|---|---|
| **1 — File** | Extension, MIME type, size ≤ 5 MB, both sheets present, header row matches the template exactly, row count ≤ 2,000 | **Rejected at upload.** No import record is created |
| **2 — Cell** | Type, format, mandatory, enum membership, per-column rules above | `errors[]`, one entry per failing cell |
| **3 — Cross-row and cross-system** | `cardNo` unique in file and in the member register · `memberNo` unique in file · coverage inside the policy period · `planCode` resolves in the catalogue · `benefitLevelNo` consistent · re-import diff | `errors[]` and `warnings[]` |

| Condition | Severity | Code |
|---|---|---|
| Unparseable date, e.g. `31/02/1990` | **Error** | `BAD_DATE` |
| Mandatory column blank | **Error** | `REQUIRED` |
| Value not in the enum | **Error** | `BAD_ENUM` |
| `planCode` not in the catalogue | **Error** | `UNKNOWN_PLAN_CODE` |
| `coverageFrom` / `coverageTo` outside the policy period | **Error** | `COVERAGE_OUTSIDE_POLICY` |
| `cardNo` already held by another member | **Error** | `CARD_IN_USE` |
| `cardNo` duplicated within the file | **Warning** | `DUPLICATE_IN_FILE` |
| Account columns partially supplied | **Warning** | `PARTIAL_ACCOUNT` — the member is created, the account is not |
| Re-import changes the policy period | **Warning** | `PERIOD_CHANGED` |
| Re-import drops a member present in the register | **Warning** | `MEMBER_END_DATED` |
| **The catalogue or the member register cannot be reached** | **Neither** | **`VALIDATION_INCOMPLETE`** — pass 3 could not run. The state is `VALIDATING`, not `VALIDATED_WITH_ERRORS`, and **commit is unavailable in both.** New in v0.2: pass 3 used to read a local table and now reads across an interface, and an unreachable dependency must not be rendered as a file that is wrong (§2.10) |

#### 3.6.3 The validation report

```
Purpose          Show what the file will do, and what is wrong with it, before anything is written.
Entered from     §3.6.4 upload, or the import list on S-09.
Who may open it  ADMIN only — A3 §3.2, scope MASTER
```

**Per file**, at the top:

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| `importId`, filename, uploaded by, uploaded at | Identity of the run |
| State | §3.6.5 |
| `policyCount`, `memberCount` | What would be written |
| Error count and warning count | The two numbers that decide whether commit is available |
| **Target** | **Where the members will be written — §3.6.7.** Displayed rather than assumed. **From v0.4 it always reads *InsureMO*** (`C-IMO-10` answered yes), and it is kept because an administrator committing a group's cover is entitled to see the destination on the screen where they commit it — a confirmation reads a constant usefully in a way a search grid does not |
| Diff summary, on re-import only | Added / unchanged / changed / **end-dated** counts |

**Per row**, one line per finding, sorted by row then column:

| Column | Content |
|---|---|
| Dòng | The **spreadsheet row number**, as the administrator sees it in Excel — 1-based, including the header. Not a zero-based index into a parsed array |
| Cột | The template column name |
| Mã lỗi | The code from §3.6.2 |
| Giá trị | The offending value, verbatim |
| Mô tả | The Vietnamese description of the code — *(new A2 item needed — **D2-09**, one item carrying the code → text table)* |

**Errors and warnings are in one list, not two tabs**, distinguished by a severity column and sortable by it. Two lists means the warnings are never read.

#### 3.6.4 The two-phase flow, and the second administrator

```
upload            →  importId, state VALIDATING
report            →  the validation report
commit request    →  state PENDING_CONFIRMATION, nothing written
commit confirm    →  applied, by a different administrator
```

**Nothing is written until commit.** The report is reviewed by a human first, and then by a second human.

| Step | Actor | What happens | Message |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 · Tải tệp lên | `ADMIN` A | File accepted, `importId` issued, validation starts. `Idempotency-Key` per D3 §1.3 | *(new A2 item needed — D2-09)* on rejection at pass 1 |
| 2 · Xem báo cáo kiểm tra | `ADMIN` A | §3.6.3 | — |
| 3 · Yêu cầu ghi nhận | `ADMIN` A | Only if error count = 0 **and pass 3 completed**. State → `PENDING_CONFIRMATION`. **Nothing is written yet** | **`CLM-CONSOLE-008`** — *"This change requires confirmation by a second administrator. Requested by {requestedBy} at {requestedAt}."* |
| 4 · Xác nhận ghi nhận | `ADMIN` **B** | **A3 §4.9.** A different administrator commits. **All rows written in one transaction** — see the note below | *(new A2 item needed — D2-09)* on success |
| 4′ · The same administrator tries | `ADMIN` A | **Refused** | **`CLM-CONSOLE-009`** — *"You requested this change and cannot confirm it. A different administrator must confirm."* |

**A3 §4.9 in full:** *"Import upload and validation are open to an administrator; **commit** requires a second administrator. A bad commit rewrites a whole group's cover. Validation is free to run; committing is not."* This is one of only two places in the solution where the deliberate two-level model is exceeded, and both guard an action whose blast radius is far wider than one claim (A3 §0.2). The other is the auto-approval threshold, §5.16.

**Both identities go to the audit log** — requester and confirmer, with both timestamps. A3 §4.7 states this explicitly for the threshold; F63 requires it here, and a two-person control that records one person is a one-person control.

> **"One transaction" is a promise this Part cannot make unqualified, and pretending otherwise would be the worst kind of defect.** The member rows are written into InsureMO across an interface (§3.6.7), while the payout accounts and beneficiaries are written into our own database. **Two systems, no distributed transaction.** What is achievable, and what F59 must therefore do:
>
> - **The upstream write goes first, and it is the transaction boundary.** Members are written to InsureMO in one operation. Only when it succeeds are the payout accounts and beneficiaries written locally.
> - **A failure of the upstream write commits nothing anywhere.** The import stays in `PENDING_CONFIRMATION` and is retried; it does not move to `COMMITTED`.
> - **A failure of the local write after a successful upstream write is an operator-queue item, not a rolled-back import.** The members are covered — which is the fact that matters — and the missing payout accounts are captured by the customer in the app (Part IV §4.5) or by an assessor on §5.20. **Cover without an account is a delay; an account without cover is a payment against nothing.** The asymmetry decides the order.
>
> **In v0.3 this note carried a second paragraph saying that under path B both writes would be local and the original single-transaction guarantee would hold. `B7` answers `C-IMO-10` yes, so there is no path B and the qualified promise above is the only one.** The three rules are not a degradation of a stronger guarantee we might have had — they are the guarantee, and they are what F59 is built to.

**How long a pending confirmation stays valid is not specified by any source.** This document proposes that a request in `PENDING_CONFIRMATION` expires after 7 days and must be re-requested, because a stale request confirmed a month later commits a file nobody has re-read. **D2-09** covers the message; the window itself is the open half.

#### 3.6.5 Import states

| State | Meaning | Commit available |
|---|---|---|
| `VALIDATING` | Passes 2 and 3 running, **or pass 3 blocked on an unreachable dependency** (§3.6.2) | No |
| `VALIDATED` | Complete, **zero errors**, all three passes run. Warnings may be present | Yes — to `ADMIN` A, as a *request* |
| `VALIDATED_WITH_ERRORS` | Complete, one or more errors | **No** |
| `PENDING_CONFIRMATION` | Requested by one administrator | Yes — to a **different** administrator |
| `COMMITTED` | Written. Terminal | No |
| `ABANDONED` | Superseded or cancelled. Terminal. Report retained | No |

`VALIDATED_WITH_ERRORS`, `PENDING_CONFIRMATION` and `ABANDONED` are this document's; D3 §I-14 names only `VALIDATING` and `VALIDATED`. They are states the two-phase flow with a second administrator requires and are additive to the contract.

#### 3.6.6 Three questions, answered

**A file where 3 of 400 rows fail.** Commit returns a refusal. The state is `VALIDATED_WITH_ERRORS`, the report lists exactly three rows with row number, column, code and value, the other 397 are shown as valid, and **nothing whatsoever is written**. The administrator corrects the workbook and uploads it again as a **new `importId`** — the failed run is retained, not edited, so that "we fixed it in the file" is a traceable statement rather than a claim.

**Is partial commit allowed? No, and this is a decision, not an omission.** D3 §I-14 states it and the reason is worth repeating in build terms: *a half-loaded group policy is worse than none, because claims will be assessed against it.* The 397 loaded members would be indistinguishable from a complete import — no "incomplete" marker exists on a member register and there is no workflow in which to carry one. The three missing employees would be uncovered, would submit claims, would be declined `AFTER_MEMBER_COVERAGE` or found by no search at all, and nobody would connect the decline to an import three weeks earlier. A blocked import is visible on the day it happens and costs one email to the employer. **The asymmetry is not close, and it is wider now than it was**: the half-loaded state would be in a vendor's system (§3.6.7), where we cannot see it, cannot mark it and cannot clean it up.

There is a second reason, narrower and equally decisive: **`memberNo` is sequential within the policy**, and a partial commit followed by a corrected re-import would either renumber the members already loaded or leave gaps that the next run's uniqueness check trips over.

**Re-import of a file already imported.** `policyNo` populated on Sheet 1 means re-import. Then:

| Behaviour | Rule |
|---|---|
| The member list is **replaced wholesale** | Matching is on `cardNo`, which is unique across the register. `memberNo` is not a match key — an employer's spreadsheet renumbers between runs |
| **The diff is reported before commit** | Added, unchanged, changed and end-dated counts in the report header; each end-dated member listed by name and card number |
| A member present in the register and **absent from the new file** is **end-dated, never deleted** | A departed member's past claims must stay assessable — this is Case A of §3.4, arriving through the import rather than through an edit. **This is a requirement on InsureMO's bulk load and not a behaviour we implement**: a load that replaces a member list by deleting and re-creating it destroys the leaver, and every one of that leaver's open claims with it. **`B7` confirms both operations — create and end-date — so the requirement is satisfiable rather than hoped for**, and F59 calls the end-date operation for every dropped member rather than sending a shorter list and trusting the load to work out the difference. **What is owed is the contract**: D3 §I-14 does not carry either operation, which is `D2-172` |
| The end date is **entered by the administrator on the commit screen**, not inferred | Field: *Ngày kết thúc cho thành viên rời khỏi danh sách*, `date`, mandatory on any re-import that end-dates at least one member, defaulting to the day before today. **Nothing must invent this date** — the employer knows when the employee left, and a silently chosen date silently changes what is payable |
| A changed policy period is a **warning**, not an error | `PERIOD_CHANGED`. Correcting a period is what "no endorsement transactions" means; it is shown so it is deliberate rather than blocked so it is impossible |
| `benefitLevelNo` | Still one per run. Re-importing level 1 does not touch members on level 2 |
| A `cardNo` already held by a member on a **different** policy | **Error** `CARD_IN_USE`. Card numbers are unique across the register, not within a policy |

#### 3.6.7 Where the imported members are written — answered

**`C-IMO-10` is answered yes** — decision **`B7`**, 24 August 2026. **InsureMO exposes a bulk member load, with a create operation and an end-date operation.** F59 validates, holds the two-phase confirmation, and then writes through it.

**One path, and v0.3's second path is withdrawn rather than left standing as a conditional.** A branch that has been answered and is kept "in case" is not caution, it is two systems to build and one of them dead; and the dead one is the one nobody tests. **The claim-side member extension is not built.**

| | **What happens** |
|---|---|
| Where members land | **InsureMO**, through the bulk member load. The account and beneficiary rows land with us (F58) — §3.6.1, and §3.6.4's ordering note is what governs the two writes |
| Member lists | **One.** Every insured member in the solution is in InsureMO's register, whether the policy was issued in J1 or loaded through F59 |
| What `I-05` answers for an imported member | **Everything.** The member is in the register like any other, and nothing about claim registration distinguishes them |
| What §5.2.2's registration does | **Unchanged: three reads to `I-05`.** There is no local resolution step and no precedence rule, because there is no second list to prefer |
| What §3.3.3's coverage algorithm runs against | **InsureMO's facts, evaluated by us** — reading B, confirmed by `B5`. The same algorithm on the same five tests for every member, however they arrived |
| What the benefit schedule read does | **Unchanged.** The schedule is InsureMO's, fetched by `planCode`, and it always was — this is the half that never forked |
| `policy.source` | **Still meaningful and still required** (§3.2.5). `ISSUED_J1` and `IMPORTED` now distinguish *how a policy arrived* rather than *which system to believe about it* |

**Three costs the `no` answer would have imposed, recorded because they are what the answer bought.** They are stated in the past tense deliberately: a reader who finds a reconciliation obligation in a later document should know that this document expected one and it did not arrive.

1. **There is no precedence rule to get wrong.** Under the withdrawn branch every group claim had to decide which of two lists to believe, resolved local-first because an imported member was only in ours — a rule that would have failed silently the day the same `cardNo` appeared in both.
2. **`cardNo` uniqueness stays an invariant.** V-107 checks one register and that register is complete. Under the withdrawn branch a card number issued by InsureMO in J1 and re-used in an employer's spreadsheet would have passed validation and produced two members with one card, which is exactly the multi-match at §5.2.3 that has no automatic resolution.
3. **A group member can buy an individual policy without becoming two people.** J1 issues into InsureMO and F59 writes into InsureMO; one person, one register, one card number.

**What the answer costs instead, and it is a real cost rather than a rhetorical one.** Two things move from us to a vendor.

- **The transaction guarantee is qualified and stays qualified** — §3.6.4. Two systems, no distributed transaction, and the upstream write is the boundary. That is the paragraph the withdrawn branch would have removed.
- **End-dating is now a requirement on somebody else's API.** §3.6.6 requires that a member dropped from a re-imported file is **end-dated and never deleted**, because a departed member's past claims must stay assessable. `B7` confirms an end-date operation exists; **what it does to that member's history is not confirmed, and it is the first thing to test on the sandbox** (`C-IMO-06`). A load that end-dates by deleting and re-creating with a shorter window would satisfy the operation name and destroy the leaver, and no claim of ours would notice until one was disputed.

**F59 itself is unchanged by the answer.** Its validator, its report, its two-phase commit and its second-administrator rule were written to be identical under either path and are identical still. **What changes is that §3.6.3's *Target* row stops being a deployment setting and becomes a statement** — it still displays where the members will be written, because an administrator committing a group's cover is entitled to see it, and a row that always reads the same thing is acceptable on a confirmation screen in a way it is not on a search grid (§3.3.1's `orgUnit`): here the reader is about to commit, and the value is confirming an action rather than discriminating between rows.

---

### 3.7 What a consumer must not assume

Six assumptions that look safe and are not. Each has cost the industry a defect. **Several were written about a store we owned; they are re-aimed here, and three of them are sharper than they were**, because an assumption about your own component is testable and an assumption about a vendor's is a belief.

1. **The policy side is not authoritative for anything after the snapshot is taken.** Policy data is snapshotted onto the claim at registration and the benefit schedule as at the service date, and **frozen** (Framework P-02, D1 §7.2). A screen that re-reads InsureMO to display a claim's cover is showing today's contract against yesterday's treatment. §2.4 draws the line for this document: `snapshot` is *never re-read*, and `imo:I-05` is permitted **only before the snapshot is taken**. **P-02 carries more weight in v2.0 than it did in v1.5**: the snapshot is now the only *local* record of what the contract said when the claim was assessed, and it is the single thing that keeps a settled claim reproducible if InsureMO changes a product version, loses an effective date, or is simply unavailable when someone asks why a claim paid what it paid.

2. **It holds no claim data, and therefore cannot warn about consequences.** Editing a member's coverage dates does not check whether claims exist against the affected period. In v0.1 that was a limit of a component we built; it is now a **property of a boundary** — InsureMO cannot see our claims and never will. The control is F63's audit trail and the second-administrator rule on the bulk path, and **on the InsureMO path there is now no control at all on our side**: a coverage date changed there produces no event, no alert and no entry in our log. Only the snapshot protects the claims already assessed (§3.5).

3. **It does not accumulate anything.** There is no consumption, no remaining limit and no counter on the policy side. **The limit ledger is the Claim Platform's and it is immutable** (Framework P-04): consumption is never deleted, only reversed or offset, and posting is two-phase — provisional at calculation, final at approval. A consumer asking InsureMO "how much of the 20.000.000 outpatient limit is left" is asking the wrong system; `annualSumInsured` is the **maximum**, never a balance. **This is now a decision rather than a discovery** — C-IMO-02 is moot, not confirmed: whatever InsureMO accumulates, we neither read it nor write to it, because the claim side is entirely ours (Framework §9.1).

4. **`covered: true` is not "payable".** It is five date-and-status comparisons (§3.3.3). Waiting periods, exclusions, the premium test, benefit mapping, co-payment, the deduction ratio and every limit are downstream, in the Claim Platform, in the fourteen-step chain at A5 §6.1. **And under D2-10's reading B we may be the ones computing `covered` too** — which changes who runs the test and changes nothing about what it means.

5. **The sentinels are sentinels.** `maxCount: 0` is *unlimited*; `coPaymentBp: "INHERIT"` is *resolve against the nearest ancestor*; `waitingPeriodDays.BIR: null` is *this combination cannot arise, and a claim that produces one is a data error*. None of the three is a number to compute with, and each fails silently rather than loudly if it is treated as one — which is why the second is a string. **Each is now a term of a contract with a third party rather than a column we wrote**, which is why §3.2.3 says they have to be asked for, and why the adapter checks them on every read (§3.8).

6. **It answers as at a date; it does not answer as at a version.** Effective dating on the benefit schedule and the benefit level answers *what did the contract say on 14 July*. A change to a member's name, card number or coverage dates **overwrites**. **In v0.1, F63 at least recorded that the change happened, who made it and what the values were. It no longer does** — the record is InsureMO's, in InsureMO's format, and no read of ours can reconstruct a member record as it stood last Tuesday. Declared simplification S-05, arriving with a wider blast radius than when it was declared.

---

### 3.8 Validation rules

The rules §3.6 cites by identifier, plus the structural checks that are now performed **at the adapter boundary** rather than on a screen. Part VIII §8.1 indexes them. **Sixteen identifiers are allocated out of the `V-101 … V-199` range** — twelve carried from v0.2, and four added in v0.3 for the claimant record (§3.2.10) and the waiting-period anchor (§3.3.3).

> **Three identifiers are retired with the administration UI: `V-101`, `V-102` and `V-103`.** V-101 (a search runs only with a criterion) and V-102 (more than 50 hits is refused, not truncated) were screen rules on a screen we deleted; both survive as **requirements on I-05** at §3.3.1, and V-102's enforcement moves to the console as **V-501** (§5.2.5). V-103 (a mandatory name may not be saved blank) was a rule on a form we no longer render; the import's `REQUIRED` code carries it. **Retired identifiers are not reused** — the numbering gap is deliberate.

**Where each rule now runs, and why that matters.** **Seven of the twelve — V-104 to V-110 — are enforced by the import** (§3.6), which is ours, and they are unchanged; two of the seven, **V-105 and V-108**, additionally raise an alert at the adapter, because the condition they test can arrive from InsureMO as well as from a spreadsheet. **The remaining five — V-111 to V-115 — run only at the adapter boundary** (D3 §1.6), on the tree as it comes back from I-05, before it is mapped into the adjudicable product model and snapshotted. **That is a strictly weaker position than v0.1's and it should be read as one:** a rule that used to refuse a keystroke now raises an alert on a claim that has already arrived. It cannot prevent a bad schedule; it can only stop us settling against one.

| # | Rule | Enforced | On failure |
|---|---|---|---|
| **V-104** | **A policy period ends on or after it begins** | Import (both) | *(new A2 item needed — D2-09)*; `BAD_DATE` on import |
| **V-105** | **A policy period must contain the coverage period of every member on the policy.** In v0.1 this refused a shortened period on a screen. It is now an **import cross-row check** and, on the InsureMO path, a **requirement on the register**: a policy period shortened past a member's cover produces a member whose coverage window falls outside their policy, and §3.3.3 then returns `AFTER_POLICY_END` on a member whose own cover is live. Nothing on our side can prevent it and the coverage read will not explain it | Import (server); otherwise an adapter alert | `COVERAGE_OUTSIDE_POLICY` |
| **V-106** | **A date of birth is not in the future** | Import (both) | `BAD_DATE` |
| **V-107** | **A card number is unique across the member register**, not within a policy — it is the one search key that finds a dependant, and a reused one finds the wrong person. **The register is one register from v0.4** (§3.6.7, decision `B7`), so this check sees every member and uniqueness is an invariant rather than an aspiration. v0.3 carried a caveat here for the branch in which it could not see InsureMO's members; that branch is withdrawn | Import (server) | `CARD_IN_USE` |
| **V-108** | **A member's benefit level must be a level on that member's own policy, and effective on the member's coverage start date** | Import (server); adapter on read | `422 NO_BENEFIT_LEVEL_AT_DATE` — §3.4 Case D |
| **V-109** | **A member's coverage window lies inside the policy period and ends on or after it begins** | Import (both) | `COVERAGE_OUTSIDE_POLICY` |
| **V-110** | **The three payout-account fields are supplied together or not at all** — bank code, account number, account name. There is no half-saved account. **Cited by §5.20 as well as by §3.6** | Import (warning); §5.20 (both) | `PARTIAL_ACCOUNT` on import; *(new A2 item needed — D2-09)* on §5.20 |
| **V-111** | **A parent benefit line is on the same plan, does not create a cycle, and sits exactly one level above** — the parent's `depth` is this line's `depth` − 1 | **Adapter** | Mapping refused; operational alert on S-03; `CLM-CONSOLE-007` to the assessor — escalate, do not proceed |
| **V-112** | **Exactly the limit amount that matches the limit type is present** — `annual_cap` iff `annual`, `per_event_cap` iff `per_event`, `per_day_cap` iff `per_day` | **Adapter** | As V-111 |
| **V-113** | **Co-payment is either a percentage or the sentinel `INHERIT`, and an `INHERIT` that reaches the root without finding an integer is a schedule error.** In v0.1 this was refused at entry, *"because refusing it at entry is cheaper than failing at the adapter boundary six weeks later."* **We now fail at the adapter boundary six weeks later** — the sentence was written as an argument for a control we no longer have, and it is kept because it names the cost exactly | **Adapter** (D3 §1.6) | As V-111 |
| **V-114** | **A deduction condition is present where a deduction ratio is set, and absent where it is not** | **Adapter** | As V-111 |
| **V-115** | **Two effective windows for the same plan and benefit code may not overlap.** Where they do, the as-at-a-date read is ambiguous and the tree it returns is not reproducible | **Adapter** | As V-111 |
| **V-116** | **A claimant's family relationship is present where standing is not `SELF`, and absent where it is.** The two dimensions are independent, but *bản thân* is the one combination in which the second has no meaning: a person is not their own father | Client and server | Mobile: *(new A2 item needed — **D2-39**)* · Console: stated inline at §5.4.2 F37 |
| **V-117** | **Where standing is `SELF`, the claimant's name and identity number equal the insured member's, and a save that makes them differ is refused.** Not corrected, not warned about — **refused**. A claimant who says they are the insured and then gives a different identity number is either a mistyped claim or a misdirected one, and both need a person to look (register **B-08**) | Client and server | Mobile: *(new A2 item needed — **D2-40**)* · Console: **V-709** (§5.20.5), `D2-125` |
| **V-118** | **Where standing is not `SELF`, the document requirement its row in §3.2.10 names is added to the claim's checklist at `REQUIRED`**, and the claim cannot reach a settlement plan without it. This is a checklist rule expressed as a validation because the checklist is generated, not typed | Server, at registration | Checklist item, not a message. The checks at §5.10.2 report it |
| **V-119** | **A waiting-period test with no anchor is inconclusive, never failed.** **Narrowed at v0.4** (decision `B1`): the rule now fires **only where `renewalStatus` is `KHÔNG_XÁC_ĐỊNH`** — InsureMO holds the member and cannot itself establish continuity. It no longer fires on an absent `continuousCoverFrom`, because absent now means `LẦN_ĐẦU` and `LẦN_ĐẦU` is a determinate answer with `coveragePeriod.from` as its anchor (§3.3.3's three-case table). Where it does fire the test does not decline: it returns *inconclusive* and the claim goes to an assessor with the missing input named. **The narrowing is what turns this from the ordinary case into a data exception** — in v0.3 it fired on every renewing member on every claim | Server, adapter and chain | `CLM-CONSOLE-004` variant naming the missing input — *(new A2 item needed, folded into **D2-88**)* |

**The import applies its rules and reports them differently.** §3.6 has no field to attach a message to, so V-106, V-107 and V-109 arrive as the row-level codes in §3.6.2 — `BAD_DATE`, `CARD_IN_USE`, `COVERAGE_OUTSIDE_POLICY` — one line per failing cell in the validation report, against the spreadsheet row number the administrator can see.

**One divergence between two surfaces is real and is named here rather than left to be found.** A partially supplied payout account is an **error** on §5.20 under V-110 and a **warning** on import (`PARTIAL_ACCOUNT`, §3.6.2), where the member is created and the account is not. The two surfaces do not agree about the same three columns. Which one is right is a business decision, not a formatting one, and it is not taken here. **The divergence survived the move of the payout account to F58 unchanged**, because it was never about where the record lived.

**Every message in the last column is still to be written.** A2 v1.0 carries no message family for the import; **`D2-09` is the group it needs**, and until A2 has written it the *On failure* column is a request rather than a code. `D2-06`, `D2-07` and `D2-08` are **retired** with the screens that needed them.

## Part IV — Mobile application (F21 … F30)

**Surface:** the insured customer's phone. Android and iOS, current and one prior major version (D1 NFR-9). **Vietnamese only** (D1 NFR-10, A2 rule M-1, D2 §1.1) — see §4.10.

This part specifies fourteen screens. It follows §2.1 throughout: purpose, entry, who may open it, the field table of §2.2, the action table of §2.5, rules, and empty-and-error behaviour. Types are §2.3's, Source values are §2.4's, and every message cited is an A2 code. Where a message the app needs does not exist in A2, the row reads *(new A2 item needed — D2-nn)* and the item is listed in Part X.

Two rules from Part II govern more of this part than any others, and they are worth restating before the screens:

- **§2.10 — an operational failure is never expressed as a claim outcome.** Three internal states (`EXTRACTION_ERROR`, a stalled `DOC_PROCESSING`, a stalled `PAYMENT_IN_PROGRESS`) exist on claims this app displays, and none of them may reach the customer as itself. §4.7 is the mapping that makes that concrete.
- **§2.6 — a screen never concatenates a Vietnamese sentence from fragments.** This is what §4.9 is built around, because the settlement screen is the one screen in the product that renders a dozen sentences at once.

Giving either its own destination would put the customer in a place where they cannot see the claim it is about.

### 4.2 Onboarding — registration, login, member linking and consent

#### S01 — Đăng ký và đăng nhập [F21]

| | |
|---|---|
| **Purpose** | Identify the customer by mobile number; there is no password and no username in MVP 1. |
| **Entered from** | App launch with no valid refresh token; sign-out; the "Tiếp tục mua" action on S05. |
| **Who may open it** | Anyone. Unauthenticated (A3 §1 — F22 needs no authentication, and S01 is reached from it). |

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Số điện thoại | `text(10)` | `user` | M | Exactly 10 digits, leading `0`, a Vietnamese mobile prefix. Digits only — the field strips spaces and dots on blur rather than rejecting them | `AUTH-VAL-001` |
| F2 | Tôi đồng ý với Điều khoản sử dụng | `bool` | `user` | M | Must be `true` to enable the action | *(new A2 item needed — D2-21)* |

**Actions**

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tiếp tục | `CUST` | F1 valid, F2 true | Issues an OTP against F1 and navigates to S02. **The same action serves registration and login** — the platform does not disclose whether the number is already known | Success: silent navigation · Failure: `SYS-ERR-002` |

**Rules**

- **Registration and login are one action.** A separate "register" path would tell an unauthenticated caller whether a number exists on the platform, which is the same enumeration weakness A2 documents against `AUTH-VAL-005`. The number either receives an OTP or it does not, and the screen looks identical either way.
- Rate limit: **3 OTP issuances per number per 15 minutes**, and 10 per device per hour. Exceeding either shows `AUTH-VAL-004` with `{minutes}` set to the remaining lockout. *(Decision — no source sets these numbers; see Part X.)*

**Empty and error.** No empty state. If the OTP service is unreachable the screen stays put and shows `SYS-ERR-002`; F1 is not cleared.

#### S02 — Xác thực OTP [F21]

| | |
|---|---|
| **Purpose** | Prove control of the mobile number and issue the session. |
| **Entered from** | S01. |
| **Who may open it** | Anyone holding an in-flight OTP challenge. The screen is not reachable by deep link. |

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Mã xác thực | `text(6)` | `user` | M | Exactly 6 digits. Submitted automatically on the sixth character | Wrong: `AUTH-VAL-002` with `{attemptsLeft}` · Expired: `AUTH-VAL-003` · Locked: `AUTH-VAL-004` with `{minutes}` |
| F2 | Gửi lại mã sau {n} giây | `derived` | `system` | — | — | — |
| F3 | Số điện thoại nhận mã | `derived` | `user` | — | — | — |

**Notes on the fields above.** F2 and F3 are displayed, never entered, so there is nothing to validate and nothing to tell the customer (§2.2). F2 counts down from the resend interval and the *Gửi lại mã* control stays disabled until it reaches zero. F3 echoes S01 F1, masked to the last three digits.

**Actions**

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Xác nhận | `CUST` | F1 has 6 digits, challenge not expired, not locked | Validates the OTP. On success issues the token pair and routes to S03 if no member is linked, otherwise to S08 | Failure: `AUTH-VAL-002` / `-003` / `-004` |
| Gửi lại mã | `CUST` | F2 countdown at zero, resend budget not exhausted | Invalidates the outstanding OTP and issues a new one. **The failed-attempt counter is not reset** | Budget exhausted: `AUTH-VAL-004` |
| Đổi số điện thoại | `CUST` | Always | Discards the challenge, returns to S01 | — |

**OTP parameters.** None of these is settled by D1, A2 or A5; they are specified here and listed in Part X as decisions taken by this document.

| Parameter | Value | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| Length | **6 digits** | Numeric so it is enterable on a phone keypad in one hand; six is the SMS convention in this market |
| Validity | **5 minutes** | Long enough for a delayed SMS, short enough that a shoulder-surfed code is stale |
| Resend interval | **60 seconds**, and at most **3 resends per challenge** | Below 60 seconds the resend competes with the original delivery and the customer enters the older code |
| Failed attempts | **5**, counted per number across resends | `AUTH-VAL-002` carries `{attemptsLeft}` so the customer is never surprised by the lockout |
| Lockout | **15 minutes** per number after 5 failures | `AUTH-VAL-004` states the wait. A permanent lock would need a support channel MVP 1 does not have |

**Why the counter survives a resend.** Resetting the attempt counter on resend makes the lockout unreachable — an attacker requests a new code every four attempts and brute-forces indefinitely. The resend budget and the attempt budget are separate counters and both must be exhausted before the number locks.

**Empty and error.** If the token exchange fails after a correct OTP, the screen shows `SYS-ERR-004` with the correlation id and offers a retry; the OTP is not consumed until the token is issued.

#### S03 — Liên kết hợp đồng và đồng ý xử lý dữ liệu sức khỏe [F21]

| | |
|---|---|
| **Purpose** | Attach the authenticated phone number to an insured member record, and take consent to process health data before any is shown or captured. |
| **Entered from** | S02 on first session; S10 to link an additional policy. |
| **Who may open it** | `CUST`, authenticated. Scope `SELF` (A3 §1). |

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Số hợp đồng bảo hiểm | `text(20)` | `user` | M | Non-empty; trimmed; case-normalised to upper. **Format is not validated client-side** — a format check tells the caller what a valid policy number looks like | `AUTH-VAL-005` |
| F2 | Số giấy tờ tùy thân | `text(20)` | `user` | M | Non-empty; digits and letters only. CCCD, hộ chiếu or giấy khai sinh number | `AUTH-VAL-005` |
| F3 | Tôi đồng ý để công ty thu thập và xử lý dữ liệu sức khỏe của tôi nhằm mục đích thẩm định và chi trả bồi thường | `bool` | `user` | M | Must be `true` before F5 is enabled | *(new A2 item needed — D2-22)* |
| F4 | Nội dung đồng ý đầy đủ | `derived` | `master` | — | — | — |

**Notes on the fields above.** F4 is the full consent text, versioned; the version the customer accepted is stored against the account with the timestamp. It is displayed, not entered (§2.2).

**Actions**

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Liên kết | `CUST` | F1, F2 non-empty, F3 true | Searches InsureMO's member register on `policyNo` + `idNumber` (`I-05` member search, exact match on `idNumber`). On a single match, links the member to the account, records the consent version and timestamp, routes to S08 | No match: `AUTH-VAL-005` · InsureMO unavailable: `SYS-ERR-002` · More than one match: `SYS-ERR-004` |
| Để sau | `CUST` | Always | Enters browse-only mode. S08 and S13 show their empty states with a prompt back here | — |

**Rules**

- **Both values are required and neither is validated on its own.** `AUTH-VAL-005` deliberately does not say which of the two was wrong (A2 §1). The screen must not highlight one field and not the other, and must not disable the action on a "policy number not found" pre-check — either would leak the same fact the message is written to withhold.
- **Rate limit on linking: 5 attempts per account per hour**, then `AUTH-VAL-004`. Linking is an unauthenticated-quality guess against a two-value key, and it is the one place in the app where a valid answer discloses someone else's cover.
- **No match** is not a failure state and never becomes one. The customer stays on the screen, the fields keep their values, and `AUTH-VAL-005` tells them what to check. This is the same posture D1 §3.2.3 takes for a claim whose member cannot be found: a data problem is never converted into a decision.
- **More than one match is a data defect, not a customer error.** `policyNo` + `idNumber` identifies at most one member on a well-formed policy; two matching rows mean duplicate member records in the register (§3.2.7). The customer is shown `SYS-ERR-004` with the correlation id — not `AUTH-VAL-005`, which would tell them to re-check details that were correct — the link is not made, and an operational alert is raised for an administrator. **Silently linking the first row would attach the customer to an arbitrary one of two cover records**, and every remaining limit and every claim thereafter would be computed against a record chosen by row order.
- **One account may link several policies** — an individual policy and an employer group scheme is the common case (D1 §10.2 GAP-7). Each link is a separate S03 pass from S10. Claims and cover are then presented per policy, never merged.
- **Consent is a precondition, not a preference.** F3 cannot be revoked to `false` while a claim is in flight, because the data has already been processed and the claim cannot be assessed without it. Revocation is available from S10 only when the customer has no claim outside a terminal state, and revoking unlinks every member.

**Empty and error.** InsureMO unavailable: `SYS-ERR-002`, fields preserved, retry available. There is no partial success — the link is written or it is not.

#### Notification preferences (S10, first section) [F21]

Specified here because it is F21's fourth element; the rest of S10 is in §4.5.

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Thông báo đẩy về tiến trình hồ sơ | `bool` | `user` | O | — | Save failure: `SYS-ERR-002` |
| F2 | Thông báo đẩy về hợp đồng | `bool` | `user` | O | — | Save failure: `SYS-ERR-002` |
| F3 | Email nhận thư từ | `text(120)` | `user` | M | RFC-shaped address | *(new A2 item needed — D2-23)* |
| F4 | Thông báo trong ứng dụng | `derived` | `system` | — | — | — |

**Notes on the fields above.** A switch cannot be invalid, so the only failure these rows have is a failure to save (§2.2). F1 and F2 default to `true`; F1 controls the `PUSH` channel for `CLM-NOTIF-*`, `DOC-NOTIF-*` and `PAY-NOTIF-*`, F2 controls it for `POL-NOTIF-*`. **F3 cannot be switched off** — it is the `EMAIL` channel for correspondence. F4 is always on and is shown as a locked row with an explanation.

**Rules**

- **The customer may turn off push. They may not turn off in-app or correspondence.** A2 §0.3 makes the in-app timeline *the record* of a claim, and `CLM-LETTER-001` / `-002` are correspondence about a decision that affects money — neither is a notification the customer can decline without losing the audit trail they may later need. Push is genuinely optional because A2 already guarantees no push carries an amount, a diagnosis, a benefit name or a decline reason (D1 BR-MSG-1), so switching it off costs the customer timeliness and nothing else.
- Turning F1 off does **not** suppress the badge on the *Hồ sơ* tab. A pending information request must remain visible in the app whatever the notification settings, because `DOC-NOTIF-005`'s reminder is a push and the customer who silenced push is exactly the one who will otherwise let a claim stall.

---

### 4.3 Buy — plans, quote, application, payment and certificate (F22, F23, F24)

**This journey performs eligibility screening, not underwriting.** A5 §2 states the product is written on declaration only — no medical examination, no underwriter referral — and A5 §3 states that any "yes" to Q1 to Q4 declines the application. There is **no referral queue in MVP 1**: a disqualified application is declined on the spot with `POL-VAL-002`, which names a contact channel so the customer has a route to a human, and nothing is queued, held or reviewed inside the platform. The distinction matters for the screen because it removes an entire state — there is no "under consideration" application, and the app never shows one.

#### S04 — So sánh chương trình bảo hiểm [F22]

| | |
|---|---|
| **Purpose** | Show the three plan tiers side by side with their benefits and limits, before anyone signs in. |
| **Entered from** | App launch, tab bar, S08's "Mua thêm". |
| **Who may open it** | Anyone. **No authentication** (A3 §1, F22). |

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Chương trình bảo hiểm | `enum(planCode)` | `master` | — | — | — |
| F2 | Quyền lợi | `derived` | `master` | — | — | — |
| F3 | Số tiền bảo hiểm năm | `money` | `master` | — | — | — |
| F4 | Hạn mức số lần / số ngày | `int` | `master` | — | — | — |
| F5 | Đồng chi trả | `pct` | `master` | — | — | — |
| F6 | Thời gian chờ | `derived` | `master` | — | — | — |

**Notes on the fields above.** Nothing on this screen is entered, so no row carries a validation and no row needs a message (§2.2). What follows is display behaviour, which is where it belongs:

- **F1** is the three plan codes of A5 §1 — `HC-STD` · `HC-PLS` · `HC-PRM` — as three columns, all shown.
- **F2** is the benefit tree of A5 §4.1, rendered to depth 2 by default with depth 3 behind a disclosure.
- **F3 and F4** are A5 §4.2's amount and count columns. **`0` is a sentinel and renders as *"không giới hạn"***, never as `0 đ` or `0 lần` (A1 §3). **This is a rendering rule, not a validation** — there is no input to reject — and the same rule governs S09 F3 and F4.
- **F5** is A5 §4.2's co-payment rate; `inherits` on a child renders the ancestor's rate with a note, never the word "inherit".
- **F6** is A5 §5 by condition class; `n/a` renders as *"không áp dụng"*.

**Actions**

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lấy báo giá | anyone | A plan selected | Navigates to S05 carrying `planCode` | — |

**Rules**

- **The `0` sentinel is rendered, never displayed raw.** A1 §3 makes `0` mean unlimited; a customer shown "0 lần" on physiotherapy would read the opposite of the truth. This applies identically on S09 and in the settlement screen.
- **Waiting periods appear on the comparison screen, not only on the certificate.** A2 §7.3 puts the waiting-period table in the certificate email because it is the largest single cause of a surprised, disputed claim (D1 §3.1). Putting it in front of the customer at the comparison step costs nothing and is the earlier of the two cheap moments.

**Empty and error.** Master data is bundled with the release and cached; the screen has no empty state. If the cached schedule is older than the current release the screen loads the bundled copy and refreshes silently.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Purpose** | Turn an age and a plan into a premium with a stated validity. |
| **Entered from** | S04. |
| **Who may open it** | Anyone. Authentication is required only to continue into S06. |

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Chương trình bảo hiểm | `enum(planCode)` | `user` | M | — | — |
| F2 | Ngày bắt đầu hiệu lực | `date` | `user` | M | Not before today; not more than 90 days ahead | *(new A2 item needed — D2-24)* |
| F3 | Ngày sinh — người được bảo hiểm | `date` | `user` | M | Repeating, 1 to 6 rows (A5 §2). Age at F2, last birthday, must be **0 to 65** | `POL-VAL-001` with `{minAge}` 0, `{maxAge}` 65 |
| F4 | Mối quan hệ | `enum(relationship)` | `user` | M | `SELF` · `SPOUSE` · `CHILD` · `PARENT`. Exactly one row is `SELF` | *(new A2 item needed — D2-32)* |
| F4a | *(composition check)* | `derived` | `system` | — | A5 §2: a member aged 0–17 requires **at least one member aged ≥ 18** on the same quote | *(new A2 item needed — D2-33)* |
| F4b | *(composition check)* | `derived` | `system` | — | A5 §2: **1 to 6 members** per policy | *(new A2 item needed — D2-34)* |
| F5 | Phí bảo hiểm | `money` | `imo:I-02` | — | — | — |
| F6 | Chi tiết phí theo người | `money` | `imo:I-02` | — | — | — |
| F7 | Báo giá có hiệu lực đến | `date` | `imo:I-02` | — | `validUntil`, compared against the device clock **and** the server clock at S06 entry | `POL-VAL-003` |
| F8 | Mã báo giá | `derived` | `imo:I-02` | — | — | — |

**Notes on the fields above.** F1 is a chooser over the three plan codes, pre-filled from S04; there is no free entry for the screen to reject. F5 to F8 are returned by the quotation service and displayed, not entered (§2.2): **F5 is never computed in the app**, F6 is `breakdown[]` from I-02 with one row per insured, and F8 is `quoteId`, carried into I-03.

**Actions**

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tính phí | anyone | F1–F4 valid | Calls I-02. Renders F5–F8 | Age band: `POL-VAL-001` · Service unavailable: `SYS-ERR-002` |
| Tiếp tục mua | `CUST` | A quote exists and `validUntil` has not passed | Requires authentication (routes through S01/S02 and returns here), then navigates to S06 carrying `quoteId` | Expired: `POL-VAL-003` |

**Rules**

- **A quote either still holds or is visibly expired.** D1 §3.1 and D3 §I-02 both make `validUntil` a contract, not a hint. The app re-checks it on entry to S06 and again immediately before submitting the application; a quote that expired between screens shows `POL-VAL-003` and returns the customer to S05 with their inputs intact. **Silently re-quoting is prohibited** — it is the single most common trust failure in an online insurance journey and the customer would discover it only on the certificate.
- **The premium is never calculated in the app**, even though A5 §11's table is small enough to embed. The app displaying one number while InsureMO issues on another is a defect the customer finds; sourcing from `imo:I-02` makes it impossible.
- **Two composition rules from A5 §2 are enforced here and again server-side:** a child aged 0–17 may only be insured alongside at least one adult on the same policy, and a policy carries 1 to 6 members. Both are checked before the quote call so the customer is not priced on a composition that cannot be issued.

**Empty and error.** Before *Tính phí*, F5–F8 are absent, not zero. If I-02 fails, F5–F8 stay absent and `SYS-ERR-002` shows; the inputs are preserved.

| F7.4 | Mối quan hệ với bên mua bảo hiểm | `enum(relationship)` | `user` | M | `SELF` · `SPOUSE` · `CHILD` · `PARENT` | *(new A2 item needed — D2-25)* |

**Section 3 — Khai báo sức khỏe** — the five questions of A5 §3, verbatim, per insured.

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |

| F8.2 | Trong 24 tháng qua anh/chị có nằm viện hoặc phẫu thuật không? | `bool` | `user` | M | `true` **disqualifies** | `POL-VAL-002` |
| F8.3 | Anh/chị đã được chẩn đoán ung thư, bệnh tim, đột quỵ, tiểu đường, bệnh thận, bệnh gan hoặc HIV chưa? | `bool` | `user` | M | `true` **disqualifies** | `POL-VAL-002` |
| F8.4 | Anh/chị có bệnh bẩm sinh hoặc khuyết tật không? | `bool` | `user` | M | `true` **disqualifies** | `POL-VAL-002` |
| F8.5 | Anh/chị hiện có đang mang thai không? | `bool` | `user` | M | `true` does **not** disqualify. Sets F7.6 to `false` for that insured | *(new A2 item needed — D2-26)* |
| F9 | Tôi xác nhận các thông tin khai báo là đúng sự thật | `bool` | `user` | M | Must be `true` to enable submission | *(new A2 item needed — D2-21)* |

**Actions**

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kiểm tra điều kiện | `CUST` | All of F1–F9 complete | Evaluates the eligibility screen **client-side** for immediate feedback. Does not submit | Disqualified: `POL-VAL-002` with `{contactChannel}` · Age: `POL-VAL-001` |
| Nộp hồ sơ | `CUST` | Eligibility passed client-side, quote still valid | Calls I-03 with `quoteId`, applicant, insureds and the declaration answers. **The server re-evaluates eligibility and the quote's validity — that is the enforcement point** (D1 J1-4, A3 §6). On acceptance, routes to S07 | Disqualified server-side: `POL-VAL-002` · Quote expired: `POL-VAL-003` · Service unavailable: `SYS-ERR-002` |
| Lưu và thoát | `CUST` | Always | Persists the draft application locally. Does **not** extend `validUntil` | — |

**Rules**

- **Eligibility is evaluated twice and enforced once.** The client-side pass exists so the customer is not made to complete an application that cannot succeed (D1 J1-4); the server-side pass at submission is the control. A client that skipped the questions, or answered them and edited the payload, is rejected identically.
- **A disqualifying answer declines immediately and names a contact channel.** `POL-VAL-002` is shown as a full-screen result, not a field error, because the application is over. It deliberately does **not** say which answer disqualified the customer — that is medical information a validation message should not surface (A2 §2) — and it always names `{contactChannel}`. **There is no referral queue**: nothing is created on the platform, no application record is retained beyond the audit entry, and no assessor or administrator sees it. The route to a human is out of band.
- **Q5 is the one exception and is implemented as such** (A5 §3). A declared pregnancy sets `maternity_eligible = false` for that insured and the application proceeds. The screen must **tell the customer this at the point of answering** — a maternity benefit that silently does not apply is exactly the surprised, disputed claim the waiting-period table exists to prevent — which is why D2-26 is needed.
- **Editing a date of birth after the quote invalidates the quote.** Age drives the premium band (A5 §11); an application submitted on a quote priced for a different age is the silent re-pricing D1 §3.1 forbids, arriving from the other direction.
- Declaration answers are sent to InsureMO on I-03 and are **not** retained on the Claim Platform beyond the audit trail. They are underwriting evidence for the issuer, not claim data, and they are the most sensitive personal data the buy journey touches.

**Empty and error.** A saved draft reopens at the section it was left in. If I-03 returns an unmapped error the screen shows `SYS-ERR-004` with the correlation id and keeps the draft — **it never shows a decline**, because an integration failure that looked like a declined application is precisely §2.10's prohibition applied to J1.

| **Who may open it** | `CUST`, authenticated, on their own application (A3 §1, F24). |

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Phí bảo hiểm phải thanh toán | `money` | `imo:I-02` | — | — | — |
| F2 | **Đây là giao dịch thanh toán mô phỏng. Không có khoản tiền nào được thu và không có thông tin thẻ hoặc tài khoản nào được nhập hoặc lưu trữ.** | `derived` | `master` | — | — | *(the banner text itself is a new A2 item — D2-27)* |
| F3 | Phương thức thanh toán | `enum(paymentMethod)` | `user` | M | — | — |

| F5 | Thời hạn bảo hiểm | `derived` | `imo:I-05` | — | — | — |
| F6 | Chương trình bảo hiểm | `derived` | `imo:I-05` | — | — | — |
| F7 | Giấy chứng nhận bảo hiểm (PDF) | `file` | `system` | — | — | `SYS-ERR-004` on generation or retrieval failure |

**Notes on the fields above.** Nothing here except F3 is entered, and F3 has one value, so no row carries a validation (§2.2):

- **F1** is the quoted premium, unchanged. A different figure here is a defect, not a re-price.
- **F2** is a persistent banner, above the pay action and not dismissible. It is a sentence a customer reads, so it is A2's to own — see D2-27 and the paragraph below.
- **F3** carries the single value `MOCK` in MVP 1 and is rendered as a labelled row rather than a chooser.
- **F4** is the policy number at `text(20)` per §2.9, present once InsureMO has issued the policy and answered for it — see the rule below. **F5** renders `policyPeriod.from` – `policyPeriod.to` as `dd/mm/yyyy` and **F6** renders `planCode` as its Vietnamese plan name.
- **F7** is generated by F61 and is downloadable and shareable.

**Actions**

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Thanh toán | `CUST` | An accepted application exists | Calls I-13 (`POST /v1/payments/mock`), which confirms immediately and sets `premiumPaid`. Then waits for the policy to land via I-04 | Success: `POL-NOTIF-001` · Failure: `SYS-ERR-004` |
| Tải giấy chứng nhận | `CUST` | F7 present | Downloads the PDF | `POL-NOTIF-002` on availability; `SYS-ERR-003` on download failure |
| Xem hợp đồng của tôi | `CUST` | F4 present | Navigates to S08 | — |

**What "mocked" means, precisely, and what the screen says.** Boundary condition BC-3 (D1 §5.6a, Framework §9.4) is that **no real money moves in MVP 1**. On this screen that means: no card, bank or wallet credential is collected, entered or stored; no payment gateway is called; `POST /v1/payments/mock` (D3 §I-13) returns an immediate confirmation and the policy's `premiumPaid` flag is set to `true`. The customer is told this in F2's banner, in those words, before they tap. **This is not a disclaimer in small print** — an insurance app that appears to take a payment and does not is the kind of ambiguity a demonstration audience and a regulator read the same way. D3 specifies I-13 as a real contract precisely so the eventual gateway is a swap rather than a redesign, and F3's single-value enum is where that swap lands.

**Rules**

- **The certificate renders from the register, not from the issuance response.** I-03 returns `policyNo` synchronously, but the policy becomes readable through I-04 and I-05 (style still open — C-IMO-04). Rendering from the read path means what the customer sees on day one is exactly what the claim journey will read on day one, which is BO-8 / SC-08 stated as a screen rule — and **from v2.0 it proves more than it used to**, because the policy is now bought into InsureMO and claimed out of InsureMO rather than handed between two of our own components. While the read has not yet answered, F4–F7 show a waiting state — **not an error, and not a retry prompt** — and the screen polls. If it has not landed within 15 minutes, the screen shows `SYS-ERR-002` and the customer is notified by `POL-NOTIF-001` when it does; the policy is issued either way and nothing the customer does affects it.
- `POL-LETTER-001` is emailed to S06 F5 on issuance and **carries the waiting-period table** (A2 §7.3, D1 §3.1). The in-app certificate view shows the same table.

**Empty and error.** Before payment, F4–F7 are absent. A failed mock payment leaves the application accepted and unpaid, and the screen offers a retry — there is no partial state.

**Notes on the fields above.** This screen is read-only for the customer (A3 §1, F25), so no row carries a validation and none needs a message (§2.2). What the column used to hold is rendering:

- **F1** is one card per linked policy, at `text(20)` per §2.9. **F2** renders `planCode` as its Vietnamese plan name and **F3** renders `policyPeriod`.
- **F4** renders `ACTIVE` as *"Đang hiệu lực"* and every other value as *"Không còn hiệu lực"*. **The raw status is never shown** (A2 rule M-3) — a rendering rule, not a validation.
- **F5** is one row per member: name, relationship, `cardNo` (`text(20)`, §2.9) and `coveragePeriod`. **F6** shows `coveragePeriod` **per member**, separately from F3.
- **F7** is the certificate, one per policy.

**Actions**

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Xem quyền lợi | `CUST` | A member selected | Navigates to S09 for that member | — |
| Tải giấy chứng nhận | `CUST` | F7 present | Downloads the PDF | `SYS-ERR-003` on failure |
| Tạo hồ sơ bồi thường | `CUST` | Policy `ACTIVE`, at least one member | Navigates to S11 with the policy and member pre-selected | — |
| Liên kết hợp đồng khác | `CUST` | Always | Navigates to S03 | — |

**Rules**

- **The member's coverage period is displayed as prominently as the policy's, and separately.** They differ on group cover, and the member's is the one the date-validation chain tests (D1 §3.2.1). A customer who sees only the policy period will submit claims for dates outside their own cover and be declined with `PERIOD` for a reason the screen concealed.
- **`policyStatus` is rendered, never printed.** A2 rule M-3 forbids showing an internal enum to a customer, and this is the one place in the cover journey where an enum reaches a screen.

**Empty and error.** No linked member: an empty state with a prompt into S03 — not an error. InsureMO unavailable: `SYS-ERR-002` over the last successfully loaded data, marked stale with the time it was loaded (§4.10).

| **Entered from** | S08. |
| **Who may open it** | `CUST`, read only, scope `SELF`. **Remaining limits for every member on the policy; claim history only for claims this customer submitted** (A3 §4.3). |

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Quyền lợi | `derived` | `imo:I-05` | — | — | — |

| F5 | **Hạn mức còn lại trong năm hợp đồng {kỳ}** | `money` | `system` | — | **Rendered once per `periodKey`, labelled with that policy year's two dates, and never summed across periods — V-408.** The label carries **chỉ tính các hồ sơ đã duyệt** on the figure itself, not in a footnote | Ledger unreachable: `SYS-ERR-002` |
| F6 | Số lần / số ngày còn lại trong năm hợp đồng {kỳ} | `int` | `system` | — | **The same period dimension and the same prohibition on summing — V-408.** Absent where `maxCount` is `0` | Ledger unreachable: `SYS-ERR-002` |

| F11 | Hồ sơ đang xử lý | `derived` | `system` | — | — | — |

**Notes on the fields above.** Every row is read, none is entered, so the only failure this screen has is a read that did not answer (§2.2):

- **F1** is the benefit tree for `planCode` as at today, to depth 2 with depth 3 behind a disclosure.
- **F2** is `annualSumInsured`; `included` renders *"theo hạn mức của {parentBenefitName}"*. **F3** is `perEventLimit` / `perDayLimit`.
- **F4** is `maxCount` + `countUnit`, and **`0` renders *"không giới hạn"*** (A1 §3). **This is a rendering rule, not a validation** — the same sentinel as S04 F4, and it is stated here rather than in the *Validation* column because there is no input for it to govern.
- **F5** is the annual sum insured **minus final consumption** on the limit ledger and **F6** is the count dimension of the same counter, absent where `maxCount` is `0`. Both are read live — see the table below. **F7** is the instant they were read, and is always shown; **it is one instant, stated once, and it applies to every period block rendered** — two blocks are one read, not two, and that is a rendering rule rather than a validation, so its cell is empty (§2.2, `V-408`). **F5 and F6 carry the counter period, and until v0.6 neither did** — see `V-408` below.
- **F8** is `coPaymentBp` resolved; `"INHERIT"` never reaches the screen. **F9** is the waiting period per condition class (A5 §5) with the date it counts from (`coveragePeriod.from`).
- **F10** lists claim number, service date, status chip (§4.7) and settlement amount where terminal, and **F11** the count and requested amount of non-terminal claims — both **only for claims this customer submitted** (A3 §4.3). F11 is **not deducted from F5**; the reason is below.

**Actions**

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Làm mới | `CUST` | Always | Re-reads F5–F7 from the ledger | `SYS-ERR-002` on failure |
| Xem hồ sơ | `CUST` | A row in F10 | Navigates to S13 detail for that claim | — |
| Tạo hồ sơ bồi thường | `CUST` | Policy `ACTIVE` | Navigates to S11 with this member selected | — |

**Where the remaining limit comes from, how fresh it is, which period it belongs to, and what it excludes.** This figure is the customer-facing face of the limit ledger (D1 §5.9), and **four** properties are specified rather than left to the implementation:

| Property | Specification | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Source** | The limit ledger on the Claim Platform, read live at screen open and on *Làm mới*. Source `system`, **never** `snapshot` | D1 §7.1: *"The remaining limit a customer sees and the one the engine enforces are the same number."* A snapshot is per claim and as at a service date; this is the member's position today |
| **Freshness** | Read on every open. No background cache beyond the screen session. **F7 always states the instant it was read** | A limit that moved while the screen was open is the normal case when a claim is approving. Stating the read time makes a changed figure explicable rather than alarming |
| **Period** | **The counter period is the policy year** (`L-1`), derived from the policy inception date, **never the calendar year**. **The counter is keyed on it** — `(memberId, policyId, benefitCode, periodKey, counterType)`, `V-723` — so *"the remaining limit"* is not a number this ledger holds: it holds one per period. **The screen renders one block per `periodKey`, labelled with that year's two dates, and never sums them.** **New at v0.6 — `V-408`** | Below |
| **Basis** | **Final consumption only** (A1 §3 — *"Sum insured minus final consumption"*). Provisional postings are excluded | Below |

**`V-408` — the app was showing one remaining-limit number across a policy-year boundary, which is the exact thing `V-730` forbids the console from doing.** §0.6d row 7 of v0.5's changelog claimed that decisions `D-7` and `D-8` had moved §4.4. **They had not.** `V-723` gained `periodKey`, §5.9.3's console panel gained a *Kỳ hạn mức* column and `V-730` and `V-731` were written for the console — and **S09, the screen a customer actually reads, was untouched.** F5, F6 and F7 carried no period dimension at all, so on any member whose policy year had turned during the window the app was reading two counters and rendering one figure. **On a policy-year basis every member's boundary falls on a different day**, so this is an ordinary case rather than a December edge case, and the customer it misleads is the one who most needs the number: somebody deciding whether to claim.

| # | The rule |
|---|---|
| **V-408** | **F5 and F6 render per `periodKey`, labelled with the policy year's start and end dates, and are never summed.** Where the member's ledger holds counters in two policy years the benefit tree renders **twice, once per period**, each with its own sum insured, consumption and remaining — and **there is no combined figure, because the member does not have one allowance, they have one in each year** (`L-1`, `L-3`, `V-730`). **F7's read instant is stated once and applies to both blocks.** **And `V-731`'s labelling is on the figure, not in a footnote**: the label reads *"Hạn mức còn lại — chỉ tính các hồ sơ đã duyệt"*, in the same string as the number, because a customer who reads it as *available* meets the difference as a settlement that moved. **The console reached this answer at v0.5 and the app did not; the two now say the same thing about the same counter**, which is the whole of D1 §7.1's promise |

**Provisional postings are not visible to the customer, and that is a decision this document takes deliberately.** D1 BR-LEDGER-1 makes consumption two-phase — provisional at calculation, final at approval — and BR-LEDGER-2 makes provisional postings invisible to other in-flight claims. Three arguments settle it the same way:

1. **A provisional posting can evaporate.** A claim can be returned, cancelled, declined, or re-run under BR-TRACK-4 with a different total. A remaining limit that fell by 3,000,000 and then rose again reads to a customer as either a bug or bad faith, and support has no way to explain a number that was never final.
2. **Showing it would make the app's number differ from the engine's.** BR-LEDGER-2 already excludes provisional postings from what the engine sees when it adjudicates a second claim. If the app netted them off, the customer would be told they had less limit than the engine would in fact grant them — and would then be paid more than the app said was available, on the same screen that promised the figures agree.
3. **A1 already defines the term this way.** *Hạn mức còn lại* is sum insured minus **final** consumption. Rendering something else under that label is a defect in this document, not a design choice.

**What is shown instead.** F11 states, without arithmetic, that the customer has *n* claims in progress for this member and what was requested on them — so a customer who is about to claim can see that something is already in flight, without the app implying a number that has not been decided. **F11 covers only claims this customer submitted**, per A3 §4.3.

**A residual, stated rather than hidden.** A3 §4.3 keeps a claim submitted by another member on the same policy invisible to this customer, and A3 §4.3 further requires remaining limits to be shown *as amounts only, never itemised by who consumed them*. The consequence is that F5 can fall between two openings for a reason the customer cannot see — a spouse's claim approving against a shared annual cap. This is the privacy-preserving default A3 chose knowingly (A3-03 is open at MVP 2), and the screen does not paper over it: F7's timestamp is what makes the movement attributable to *a claim approving*, and the customer support script for "my limit changed" is the same answer. **The app must not invent an explanation it is not permitted to give.**

**Empty and error.** A member with no consumption shows F5 equal to F2 — never a blank. Ledger unreachable: F5/F6 show the last read with F7's timestamp and a stale marker, plus `SYS-ERR-002`; the figures are never shown as current when they are not. **A member whose ledger holds one period only renders one block and no period selector** — a chooser with one option teaches the reader that there is a choice — **but the block is still labelled with its policy year's dates**, because the label is what makes the figure interpretable and it costs nothing when there is one of them.

Notification preferences are specified in §4.2. The payout-account section is specified in §4.5, because A3 §4.5's rule is the same wherever the account is changed.
