F8 is **never validated against ICD-10 in the app** — the diagnosis of record is extracted from `T1-03` and confirmed by an assessor — which is why the row has no rule and no message. **F9 is new and is the only free-text clinical field the app asks for; see below.** F10 is grouped on display and accepts no decimal separator (§2.3). **F11 to F14 are the claimant block and F15 and F16 are the claim's contact block; both have their own note below, and from v0.4 they are two blocks rather than one.** F18 is held at `text(30)` per §2.9. **F19, F20, F21, F22 and F23 are written by the platform and never by the customer.**

**Renumbering, stated once.** The claimant block and the narrative are inserted rather than appended, so **F9 to F14 of v0.2 have moved**: v0.2's amount F9 is now **F10**, its bank F10 is **F17**, its account number F11 is **F18**, its account name F12 is **F19**, its verification flag F13 is **F20** and its payee reuse F14 is **F21**. Every reference in the rest of this section, in §4.10 and in Part VII uses the new numbers. **The alternative — continuing at F15 and leaving the block scattered — was rejected here** because S11 is a single wizard step whose fields render in the order they are numbered, unlike S-02, where §5.4.1's note explains why the opposite choice was correct on a screen with two tables.

### The loss type — two dimensions, eight values

*(Register: **S-10**, reduced)*

`episodeType`'s five values collapsed **pathology** and **place of treatment** into one axis, which is why *dental* and *maternity* had no inpatient form and why A4 §6's checklist could not distinguish an outpatient accident from an admitted one. **`lossType` replaces it as the captured field on every surface. It does not retire it** — the five values survive as a projection, on the console's event at §5.7.2 F5, because A5 §8.1 keys its benefit mapping on them (A1 §4.2).

| Pathology \ Place | Ngoại trú (outpatient) | Nội trú (inpatient) |
|---|---|---|
| **Bệnh** (illness) | `ILL_OP` | `ILL_IP` |
| **Nha khoa** (dental) | `DEN_OP` | `DEN_IP` |
| **Tai nạn** (accident) | `ACC_OP` | `ACC_IP` |
| **Thai sản** (maternity) | `MAT_OP` | `MAT_IP` |

**The screen renders one control, not two**, showing the eight combined Vietnamese labels — *Bệnh (ngoại trú)*, *Bệnh (nội trú)*, … — because a customer choosing two dropdowns can produce a combination and then change one half of it, and the app would have to explain the result. **The model holds two dimensions; the control offers eight rows.** The prototype's S09 draws it this way.

> **Reduced from the register's S-10, and here is what was left out.** The reference carries **twelve** values: the eight above plus *tử vong do bệnh hoặc thai sản*, *tử vong do tai nạn*, *thương tật vĩnh viễn do tai nạn* and *tổn thương sức khoẻ vĩnh viễn do bệnh*. **The four we left out are the death and permanent-disability variants, and they are left out of the *app*, not out of the model.** A death claim is not submitted by the insured from their own phone; it is submitted by an heir, usually at a counter, with documents the app's checklist does not contain. Offering the customer a *tử vong* option on a screen that then asks them to photograph a cost statement is worse than not offering it. **`enum(lossType)` is specified with all twelve values so that the console and A4 can carry them**, and the app's control renders the first eight. On the counter-intake route of §7.2 it renders all twelve, and so does the console (§5.4.1 F7, §5.7.2 F18). **`D2-115` asked A1 to register the set and A1 v1.2 §4.2 did; A1 v1.5 §4.2 has since re-cut the members to match this table — `D2-119` closed**, together with the statement that `lossType` **subsumes** `episodeType` rather than superseding it — which is why A1's `episodeType` entry stands rather than being struck, and why §5.7.2 F5 still carries the five values for A5 §8.1 to map on.

> **A1 §4.2 registers twelve values and they are not these twelve, and that must not be discovered by an implementer.** A1's twelve are **condition class × setting** — `PRE_OP`, `SPE_IP`, `GEN_OP`, `ACC_IP`, `BIR_OP`, `MAT_IP` and their pairs — and the eight it says the app can determine are rows 1 to 8 of *that* set. This document's twelve are **pathology × setting** — `ILL`, `DEN`, `ACC`, `MAT` — plus the four death and permanent-disability variants. **The two sets agree on the count, on the name and on the shape of the argument, and disagree on the members.** The disagreement is not cosmetic: A1's set has no dental value at all, and its app-determinable eight include `PRE` and `SPE`, which a customer can no more distinguish than they can separate childbirth from a maternity complication — the same objection A1 §4.2 makes about its own rows 9 to 12. **A1 owns the enum codes (§0.5) and this document did not re-cut the set**; it was raised as **`D2-119`**. **A1 v1.5 §4.2 has re-cut it, and `D2-119` closes.** A1 took this document's axis — **pathology × setting, plus the four death and permanent-disability variants** — and records the reason in one sentence: *"A1 was the outlier; D2 was right."* The set now has a dental value, the eight the app offers are the eight a customer can actually distinguish, and **`enum(lossType)` means the same twelve values in A1, in this document and in A4's re-cut checklist**. The table above is unchanged, which is the point: nothing here moved, the annex moved to it.

> **Part V now keys on the same axis, and `D2-44` is closed.** This block made the change on the app surface; §5.7.2 **F18**, §5.4.1 **F7** and §5.5.1 have since made it on the console, after **A1 v1.2 §4.2** registered `lossType` and stated that it **subsumes `episodeType` rather than replacing it**. **`episodeType` is not retired.** It survives with its five values as a **projection**, held on the insured event at §5.7.2 F5, read-only, because that is what **A5 §8.1's benefit mapping** keys on and A5 is unchanged. **The direction is fixed and one-way**: `lossType` is captured, `episodeType` is derived from it, and code that lets the two disagree has a defect (A1 §4.2). A4 §6's checklist is keyed on eight values in both parts, plus the claimant's standing. **A1 §4.2 names the condition on which `episodeType` finally retires** — when the checklist becomes per-loss-type per event, which is Framework **S-38** and **D2-135** — and that is not this reissue.

### The claimant block — F11 to F14

*(Register: **B-07**, **B-08**)*

**This is the one thing added to the customer's journey by the whole of this reissue, and it is one question with a default answer.** F11 defaults to *Bản thân* and, while it holds that value, F12 is hidden and F13 and F14 are filled from the insured member and cannot be edited. **A customer claiming for themselves sees one extra read-only line and answers nothing.**

The block opens only when the customer says they are not the insured — which they must already have said implicitly by choosing a dependant at F2, and which the app can therefore **pre-suggest**: where F2 is not the account holder's own member record, F11 pre-selects `GUARDIAN` and F12 pre-selects the relationship from `insured_member.relationship` where one maps. The customer confirms or corrects.

**V-117 refuses, and refusing is the point.** A customer who chooses *Bản thân* and then edits the name or the identity number is describing a claim in which the person asking is not the person insured while asserting that they are. That is either a typing error or the first move of a misdirected payment, and the two look identical from here. The screen does not correct it and does not warn about it; it will not save. The console enforces the same rule at **V-709** (§5.20.5).

**What the extra document costs the customer.** Where F11 is not `SELF`, S12's checklist gains one `REQUIRED` row (§3.2.10's table, V-118) and the customer is told what it is before they leave this screen, not after they have submitted.

### The claim's contact block — F15 and F16

*(Decision **`B4`**, 24 August 2026.)*

**F15 and F16 were *the claimant's* email and telephone in v0.3 and they are *the claim's* from v0.4.** The change is one of meaning rather than of layout: the customer still answers two questions on the same screen, and the two answers are now **the contact details for this claim** — the address and the number every message the platform sends about **this** claim goes to. **F16 becomes mandatory**, because a telephone number is the fallback an assessor actually uses when an address bounces and there is no other route to the person who asked.

**They are not read from anywhere.** Not from the app account, not from the insured member record, not from the claimant's previous claim. **The customer types them, on the claim, at the moment they claim** — which is the only moment at which anyone can say with confidence which address that person is currently reading.

> **This replaces the *which email do we use* problem rather than answering it.** `G-B-03` recorded that `insured_member` carries no email column and that the `EMAIL` channel therefore delivered to a field the data model did not contain; **`D2-14`** asked InsureMO whether the register held one. **The question is withdrawn.** It is still unanswered and it now has no consumer: §6.1.2a resolves every customer-facing email from F15, and there is no row on that list waiting for a vendor.

**Three consequences, written down because a reader will otherwise assume each of them the other way.**

| # | Consequence |
|---|---|
| **1** | **It is snapshot-safe by construction.** The contact is captured **with the claim** — one row per claim, §3.2.10 — so a later change to the customer's account cannot redirect correspondence about a claim already decided. This is `P-02`'s guarantee obtained **structurally rather than by a rule**: there is no live read to forbid, because there is no second place the address lives. A customer who updates their profile in March does not move February's decline letter |
| **2** | **It splits J1 from J2, and the split must be said rather than left to be inferred.** **The certificate at purchase goes to the account's registered address** (§4.3) — at that moment there is no claim and no claim contact, and the customer is buying rather than claiming. **Everything about a claim goes to F15.** The two strings are usually identical and are never the same field, and the case that separates them is ordinary: a policyholder buys family cover under his own address and his adult daughter, claiming on her own cover, gives hers. **A2 owns which audience a message addresses and must carry the split — `D2-141`** |
| **3** | **A customer can type any address, and the answer is confirmation rather than a control.** Nothing prevents a typo or a foreign address. **This is not the payment-redirection risk and must not be handled as though it were** — correspondence is not money, and BR-PAY-1 to BR-PAY-4 and A3 §4.6 stand between an address and a payment. **But a decline letter is a document about someone's health**, and one wrong character sends it to a stranger, so the pair is **echoed back for confirmation before submission** — **`V-407`** |

> **Why an echo-back and not a second entry box, and why not a verification loop.** **A confirm-by-retyping box catches nothing**: a customer who mistypes an address types the same thing twice, because the error is in what they believe the address to be, not in their fingers. **Reading it back to them, in full, on the review step they were already going to see, is what catches it** — it costs one glance and it is the only mechanism that puts the actual string in front of the only person who knows whether it is right. **A verification loop — a code emailed to the address before the claim may be submitted — is deliberately not built**, and the reason is §2.10: it would block a claim on a mail server, and an operational failure must never be rendered as a claim outcome. **The customer's remedy after submission is an information request**, the same route as any other correction to a submitted claim (§4.8), and the assessor may correct the block on the console (A3 §4.18, §5.4.2 F40 and F41).

### F22 — the request-received date

*(Register: **B-06**)*

`requestReceivedDate` has been in the date chain since v0.1 and **no screen has ever collected it** — that is `G-B-06`, and it means the third line of the chain below has never been testable. On this screen it is not collected either: **it is the submission date, it is written by the platform, and it is read-only.** A claim that arrived through the app arrived on the day the app sent it, and there is no version of that fact a customer could usefully type.

**It becomes a field a person enters only on the counter-intake route** (§7.2, register `B-03`), where the customer handed over paper on a date that is not the date we keyed it. **That is the same distinction `B-24` makes for supplementary documents**, and it is the same rule: the date the customer acted, recorded separately from the date we acted. §5.4.1's *Reduced from S-06* note says the request-received date is "an intake field on a screen this pass does not touch" — **this is that screen, and F22 is that field.**

### F21 — reuse of a proven payee

*(Register: **B-10**)*

**The v0.2 matching rule excluded the case the payee entity exists to handle, and this replaces it.** BR-PAY-4 matched a previously paid payee on *name + date of birth + identity number* — of the **payee**. A parent who has been paid twice for their child matches on the second claim; a parent claiming for their *second* child does not, because the key it matched on was the payee's identity and the two claims share no other key the rule looked at.

**The revised rule.** F21 offers the distinct **account holders** who have been paid on any **previously paid** claim **for the same insured member** — the key is `member_id`, not the payee's identity — and each offered row shows the payee's name, their relationship to the insured, and the masked account. Selecting a row fills F17, F18, F19 and F20 together and the account arrives **already verified**, so F20 may be `true` at submission. **Editing any of the four clears F19 and F20** under BR-PAY-2, unchanged.

> **The wider case is a decision, not an omission.** The reference matches account holders across **every prior claim of the same insured person**, identified by name + date of birth + identity number, which reaches across policies. We match within `member_id`, which does not. Reaching across policies means reading claims the actor's data scope may not cover, and A3 §0.3 has no answer for a lookup that returns a row from outside the scope in order to fill a form inside it. **Recorded rather than fixed**, and the wider match is what `BR-PAY-4` should say if the business wants it — **D2-43**.

**Actions**

*(Register: **B-04**, reduced)*

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tiếp tục | `CUST` | F1–F18 valid, including the claimant block **and the contact block, which has been echoed back and confirmed — `V-407`** | Creates the claim in `DRAFT` and navigates to S12 with the checklist for F3 **and for F11** | Date chain: as per the field rows |
| Lưu nháp | `CUST` | F1–F3 present | Persists locally and server-side as `DRAFT`. Nothing is submitted | — |
| **Dùng lại thông tin hồ sơ trước** | `CUST` | The customer has at least one prior claim for the member selected at F2 | **Pre-fills the claimant block (F11–F14), the contact block (F15, F16) and the payout block (F17–F21) from that claim.** Nothing clinical is copied: F3 to F10 stay empty. The prior claim is named on the control. **A pre-filled contact is still echoed back and still confirmed** (`V-407`) — a value carried from a claim eighteen months ago is exactly the one a customer should be shown before it is used again | — |
| Đổi tài khoản nhận tiền | `CUST` | The claim is before `PENDING_APPROVAL` (A3 §1 — *change payout account*, `C`, scope `SELF`; A3 §4.5) | Replaces F17 and F18 on the claim and clears F19 and F20 — BR-PAY-2 | Save failure: `SYS-ERR-002` |

> **Reduced from the register's B-04, and here is what was left out.** The reference's *copy claim* opens a whole new record carrying the policy, the insured, the payee **and the document checklist**, clearing only the number, the status, the dates and the trail. We copy **the parties and the account, never the documents and never the episode.** Copying a checklist copies the *state* of a checklist — which items were satisfied, which were waived — onto a claim whose documents do not exist yet, and every one of those states would be a lie until the customer photographed something. Copying an episode copies dates and a diagnosis onto a different visit, which is the error the date chain exists to catch and which a pre-filled field defeats. **What is worth reusing is what does not change between two claims by the same person, and that is exactly the two blocks above.**

**The date-validation chain.** D1 §3.2.1 is checked **at capture, not at assessment**, and in full:

```
eventDate ≤ treatmentFrom ≤ treatmentTo ≤ today
coveragePeriod.from ≤ treatmentFrom     and    treatmentTo ≤ coveragePeriod.to
treatmentTo ≤ requestReceivedDate ≤ today
```

Three points the screen must get right. **The member's coverage period is tested, not the policy's** — on group cover members join and leave mid-term, and testing the policy either admits claims for people who had left or rejects claims for people who had joined (D1 §3.2.1); F2's `coveragePeriod` from I-05 is the value used. **The whole chain is tested, not just the cover window** — chained inequalities catch transposed and swapped dates, the commonest entry error, at the moment they cost the customer ten seconds. `CLM-VAL-002` renders `{serviceDate}`, `{coverageFrom}` and `{coverageTo}`, so a customer who mistyped a year can see it. **And the third line is now testable**, because F22 exists: on this screen `requestReceivedDate` is the submission date and the third line can only fail where `treatmentTo` is in the future, which the first line has already caught. **That is not a reason to drop it** — the same chain runs on the counter-intake route where the two dates genuinely differ, and a chain that is only enforced on one of two entry points is a chain that will be found to have a hole.

**Payout account — who enters it, who verifies it, and what each rule therefore blocks.**

**The customer enters the account. The customer does not verify it.** A3 §1 gives `CUST` exactly one grant over the payout account — **change it** (`C`, scope `SELF`). Verification is a different action with a different holder: A3 §3.2 assigns *verify a payout account* to `ASSESSOR` and `ADMIN` at scope `ASSIGNED`, **Part V §5.20 is the screen it happens on** — it was Part III §3.5.3 in v0.1, and it moved with the record (F58) — and Part V §5.12 is where its absence bites. The app therefore captures F17 and F18 and records the account **unverified**; verification happens on the console after registration, which is the first moment a claim exists that an assessor can be assigned to.

| Rule | Where it bites, and what it actually blocks |
|---|---|
| **BR-PAY-1** — the name is never typed | F19 has no keyboard on any surface. In this app it is empty until the console's verification writes it, and read-only thereafter. There is no "type it yourself" path and no override |
| **BR-PAY-2** — changing the number clears the verified name | Editing F17 or F18 blanks F19 and sets F20 `false` immediately, **on edit and not on save**, so the screen can never briefly show a verified name against a different account. Server-side the same clearing runs on every claim that references the account (A3 §4.5) |
| **BR-PAY-3** — no settlement on an unverified account | **This does not gate submission from the app.** It is enforced where the account is first used: the console refuses to submit a settlement plan while `accountNameVerified` is `false` (Part V §5.10.2, check **V-593**, `CLM-CONSOLE-006`) |
| **A3 §4.6** — no payment to an unverified account | The last control and the real one. A payment instruction may issue only on a claim in `APPROVED`, only for the approved amount, and only to a verified account; `I-11` refuses `422 ACCOUNT_NOT_VERIFIED` (D3 §I-11). **No money leaves against an account nobody checked** |
| **BR-PAY-4** — reuse of a proven payee | F21 offers account holders paid on any previously **paid** claim for the same insured member — **the revised match key above**, `member_id` rather than the payee's identity. A payee proven that way arrives already verified, so F20 can be `true` at submission; editing any field of the selection clears it again under BR-PAY-2 |

**So a claim can be submitted on an unverified account, and that is deliberate.** Reading BR-PAY-3 as a submission gate deadlocks the app: it would require verification on a `DRAFT` claim, and a `DRAFT` has no claim number, no assignment and therefore no assessor holding the `ASSIGNED` scope A3 §3.2 requires — nothing would ever be submitted, and no assessor could ever see the claim that was waiting. Verification moves to the first moment a person with the grant exists, and the money is held behind A3 §4.6 until it succeeds. **What is blocked is the payment, never the customer's ability to ask.**

**What the customer sees in the meantime.** F20 renders as a plain progress line — that the account will be checked before payment — not as an error, not as a warning, and not as something to fix. It is A2 rule M-7 applied to a state the customer neither caused nor can act on, and §2.10 applied to a step that is not an outcome. That sentence does not exist in A2 and is **D2-37**.

**When verification does not succeed.** The assessor's verification failing is the one case in which the customer is told anything: `CLM-VAL-005` is shown against F20 — *"Chưa xác thực được tên chủ tài khoản. Vui lòng kiểm tra lại số tài khoản và ngân hàng."* — and their remedy is the single grant they hold, *Đổi tài khoản nhận tiền*. Note what the message still does **not** do: it does not name the account holder the bank returned, it does not say the name did not match the insured, and it does not offer an override. A customer who genuinely cannot verify an account has one remedy, a different account. That is a hard edge and it is the correct one — a misdirected payment is the most expensive and least recoverable error a claim system makes (D1 §3.2.2). A verification the service could not perform at all is not the customer's error to fix and is not shown to them; it is an operator's problem with an operator's queue (§2.10, A2 rule M-7).

> **Open item — D2-36.** `CLM-VAL-005` is a screen message, and a customer whose verification failed is not on the screen. Nothing in A2 carries it to them as a notification, D1 sets no limit on how long a claim may sit on an unverifiable account before an assessor must ask for another, and A3 §4.5 does not say who asks. **A business answer is needed**, and an A2 item with it.

**Changing the payout account later — A3 §4.5.** The account can be changed from S10 or from a claim in a pre-approval state. Two consequences, both enforced server-side:

1. **Verification is cleared and must run again, always.** The change is BR-PAY-2 applied outside the claim form: the stored `accountName` (F19) is cleared and `accountNameVerified` (F20) set `false` the moment the number changes, on every claim that references the account. A claim in `PENDING_APPROVAL` or earlier keeps moving — the customer is not blocked — but **no settlement plan can be submitted and no payment can issue on it** until an assessor has verified the new account.
2. **If a settlement is already approved, the payment is held for an approver to re-release.** A3 §4.5 exists for one attack — submit a clean claim, change the account after approval — and D1 §3.2.2 names it. The app tells the customer the account was changed and that the payment will follow once checked; it does **not** tell them a payment is held pending an internal re-release, because that is an internal control and describing it teaches the attack. The console side is `CLM-CONSOLE-010` (A3 §4.5). *The precise customer-facing wording is D2-29.*

**Rules**

- The claim is created in `DRAFT` on *Tiếp tục*, **and no claim number is allocated** (D1 J2-6, S-09). The number is allocated once, at registration, after coverage validation (F41). Until then the app identifies the claim by a client-generated submission key, which is also the idempotency key for the eventual submission (§4.10).
- **A duplicate is never mentioned to the customer.** BR-DUP-4 is absolute: duplicate detection is an internal control and the app has no surface for it, not even a soft warning.

**Empty and error.** A `DRAFT` claim resumes at S11 with every field intact. F19 and F20 are **re-read from the claim rather than restored from local state** — a draft left for a week must not show a verification that has since been cleared, and the app has no way of its own to establish one. **F22 and F23 are written at submission, not at draft creation**, so a resumed draft carries neither until it is sent. **F15 and F16 are restored as typed and their confirmation is not** — `V-407`'s confirmation is recorded against a submission, so a draft resumed a week later is echoed back and confirmed again rather than arriving pre-confirmed.

### 4.6 Guided document capture (F27)

#### S12 — Chụp chứng từ [F27, and F29 in response mode]

| | |
|---|---|
| **Purpose** | Capture the right documents for the episode type, one type at a time, with quality checks at the moment of capture. |
| **Entered from** | S11 (initial capture); S13's information-request card (response mode). |
| **Who may open it** | `CUST`, scope `SELF`, on a claim they created (A3 §1, F27). |

**The checklist is driven by F3 and F11 of S11.** *(Register: **S-10** · **B-07**/**V-118** · **B-18**.)* A4 §6 is the authority; the app renders the rows for the chosen loss type **and the row the claimant's standing requires**, and never invents one.

| Loss type (S11 F3) | Bắt buộc (`REQUIRED`) | Nên có (`EXPECTED`) | Tùy chọn (`OPTIONAL`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ILL_OP` — Bệnh, ngoại trú | T1-01, T1-03 | T1-04, **T1-02** | T2-01, T2-02, T2-03 |
| `ILL_IP` — Bệnh, nội trú | T1-01 | T1-04, T2-03 | T1-02, T2-01, T2-02 |
| `DEN_OP` — Nha khoa, ngoại trú | T1-01, T1-03 | T1-04 | T2-01 |
| `DEN_IP` — Nha khoa, nội trú | T1-01 | T1-04, T2-03 | T2-01, T2-02 |
| `ACC_OP` — Tai nạn, ngoại trú | T1-01, T1-03 | T1-04, T2-02 | T1-02, T2-01 |
| `ACC_IP` — Tai nạn, nội trú | T1-01 | T1-04, T2-02, T2-03 | T1-02, T2-01 |
| `MAT_OP` — Thai sản, ngoại trú | T1-01, T1-03 | T1-04 | T1-02, T2-01, T2-03 |
| `MAT_IP` — Thai sản, nội trú | T1-01 | T1-04, T2-03 | T1-02, T2-01, T2-02 |
| **Any, where S11 F11 ≠ `SELF`** | **the standing document of §3.2.10** | — | — |

**Two structural facts this table now shows that the five-value table could not.** *Nha khoa* and *thai sản* have an inpatient form, and their checklists differ from their outpatient forms in exactly the way every other pathology's does — `T1-03` the examination record drops out and `T2-03` the medical report comes in, because an admitted patient is discharged with a report rather than an examination slip (A4 §1.6). And *outpatient with medication* is **not a loss type**: it was a row in the v0.2 table that named a pathology-and-treatment combination the customer cannot know at capture time. It is gone; `T1-02` is `EXPECTED` on `ILL_OP` and the reconciliation decides afterwards whether a prescription should have existed. **That closes `D2-105`'s app half** — A1's five-value `episodeType` could not express A4 §6's six-row split, and the eight-value set does not need to.

**`T1-02` prescription is `EXPECTED` for `ILL_OP`** (D1 B-02, A4 §6). The screen must therefore *ask* for it and let the customer proceed without it, which is exactly the behaviour `EXPECTED` names: the clinical appropriateness track reasons about drugs against the diagnosis and has nothing to work with when the prescription is absent, but a visit that legitimately produced no prescription must not stall. `REQUIRED` would stall it; `OPTIONAL` would never ask.

**The standing row is `REQUIRED` and it is the only checklist row not driven by the loss type.** V-118 puts it there; the customer sees it named on S11 before they arrive here.

> **The A4 mapping A4 does not yet carry.** A4 §6's checklist is keyed on `episodeType`'s five values. This table is keyed on eight, plus a second key. **A4 must be re-cut and this document must not re-cut it** (§0.5) — **D2-114**, with the two standing documents. **§5.5.1 now generates the console's checklist on the same two keys**, so the two surfaces ask for the same documents and the console half of **D2-44** is closed; what is still owed is A4's own re-cut, and **until it lands both surfaces read the eight rows above** — one transitional read of the annex's data through the one place D2 has written it down, not a second definition of it.

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Loại chứng từ | `enum(documentType)` | `master` | — | — | — |
| F2 | Mức độ cần thiết | `derived` | `master` | — | — | — |
| F3 | Hướng dẫn chụp | `derived` | `master` | — | — | — |
| F4 | Ảnh / tệp | `file` | `user` | C — mandatory for every `REQUIRED` row | JPG, PNG, PDF; **XML for `T1-04` only** (A4 §1.5). ≤ 10 MB per file, ≤ 20 pages per type, ≤ 50 files per claim (§2.7) | `CLM-VAL-006` with `{fileName}`, `{maxSize}` |
| F5 | Trang | `int` | `system` | — | — | — |

**Notes on the fields above.** Only F4 and F9 are entered; the rest are master data or values the app writes, so they carry no validation (§2.2). F1 renders the A4 type names in Vietnamese (A1 §6) — *Bảng kê chi phí khám chữa bệnh*, *Đơn thuốc*, … — and **never the codes** `T1-01` (A2 rule M-3). F2 renders as *"Bắt buộc"* · *"Nên có"* · *"Tùy chọn"*, **never as `REQUIRED`**. F3 is the per-type capture guidance: what the page must show, how to frame it, and for `T1-01` that every page of a multi-page statement is needed. F5 is the page ordinal within the type, reorderable by drag and deletable individually. F7 is present only after processing, on a re-entry. F8 is `Chờ tải lên` · `Đang tải` · `Đã tải lên`, visible per page. **F9 is a group rather than a checklist row — see below.**

### The other-documents group

*(Register: **B-21**)*

**F9 is a group, not a type**, rendered beneath the checklist with its own capture and upload controls and no requirement level. It exists because **the customer has, today, nowhere to put a document that is not one of the seven** — that is `G-B-14`, and the seven are a Tier-1 extraction catalogue, not an inventory of what a hospital hands a patient.

| Property | Statement |
|---|---|
| **What goes in it** | Anything the customer thinks is relevant and the checklist does not name. A referral letter, a second provider's receipt, a translated document, a letter from an employer |
| **What happens to it** | It is uploaded with the package and **submitted for classification like every other page** (D3 §I-07). Where IDP classifies it as one of the seven, `DOC-VAL-004` states so and it is **moved into that checklist row**, which is the same behaviour F7 already specifies for a mis-filed page. Where IDP cannot classify it, it stays here, visible to the assessor as an unclassified attachment |
| **What it never does** | **It never satisfies a `REQUIRED` row.** *Gửi hồ sơ* still requires a page in every `REQUIRED` row, and a customer who puts their cost statement in the other-documents group has not supplied a cost statement until classification says so. A group that could satisfy a requirement would be a way around the checklist |
| **Limits** | The §2.7 package limits are shared with the checklist, not additional to it. Twenty documents means twenty |

> **The console already has the other half of this** — §5.5.6's *Chưa phân loại* listing — and has had it since v0.1. What was missing was the customer's end of it, so the only unclassified pages that could ever exist were ones IDP failed to classify, never ones the customer deliberately sent. **§5.5 gains nothing new from this block**: the same listing renders the same pages, and whether it is promoted from an *Empty and error* row to a section of the checklist tab with the classified page's upload, download, re-extract and delete controls is a Part V presentation decision recorded at **D2-45**.

### The extractor's document classes

*(Register: **B-18**, reduced)*

**A4 defines seven document types; IDP returns a `classification` on every page; nothing in the document set says which of IDP's values means which of A4's.** Today that mapping lives in whatever the adapter's author writes, which is the definition of a fact nobody can check.

**The reduced requirement, and it is a requirement on A4 rather than a build here:** A4 §3's type table gains a column carrying **the IDP classification value or values that map to that type**, one type to many classes, and the adapter reads it rather than hard-coding it. A class IDP returns that maps to nothing is **`UNCLASSIFIED`** and lands in the other-documents group above — not an error, not a guess.

> **Left out.** The reference carries the mapping **inside its own specification** and lets it be edited. We do not build an editing screen for it, and we do not put the table in D2 — it is A4's table, A4 owns document types (§0.5), and a copy here would disagree with A4 within one release. What this section requires is that the column exists and that the adapter is driven by it. **D2-116**, a correction owed to A4, and it is on the critical path for `I-09`'s adapter rather than for a screen.

**Actions**

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chụp | `CUST` | Camera permission granted | Captures a page, runs the quality check, appends to the type | `DOC-VAL-001` / `-002` / `-003` where a check fails |
| Chọn từ thư viện | `CUST` | Photo permission granted | Same, without the camera | `CLM-VAL-006` on type or size |
| Chụp lại | `CUST` | A page selected | Replaces that page in place, keeping its ordinal | — |
| Xóa trang | `CUST` | A page selected, claim not submitted | Removes the page | — |
| Gửi hồ sơ | `CUST` | Every `REQUIRED` row has ≥ 1 page, **every file uploaded** | Submits the claim. State → `SUBMITTED`; the platform allocates the claim number at registration | No document at all: `CLM-VAL-003` · Submitted: the screen confirms receipt in place and routes to S13 · **`CLM-NOTIF-001` is raised at registration, not here** — see §4.7 · Failure: `SYS-ERR-003` |

**The quality check, and what happens when it fails.**

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Where it runs | **On the device, at capture**, before any upload. §2.7: *a bad photograph rejected at capture is not a failed extraction three minutes later* |
| Blur | Variance-of-Laplacian over the detected document region, against a threshold held as `config` and tunable without a release. Below threshold → `DOC-VAL-001` |
| Edges | Quadrilateral detection; a page whose detected boundary touches or leaves the frame on any side → `DOC-VAL-002` |
| Glare | Saturated-pixel proportion over the document region above a `config` threshold → `DOC-VAL-003` |
| **What the customer sees** | The captured image, the A2 message beneath it, and two controls: **Chụp lại** and **Dùng ảnh này**. The message is advisory in tone by construction — A2 rule M-7 phrases all three as a property of the image, never of the photographer (*"Ảnh chưa đủ rõ để đọc"*, not *"bạn chụp sai"*) |
| **Whether it blocks** | **It does not.** *Dùng ảnh này* is always available |

**Why a failed quality check does not block.** Two reasons, and the second is the stronger. First, some documents cannot be photographed to threshold — a faded thermal cost statement, a carbon-copy prescription — and a blocking check traps the customer with a valid claim and no exit. Second, **a poor image has a recovery path and a blocked capture does not**: an unreadable field produces `MISSING_FIELD`, an information request and `DOC-NOTIF-002` naming the field and the document, which is a specific, actionable ask. A capture the app refused produces nothing at all. The check is worth running because a retake at capture costs ten seconds and a retake after extraction costs a day — but its value is in the prompt, not in the veto.

**Type mismatch is informational.** Where IDP's classification disagrees with the row the customer filed the page under, `DOC-VAL-004` states what happened and that nothing is required of them; per D3 §I-07 the classification wins (A4 §3's conflict rule). Silently overriding what someone told you erodes trust; asking them to fix a disagreement the system has already resolved wastes their time.

**Offline capture.**

| Situation | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Capture with no connectivity | Pages are written to an **encrypted local queue** on the device and shown with F8 = *Chờ tải lên*. The claim stays `DRAFT`. Quality checks still run — they are on-device and need no network |
| Connectivity returns | The queue uploads in the background, oldest first, resumable. F8 advances per page |
| Submission attempted while pages are queued | **Blocked.** *Gửi hồ sơ* requires every file uploaded. The screen states how many pages remain rather than failing |
| Queue retention | 7 days. After that the customer is prompted to retake or discard; the images are deleted from the device on discard and on successful submission |
| Queue limits | The §2.7 limits apply to the queue, not only to the upload: 10 MB per file, 20 pages per type, 50 files per claim |

**Why submission waits for the upload.** D3 §I-07 submits the document package **by reference**. A package referencing an object that has not landed is a broken package, and the claim would enter `DOC_PROCESSING` and fail there — producing an `EXTRACTION_ERROR` and an operator queue for a cause that was known on the device before submission. Waiting is also kinder: a claim submitted with a partial package fails checklist reconciliation and returns an information request for documents the customer had already photographed.

**Rules**

- **`T1-04` VAT invoice accepts XML only** (A4 §1.5, §2.7). The row's capture guidance says so and the file picker filters to `text/xml`. There is no OCR path for invoice images, and a photographed invoice is not accepted here — it would silently produce a document nothing reads. Where no XML exists the customer proceeds without it: the invoice is `EXPECTED` on every episode type, and reconciliation rule R6 is skipped with a warning rather than the claim stalling (A4 §1.5 consequence 2).
- **Inpatient claims capture `T1-01` only as `REQUIRED`.** A4 §1.6: the discharge form is out of Tier 1 and inpatient episode facts are keyed by an assessor. The screen should not ask the customer for a document nothing will read.

**Empty and error.** A type with no pages shows its guidance and the capture control, not an error. Upload failure: `SYS-ERR-003` per page with a retry; the page stays in the queue and is never silently dropped.

### 4.7 Claim list and status timeline (F28)

#### S13 — Danh sách hồ sơ và tiến trình [F28, F29]

| | |
|---|---|
| **Purpose** | List the customer's claims, show each one's progress, and carry any outstanding information request. |
| **Entered from** | Tab bar; push notification deep link; S09. |
| **Who may open it** | `CUST`, **read only**, and **only claims they submitted** — a claim submitted by another member on the same policy is not visible, even to the policyholder (A3 §4.3). |

**List row**

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Số hồ sơ | `text(20)` | `system` | — | — | — |
| F2 | Người được bảo hiểm | `derived` | `snapshot` | — | — | — |
| F3 | Ngày điều trị | `date` | `system` | — | — | — |
| F4 | Số tiền yêu cầu | `money` | `system` | — | — | — |
| F5 | Trạng thái | `derived` | `system` | — | — | — |
| F6 | Cập nhật gần nhất | `datetime` | `system` | — | — | — |

**Timeline entry**

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F7 | Thời điểm | `datetime` | `system` | — | — | — |
| F8 | Nội dung | `derived` | `system` | — | — | — |
| F9 | Trạng thái | `derived` | `system` | — | — | — |

**Notes on the fields above.** The whole screen is read-only (A3 §1, F28), so no row carries a validation and none needs a message; the failure this screen has is a list that would not load, and that is in *Empty and error* (§2.2).

- **F1** is `CLM-YY-NNNNNN`, held at `text(20)` per §2.9. **It is absent on a `DRAFT`** — the number is allocated once, at registration (Part V §5.2.1) — and the row shows the treatment dates and the member instead.
- **F2** comes from the claim's policy snapshot and is never re-read. **F3** renders `treatmentFrom` – `treatmentTo` and **F4** renders `amountClaimed`.
- **F5** is the **customer-facing status** of the table below. **The internal state identifier is never rendered** (A2 rule M-3).
- **F6** is the timestamp of the most recent timeline entry. **F7** renders `dd/mm/yyyy HH:mm` in Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh.
- **F8** is **one complete A2 template** with its placeholders filled, never assembled on the screen (§2.6). **F9** is the customer-facing status the entry moved the claim into.

**The thirteen internal states, and what the customer is shown.**

| Internal state | Shown to the customer? | Customer-facing status (VI) | Timeline sentence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DRAFT` | Yes | **Nháp** | *(none — no notification is raised on a draft)* |
| `SUBMITTED` | Yes | **Đã gửi** | `CLM-NOTIF-001`, **at registration** — see the note below the table |
| `DOC_PROCESSING` | Yes | **Đang xử lý chứng từ** | `CLM-NOTIF-002` |
| `EXTRACTION_ERROR` | **No — shown as `DOC_PROCESSING`** | **Đang xử lý chứng từ** | `SYS-ERR-001` |
| *stalled* `DOC_PROCESSING` | **No — shown unchanged** | **Đang xử lý chứng từ** | `SYS-ERR-001` at the stall threshold, then nothing further |
| `PENDING_INFO` | Yes | **Cần bổ sung chứng từ** | `CLM-NOTIF-003`, and `DOC-NOTIF-001`/`-002` naming what is missing |
| `UNDER_ASSESSMENT` | Yes | **Đang thẩm định** | `CLM-NOTIF-004` |
| `PENDING_APPROVAL` | **No — shown as `UNDER_ASSESSMENT`** | **Đang thẩm định** | *(no new entry)* |
| `APPROVED` | Yes | **Đã duyệt** | `CLM-NOTIF-005`, or `CLM-NOTIF-008` where the settlement is less than claimed |
| `DECLINED` | Yes | **Từ chối** | `CLM-NOTIF-006` |
| `PAYMENT_IN_PROGRESS` | Yes | **Đang chi trả** | `PAY-NOTIF-001` |
| *stalled* `PAYMENT_IN_PROGRESS` | **No — shown unchanged** | **Đang chi trả** | *(no new entry; nothing is said until finance answers)* |
| `PAID` | Yes | **Đã chi trả** | `PAY-NOTIF-002` |
| `CLOSED` | Yes | **Đã đóng** | *(no new entry — closure is administrative)* |
| `CANCELLED` | Yes | **Đã hủy** | `CLM-NOTIF-009` — only on a registered claim; see the note below the table |

**Two messages in the table render `{claimNo}`, and a claim does not always have one.** `CLM-NOTIF-001` and `CLM-NOTIF-009` both bind the claim number, and the number is allocated once, at registration, after coverage validation (Part V §5.2.1, D1 J2-6, S-09). Two triggers therefore move rather than the wording:

- **`CLM-NOTIF-001` fires at registration, not on `SUBMITTED`.** The chip moves to *Đã gửi* the instant the package is accepted and S12 confirms receipt in place; the timeline entry arrives a moment later, when there is a number to put in it. Part V §5.2.3 already raises it there, so this is the app conforming to the console rather than a new rule. A claim that never reaches registration — an infrastructure failure at J2-7 — is an operator's problem, and the customer's chip stays at *Đã gửi* (§2.10).
- **A `DRAFT` is discarded, not cancelled, and raises nothing.** `CLM-NOTIF-009` fires only on a claim that has a number. A draft is not a claim: it has no number, no registration and no state to leave, and **a claim number is never burned on something that was never a claim** (S-09). The two actions are separate controls on S13 for exactly this reason.
- **Neither message's wording changes.** Both keep `{claimNo}` and both are always rendered with it bound. **Open item — D2-38:** A2 records `CLM-NOTIF-001`'s trigger as `SUBMITTED`, which is now wrong by one step; the trigger column needs restating as *registration*. No Vietnamese text is affected.

**Eleven customer-facing statuses from thirteen internal states.** The chips are the A1 §5.1 Vietnamese labels wherever a state is shown as itself; the four concealments — two states collapsed onto another chip, two stalls that add nothing — each have a reason.

- **`EXTRACTION_ERROR` → *Đang xử lý chứng từ*.** D1 §4.3 is the strongest statement in the lifecycle: operational states are not decisions, and *a claim declined because a service was down is indistinguishable from a correct decline unless the states are kept apart*. A1's own label for this state is *"Lỗi xử lý tài liệu"* — accurate internally, and unusable on a customer's screen, because a customer reading "error" on their claim has learned only that something is broken and cannot act on it (A2 rule M-3). `SYS-ERR-001` is deliberately written to look like a progress update, *because from the customer's side it is one*: the failure is recoverable, invisible to them, and requires nothing of them.
- **A stalled `DOC_PROCESSING` shows nothing new.** The temptation is to add elapsed time — *"đang xử lý đã 2 giờ"* — which converts a normal state into an implied fault. D1 NFR-2 targets a five-minute median and a thirty-minute 95th percentile; a stall is an operator's problem with an operator's queue (D3 G-3). `SYS-ERR-001` fires **once**, at the stall threshold, and the timeline then says nothing further. Repeating it would turn silence into alarm.
- **A stalled `PAYMENT_IN_PROGRESS` shows nothing new.** `PAY-NOTIF-001` already says a payment is in progress. The app must not say a payment failed until finance actually returns `REJECTED` or `RETURNED`, at which point `PAY-NOTIF-003` fires — and note that `PAY-NOTIF-003` asks the customer to do nothing, because a returned payment is as often our data as theirs.
- **`PENDING_APPROVAL` → *Đang thẩm định*.** Not an operational concealment but a deliberate one: A2 carries **no notification for `PENDING_APPROVAL`**, and that absence is correct. To the customer, assessment is one phase; naming an internal approval step invites *"who is the approver and why are they slow"* and exposes the segregation-of-duties structure (A3 §4.1) to no benefit. The claim's own timeline entry from `CLM-NOTIF-004` stands until an outcome exists.

**A2 rule M-6, stated as a screen constraint.** No cell in the *Timeline sentence* column above is a decision phrased as a failure or a failure phrased as a decision. The only messages in the whole table that state an outcome are `CLM-NOTIF-005`, `-006`, `-008` and `PAY-NOTIF-002`/`-003` — all of which follow an actual decision by a person or by the auto-approval gate. **`SYS-ERR-001` is the only system-error message a customer sees on a claim, and it says the opposite of a decision.**

**Actions**

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mở hồ sơ | `CUST` | A row | Expands to the timeline | — |
| Bổ sung chứng từ | `CUST` | An open information request on the claim | Opens S12 in response mode — §4.8 | — |
| Xem kết quả | `CUST` | State in `APPROVED`, `DECLINED`, `PAID`, `CLOSED` | Navigates to S14 | — |
| Tiếp tục hồ sơ nháp | `CUST` | State `DRAFT` | Returns to S11 or S12 at the step it was left | — |
| Xóa hồ sơ nháp | `CUST` | State `DRAFT` | Requires a confirmation. Deletes the draft and its queued pages, on the device and server-side. **No state transition, no number, no notification** | Delete failure: `SYS-ERR-002` |
| Hủy hồ sơ | `CUST` | The claim is **registered** and its state is before `UNDER_ASSESSMENT` (A3 §1) | Requires a confirmation. State → `CANCELLED` | Success: `CLM-NOTIF-009` · State moved on: *(new A2 item needed — D2-30)* |

**Rules**

- **The timeline is the record** (A2 §0.3). Every message with an `IN_APP` channel lands here whether or not push is enabled, and entries are append-only — a superseded entry is never edited or removed.
- **Withdrawal is checked server-side against the current state, not the state the list was rendered with.** A customer who taps *Hủy hồ sơ* on a claim that moved to `UNDER_ASSESSMENT` in the interim needs a message saying so; D2-30 exists for that, and `CLM-NOTIF-009` must not fire for a cancellation that did not happen.
- **Withdrawal is offered from registration onward, and discarding is offered before it.** In the short window between *Gửi hồ sơ* and registration a claim is `SUBMITTED` with no number; neither control is shown, because there is nothing to discard locally and nothing to name in `CLM-NOTIF-009`. The window is a system step, not a wait the customer is asked to sit through (Part V §5.2).

### The messages sent about a claim appear on that claim

*(Register: **S-43**, the mobile half)*

**Every message the customer has been sent about a claim is listed on that claim's timeline**, in time order, with its subject line, its channel and the moment it was sent — and the in-app body is readable in place.

This costs nothing to build, because §6.1.2 already establishes that **the in-app record is the record**: every message that goes anywhere else also goes to `IN_APP`. What was missing was the **link from the claim to the messages about it**, so a customer looking at a claim could not see the letter they had been sent about it without going to a separate list and matching claim numbers by eye.

| Property | Statement |
|---|---|
| What is listed | Every `IN_APP` record carrying this `claimNo`, which by §6.1.2 is every message sent about the claim on any channel |
| What is shown per row | The moment, the subject or first line, and the channel it also went out on — *"đã gửi qua email"* |
| Attachments | Where the message was a `LETTER`, the stored PDF is opened in place (F61-R9). **The stored bytes, never a regeneration** (F61-R8) |
| **Delivery status** | **Not shown to the customer.** A message that bounced, retried and succeeded is a fact about our infrastructure; a message still retrying is not a thing the customer can act on. §2.10 — an operational failure is not a claim outcome, and a delivery state rendered next to a claim reads as one |

> **The console's half of `S-43` is the larger one and it is already built.** §5.14.1's fourth view and **§5.22** list every letter and notification sent about the claim **with** the delivery status the customer is not shown, the addresses it went to, the A2 code and template version, and §6.1.6's resend control (V-718, V-719). The register's **B-35** is the same requirement seen from the console, and this block is the customer's end of it.

**Empty and error.** No claims: an empty state with a route to S11. List load failure: `SYS-ERR-002` over the cached list, marked stale. **A claim with no messages yet is a claim in `DRAFT`**, and the correspondence region is absent rather than empty (§2.11 UI-25).
