### 4.8 Respond to an information request (F29)

**F29 has no screen.** An information request appears as a card at the top of the affected claim in S13, and its action re-enters S12 in response mode. The design follows D1 B-14's closing note directly — *"no new feature, no new state"* — and it is the right shape for two independent reasons: a request is always about one claim and belongs on it, and the response is a document capture, which S12 already specifies completely.

**The request card, on S13**

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Nội dung yêu cầu | `derived` | `system` | — | — | — |
| F2 | Chứng từ còn thiếu | `derived` | `master` | — | — | — |
| F3 | Trường không đọc được | `derived` | `idp:I-09` | — | — | — |
| F4 | Yêu cầu từ ngày | `date` | `system` | — | — | — |
| F5 | Ghi chú của Quý khách | `textarea(1000)` | `user` | O | — | — |
| **F6** | **Ngày Quý khách gửi** | `date` | `system` | **M** | **The date the supplementary package left the customer.** On this screen it is the submission date, written by the platform, read-only. **`V-406`** | — |
| **F7** | **Nguồn bổ sung** | `enum(intakeSource)` | `system` | **M** | `MOBILE_APP` on this screen, always. Read-only. §2.11 UI-27 | — |

**Notes on the fields above.** F1 to F4, F6 and F7 are written by the platform, and F5 is optional free text the control caps at 1,000 characters, so no row has a rule a customer can break (§2.2):

- **F1** is **one complete A2 template**: `DOC-NOTIF-001` (a required type is missing), `DOC-NOTIF-002` (a field could not be read) or `DOC-NOTIF-005` (a reminder). `DOC-NOTIF-004` (a physical original) stays in the model and is **never sent in the pilot** — originals are not required (D1 B-06, Part V §5.5.2) — so no card ever renders it.
- **F2** renders `{missingDocuments}` as the **Vietnamese document names** of A1 §6 — *Bảng kê chi phí khám chữa bệnh*, *Đơn thuốc* — never the type codes (A2 §3.4).
- **F3** binds `{fieldLabel}` and `{documentType}` for `DOC-NOTIF-002`, so the ask is a specific field on a specific document. **F4** is `{requestedAt}`, used by `DOC-NOTIF-005`.
- **F5** accompanies the response and carries the clinical escalation below.
- **F6 and F7** are new in v0.3 and are the customer's half of register row **B-24** — see the block below.

### The customer-sent date, and why one column matters more than one screen

*(Register: **B-24**)*

**We record the date we received a document. We have never recorded the date the customer sent it, and the two are the same date only when the customer used the app.**

§5.5.2 carries `Ngày nhận` — F9 — and nothing else. That is correct for a supplementary package that arrives through F29, where the customer's action and our receipt are the same instant. **It is wrong for every other route**, and the other routes are the ones a customer takes at exactly the moment they are least likely to open an app: they are standing in a hospital corridor holding a sheaf of paper somebody has just handed them.

**Why one column, and why now.**

**`V-504` records the moment a claim became complete and valid, and D1 §8.1 says why it cannot be reconstructed afterwards**: it is the anchor the fifteen-day statutory clock will need when `S-19` is lifted. If the customer sent their documents on the third and the counter keyed them on the seventh, the system records the seventh. **The clock then runs from a date four days later than the truth — in our favour, and wrong** — and there is no retrospective fix, because the third of the month was never written down anywhere.

**Therefore:**

| Rule | Statement |
|---|---|
| **Every supplementary package carries a customer-sent date.** | Not optional, not derived. `null` is not a value it can hold |
| **Where the package arrived through the app, the platform sets it** to the submission date and it is read-only (F6 above, §2.11 UI-27) | The customer neither enters it nor can change it |
| **Where the package arrived any other way, a member of staff enters it**, and the control will not accept a date after today or before the claim's `requestReceivedDate` | §5.5.2 **F16** and §5.5.4's *Ghi nhận bổ sung tại quầy* |
| **`V-504` anchors on the customer-sent date, not the received date**, whenever the two differ | The received date is retained and both are displayed; nothing is overwritten. **V-504 is defined at §5.2.6 and the re-anchoring is not applied there** — see the note below |
| The received date keeps its own meaning | It is what our SLA clock runs on, because our clock cannot start before we have the documents. **Two clocks, two anchors, and it is the statutory one that needed the second date** |

> **Two consequences land in Part V and only one of them is small enough to take here.** §5.5.2 gains **F16** and §5.5.4's counter-delivery action gains the date, both applied in this pass. **Re-anchoring `V-504` is not**: the rule is defined at §5.2.6 as *the moment the document set first reaches `COMPLETE`*, it is displayed on S-02.1 and on the work list, nothing measures against it under **S-19**, and changing what it anchors on is a change to a rule Part V owns and to the statutory-clock posture the business has not yet asked for. **Carried as `D2-46`**, with the note that the field it would anchor on now exists.
>
> **And one omission that should be declared rather than dropped.** The reference carries a **bulk counter-supplement screen** — tick several waiting claims, attach one file to each, enter one date each, submit. **It is left out of MVP 1.** A single-claim dialogue on the documents tab is enough at pilot volume. Register **B-24** proposes declaring the bulk form as a simplification; **the identifier is the Framework's to allocate**, and the request joins **D2-135**'s list rather than inventing an `S-` number here.

**Actions**

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bổ sung chứng từ | `CUST` | State `PENDING_INFO`, or an outcome carrying a `NOTREL` line (below) | Opens S12 in **response mode**: the checklist is filtered to the requested types, already-supplied documents are read-only, and only new pages may be added | — |
| Gửi bổ sung | `CUST` | ≥ 1 new page uploaded, or F5 non-empty | Submits the supplementary package. Re-enters the pipeline — see below | *(new A2 item needed — D2-31)* |

**What the customer is told is missing.** The request names documents and fields, never states. `DOC-NOTIF-001` renders the Vietnamese document names; `DOC-NOTIF-002` names the field and the document it is on. This is A2 rule M-2 doing real work: *"Hồ sơ chưa hợp lệ"* tells the customer nothing, *"Thiếu Bảng kê chi phí — vui lòng chụp và tải lên"* tells them exactly what to do. **`DOC-NOTIF-003` (reconciliation mismatch) is the one that is shown but carries no action** — it tells the customer we noticed and that they need do nothing, because a mismatch between two documents is usually ours to resolve.

**Re-entry into the pipeline.** On *Gửi bổ sung*:

1. The new documents are added to the claim's package. **Nothing existing is mutated or removed** — D1 §1.4 AR-3.
2. A **new** extraction request is created for the package (D3 §I-07). The prior extraction result is untouched and stays comparable (BR-DATA-1).
3. The claim leaves `PENDING_INFO` and returns to `DOC_PROCESSING`. Every requested checklist item leaves the *we asked* state, into one of BR-DOC-2's two terminal states — *supplied*, or *requested-and-not-supplied* — so the claim moves on rather than waiting forever on a document that will never arrive.
4. **A claim in `PENDING_APPROVAL` cannot receive one.** BR-DATA-3 prohibits re-running extraction while a claim is pending approval, and D1 §3.2.5's lock covers document actions precisely because a re-read can change the settlement under the approver. In that window the *Bổ sung chứng từ* action is not shown.

**This same feature carries the clinical escalation route (D1 B-14).** When a cost line is declined `NOTREL`, A2 §4's approved wording ends *"Nếu Quý khách có thông tin y tế bổ sung, vui lòng gửi để chúng tôi xem xét lại."* That sentence is a promise, and F29 is the mechanism that keeps it: the settlement screen (§4.9) renders a **Gửi thông tin y tế bổ sung** action against any `NOTREL` line, which opens the same response mode on S12 with the medical-report and lab-result types offered and F5 available for the customer's own account. The response returns the claim to an assessor with the new material attached.

Three properties of this route are load-bearing and follow from D1 §5.10.6:

- **It is available on a claim that has already been decided**, which is the whole point — the decline is where the customer learns they disagree. Note the boundary: a *fully declined* claim is `DECLINED` and, under S-13, cannot be re-opened; what the route delivers there is material for the out-of-band review channel of `CLM-LETTER-002` and BR-MSG-3. On a **partially** settled claim not yet closed, the material re-enters as an information request and the assessor reconsiders the line.
- **The customer is never told the recommendation came from a model.** D1 §5.10.6: a human confirmed it, so the decision is the insurer's, and saying otherwise is both inaccurate and an invitation to ask for the human review that already happened.
- **Nothing on this screen characterises the treating doctor's decision.** The invitation is to send more medical information about the *cover* question, not to defend a prescription.

**Empty and error.** No open request: the card is absent, not empty. Submission failure: `SYS-ERR-003`, the package stays queued, the claim stays in `PENDING_INFO`.

---

### 4.9 Settlement result (F30)

#### S14 — Kết quả chi trả [F30]

| | |
|---|---|
| **Purpose** | Show what was paid, benefit by benefit, what was not, why, and when the money moved. |
| **Entered from** | S13, and from the deep link on `CLM-NOTIF-005` / `-006` / `-008` / `PAY-NOTIF-002`. |
| **Who may open it** | `CUST`, **read only**, on a claim they submitted (A3 §1, F30; A3 §4.3). |

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Kết quả | `derived` | `system` | — | — | — |
| F2 | Số hồ sơ | `text(20)` | `system` | — | — | — |
| F3 | Số hợp đồng · Người được bảo hiểm | `derived` | `snapshot` | — | — | — |
| F4 | Quyền lợi | `derived` | `snapshot` | — | — | — |
| F5 | Chi phí yêu cầu | `money` | `system` | — | — | — |
| F6 | Được chấp nhận | `money` | `system` | — | — | — |
| F7 | Đồng chi trả | `money` | `system` | — | — | — |
| F8 | Chi trả | `money` | `system` | — | — | — |
| F9 | Khoản không được chi trả | `derived` | `system` | — | — | — |
| F10 | Giảm trừ theo điều kiện hợp đồng | `derived` | `system` | — | — | — |
| F11 | Tổng số tiền chi trả | `money` | `system` | — | — | — |
| F12 | Hạn mức còn lại sau hồ sơ này — năm hợp đồng {kỳ} | `money` | `system` | — | — | — |
| F13 | Tài khoản nhận tiền | `derived` | `system` | — | — | — |
| F14 | Ngày chi trả | `date` | `system` | — | — | — |
| F15 | Mã giao dịch | `text(40)` | `system` | — | — | — |
| F16 | Thông báo chi trả (PDF) | `file` | `system` | — | — | Download failure: `SYS-ERR-003` |
| F17 | Yêu cầu xem xét lại | `derived` | `master` | — | — | — |

**Notes on the fields above.** Nothing on this screen is entered — it is the terminal view of a decided claim (A3 §1, F30) — so no row carries a validation and only the letter download can fail (§2.2):

- **F1** is **one complete A2 template**: `CLM-NOTIF-005` (approved in full), `CLM-NOTIF-008` (partially settled) or `CLM-NOTIF-006` (not payable). Exactly one, chosen by outcome.
- **F2** is `{claimNo}` at `text(20)` per §2.9. **F3** comes from the claim's snapshot (D1 §7.2) and is never re-read.
- **F4** is the benefit name from the snapshot schedule, **one row per benefit paid**. **F5** is the requested cost on that row, **F6** the amount accepted after limits and line declines, **F7** the co-payment deducted on that benefit and **F8** the payable.
- **F9** sits **in the same table as F4–F8** (BR-LINE-4): one row per declined line, its reason cell holding one complete A2 §4 template.
- **F10** is the deduction ratio **and the condition that triggered it**, where one applied (A5 §4.3, A2 §7.1). It is absent where no condition was met — the step is skipped, not applied at zero.
- **F11** is `{settlementAmount}`, in figures **and in words** (A2 §7.1). **F12** is per benefit group, from the ledger's **final** postings — consistent with S09 F5. **It states which policy year the figure belongs to, labelled with that year's two dates, and where this claim's lines posted to two periods it shows one figure per period and never a sum** (`V-408`). Nothing on this screen is entered, so that is a rendering rule and its *Validation* cell stays empty (§2.2). **The period dimension is the ledger's**: `L-2` posts a cost line to the period containing its *treatment date*, so a claim whose lines straddle a policy-year boundary moved two counters and F12 shows what it did to each (`V-408`, `V-730`). **A single figure here would be the same defect S09 carried until v0.6**, on the screen a customer is most likely to quote back.
- **F13** is `{maskedAccount}`, last four digits only. **F14** is `{paidAt}` once confirmed and the expected date before that. **F15** is `{bankReference}`, from `PAY-NOTIF-002`.
- **F16** is `CLM-LETTER-001`, or `CLM-LETTER-002` on a full decline. **F17** is the contact channel and deadline of `CLM-LETTER-002`'s *right of review* section (BR-MSG-3), **present on every declined or partially declined outcome**.

**Actions**

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tải thông báo | `CUST` | F16 present | Downloads the letter PDF | `SYS-ERR-003` on failure |
| Gửi thông tin y tế bổ sung | `CUST` | ≥ 1 line declined `NOTREL`, claim not `CLOSED` | Opens S12 in response mode — §4.8 | — |
| Xem tiến trình | `CUST` | Always | Returns to S13 | — |

**How the screen composes without assembling fragments.**

§2.6 forbids building a Vietnamese sentence from parts, because Vietnamese classifiers and word order do not survive fragment assembly. The settlement screen renders more sentences than any other in the app, so the construction is stated explicitly:

| Element | Where it comes from | Is it a sentence? |
|---|---|---|
| F1, the outcome line | **One** A2 template — `CLM-NOTIF-005`, `-006` or `-008` — with `{claimNo}`, `{settlementAmount}`, `{amountClaimed}` bound | Yes. Rendered whole |
| Column headers (*Quyền lợi*, *Chi phí yêu cầu*, *Được chấp nhận*, *Đồng chi trả*, *Chi trả*) | **Labels**, owned by this document (A2 §0: *"screen labels, field names and button text — those are D2"*) | No. They are nouns, not sentences, and no sentence is built from them |
| Benefit names in F4 | The policy snapshot; the same strings A1 §3 fixes | No |
| Money in F5–F8, F11, F12 | The engine, formatted per A2 rule M-4 — grouped by three with `đ` | No |
| Each declined row's reason in F9 | **One** A2 §4 template for the applicable code — `LIMIT`, `PERIOD`, `NOBEN`, `WAIT`, `EXCL`, `NOTREL`, `NOTCOV` — with every placeholder bound | Yes. Rendered whole |
| The deduction line F10 | A2 §7.1's deduction wording with the triggering condition bound | Yes. Rendered whole |

**The rule, in one line: every sentence on this screen arrives as a complete string with named placeholders already bound; the screen positions sentences, it never composes them.** Concretely, the app never builds *"{benefitName}"* + *" không được chi trả"*. `NOTCOV` is one template — *"{itemName}: {itemAmount} — không thuộc danh mục chi phí y tế được chi trả."* — and it is rendered as one string or not at all.

**The declined-line text is claim data, not a template the app fills.** BR-LINE-2 allows the `NOTREL` and `NOTCOV` rationales to be AI-drafted and then **edited by the assessor before they are sent**, and BR-LINE-3 retains both versions. What reaches this screen is the *final* text held on the claim. The app therefore **renders it verbatim and post-processes nothing** — no truncation, no ellipsis, no re-wrapping that changes the sentence, no appending of a benefit name. The console is where the constraint that an edited message still names the item and the amount is enforced (A2 §4).

**The decline wording rule (D1 B-14) is absolute, and this is where it lands.**

| Requirement | How the screen satisfies it |
|---|---|
| A clinical decline states what is **covered**, never that a prescription was wrong | The only clinical decline codes reaching a customer are `NOTREL` and `NOTCOV`, and A2 §4's approved wording for both is a statement about cover — *"không thuộc phạm vi chi trả cho chẩn đoán {diagnosis} được điều trị trong lần khám này"*. The screen has **no other source of decline text**; there is no free-text field an assessor can route around it with |
| It is **never attributed to a model** | Nothing on this screen names IDP, the clinical assessment, a confidence score, a knowledge-base entry or an evidence reference. Those exist on the claim (D1 BR-TRACK-6, BR-KB-2) and are console-only. **The customer is told the insurer's decision, because that is what it is** — a human confirmed it |
| It names the reason and the item it applies to | A2 rule M-5, satisfied by the templates themselves, each of which binds `{itemName}` and `{itemAmount}` |
| A bound cap is explained | BR-TREE-5: `LIMIT` states the benefit and `{remainingLimit}`, and F12 shows the position after this claim. **Capping is allowed; capping silently is not** |
| A waiting-period decline shows the arithmetic | BR-WAIT-5: `WAIT` binds `{waitingDays}`, `{coverageFrom}` and `{serviceDate}` — the period, the date it counts from and the treatment date |
| There is always a route to challenge | BR-MSG-3: F17 is present on every declined or partially declined outcome. In MVP 1 the route is out of band — a named contact channel — because `DECLINED` has no inbound feature and re-opening is out of scope (S-13). **A decline without a stated route to challenge it is the most reliable way to turn a decision into a complaint** |

**One consequence of BR-LINE-4 worth stating on the screen.** Declined rows sit in the same table as paid rows, never in a collapsed section and never behind a *"xem chi tiết"*. Separating them makes the result look as though it is hiding something — which is precisely the reading a customer disputing a partial settlement is already primed for.

**Empty and error.** A claim not yet decided cannot reach S14 — the action is absent on S13. A full decline renders F1, F9, F16 and F17 and omits F5–F8, F11–F15: there is no payment, and showing zeroes where a payment would be is worse than showing nothing. Letter not yet generated: F16 shows a waiting state and the screen polls; the outcome itself is never withheld pending a PDF.

---

### 4.10 Cross-screen behaviour

#### 4.10.1 Offline tolerance

| Surface | Behaviour offline |
|---|---|
| S04, S05 | Plan and benefit master data is bundled with the release; comparison works offline. **The quote does not** — the premium comes from `imo:I-02` and is never computed locally (§4.3). *Tính phí* shows `SYS-ERR-002` |
| S06, S07 | Draft application persists locally. Submission and payment require connectivity |
| S08, S09 | Last-loaded data is shown, **marked stale with the time it was loaded**. F5's remaining limit is never shown as current when it is not |
| S11 | Draft persists locally, **including the payout account** — it is captured like any other field and verified on the console after registration, never on the device (§4.5) |
| S12 | **Full offline capture**, per §4.6. Pages queue locally and upload when connectivity returns |
| S13 | Cached list and timeline, marked stale. No action that changes state is available |
| S14 | Cached result, marked stale. The PDF is available if already downloaded |

**One rule across all of them: a stale figure is never presented as current.** Where a screen shows cached data it shows the instant it was loaded and a visible stale marker. The alternative — silently showing yesterday's remaining limit — produces a customer who claims against a limit that is gone.

#### 4.10.2 Session and token expiry

| Element | Value | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| Access token | **15 minutes** | Refreshed silently in the background; the customer never sees it expire |
| Refresh token | **30 days**, rotated on every use | Expiry returns the customer to S01 |
| Re-authentication | Device biometric or a device PIN where enrolled; OTP otherwise | Offered before falling back to a full OTP round trip |
| Inactivity | No idle timeout inside a session | An insurance app the customer opens twice a year is not a banking session; the refresh-token window is the control |

**What must not be lost.** Token expiry in the middle of a wizard **never discards typed data**. The buy flow (S06) and the claim flow (S11, S12) hold their state locally; on re-authentication the customer returns to the exact step, with the fields as they left them. **S11's F19 and F20 are the one thing not restored from local state**: they are not typed data, the app cannot establish them, and a verified name held in device memory across an ended session is a verification against nothing. They are re-read from the claim (§4.5).

**Revocation.** Revoking health-data consent (§4.2) or unlinking a member invalidates every issued token for the account. So does an administrator disabling the account.

#### 4.10.3 When a call fails mid-journey

Three classes, and they are handled differently because the risk is different.

| Class | Example | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| **A read failed** | S09's ledger read, S08's policy read | `SYS-ERR-002`. Retry available. No state changed, nothing lost, cached data shown as stale |
| **A write failed before the server saw it** | Connection refused; DNS failure; a 5xx with no body | Safe to retry with the **same `Idempotency-Key`** (D3 §1.3). The app retries automatically up to 3 times with backoff, then offers a manual retry |
| **A write may have succeeded** | Timeout after the request was sent; a dropped connection mid-upload | **Never auto-retried as a new operation.** The app re-issues the *same* idempotent request; if that is not possible it polls for the resulting object by the client-generated submission key and reconciles |

**Claim submission is the case that matters.** The submission carries a client-generated submission key from the moment the `DRAFT` is created (§4.5). A timeout on submission therefore resolves by polling for a claim carrying that key: found means submitted, and the app shows the claim at *Đã gửi* — `CLM-NOTIF-001` follows from registration, not from the app (§4.7); not found means it was not, and the app retries. **The app never creates a second claim to recover from a timeout**, because a duplicate submission is invisible to the customer (BR-DUP-4) and lands as a warning on an assessor's desk (BR-DUP-2) — a cost this app is able to avoid entirely and should.

**Unmapped errors.** Any error the app cannot map to a specific A2 message shows `SYS-ERR-004` with `{correlationId}`. This is the only customer-facing message in the catalogue carrying an internal identifier, and it does so because support cannot help without it; it is a correlation id, not a state name, so rule M-3 holds. The correlation id is the same one that spans all four systems (D3 G-5).

**And the rule that overrides all of the above:** no failure of any interface is ever rendered as an outcome on a claim (§2.10, D3 G-3). An app that shows *"hồ sơ không hợp lệ"* because an upload timed out has produced the single worst outcome this system can produce.

#### 4.10.4 Vietnamese only

| Rule | Statement |
|---|---|
| **Content** | Every string a customer reads is Vietnamese. There is **no language switch**, and the device locale does not select content — D1 NFR-10, A2 rule M-1, D2 §1.1 |
| **Formats** | `dd/mm/yyyy` for dates, `dd/mm/yyyy HH:mm` in Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh for instants, `.` as the thousands separator, `đ` as the unit — **regardless of device locale** (A2 rule M-4, §2.3). A device set to `en-US` must not render `1,200,000` |
| **Identifiers** | Policy numbers, claim numbers, card numbers, bank codes and transaction references are identifiers, not language, and appear as issued |
| **What is never shown** | Internal enum values in any language — `PENDING_INFO`, `NOTCOV`, `T1-01`, `ACTIVE`, `MISSING_FIELD`. A1 §4 and A1 §6 give the Vietnamese display text for each, and the screens above name where each is rendered |
| **Test rule** | **Any English string on a customer screen is a defect**, including a fallback string, a debug label and an untranslated error from a library. This is testable and should be tested |

The English in this document is specification, not product. A2's English column exists for the team and for the console (A2 §9); none of it ships in this app.

---

### 4.11 Validation rules

The rules §4.4, §4.5, §4.6 and §4.8 cite by identifier. **Eight identifiers are allocated out of the `V-401 … V-499` range**, which v0.2 reserved and left empty — six in v0.3, **`V-407` in v0.4** for the contact-block confirmation that decision `B4` requires, and **`V-408` in v0.6** for the counter period on §4.4's remaining-limit figures.

> **Why the range is being opened now rather than when D4 is written.** §8.3 named the gap and `D2-91` asked the dev lead to close it later, on the grounds that Part IV's rules were all inline and none was cited twice. That is no longer true: **V-116 and V-117 are Part III's rules enforced on a Part IV screen**, and the claimant block's rules are enforced on two surfaces. A rule enforced in two places and named in neither is the thing the identifier scheme exists to prevent. **`D2-91` narrows** to the rules that remain inline rather than closing.

| # | Rule | Enforced | On failure |
|---|---|---|---|
| **V-401** | **Loss type is one of the eight values the app offers**, and the four death and permanent-disability values of `enum(lossType)` are **not selectable on the mobile surface** — §4.5. The server enforces the surface restriction as well as the set, because a client that offered the other four would produce a claim whose checklist cannot be satisfied | Client and server | *(new A2 item needed — D2-25)* |
| **V-402** | **The date chain of §4.5 holds in full**, all three lines, on capture and on submission | Client and server | Per the field rows |
| **V-403** | **A narrative of the event is present where the loss type is an accident.** `ACC_OP` and `ACC_IP` only. Free text, 1,000 characters, and **it is never parsed** — it is read by an assessor and by nobody else | Client and server | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-41**)* |
| **V-404** | **The claim's contact email and contact telephone are present and well-formed**, on every claim, including one where the claimant is the insured. §3.2.10, §4.5 F15 and F16. **Restated at v0.4** (decision `B4`): in v0.3 this rule covered the claimant's email alone and the telephone was optional. **Both are now mandatory and both are properties of the claim rather than of a party** — they are the addresses every customer message about this claim is delivered to (§6.1.2a), and there is no second address anywhere in the model to fall back to | Client and server | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-42**)* |
| **V-407** | **The contact block is echoed back and confirmed before the claim is submitted.** The email and the telephone are rendered in full on the review step, as typed, and the customer confirms them. **A read-back, never a second entry box** — a customer who mistypes an address types the same thing twice, so re-entry catches nothing and reading it back catches most of it. **The confirmation is recorded on the claim with its instant**, because *the customer confirmed this address* is the whole answer to a letter that reached the wrong person. **New at v0.4** (decision `B4`, §4.5) | Client and server | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-47**)* |
| **V-405** | **A page in the other-documents group never satisfies a `REQUIRED` checklist row**, before or after classification, until classification has actually moved it into that row | Server | Reported as an unsatisfied checklist row, not as a file error |
| **V-406** | **A supplementary package carries a customer-sent date, and on the mobile surface that date is the submission date and is not settable by the client.** A client-supplied value is ignored, not trusted, not rejected — a claim must not fail because a device clock is wrong (§2.11 UI-9) | Server | — |

| **V-408** | **The remaining-limit figures render per counter period and are never summed across periods**, and the *final consumption only* qualification is on the figure rather than in a footnote — **§4.4 S09 F5, F6 and F7, and §4.9 S14 F12**. **Defined at §4.4** rather than here, because the argument for it is the ledger's and belongs beside the figures it governs; this row is the index entry. It is the mobile half of the console's **`V-730`** and **`V-731`**, which v0.5 wrote for §5.9.3 and did not carry to Part IV although its own changelog said it had | Client and server | Ledger unreachable: `SYS-ERR-002`. The period label itself cannot fail — it is derived from the snapshot's inception date |

**Two rules this part cites and does not define.** **V-116** and **V-117** are Part III's, defined at §3.8, because the claimant record is Part III's entity and the rules are properties of it rather than of this screen; §4.5 F12, F13 and F14 cite them. **V-118** is likewise Part III's and is what puts the standing document on §4.6's checklist.

### S-11 — the medical description fields, reduced

*(Register: **S-11**)*

The reference carries **three** free-text medical fields on the insured event: medical history, description of the injury, and the surgical or procedural method. All three are optional. **The app adds one, and only one: F9, the narrative of the event, mandatory on an accident claim** (V-403).

> **What is left out of the *app*, and why it is not simply thrift.** *Medical history* and *surgical method* are facts the documents already carry — `T1-03` the examination record and `T2-03` the medical report — and both are extracted. A free-text box asking a customer to restate what is on a document we are about to read produces a second version of a clinical fact, entered by a layperson, with no rule saying which version wins. **A second source of truth for a clinical fact is worse than one source and a gap.** The accident narrative is different in kind: it describes **how the event happened**, which is not on any medical document, which the assessor genuinely needs for an accident claim, and which nobody but the customer can supply.
>
> **The console takes all three, and has already taken them.** §5.7.2 **F19**, **F20** and **F21** carry the injury description, the surgical or procedural method and the history related to the diagnosis, all optional, entered by an assessor from the documents rather than by the customer, and §5.25's **S-11** row states what was left out there — they are not A4 extraction targets and are not carried into `I-15`. **The split is the point**: the customer supplies the one fact only they hold, and the assessor records the three a document supports.

## Part V — Claim web console (F41 … F59)

Nineteen features, four screen families, one claim record. **F58 and F59 are new in Framework v2.0**: F58 is specified at **§5.20**, F59 at **§3.6** — it is in Part III because that is where policy and member data enters the solution, not because of who builds it. This is the largest part of the document because the assessor's screen is the product: everything the platform computes is either shown here or is invisible, and every architectural rule in §1.3 is either enforced here or is a slogan.

**Four conventions apply to the whole of Part V and are stated once.**

| # | Convention |
|---|---|
| **V-a** | **Validation identifiers.** Part V reserves the whole `V-5nn` block — `V-500` to `V-599` — in Part VIII's catalogue. **`V-500` marks the start of the block and is not a rule**; the first identifier Part V allocates is `V-501`, and nothing cites `V-500`. Where a rule is narrow enough to read as a sentence it is written inline in the *Validation* column, per §2.2; where it is referenced from more than one screen it carries a `V-5nn` identifier, defined at the section where it first applies |
| **V-b** | **Open items.** Part V reserves `D2-51 … D2-79` in Part X. A message this part needs that A2 v1.0 does not carry is marked *(new A2 item needed — D2-nn)* at the point of use and collected at the end of the part |
| **V-c** | **Console language.** §2.6 says everything an assessor reads is Vietnamese. **A2 §8 writes the `CLM-CONSOLE-*` family in English, and A2 owns wording (§0.5).** The resolution, stated so nobody has to guess: **screen labels, field names, action labels and enum display text are Vietnamese; the `CLM-CONSOLE-*` sentences are shown exactly as A2 writes them.** NFR-10 calls the console bilingual and this is what that means in practice |
| **V-d** | **Source vocabulary.** §2.4 has no value for a fact arriving on an inbound webhook — the payment confirmation on `I-12`, the processing outcome on `I-08`. Those are recorded as **`system`**, because what the screen reads is the platform's own record of the callback, not the callback. Raised as **D2-51** so §2.4 can be extended if the distinction is wanted |

---

### 5.1 Screen inventory and the shape of the console

**Purpose.** Fix which screens exist, which feature each serves, and which claim states each is reachable in — so that no feature in F41…F59 is left without a surface and no screen is invented later without a feature.

| **S-02** | Chi tiết hồ sơ — claim detail shell, five tabs | F44–F48, F56 | `ASSESSOR` **F**/`APPROVER` **R** on the assessment tabs; `ADMIN` **C** | Any state from `SUBMITTED` |
| S-02.1 | Tab *Thông tin chung* — general | F45 | as above | Any |

| **S-03** | Hàng đợi vận hành — operator queue for stalled and failed processing — **§5.19** | F41, F53 (operational) | `ASSESSOR` **F**, `ADMIN` **R** | Always |
| **S-04** | Đối chiếu người được bảo hiểm — member disambiguation at registration | F41 | `ASSESSOR` **F** | `UNDER_ASSESSMENT` after a multi-match |
| **S-05** | Phê duyệt phương án — approval | F50 | `APPROVER` **F** | `PENDING_APPROVAL` |
| **S-06** | Chi trả — payment instruction and status | F51 | `APPROVER` **C** (A3 §4.6) | `APPROVED`, `PAYMENT_IN_PROGRESS` |
| **S-07** | Lịch sử & nhật ký — history, processing trail, audit | F53 | `ASSESSOR` **R**, `APPROVER` **R**, `ADMIN` **C** | Always |
| **S-08** | Bảng điều khiển — dashboard | F54 | all three, **R** | Always |
| **S-09** | Quản trị — administration (users, roles, threshold, document types, master data) | F55 | `ADMIN` **F**/**C** | — |
| **S-10** | Danh mục cơ sở y tế — provider master | F57 | `ADMIN` **C** (A3 §4.14) | — |
| **S-11** | Sổ theo dõi hạn mức — limit ledger lookup | F48 | `ASSESSOR` **R**, `APPROVER` **R** | Opened from S-02, one click |
| **S-12** | Tài khoản nhận tiền & người thụ hưởng — payee and payout-account master — **§5.20** | **F58** | `ASSESSOR` **F** (`ASSIGNED`), `APPROVER` **R**, `ADMIN` **F** (`MASTER`) | Opened from S-02.1 or S-04; navigation |
| **S-13** | Sổ điều khoản hợp đồng — term register administration — **§5.28** | **F65** | `TERM_AUTHOR` **F**, `TERM_APPROVE` **F**, `ASSESSOR`/`APPROVER` **R** (A3 v1.5 — **`D2-175` closed**) | — |
| **S-14** | Hàng đợi điểm kiểm điều khoản — term checkpoint queue — **§5.29** | **F67** | `ASSESSOR` **F** (`ASSIGNED`), `APPROVER` **R**. **`ADMIN` has no access** (A3 §4.11) | Opened from S-02, from §5.9.1a, or from navigation |

**F59 (group import) has no screen in this table, and that is deliberate.** Its upload, validation report and two-phase commit are an administration area on **S-09**, and they are specified at **§3.6** rather than here, so that everything about how policy and member data enters the solution sits in one place. A2's `CLM-CONSOLE-008` and `-009` — the second-administrator messages — belong to it.

**Two identifiers are allocated in v0.5, and the reasoning is the opposite of the paragraph below rather than an exception to it.** **S-13** and **S-14** are not views on an existing screen: each serves a feature of its own — **F65** and **F67** — each has its own permission set, and neither hangs off a claim. **F66 gets no identifier**, because the term evaluation service has no user and no surface; it is specified at **§5.9.7** and rendered at **§5.9.1a**, on the same reasoning §5.1 gives for F52 having no screen. **§5.1's job is to prove no feature lacks a surface**, and the one feature in this document that lacks one — **F68** — is named rather than quietly absent (§0.3, **D2-158**).

**Four surfaces added in v0.3 are not new screens, and the table is deliberately not extended.** The settlement-plan versions (**§5.21**), the correspondence history (**§5.22**) and the prior-claims list (**§5.24**) are views on **S-02**, **S-07** and **S-11** respectively; the staff notification panel (**§5.23**) is on the console shell and belongs to no claim. **No new `S-nn` identifier is allocated**, and the reason is narrow: the `S-nn` space in this table and the `S-nn` simplification codes in Framework §7.4 are already two namespaces that look alike, and every new entry in one makes a sentence in this part harder to read. **A tab is not a screen** and §5.1's job is to prove no feature lacks a surface, which none does.

**F52 (closure) has no screen of its own.** It is one action on S-05/S-06 plus a system transition; giving it a screen would imply a decision that closure does not carry — see §5.13. **F66 has none either, and for the same kind of reason** — §5.9.7.

**Why the claim detail is one screen with five tabs, and not five screens.** Reference System A arranges the same five things as a wizard, and its prototype shows the arrangement works (D1 §6.2). We keep the sequence and reject the wizard's page-per-step model for four reasons, each of which is a defect avoided rather than a preference:

- **The pinned snapshot must never leave the screen.** D1 §6.2 requires that the assessor never has to leave the claim to see what the member is covered for. A header carrying member, plan, coverage period and the benefit snapshot is rendered once by the shell and persists across tab changes.
- **The claim is one lock, not five.** On submission for approval the *entire* claim becomes read-only (D1 §3.2.5) — amounts, coverage, documents and re-extraction alike. One shell means one lock check and one banner. Five screens means five places to enforce it, and the one that is missed is the one an assessor uses.
- **Warnings are anchored where they arose, and the arguments span tabs.** A reconciliation warning attaches to a field on a document (§2.10); the decision it affects is a cost line; the amount it changes is on the settlement tab. Tabs keep one claim in one browser context, so an anchor can be followed without a reload and without losing unsaved edits.
- **The calculation is recomputed from a single working set.** Confirming a clinical recommendation re-runs the whole chain (BR-TRACK-4). If the settlement lived on a separate screen, the assessor would leave the recommendation, arrive at a total that had moved, and have nothing on the screen to explain it. That is precisely the failure mode §5.8 is written to prevent.

**What the tabs are not.** They are not a wizard: an assessor may work in any order, and nothing forces tab 3 to be complete before tab 4 is opened. The ordering constraint that does exist is in the *validation* at submission (§5.10), not in navigation — D1 §6.2's one change to the reference sequence, coverage before cost, is a recommendation to the assessor expressed as tab order, not a gate.

### 5.2 Claim registration and coverage validation (F41)

**Purpose.** Turn a customer submission into a registered claim: allocate the number, ask InsureMO whether the member was covered on the service date, and take the snapshot the rest of the claim is assessed against.

**Entered from.** J2-6 — the customer submits in the app. Registration (J2-7) is a **system step**, not a screen. The console surfaces it in three places: the new claim appears on S-01; a multi-match lands on S-04; and an infrastructure failure lands on S-03 (§5.19).

**Who may open it.** `ASSESSOR` **F**, scope `QUEUE` (A3 §2.1 F41). No approver or administrator function.

#### 5.2.1 The claim number

Per Framework §7.5, restated because the console displays, searches and prints it:

```
CLM-YY-NNNNNN          e.g. CLM-26-000417
Insured event:  CLM-26-000417/1, /2, …
```

| Rule | Behaviour on the screen |
|---|---|
| Allocated **once**, at registration, after coverage validation | A claim in `DRAFT` or `SUBMITTED` shows no number; the work list shows it only from registration onward. **A claim number is never burned on something that was never a claim** (S-09) |
| `YY` is the year of **registration**, not of the service date | A December service date registered in January carries the January year. Stated because it looks like a defect to a reader who has not read Framework §7.5 |
| **Immutable** | No screen offers an edit. A cancelled claim re-submitted receives a new number; the old one is never reused |
| Gaps tolerated | The console never asserts a contiguous sequence, and no report counts on one |
| Events are `claimNo/n` | Every event-level control in §5.7 and §5.9 labels itself with the full event number, because one claim carries many events and assessors quote them individually |

#### 5.2.2 The coverage check — three calls to `I-05`

| Order | Call | What the console does with it |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `GET /v1/members?…` — match on card number, ID number, or name + date of birth | 0 matches, 1 match or several. `422 TOO_BROAD` (>50) is impossible on an app-submitted claim, which carries the member id; it is reachable only from S-04's manual search and is shown as "hãy thu hẹp điều kiện tìm kiếm" |
| 2 | `GET /v1/members/{memberId}/coverage?asOfDate={serviceDate}` | `covered`, `reasons[]`, plan, benefit level, both periods, `premiumPaid`, payout account and its verification flag, beneficiary |
| 3 | `GET /v1/plans/{planCode}/benefits?asOfDate={serviceDate}` | The whole benefit tree, in one response, complete (D3 §I-05 property 3) |

**Calls 2 and 3 are made together and written atomically** — D3 G-1. **The payee and payout-account read is a third read, against our own records** (F58), and it joins the same atomic write: a snapshot assembled from two systems minutes apart can pin an account that has since been changed. A snapshot assembled from two reads minutes apart can straddle an administrative edit and produce a schedule that never existed.

**`covered` is computed by us, from InsureMO's facts** — decision **`B5`**, and **`D2-10` closes with it**. `I-05` returns the policy status, both periods, the member's coverage window and the level pointer; **the console runs §3.3.3's steps 5 and 6 against the snapshot** and maps a reason to a decline reason for display. The five reason codes are therefore **an internal enum rather than a contract term**, and the two inclusive boundaries at §3.3.3 property 2 are ours to guarantee — which is why §3.4's cases A to E are acceptance tests run against the sandbox and not only against the mock (C-IMO-06). **Where `I-05` returns a verdict of its own the console compares rather than replaces**, and a disagreement is an operational alert on S-03, never a silent choice (§2.10). **That branch is kept although the answer came back *facts***: the reason to compare was never doubt about today's payload, it was that a platform which starts returning a verdict in a later release must not be able to move an outcome without anybody noticing. `premiumPaid` is deliberately outside `covered` and is tested by the engine at chain step 1 (A5 §6.1) — the console shows the flag and does not act on it.

#### 5.2.3 The four outcomes

Per D1 §3.2.3. This table is the whole of F41's behaviour and the console implements it without variation.

| Outcome | Claim state | What the console does | Message |
|---|---|---|---|
| Member found, `covered = true` | proceeds to `DOC_PROCESSING` | Number allocated, snapshot taken, package submitted to IDP (`I-07`) | `CLM-NOTIF-001` to the customer |
| Member found, **not covered on the service date** | `UNDER_ASSESSMENT` | Number allocated, snapshot taken, the claim reaches an assessor with the coverage reason attached as `PERIOD`. **Not auto-declined** — dates may be wrong, or an endorsement may not have loaded | `CLM-CONSOLE-004` where the reason is a waiting period; the coverage reason is shown on S-02.1 as a flag |
| **No member matches** | `PENDING_INFO` | Number allocated. The customer is asked to check the policy number and the ID number. **Not declined and not left in limbo** | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-52**)* — console notice and the customer-facing companion |
| **Several members match** | `UNDER_ASSESSMENT` | Number allocated, **no snapshot yet**, claim routed to S-04. The platform never auto-selects | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-53**)* |

> **The snapshot is taken only when the member is unambiguous.** In the multi-match case the assessor's selection on S-04 is what triggers calls 2 and 3; taking a snapshot against a guessed member and correcting it later would leave two snapshots on one claim and no way to say which priced the settlement.

#### 5.2.4 The snapshot — what is copied, at which date, and why it is never re-read

**What is copied**, precisely (D1 §7.2, Framework §7.4 S-05 precision note):

| Group | Fields | As at |
|---|---|---|
| **Benefit schedule** | The whole tree: `code`, `parentCode`, `depth`, `name`, `annualSumInsured`, `perEventLimit`, `perDayLimit`, `maxCount`, `countUnit`, `coPaymentBp`, `deductionRatioBp`, `deductionCondition`, `waitingPeriodDays` for all six condition classes, `effectiveFrom/To`, per node | **The service date** |
| **Policy and member** *(InsureMO)* | `policyNo`, `policyStatus`, `planCode`, `benefitLevelNo`, `policyPeriod`, `coveragePeriod`, `premiumPaid`, `cardNo`, `memberId`, member name and date of birth | **Registration** — they are not effective-dated (S-05) |
| **Payee and payout account** *(Claim Platform, F58)* | `payoutAccountRef`, bank, masked account number, `accountName`, `accountNameVerified`, payee name, relationship and identity number | **Registration.** They come from **our** records, not from I-05 — §3.2.8, §3.2.9, §5.20. **This is a second read, and it is new in v0.2**: v0.1 took the whole group from one I-05 response |
| **Configuration in force** | Auto-approval threshold **and the version of it in force — `autoApprovalThresholdAsOf`, new in v0.3, V-722**; the adjudication step switches per benefit, the service-category → benefit map, the decline-reason list, and `providerMasterAsOf` (§5.17) | **Registration** |
| **Claimant** *(Claim Platform)* | Claimant name, identity number, legal capacity and family relationship — §5.4.2 F34 to F37. **New in v0.3.** They are on the claim because A3 §4.12 compares against them and BR-PAY-3 measures the verified account name against them (§5.20.5) | **Registration**, and editable on the claim thereafter with the change audited |
| **Claim contact** *(Claim Platform)* | **The contact email and contact telephone the customer typed on the claim** — §3.2.10, §4.5 F15 and F16, rendered at §5.4.2 F40 and F41. **New in v0.4** (decision `B4`). They are on the claim because **every customer message about this claim is addressed from them** (§6.1.2a), and they are captured with the claim rather than read from an account so that a later profile change cannot redirect a letter about a claim already decided | **Submission.** Editable by an assessor on an assigned claim thereafter, audited, and a change applies to correspondence from that point and not retrospectively (§5.22's F61-R11) |
| **Term register** *(Claim Platform, F65)* | **The set of `ACTIVE` term versions bound to the claim's `ruleSetRef`** — each as `termId` **plus the version identifier of that term**, and **the register's own version identifier** alongside them. **New in v0.6.** It is on the claim because §5.9.1a, §5.9.7 and §5.29.2 all render *the version evaluated* rather than the version in force today, and five fields across those two sections are marked `snapshot` with nothing in this table behind them. D1 v0.5 binds the register **at registration**, onto the snapshot, and this row is that binding | **Registration** |
| **Policy attributes read once** *(InsureMO)* | **Renewal status, the continuous-cover start and the policy's rule-set reference** — §5.4.2 F38 and F39, §3.2.7, §3.2.5. **Confirmed available at v0.4** (`B1`, `B2`); the vendor conditions `D2-129` and `D2-130` are closed. **Frozen like everything else, and this is the one row where the freeze has an exception**: the renewal status may be re-read on a bounded, logged, calculation-invalidating control — **§5.4.5**, decision `A1`. The re-read does not overwrite the snapshot silently; it writes a new value beside the old one and marks the calculation stale | **Registration**, and re-readable under §5.4.5 |

**The term register binds at registration, and v0.5 said two different things about when.** §5.4.2 **F39** pinned `ruleSetRef` at registration; §5.9.7 requirement 4 and §5.28.5 both said *at submission*. **D1 v0.5 settles it at registration** and every statement in this document now reads the same way: the rule-set reference, the set of `ACTIVE` term versions and the register's own version identifier are all written onto the snapshot **at registration**, and a term authored, corrected or withdrawn afterwards does not disturb the claim (BR-TERM-4). **`V-737`'s back-dating check inherits the same instant** — *the earliest open claim bound to that rule set* is measured against the registration of that claim, which is the moment the claim acquired the register. The two instants are one step apart on the app route and further apart on the counter route, and one step apart is enough: a claim registered on Monday and submitted on Wednesday would otherwise be evaluated against a Wednesday register while its rule-set reference named a Monday one.

**Two resolutions happen at snapshot time, not at calculation time.** `coPaymentBp: "INHERIT"` is resolved to the nearest ancestor's integer rate and the resolved integer is written onto the claim; an `"INHERIT"` reaching the root without an integer is a schedule error and fails at the adapter (D3 §I-05 property 4). And a `waitingPeriodDays` entry of `null` is written as `null` and means *the combination cannot arise* — a claim that later produces one is a data error, never a zero-day wait (A1 §4, BR-WAIT-4).

**Why it is never re-read.** Four reasons, and each is a defect avoided:

1. **The settlement must be reproducible.** BR-TRACK-4 re-runs the entire chain when a clinical recommendation is confirmed. If the chain read live data, the second run could differ from the first on the same inputs.
2. **A claim in an approver's queue must not change under them.** This is the same hazard AR-3 removes on the extraction side, applied to policy data.
3. **An administrative edit — a corrected coverage date, a re-imported group file — must not re-price a claim already assessed.** Re-import end-dates members rather than deleting them (BR-IMP-4) precisely so past claims stay assessable; re-reading would defeat that.
4. **A settlement must be explainable six months later.** The schedule that produced it is on the claim, not in a table that has since moved. The same reasoning as BR-KB-4 for the knowledge base.

**A consequence, stated because assessors will meet it:** where policy data is genuinely wrong, correcting it in InsureMO does **not** change the claim. The claim must be cancelled and re-submitted (A3 §2.1, before `PENDING_APPROVAL`), which allocates a new number. There is no re-snapshot action, and adding one would reintroduce every hazard above.

#### 5.2.5 Field table — S-04 member disambiguation

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Số hồ sơ | `text(20)` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F2 | Họ tên người được bảo hiểm (khai báo) | `text(200)` | `user` | M | — | — |
| F3 | Ngày sinh | `date` | `user` | O | — | — |
| F4 | Số giấy tờ tùy thân | `text(20)` | `user` | O | — | — |
| F5 | Số thẻ bảo hiểm | `text(20)` | `user` | O | — | — |
| F6 | Kết quả tìm kiếm | `lookup(member)` | `imo:I-05` | M | At least one search parameter; **V-501** more than 50 results is refused, not truncated — a truncated list silently hides the right member (D3 §I-05) | inline: "hãy thu hẹp điều kiện tìm kiếm". No match at all: *(new A2 item — **D2-52**)* |
| F7 | Người được bảo hiểm được chọn | `lookup(member)` | `user` | M | Exactly one. Selecting triggers calls 2 and 3 and takes the snapshot | *(new A2 item — **D2-53**)* |
| F8 | Ngày điều trị (ngày lấy bản ghi nhận) | `date` | `user` | M | — | — |
| F9 | Lý do chọn | `text(200)` | `user` | M | Recorded on the claim and in the trail (BR-AUDIT-2) | *(new A2 item — **D2-53**)* |
| **F10** | **Số hợp đồng** | `text(20)` | `user` | O | **Exact match.** §3.3.1's narrowing key — the one an assessor reliably holds | inline |
| **F11** | **Mã sản phẩm** | `text(16)` | `user` | O | **Exact match.** §3.3.1 | inline |

**Notes on the fields above**, so that nothing descriptive sits in a *Validation* cell with no error path (§2.2). **F1 to F5 are read-only here**: F1 is the number allocated at registration, and F2 to F5 are the identifiers exactly as the customer submitted them. F3, F4 and F5 are used as **exact-match search parameters** against date of birth, identity document number and card number. **F8 is the `asOfDate` carried into calls 2 and 3**, displayed so the assessor can see which date the schedule will be read at. Widths follow §2.9: claim number `text(20)`, person's name `text(200)`, card and identity numbers `text(20)`.

**F10 and F11 are the only editable search parameters on this screen.** §3.3.1 adds two keys to I-05's member search — policy number and product code — and `G-B-08` records why: an assessor searching a common Vietnamese given name reaches V-501's fifty-hit refusal and has **no way to narrow it**, because F2 to F5 are what the customer submitted and are read-only. **The policy number is on almost every document the customer sent**, and typing it turns a refused search into a single hit. Neither is mandatory and neither changes V-501: the refusal rule is unchanged, and the keys reduce how often it is reached.

> **F12 was *Đơn vị cấp đơn* in v0.3 and it is removed at v0.4.** **MVP 1 has exactly one organisational unit** — decision `B3`, a client scope decision — so the parameter narrowed nothing and the column would have rendered the same value on all fifty rows of the grid it was added to help an assessor read. **A column that discriminates nothing on the one screen where a reader is matching a name under time pressure is worse than an absent column**, because it teaches them it discriminates. §3.3.1 removes the parameter; this removes the field and the grid column; **`D2-12` closes as withdrawn**, and it returns with the second unit rather than before it.

**F6's result grid carries §3.3.1's columns**, one row per **insured member × policy pair** — `memberId`, `fullName`, `dateOfBirth`, `cardNo`, `policyNo`, `policyType`, `policyStatus`, `productCode`, `planCode`, `benefitLevelNo`, `coveragePeriod`, `continuousCoverFrom`, `renewalStatus`, and — **new at v0.4, decision `B6`** — **`customerCode`** and **`distributionChannel`**. **`agent` and `customerGroup` are available from `I-05` and are deliberately not rendered**: we have no CRM and no agent model, so both would be identifiers that resolve to nothing in this system, and §3.3.1's note is where the reasoning lives so that it is argued once rather than at every grid. **A member on two policies is two rows, not one**, which is exactly the disambiguation this screen exists to perform. Grid behaviour is §2.11.3's and V-711's: **the default sort is `fullName` ascending then `policyNo` ascending** — the one grid in Part V that does not sort by recency, because the reader is matching a name rather than triaging a queue — and `fullName`, `policyNo` and `cardNo` are never truncated (§2.11 UI-19).

**Actions — S-04**

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Chọn người được bảo hiểm** | `ASSESSOR` | Exactly one row selected, F9 completed, no conflict of interest | Snapshot taken (calls 2 and 3, atomic); claim proceeds to `DOC_PROCESSING`; package submitted on `I-07` | Success: none. Failure: `CLM-CONSOLE-007` on `422 NO_SCHEDULE_AT_DATE` |
| **Yêu cầu bổ sung** | `ASSESSOR` | No acceptable match | Claim → `PENDING_INFO`, information request raised | `DOC-NOTIF-001` |
| **Hủy hồ sơ** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER` | State before `PENDING_APPROVAL`; reason mandatory | Claim → `CANCELLED` | `CLM-NOTIF-009`; reason missing → *(new A2 item — **D2-66**)* |
| **Khai báo mối quan hệ** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER` | Always available | Declaration recorded; claim returned to the queue | `CLM-CONSOLE-012` |

#### 5.2.6 Rules

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| **V-502** | **The conflict-of-interest check runs at registration and again at assignment.** An ID-number match between the acting user and the insured, claimant or beneficiary blocks every claim action and returns the claim to the queue — `CLM-CONSOLE-011`, A3 §4.12. Any other relationship is the user's to declare — `CLM-CONSOLE-012` |
| **V-503** | **Duplicate detection runs at registration** (BR-DUP-1): same insured member, same provider, overlapping treatment dates, on any non-cancelled claim. A match raises a warning naming the other claim number; a matching extracted invoice number is flagged as the stronger signal (BR-DUP-3). **It never blocks, and the customer is never told** (BR-DUP-2, BR-DUP-4) — *(new A2 item needed — **D2-55**)*. **Extended in v0.3 — a matching occurrence date (§5.7.2 F16) is a third signal**, and it is the one that catches the case the provider key cannot: **one accident treated at two different hospitals produces two claims that today match on nothing**, because the key is locked to the provider. Same member and same occurrence date is a duplicate signal on its own, ranked below a matching invoice number and above overlapping treatment dates alone (**S-08**) |
| **V-504** | The **complete-and-valid-file timestamp** is recorded when the document set first reaches `COMPLETE` and is displayed on S-02.1. **Nothing measures against it** in MVP 1 — S-19. It is captured because it cannot be reconstructed later (D1 §8.1) |
| **V-505** | Registration posts `I-06` to InsureMO **fire-and-forget**. Its failure raises an operational alert and blocks nothing (D3 §I-06) |

#### 5.2.7 Empty and error

| Condition | What the console shows |
|---|---|
| `I-05` returns `404` on member, policy or plan | Treated as *no member matches* — the `PENDING_INFO` path, never a decline |
| `I-05` returns `422 NO_SCHEDULE_AT_DATE`, `422 NO_BENEFIT_LEVEL_AT_DATE`, or a `covered: true` answer with a **null `planCode`** (§3.4 Case D) | **`CLM-CONSOLE-007` — "Escalate, do not proceed."** No snapshot is written, the claim is held on S-03 (§5.19), and no assessment action is offered. A claim assessed against the wrong schedule is worse than a claim that waits |
| `I-05` unavailable — `503`, timeout, circuit open (G-6) | Registration is retried on the standard backoff (D3 §1.3). The claim holds in `SUBMITTED` and appears on S-03 (§5.19) with the elapsed time. **Never `DECLINED`** — G-3. **No claim can be registered while InsureMO is unreachable**, and §6.4.2 says what that means for the whole console |
| The adapter refuses the benefit tree — **V-111 … V-115** (§3.8) | The tree is structurally wrong: a cycle, a limit amount that does not match its type, an unresolvable `INHERIT`, a missing deduction condition, overlapping effective windows. **No snapshot is written**, the claim holds on S-03, and the alert names the plan, the node and the rule. **This path is new in v0.2** — v0.1 refused these at the keystroke on a screen we owned, and there is no such screen now (§3.1) |
| `I-07` refuses the package — `422 PACKAGE_TOO_LARGE`, unfetchable URI, hash mismatch | Claim holds, operator queue on S-03 (§5.19), the specific document named. The customer sees a progress message, not a failure — `SYS-ERR-001`, rule M-6 |

### 5.3 Work list (F42) and assignment (F43)

**Purpose.** Find a claim, see what is waiting and how long it has been waiting, and take or give out work.

**Entered from.** Login, and from S-08's tiles. It is the console's home screen.

**Who may open it.** `ASSESSOR` **F** and `APPROVER` **F** over `QUEUE`; `ADMIN` **R** over `ALL_CLAIMS` with clinical fields redacted and the read logged (A3 §4.11). Scope is applied as a **predicate at the query layer** — a claim outside scope is never loaded, so it cannot leak through a count or an error message (A3 §6).

#### 5.3.1 Search and filter — field table

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Tìm kiếm nhanh | `text(40)` | `user` | O | — | — |
| F2 | Trạng thái | `enum(claimState)` multi | `user` | O | — | — |
| F3 | Loại hình tổn thất | `enum(lossType)` multi | `user` | O | — | — |
| F4 | Cán bộ xử lý | `lookup(user)` | `user` | O | — | — |
| F5 | Nhóm quá hạn | `enum(ageingBucket)` | `user` | O | — | — |
| **F6a** | **Loại ngày lọc** | `enum(dateFilterType)` | `user` | O | Defaults to *Ngày gửi*. Selects **which** date F6's range is applied to | — |
| F6 | Khoảng ngày — từ / đến | `date` | `user` | O | `from ≤ to`; `to ≤ today`. Applied to the date named by **F6a** | `CLM-VAL-001` |
| F7 | Cơ sở y tế | `lookup(provider)` | `master` | O | — | — |
| F8 | Số tiền yêu cầu từ / đến | `money` | `user` | O | Integer dong, `from ≤ to` | `CLM-VAL-004` |
| F9 | Số hợp đồng | `text(20)` | `user` | O | — | — |
| F10 | Cờ đánh dấu | `enum(flag)` multi | `system` | O | — | — |
| F11 | Chỉ hồ sơ chưa giao | `bool` | `user` | O | — | — |

**Notes on the fields above.** None of F1 to F5, F7, F9, F10 or F11 carries a validation, because a filter that matches nothing is an empty result and not an error — what each accepts is stated here rather than in a *Validation* cell with no error path (§2.2).

- **F1** matches `claimNo`, `cardNo`, `policyNo` and the identity document number **exactly**, and the member name as a diacritic-insensitive contains-match.
- **F2** offers A1 §5.1's thirteen states. The default is the six live states, excluding `PAID`, `CLOSED`, `CANCELLED` and `DECLINED`.
- **F3** offers the **twelve** values of `lossType` (A1 §4.2, and §4.5 for the set as this document renders it) — the eight the app can produce and the four that reach the console only through counter intake. It filters on the claim's F7 (§5.4.1), which is the same value the checklist is keyed on, so a filtered list and a claim's checklist can never be reasoning from two different answers.
- **F4** offers `Của tôi` · `Chưa giao` · a named user · `Tất cả`, and `Của tôi` is the default landing filter. **F11** is shorthand for F4 = `Chưa giao`.
- **F5** offers `TRONG_HẠN` · `ĐẾN_HẠN` · `QUÁ_HẠN`, defined in §5.3.2.
- **F6a** offers **`NGÀY_GỬI` · `NGÀY_DUYỆT` · `NGÀY_CHI_TRẢ` · `NGÀY_ĐÓNG_HỒ_SƠ`** — the four dates the console records at claim level and can therefore filter on. The set is named here and **belongs in A1 §4** — raised as **D2-124**, per §2.3. A claim that has not reached the selected milestone is **excluded, not shown with a blank date**: filtering on *ngày chi trả* returns claims that were paid, which is the question being asked.
- **F7** lists the provider master (F57). **F9** matches exactly.
- **F10**'s set is `TRÙNG_HỒ_SƠ` (duplicate) · `ĐỘ_TIN_CẬY_THẤP` · `CÓ_KHUYẾN_NGHỊ` (recommendations outstanding) · `ĐÁNH_GIÁ_LÂM_SÀNG_LỖI` · `NGOÀI_PHẠM_VI` (a coverage reason attached) · `CƠ_SỞ_Y_TẾ_CHƯA_CÓ_TRONG_DANH_MỤC` · `TÀI_KHOẢN_CHƯA_XÁC_THỰC`.

> **X-3 closed, and it is worth naming why it was a defect rather than an omission.** The prototype has drawn a *Loại ngày lọc* selector since 23 August 2026 and this table carried only *Ngày gửi từ / đến*. The prototype is what the business confirms requirements against; this document is what a developer builds from. Two documents disagreeing about a control on the console's home screen guarantees that one of them is wrong, and the register raised it as **X-3** for exactly that reason. **The prototype was right and this table is now made to match it** — including its four values rather than the reference's five, because *ngày giao việc* and *ngày chấp thuận* are milestones our lifecycle does not carry separately (S-48, B-26, **G-V-11**).

**Why this is not cosmetic.** Without it, *"what did we approve last week"* and *"how much did we pay out in March"* have no answer on any screen in this document — the ageing clock measures from submission and every filter hangs off it. Both questions are asked of a claims operation in its first month.

**V-506 — the quick search is never parsed for meaning.** No screen in Part V infers a year, a branch or a sequence from a claim number, and no filter is built on a substring of one (Framework §7.5). It is a search key, not a data structure.

**F10 is not decoration.** Each flag corresponds to something that will otherwise be discovered late: the unmatched-provider flag is how an unloaded provider master becomes visible before it applies a 20% deduction to every outpatient and dental claim (Framework §7.1 note on F57), and the clinical-failure flag is how `CLM-CONSOLE-015` reaches an assessor who did not open the claim.

#### 5.3.2 The list, and the ageing clock

| Column | Source | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Số hồ sơ | `system` | Links to S-02 |
| Người được bảo hiểm | `snapshot` | Redacted to initials for `ADMIN` |
| Loại hình tổn thất | `user` | §5.4.1 F7's value, rendered as its Vietnamese label from A1 §4.2 |
| Trạng thái | `system` | Vietnamese label from A1 §5.1 |
| Ngày gửi | `system` | `dd/mm/yyyy HH:mm`, `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh` |
| **Số ngày xử lý** | `system` | `derived` — elapsed since submission, on the internal clock |
| Nhóm quá hạn | `system` | `derived` — the bucket, from the elapsed time and the configured target |
| Số tiền yêu cầu | `snapshot` | |
| Số tiền dự kiến chi trả | `system` | `derived` — the current calculated payable; blank before the first chain run |
| Cán bộ xử lý | `system` | |
| Cờ | `system` | F10's flags as icons, each with its A2 message on hover |

**The clock is internal and it measures from submission.** D1 B-04 and D1 §8.1: MVP 1 tracks **one** clock, the internal SLA, measured from the customer's submission because that is what the customer experiences and what SC-04 targets.

**The statutory clock is not tracked.** The Law on Insurance Business sets 15 days from receipt of a complete and valid file. **MVP 1 does not run that clock and does not flag a claim approaching it** — declared simplification S-19, valid only under BC-2. The complete-and-valid-file timestamp is displayed on S-02.1 and on this list as a column available but not filtered on; **no bucket, no counter and no dashboard tile in this document measures against it**, and that is deliberate rather than an omission.

| Bucket | Default | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `TRONG_HẠN` | Elapsed ≤ 1 working day | `config` |
| `ĐẾN_HẠN` | 1 – 2 working days | `config` |
| `QUÁ_HẠN` | > 2 working days | `config` |

**V-711 — sorting and table behaviour, specified once for every list in Part V.** §5.3.2's table names the columns; it said nothing about how the list behaves, and a developer given a column list and no ordering will pick one. The register's **B-27** is the reference's fifteen-convention table reduced to the six that change what a user can do rather than what they see:

| # | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| 1 | **Clicking a column header sorts** ascending, then descending, then back to the default. The active sort is shown on the header, never only in the URL |
| 2 | **The default sort is *Số ngày xử lý* descending** — the oldest claim first. It is not the claim number and not the submission date: in a one-queue model (S-11) the sort order *is* the prioritisation, and the only thing this document measures is age |
| 3 | **The column header row stays fixed while the body scrolls**, on every list in Part V including §5.19's operator queue |
| 4 | **A value too long for its column is truncated with an ellipsis and carries the full value on hover.** It is never wrapped to a second line — a table whose rows have different heights cannot be scanned, and scanning is what a work list is for |
| 5 | **Double-clicking a row opens it**, equivalently to the row's primary link. Stated because it is the interaction assessors coming from Reference System A will try first |
| 6 | **Sorting and paging are server-side and scope-filtered as a predicate** (A3 §6). A sort that reorders only the loaded page silently lies about which claim is oldest |

**V-712 — a selection survives a change of filter.** Rows ticked for *Giao việc hàng loạt* or *Nhận xử lý hàng loạt* stay ticked when the filter is re-applied, and the count of selected rows is shown beside the action with a control to clear it. §5.3.3 permits up to 50 rows in one bulk action; a selection that silently empties on every filter change makes 50 unreachable in practice. **Reduced from B-25**: the reference's two-tier filter — a collapsed bar whose hidden criteria stay in force — is **not** adopted. A criterion that is applied but not visible is how a user concludes the list is broken, and §5.3.4 already requires the filter to be shown beside an empty result.

Two behaviours of the clock that no source settles and that are therefore specified here as the console's own, and flagged as **D2-54**: the clock **runs continuously from submission and is not paused while the claim is in `PENDING_INFO`**, because the customer's experience does not pause either; and the list additionally shows **time in the current state**, so an assessor can tell a claim that is old from one that is stuck. If the business wants the statutory posture — a clock that stops while the file is incomplete — that is a change to this section and to §5.15, not to the data model.

#### 5.3.3 Actions

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Nhận xử lý** (assign to me) | `ASSESSOR` | Claim **unassigned** and in the user's queue; no ID-number conflict (A3 §4.12) | `assignee` = the user; trail entry | Blocked by conflict: `CLM-CONSOLE-011` |
| **Trả về hàng đợi** (release) | `ASSESSOR` | Claim assigned to the user; state before `PENDING_APPROVAL` | `assignee` cleared; trail entry with the reason where a relationship was declared | `CLM-CONSOLE-012` where released after a declaration |
| **Giao việc** (assign / reassign to another user) | `APPROVER` | Target user holds `ASSESSOR`; no ID-number conflict for the target | `assignee` = target; trail entry naming both users | Conflict on the target: `CLM-CONSOLE-011` |
| **Giao việc hàng loạt** (bulk assign) | `APPROVER` | 1–50 rows selected, all in `QUEUE`, one target user | As above, per claim, atomically per claim and reported per claim | Partial outcomes are listed row by row; a conflict on one row does not stop the others |
| **Nhận xử lý hàng loạt** | `ASSESSOR` | 1–50 **unassigned** rows | Self-assignment, per A3 §4.2 | as above |
| **Mở hồ sơ** | all three | Scope | Opens S-02. For `ADMIN`, opens redacted and **logs the read** (BR-AUDIT-4) | — |
| **Xuất danh sách** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER` | ≤ 5,000 rows | CSV of the visible columns, scope-filtered, no clinical fields | — |

**V-713 — who may appear in an assignee list.** *Giao việc*, *Giao việc hàng loạt* and §5.19.3's *Giao lại* offer **active users holding `ASSESSOR`**, and no one else: a user whose F5 is `NGỪNG_HOẠT_ĐỘNG` is absent from the list rather than present and failing on save, and a user who holds only `APPROVER` is absent because giving assessment work to an approver defeats §5.11.3's segregation before the claim is ever submitted. The conflict-of-interest check (A3 §4.12) is then run against the chosen target, not used as the filter — a name absent for a reason the approver cannot see is worse than a name that is refused with `CLM-CONSOLE-011`.

**Reduced from B-30**: **automatic assignment at registration is not adopted, and decision `B3` makes that firmer rather than softer.** The reference allocates a claim to an assessor by a configurable rule the moment the claim is created, filtered by organisational unit and business group. We have neither — S-11 declares one queue and no unit hierarchy, and A3's data-scope model has no unit dimension (**B-40**, declared) — and **`B3` settles that MVP 1 has exactly one organisational unit**, so the filter the reference's rule is built around has one value to choose from as well as one queue. An auto-allocation rule with one queue and one group to choose from is a rule that always returns the same answer, and building it would create the appearance of an allocation model that A3 does not support. **What is adopted is the eligibility filter**, which is the half that prevents a real error.

**A3 §4.2 is the rule that shapes this screen.** An assessor may take an unassigned claim and may give one back; **reassigning to another user requires an approver**. The reason is stated in A3 and worth keeping visible in the UI's shape: self-assignment prevents quiet cherry-picking only if the alternative — moving work onto someone else — sits with a different role. So the assessor's bulk control is *take*, and the approver's is *give*.

**One queue, and what that costs.** There is no unit hierarchy and no work-allocation engine (S-11, D1 §2.2). Every claim is in one queue and F4's `Chưa giao` filter is the whole of the allocation model. This is the first simplification to reverse when a second branch appears, and it changes both A3's data-scope model and this screen.

#### 5.3.4 Empty and error

| Condition | What the console shows |
|---|---|
| No claims match the filter | "Không có hồ sơ phù hợp với điều kiện lọc." — and the filter itself, so the user can see what excluded them. **Never an empty page with no explanation** |
| A claim is outside scope | It does not appear, and no count includes it (A3 §6) |
| The claim service is unavailable | `SYS-ERR-004` with the correlation id. The list is not partially rendered from a cache — a stale work list is worse than an absent one |

### 5.4 Claim detail — General tab (F45)

**Purpose.** Show, in one place and without a navigation, who the claim is for, what they hold and what they are covered for — so the assessor never leaves the claim to answer a coverage question.

**Entered from.** S-01, S-08, a notification, or a direct link to `claimNo`. It is the default tab of S-02.

**Who may open it.** `ASSESSOR` **R** and `APPROVER` **R** (A3 §2.1 F45 — note both are *read*: nothing on this tab is an assessment); `ADMIN` **C** under A3 §4.11, with clinical detail redacted and the read logged.

> **The single most important statement about this screen: every business value on it is `snapshot`, and none of it is re-read.** The claim carries its own copy of the policy, the member and the benefit schedule, taken once at registration from one consistent read (D3 G-1, D1 §7.2). What is shown here is that copy. A change made in InsureMO after registration — a corrected coverage date, a re-imported group file, a new plan version — **does not appear here and does not affect this claim**. **That guarantee is worth more in v0.2 than it was in v0.1**, because the change is now made in a system we do not control, produces no event we receive and leaves no entry in our audit log (§3.5). §5.2.4 states why, and the tab carries a one-line note saying so, because an assessor who assumes the screen is live will eventually make a decision on that assumption.

The only values on this tab that are **not** `snapshot` are: the workflow fields (`system`), the remaining-limit figures in the benefit panel (`system` — read from the ledger, which is live by design), the assessor's own entries, and the provider's network status (`master`, pinned by `providerMasterAsOf` — §5.17).
