**On F31, and why its *Validation* column is now empty.** F31 is **derived, not validated**: it is set when the claim is first assigned and **re-set on every reassignment**, so that it measures the age of the current person's ownership rather than the age of the claim. That is a derivation rule and it belongs in this note, not in a *Validation* cell — **a platform-written date has no way to fail in front of a person, and §2.2 does not allow a rule with no way to report it firing to sit in that column.** The rule is unchanged; only where it is written has moved. *(This is one of the four rows §10.4 names — v0.6.)*

**On the numbering, once, because it recurs through this reissue.** **F31 onward continues past §5.4.2's block rather than inserting at F12.** S-02 is one screen and its field identifiers are unique across both tables (§2.2); inserting in place would renumber every field §5.4.2, §5.11, §5.12 and Part IX cite. **The number is an identifier, not a position** — where a field renders is stated in the row, and F31 to F33 render **above** F1, at the head of the claim.

**Notes on the fields above.** F1 to F6 are written by the platform and are read-only on every screen in Part V, so none of them carries a validation. F1 is immutable (Framework §7.5) and is held at `text(20)` per §2.9. F2 renders A1 §5.1's Vietnamese label and **never the identifier** in anything a customer can see. F4 changes only through §5.3.3's assignment actions. F5 is the elapsed time since F3 on the internal clock (§5.3.2). F6 is recorded once, is immutable, and is **displayed but not measured against** — declared simplification S-19.

**On F7, and where `episodeType` went, because it did not go anywhere.** F7 was `enum(episodeType)` until this pass and is now `enum(lossType)`, which is **`D2-44` closed on the console side**. **`lossType` subsumes `episodeType`; it does not replace it** (A1 §4.2). The claim carries one loss type — the one the app captured at §4.5 F3, or the one an officer keyed on the counter route — and it is the checklist's key and nothing else's. **The five-value `episodeType` survives, valued, as a projection**, held on the insured event at **§5.7.2 F5**, because that is where A5 §8.1's benefit mapping runs and A5 keys on the five values unchanged. **Nothing in A5 or D1 moves for this, and that is the whole reason the change was affordable**: the set that three documents read is still there and still carries the same five values, it is simply no longer the thing anybody types. A1 §4.2 names the condition on which it finally retires — **when the checklist becomes per-loss-type per event, which is Framework S-38** — and that is not this reissue.

**V-714 — the claim carries an alert strip, and it carries the last reason verbatim.** Two rows, one rule, because they occupy the same region and answer the same question: *what should I know about this claim before I start*.

| # | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| 1 | **F32 renders every raised flag as a line, not an icon.** F9 is the same set of flags §5.3.1 F10 shows on the list. On the list an icon with a tooltip is right — the list is scanned. On the claim it is wrong: the assessor has arrived to work and the flag is the reason they should not start at the top |
| 2 | **Order is severity, not the order they were raised**: coverage or waiting-period failure first, then a bound limit, then a duplicate, then extraction and clinical warnings. The order is fixed here so that two claims do not present the same three facts differently |
| 3 | **F33 carries the reason text as it was typed**, never a summary and never a code. A returned claim's reason is the single most useful sentence on the screen and today it is reachable only by opening the trail and reading past the field-level entries |
| 4 | **Neither field is a control.** Nothing on the strip can be dismissed, acknowledged or hidden from this screen. Acknowledgement of a reconciliation warning is V-524's, on §5.6, where the warning is anchored |

**Reduced from S-04 and B-32, and the omission is the watch list.** The reference's alert strip also carries a **customer watch-list** alert with its own record, its own resolution state and a re-check on every save. We have no watch list, no rule that populates one and no record to resolve — **S-15 and S-21 declare it** (register rows **B-12**, **S-49**), and F9's flag set is the place it would attach if it is ever built. Adding the strip without the list is the whole of the value; adding the list is a feature, not a presentation change.

**Reduced from S-06, and the omission is two of the three timestamps.** The reference shows three dates side by side at the head of the claim: the date the insurance request was received, the assignment date and the file-open date. **Only the assignment date is added (F31).** The *request-received* date is register row **B-06** — an intake field, and the intake screens were not in the Part V pass — and the *file-open* date is F3's instant under a second name, which is how a reader concludes the two differ. F31 is the one of the three that exists today only inside the trail, and the one an assessor is asked about. **The second pass collected B-06's field**: §4.5 **F22** writes `requestReceivedDate` on the app route and §7.2's counter row has it entered rather than defaulted, so the value exists and adding it here is now a display decision rather than a data one.

**Notes on the fields above.** Everything the table leaves blank is blank because the value is copied, not entered — the *Validation* column is not a place to put a description (§2.2).

- **F12 and F16** are redacted to initials for `ADMIN` (A3 §4.11). Both are held at `text(200)` per §2.9, which is the width §3.2.7 requires of the register; a narrower snapshot would truncate a long Vietnamese name at the one moment nobody is watching.
- **F15** is `memberId` — the primary key for the limit ledger and for duplicate detection (D1 §7.4).
- **F18** is the policy status **as at registration**. **F19** is one of `HC-STD` · `HC-PLS` · `HC-PRM`.
- **F20** is `benefitLevelNo`, which plan-on-policy this member points at, and is **never labelled "cấp"** (A1 §8).
- **F21** renders `policyPeriod` and **F22** renders `coveragePeriod`. **F22 is the period the date chain is tested against**, not F21 (D1 §3.2.1).
- **F23** is `premiumPaid`. It is displayed here and **tested by the engine at chain step 1, not by this screen**.
- **F24** is `covered` plus `reasons[]` from `I-05` as at registration. Where `covered` is `false` the reasons are shown in full — they are the input to the `PERIOD` decline.
- **F25** shows the last four digits of the payout account only. **F26 is never typed**: it is populated solely by the verification call (BR-PAY-1).
- **F28** defaults to the insured and may be a distinct party (A1 §5).
- **F29** is the provider the customer declared, corrected on S-02.4 from the extracted value.
- **F34 to F37 are the claimant**, and §5.20.1's assertion that *three parties are modelled separately* becomes true at this row rather than at the next revision. **F36 and F37 are two dimensions, not one, and collapsing them is the defect the reference avoids**: F36 answers *on what legal footing is this person asking for the money* and F37 answers *who are they to the patient*. A father claiming for his child is `NGƯỜI_GIÁM_HỘ` × `CON`; an adult son claiming for a deceased parent is `NGƯỜI_THỪA_KẾ` × `BỐ`; an employer's HR administrator holding a mandate is `NGƯỜI_ĐƯỢC_UỶ_QUYỀN` × `KHÁC`. One enum cannot express any of the three without either losing the standing or inventing a relationship value that is not a relationship. **A1 owns both sets** and neither may be defined here (§2.3) — **D2-124**.
- **F38** is displayed and is **not** re-read. The reference places a *fetch the latest value* button beside its equivalent, deliberately declining to freeze it; we do not, because P-02 freezes everything the settlement is reproducible from and a value that can change under an open claim would have to be recorded at the moment the chain read it. **What that costs is stated at §5.25** and the vendor question is **D2-129**.
- **F39** exists so that a decline can cite the wording the customer is actually holding. **It is not a rule input** — no step of the chain reads it, and A5 owns every benefit term. It is quoted, and quoting the wrong version of a wording is a complaint we can answer; quoting nothing is one we cannot.

Rendered as the tree, not a flat list, because the tree is what the engine walks (BR-TREE-1) and a flat list hides the ancestor path a cap comes from.

| Column | Type | Source | Note |

**Actions**

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |

| **Xem sổ hạn mức** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER` | Snapshot present | Opens S-11 for this member: every benefit with sum insured, count limit, total paid, days paid, remaining amount and remaining days. **One click from the claim, never a separate screen to navigate to** (D1 §6.2) | — |
| **Xem lịch sử bồi thường của người được bảo hiểm** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER` | Snapshot present | Opens **§5.24** — every prior claim of this member, its events, its provider, its diagnosis, what was paid and where it ended. **The read is logged** (BR-AUDIT-4) | — |

**V-725 — the cancellation reason is a catalogue value and not only free text.** Register row **S-38**, applied in a reduced form. v0.2 required *a* reason and accepted any sentence, so *"how many claims were cancelled because the customer withdrew"* is a question this system cannot answer without someone reading every cancellation. The set is small — customer withdrew, opened in error, duplicate of another claim, other — and **A1 owns it (D2-124)**; the free-text box appears only on *other* and remains at `textarea(2000)` per §2.9. **What is omitted is the reference's second half**: they additionally refuse a cancellation on a claim that already carries cost lines, payment lines or an approved reserve. **We keep the state-based block we have** — cancellation is impossible from `PENDING_APPROVAL` onward, which is the point past which anything has been committed — because refusing earlier would strand a claim opened in error the moment its extraction returned, and there is no re-open (S-13) to rescue it with.

#### 5.4.4 Empty and error

| Condition | What the console shows |
|---|---|
| No snapshot yet (multi-match pending) | The tab renders workflow fields only and states that the snapshot is taken when the member is selected. **No benefit panel is drawn from a live read as a stand-in** — that would be the one thing this screen must never do |
| `ADMIN` opened the claim | Clinical fields — diagnosis, ICD-10, condition class, cost-line item names, document images — are **absent, not blurred**, and the access is logged (A3 §4.11, BR-AUDIT-4) |
| The ledger is unavailable | The benefit panel renders from the snapshot with the consumption columns showing "chưa đọc được" and a retry. The snapshot columns are never blanked because the ledger failed — they are different data with different owners |

### 5.5 Claim detail — Documents tab (F44)

**Purpose.** Show what the claim needs, what arrived, what was asked for and what came back — and give the assessor the two decisions this screen owns: raise an information request, or waive an expected item.

**Entered from.** S-02, tab 2.

**Who may open it.** `ASSESSOR` **F**, `APPROVER` **R**, scope `ASSIGNED` (A3 §2.1 F44). No `ADMIN` access at all — a document image is the rawest form of clinical detail (A3 §3.3).

#### 5.5.1 The checklist — three requirement levels

**The checklist has two keys today and needs a third.** The rows are generated from A4 §6's table for the claim's **`lossType`** (§5.4.1 **F7**), **plus the single standing row of §3.2.10 where the claimant's standing is not `SELF`** (V-118). A4 owns the rows (§0.5); the console never invents one, **and it never chooses between two candidate checklists.**

**The third key is a term's `REQUIRE_DOC`, and there is no mechanism for it — `V-756`.** D1 v0.5 **`BR-TERM-11`** gives `REQUIRE_DOC` a mechanism at last: a term whose effect is `REQUIRE_DOC` **adds its named A4 document type to this checklist at `REQUIRED` level** and **raises a checkpoint** that stays open until the document is supplied or the requirement is waived by an assessor with a recorded reason. **Nothing new is built to ask for it** — §5.5.4's information-request flow and F29 are what reach the customer, exactly as they do for any other `REQUIRED` row.

**Two things stop it running today, and both are A4's:**

| What is missing | Consequence |
|---|---|
| **The document type does not exist.** A5 §7.2's one class-E term wants a **police or hospital statement**, and A4's catalogue carries seven types and neither of them. §5.29.2 **F7** is typed `enum(documentType)` and would render a value outside its own set | **F7 renders the term's stated requirement as text** — the term's own words, from the version evaluated — **and the checklist does not carry a row for it.** The assessor asks for the document through the ordinary information request and records the outcome on the checkpoint. It is a worse answer than a checklist row and it is an honest one |
| **A4 §6's table has no key for it.** The table is keyed on the loss type and this document reads it through §4.6's eight rows (`D2-114`); **there is no column, no row and no mechanism by which a term contributes** | **The console does not synthesise one.** A row invented here would be a checklist row this document wrote, which §0.5 forbids, and it would satisfy `V-510` — *every `REQUIRED` document is received* — against a requirement A4 never stated |

**Both are asked of A4 as `D2-179`**: the document types a class-E term may require, and **a third checklist key — *a term's `REQUIRE_DOC`* — alongside the loss type and the claimant's standing. Until it lands, `V-510` blocks nothing on a term-required document**, because there is no `REQUIRED` row for it to find missing, and **the checkpoint is what holds the claim** instead — which is `BR-TERM-11`'s second half working while its first half waits.

**Why the key changed, because a key that changed for presentational reasons would not be worth a paragraph.** A4 §6's table offers *outpatient — illness* and *outpatient — with medication* as two rows of one five-value key, and **which of the two applied depended on whether a prescription had been attached — while the checklist is the thing that tells the customer to attach one.** That is circular, and it was circular on the console exactly as it was in the app: an assessor opening a claim with no prescription, and an assessor opening the same claim ten minutes after one arrived, generated two different checklists from one unchanged event. **The eight-value `lossType` key removes the second row entirely.** `T1-02` is `EXPECTED` on `ILL_OP` (D1 B-02, A4 §6) and reconciliation decides afterwards whether a prescription should have existed — a judgement made on the evidence, after the fact, rather than a key that selects which evidence to ask for. **One loss type, one checklist, plus at most one standing row: the selection is single-valued and reads nothing the checklist itself causes.**

**Twelve values, eight checklist rows, and the gap is named rather than filled.** F7 offers twelve; §4.6's table gives rows for eight. **The four death and permanent-disability values have no checklist and this screen does not invent one** — a death claim carries documents the seven types of A4 do not contain (§4.5), and a checklist assembled here would be exactly the row A4 owns and this document may not write (§0.5). **A claim registered on one of the four renders the standing row, any document the officer attached, and a stated absence** — *"chưa có danh mục chứng từ cho loại tổn thất này"* — rather than an empty checklist that reads as *nothing is required*. **`V-510` still blocks nothing on such a claim**, because there is no `REQUIRED` row to be missing, and the assessor works from the documents in front of them. **It is part of `D2-114`**: A4 §6 re-cut on twelve keys, or on eight with the four declared out of scope for the pilot — either answer is A4's, and stating the four as unhandled is what stops the first counter-registered death claim discovering it.

> **A4 §6 is still keyed on `episodeType`'s five values and must be re-cut — `D2-114`, unchanged and now on this screen's critical path rather than Part IV's alone.** Until it is, **the console generates from the eight-row table at §4.6**, which is the same eight rows the app already renders. That is a transitional read of the annex's data through the one place D2 has already written it down, **not a second definition of it** (§0.5), and it ends the moment A4 §6 carries the eight-value key.

| Level | Identifier | Behaviour on this screen | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Bắt buộc** | `REQUIRED` | **Blocks settlement.** Cannot be waived; the *Miễn yêu cầu* control is absent, not disabled | `master` (A4 §6) |
| **Cần có** | `EXPECTED` | Triggers an information request the assessor **may waive**, with a reason | `master` |
| **Tùy chọn** | `OPTIONAL` | Never requested, never blocks. Shown so the assessor can see what arrived anyway | `master` |

**Three levels and not two, because the middle one is where the judgement is.** `T1-02` prescription is *expected* for outpatient-illness precisely so that a visit which legitimately produced no prescription is not stalled, while the clinical track still gets asked for the document it needs to reason over (D1 B-02, A4 §6).

Displayed **beside F9 and never instead of it** — Part IV §4.8 | `CLM-VAL-001` |

**Notes on the fields above.** Every row the table leaves blank is either master data or a value the platform writes, so there is nothing for a person to get wrong and nothing to tell them (§2.2).

- **F1** renders A4's seven types by their Vietnamese name from A1 §6 — **never the code** in anything a customer can see (A2 rule M-3).
- **F2** is `REQUIRED` · `EXPECTED` · `OPTIONAL`; **F3** is `CHƯA_NHẬN` · `ĐÃ_NHẬN` · `ĐÃ_YÊU_CẦU` · `ĐÃ_YÊU_CẦU_KHÔNG_BỔ_SUNG` · `MIỄN_YÊU_CẦU`, and §5.5.3 says how each is left.
- **F4** is the page count as classified. **F9** is set when the document arrives, from the customer or from an assessor upload, and **F10** is `KHÁCH_HÀNG` · `CÁN_BỘ_THẨM_ĐỊNH`. **F11** is set by the *Yêu cầu bổ sung* action.
- **F7 and F8** are `BẢN_SAO` · `BẢN_GỐC` and are **present in the model and hidden by configuration in the pilot** — see the note below the table.
- **F13** is `COMPLETE` · `MISSING_DOCUMENT` · `MISSING_FIELD` · `INCONSISTENT` · `AWAITING_ORIGINAL` · `ERROR`. It is **claim-level, produced by IDP and consumed, never re-derived** (BR-DOC-4, V-513).
- **F12** is held at `textarea(2000)` per §2.9, the same width as every other free-text reason in Part V.
- **F15** is new in v0.3 and is the reduced form of **B-23**. A package of twelve files in which one page failed to render today shows a single claim-level state, so an assessor looking at a stalled claim cannot see *which* file stalled and has nothing useful to tell the operator queue. F15 says which.
- **F16** is new in v0.3 and is register row **B-24**. **F9 is the date *we* received the package; F16 is the date the *customer* sent it**, and the two are the same date only when the customer used the app. Both are retained and both are displayed — **nothing is overwritten** — because the two clocks have two anchors: our SLA clock cannot start before we hold the documents, and the statutory clock D1 §8.1 anticipates runs from the customer's act. Part IV §4.8 carries the argument in full and **`D2-46`** carries the one consequence not applied: `V-504` is defined at §5.2.6 and still anchors on the moment the set reached `COMPLETE`.

**V-724 — F15 is shown and is not actionable, and that is the reduction.** The reference gives each file its own tick box and lets an assessor re-send a selected subset for extraction. **We do not**, and the reason is AR-3: re-extraction here is a **new request over the whole package** that mutates nothing (§5.5.4, *Gửi lại trích xuất*). A per-file re-send would produce a claim whose extraction result is a mosaic of two runs with two `requestId`s and two confidence baselines, and §5.6.5's claim-level confidence — the minimum across the mandatory field set — would then be a minimum over an inconsistent set. **Also omitted**: the reference's bulk download and bulk delete over selected files, since V-527's reasoning applies to a document exactly as it applies to a cost line, and its two-column viewer, which §5.6.1 already specifies as the layout of the extraction tab.

> **On physical originals (D1 B-06).** Originals are **not required in the pilot** — claims settle entirely on captured images. **F7, F8 and the `AWAITING_ORIGINAL` package state stay in the model, unused**, behind a configuration switch that is off. Nothing on this screen asks for an original, `DOC-NOTIF-004` is never sent, and no claim waits for paper. They remain because enabling them later must be configuration, not a change to the state machine — and because Reference System A's complete absence of any original-versus-copy attribute is a gap rather than a simplification (GAP-3, BR-DOC-5).

#### 5.5.3 The five states, and why there are two terminal ones

| State | Meaning | How it is left |
|---|---|---|
| `CHƯA_NHẬN` | Not received, not yet asked for | Receipt, or a request |
| `ĐÃ_NHẬN` | Received and classified | Terminal |
| `ĐÃ_YÊU_CẦU` | We asked the customer | **Must leave**, when a supplementary batch arrives |
| `ĐÃ_YÊU_CẦU_KHÔNG_BỔ_SUNG` | We asked; a batch came back; it still is not there | **Terminal** |
| `MIỄN_YÊU_CẦU` | An `EXPECTED` item the assessor waived, with a reason | Terminal |

**BR-DOC-2 is the rule a naive design gets wrong, and this is where it is enforced.** When a supplementary batch arrives, **every item in `ĐÃ_YÊU_CẦU` leaves that state** — into `ĐÃ_NHẬN` if it came, into `ĐÃ_YÊU_CẦU_KHÔNG_BỔ_SUNG` if it did not — and the claim moves on. Without the second terminal state a claim waits forever on a document that will never arrive, nobody is prompted to decide on the evidence available, and there is no record justifying a partial settlement or a decline. The screen therefore has no "still waiting" state that survives a response.

**BR-DOC-3: a tick is one-way.** A state can be set but not silently unset, and every transition is audited old-value → new-value. Reverting a waiver or a receipt is an explicit action with its own reason, recorded as such.

#### 5.5.4 Actions

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Yêu cầu bổ sung** | `ASSESSOR` | One or more items in `CHƯA_NHẬN`, or one or more unreadable mandatory fields; claim not locked | Selected items → `ĐÃ_YÊU_CẦU`; claim → `PENDING_INFO`; request recorded with the exact items and fields, **plus the assessor's own note where one is entered** | `DOC-NOTIF-001` (missing types) · `DOC-NOTIF-002` (unreadable field) · `DOC-NOTIF-005` on the reminder. Confirmation: *(new A2 item — **D2-65**)*. The note is a new named parameter on `DOC-NOTIF-001` — *(new A2 item needed — **D2-136**)* |
| **Hoàn thành kiểm tra tài liệu** | `ASSESSOR` | Claim in `DOC_PROCESSING`; no item is in `CHƯA_NHẬN` at level `REQUIRED`; the assessor has opened the checklist | Claim → `UNDER_ASSESSMENT`, explicitly and by a named person. The completion is recorded on the trail with the actor and the checklist as it stood | *(new A2 item — **D2-65**)*; blocked by a missing `REQUIRED` item: `DOC-NOTIF-001` |
| **Miễn yêu cầu** | `ASSESSOR` | Item is `EXPECTED`; reason entered | → `MIỄN_YÊU_CẦU`; audited | *(new A2 item — **D2-65**)* |
| **Đánh dấu đã nhận** | `ASSESSOR` | An item received outside the app — a document the assessor uploaded — **and F16 entered**, not after today and not before the claim's `requestReceivedDate` | → `ĐÃ_NHẬN`, source `CÁN_BỘ_THẨM_ĐỊNH`, **with the customer-sent date recorded beside the received date**. Where the delivery answers an outstanding request the claim follows §7.2's *Ghi nhận bổ sung tại quầy* row | F16 missing or out of range: `CLM-VAL-001`. Console confirmation *(new A2 item — **D2-139**)* |
| **Tải tài liệu lên** | `ASSESSOR` | Claim not locked; §2.7's file constraints | Stored by reference in object storage; **the claim holds a URI, never bytes** (AR-2) | `CLM-VAL-006` |
| **Gửi lại trích xuất** | `ASSESSOR`, `ADMIN` (A3 §3.3) | Claim **not** in `PENDING_APPROVAL` or later — **BR-DATA-3** | A **new** `I-07` request with a new `requestId`. **Nothing existing is mutated and nothing is deleted** (AR-3) | Blocked by the lock: *(new A2 item — **D2-56**)* |
| **Mở tài liệu** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER` | — | Opens the image or the parsed XML in the viewer. **The read is logged** (BR-AUDIT-4) | — |
| **Mở giao diện IDP** (F36) | `ASSESSOR` **C** | Assigned (A3 §4.10) | Signed URL, 15-minute expiry | — |

**Why *Hoàn thành kiểm tra tài liệu* exists at all, when the state already changes by itself.** This is register row **S-05**, and it is the smallest change in this reissue with the largest effect on how the screen reads. Today `DOC_PROCESSING → UNDER_ASSESSMENT` is derived: the package reaches `COMPLETE`, V-504 stamps the timestamp, and the claim appears on someone's list. **Nobody is recorded as having looked at the checklist**, and the two facts an audit asks for six months later — *who decided this file was complete* and *what did it look like when they decided it* — are not on the claim. The action does not replace the derivation; it names it. A claim whose documents completed while nobody was looking still arrives on the work list, and the assessor's first act is this control.

**And the note to the customer.** *Yêu cầu bổ sung* today sends a list of document types and nothing else. An assessor who can see that the prescription is present but illegible, or that the invoice covers a different patient, has no way to say so — the customer receives a list and re-sends the same document. **The note is a parameter on the existing template, not a free-composed letter**: A2 owns the sentence and the note is quoted inside it, so §6.1.9's exclusion of assessor-composed correspondence is untouched.

> **One row is owed to Part VII and is still owed.** §7.2's action matrix carries no `ASSESSOR`-actor transition for `DOC_PROCESSING → UNDER_ASSESSMENT`, because until now there was none. **Part VII has since been edited — three intake and counter-supplement rows were added from the register's Part VII scope — and this row was not among them**, because it arises from a Part V observation and belongs to whoever holds the register's `S-05` row. It stays **D2-133**: a part edited from inside another part is how an action matrix stops being the authority on transitions.

**Why *Gửi lại trích xuất* is barred once the claim is with an approver.** A re-run produces a *newer* proposal while the approver is looking at an older settlement. AR-3 already guarantees a re-read cannot mutate the claim; BR-DATA-3 closes the remaining gap by forbidding the request rather than reconciling the result. It is also the reason D1 §3.2.5's lock explicitly covers document actions and not only amounts.

#### 5.5.5 Rules

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| **V-510** | A `REQUIRED` item not in `ĐÃ_NHẬN` **blocks submission of the settlement plan** (§5.10.2 check 4, V-588) and cannot be waived |
| **V-511** | An `EXPECTED` item may be waived; the waiver reason is mandatory and is retained on the claim |
| **V-512** | `OPTIONAL` items never appear in an information request and never affect F13 |
| **V-513** | The console **does not re-derive** F13. If the claim engine's own view of the checklist disagrees with IDP's package state, both are shown and the disagreement is flagged — §2.10. It is not resolved on this screen |
| **V-514** | `PENDING_INFO` → `PENDING_APPROVAL` is a legal transition (D1 §4.1): a claim may be assessed and submitted while a **non-blocking** document is outstanding. Returning it must restore `PENDING_INFO` (D1 §4.4) |

#### 5.5.6 Empty and error

| Condition | What the console shows |
|---|---|
| Extraction has not completed | The checklist renders from A4 §6 with every row `CHƯA_NHẬN` or `ĐÃ_NHẬN` by upload, and F13 shows "đang xử lý". **No completeness state is invented** while `I-09` has not answered |
| `I-09` returns `409 NOT_READY` | Handled by the adapter on `Retry-After` (D3 §1.3). The screen shows processing, not an error |
| Package state is `ERROR` | The claim appears on S-03 (§5.19) as an operational failure with the operator queue. **It is never `DECLINED`** (G-3, D1 §4.3), and the customer sees `SYS-ERR-001` |
| A page landed in `unclassified` | Listed under *Chưa phân loại* with the image, so the assessor can attach it to a type. **It is never forced into the nearest class** (A4 §3) |
| **One or more lines could not be allocated to an insured event** | The lines are flagged in place and in the warning rail, the grid offers to filter to them, and the tab header carries the count. **The calculation is not offered** until every line carries L17 — V-705, V-706. *(new A2 item — **D2-123**)* |
| **The claim has cost lines and no insured event at all** | Every line is unallocatable by definition. The tab states so and links to §5.7, where the event is created — B-43's *Thêm sự kiện*. **No implicit event is created from the document header**, because an event carries a cover decision and a liability rationale that only a person may write (§5.7.2 F11, F13) |

---

### 5.6 Claim detail — Extraction & costs tab (F46)

**Purpose.** Put the original document beside the data read out of it, show every warning where it arose, let the assessor correct anything without destroying what the machine proposed, and take the pay-or-decline decision on every cost line.

**Entered from.** S-02, tab 3. §1.3 forward-references this section: **this is where AR-1 and AR-4 stop being architecture and become a screen.**

**Who may open it.** `ASSESSOR` **F**, `APPROVER` **R**, scope `ASSIGNED` (A3 §2.1 F46). No `ADMIN`. **Nobody may edit the raw extraction result — not even an administrator** (A3 §3.3, D3 §I-09): corrections are made to the claim's copy and the pair stays comparable forever.

#### 5.6.1 Layout — three regions, one context

| Region | Contents |
|---|---|
| **Left — ảnh gốc** | The source document at full resolution, page navigation, zoom. For `T1-04` the parsed XML rendered as a field list, since there is no image (A4 §1.5) |
| **Right — dữ liệu đã trích xuất** | Two stacked panels: the document's header fields, and the cost-line table |
| **Rail — cảnh báo** | Every warning on the claim, grouped by document, each a link to the field it attaches to |

Every extracted field carries `documentId`, `page` and `bbox` (A4 §2 *provenance*). **Selecting a field scrolls and highlights its region in the image; selecting a highlight selects the field.** That two-way anchor is the whole reason the image and the data are on one screen rather than two, and it is what makes a warning actionable in seconds rather than minutes.

#### 5.6.2 Field table — document header fields

One row per extracted header field. The example below is `T1-01`; `T1-02`, `T1-03` and `T1-04` follow the same pattern over A4 §4.2, A4 §4.3 and A4 §4.4. **Every row's Source is `idp:I-09` and every row is editable — that is AR-1, expressed as a column.**

Accepting the proposal re-derives F18, re-derives the `episodeType` A5 §8.1 maps on, and invalidates the calculation | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-74**)* |

**Note on F7.** The presence of a `Số thẻ BHYT` indicates that social health insurance was applied to the episode. It is **displayed and nothing is deducted from it** — declared simplification S-17, and the reason L6 below is carried unchanged rather than consumed.

#### 5.6.3 Field table — the cost-line table

The unit of the pay/decline decision (D1 §5.1). **One row per line, per document — and every row belongs to exactly one insured event.**

> **The grid is widened in v0.3 and the change is structural, not cosmetic.** v0.2's grid had sixteen columns and no join to the event the line was incurred in. §5.7.1 said a claim carries many events, §5.9.2 rolled up *per event*, and this table said *per document* — **and nothing anywhere joined the two**. The register raised it as **S-07** and called it the largest remaining structural hole in Part V; it is the only row in the whole comparison where not fixing it makes a real population of claims settle at the wrong number rather than merely inconvenience an assessor. **L17 is the join.** L18 to L24 are the columns the reference carries, our extraction already returns and this grid did not show (**S-15**, **S-16**, **S-17**, **S-18**), and they close **X-1** — the prototype has drawn them since 23 August 2026 and this table had not caught up.

**Notes on the columns above.**

- **L2 is quoted verbatim in the decline rationale** (A4 L2), so an edit here changes what the customer reads.
- **L6, L7 and L8** default to `0`. **L6 is displayed and deliberately not consumed** — declared simplification S-17; it is carried unchanged so that coordination of benefits is later a rule step rather than a re-extraction. **L7 is not the policy's đồng chi trả** (A1 §9).
- **L9** is `L5 − L6`, floored at `0` (A4 L14). It is **the amount presented to the benefit engine** and is never recomputed by the console.
- **L11** comes from A5 §8.1 on L10 × treatment setting, and is `500` where the event's loss type is accident. It is shown so that the mapping is visible rather than implied.
- **L16 is read-only and retained forever** (BR-LINE-3), shown beside L15 whenever the two differ. Both are held at `textarea(2000)` per §2.9.
- **L17 is mandatory and has no default value**, only a default *allocation* — V-705. A line the platform could not place is not given the first event; it is flagged.
- **L18 and L19 are what make L17 checkable by a person.** An assessor asked to confirm that a line belongs to event `/2` needs to see which document it came off and what date that document carries; without them the allocation is an assertion.
- **L20 and L21 are read and not consumed.** No step of the chain reads a unit or a drug registration number, and A5 defines no rule over either. They are on the grid because **a quantity without its unit cannot be checked against a day or count limit** (chain step 9, §5.9.1) and because a drug registration number is what makes two lines for the same medicine on two documents recognisable as the same medicine. **Whether A4 §4.1 already extracts all five of L18, L20, L21, L22 and L23 is confirmed as D2-134** — where it does not, the column is assessor-keyed and marked as such, exactly as V-515's raw-versus-corrected pair works everywhere else on this tab.
- **L22 is the reduced form of S-16.** The reference carries **two** disease-code columns per line — the code extracted from the line, and a separate *related diagnosis* code. **We carry one.** The extracted code is the one that makes a `NOTREL` conclusion argue from the line the customer is being refused rather than from the event's diagnosis of record, which is the whole of the clinical track's exposure (D1 §5.10.6, §5.7.4). The *related diagnosis* column has no extraction field behind it and would be keyed by the assessor on every line of every claim, to be read by nothing — the second column is a place to record a judgement, and L15 and L24 are already that place.
- **L23 completes a sum this document has been asserting without a term for it.** L8's validation reads *Σ (L6+L7+L8+other) = L5*, and `other` was on no screen. It is now L23.
- **L24 is optional and is deliberately not mandatory.** The reference's settlement grid marks its note column required. Requiring a note on every paid line is a **business rule**, D1 carries none, and inventing one here would be a defect under §0.5. What v0.2 had was a rationale that exists only when a line is **declined** — so the reason an assessor paid a line they hesitated over was recorded nowhere, and the second reader had no way to see that the hesitation happened.
- **L25 is S-18, and it is the number the grid was missing.** Until now the only place a payable appeared was §5.9.2's roll-up, one level up from the decision it followed from. **It is `derived` and blank before the first chain run**: a payable rendered as `0` on a line nobody has calculated is indistinguishable from a line the chain declined to nothing.

**V-705 — how a cost line is allocated to an insured event, and what happens when it cannot be.**

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| 1 | **The default allocation.** A line belongs to the insured event whose **provider (§5.7.2 F2) is the same as the source document's provider** *and* whose **treatment-date range (F4) contains the source document's date (L18)**. Both conditions, not either |
| 2 | **Exactly one event matches** → L17 is set, source `system`, and the line is marked automatically allocated. This is the ordinary case and the assessor is not asked |
| 3 | **More than one event matches, or none does** → **L17 is left empty and the line is flagged** *"chưa gán được sự kiện bảo hiểm"* on the grid and in the warning rail. **Nothing is guessed, and in particular the first event is not used as a fallback** — a claim with two visits to the same provider in overlapping weeks is precisely the case that makes an event identity ambiguous, and it is also the case where guessing wrong changes the per-event limit that prices the line |
| 4 | **The assessor may re-allocate any line**, including one the platform allocated. Re-allocation sets L17's source to `user`, is audited old → new (BR-AUDIT-2) and **marks the calculation stale** — the per-event cap at chain step 8 is computed per event, so moving a line between events changes the number |
| 5 | **L18 is missing** → the allocation cannot run and the line is flagged as in rule 3. It is not matched on provider alone |
| 6 | **A line may not be allocated to an event on another claim**, and the lookup does not offer one |

> **Why the rule matches on the document's date and not on the line's.** A cost line rarely carries a date of its own; the statement or invoice it sits on does, and A4 §4.1 extracts that. Matching on a date the extraction does not return would produce a rule that never fires and an allocation that is always manual.

**Why an unallocated line is not merely a warning.** Four things downstream read the event and none of them has an answer without it. **Chain step 8** is the per-event cap (A5 §6.1) and takes the event's set of lines as its base. **Step 11's deduction ratio** is evaluated on the event's provider (§5.7.2 F2, F3, A5 §4.3), so two visits to different networks on one claim would otherwise share one condition. **§5.9.2's per-event roll-up** has no source. And **§5.9.3's remaining-per-occurrence** cannot be computed. So the line is a **blocking check at submission — §5.10.2 check 12, V-706** — and an unallocated line **abandons the first chain run whole** rather than running it on the lines that did allocate (§5.11.4). A payable computed from part of a claim is a wrong number, not a partial one.

**V-520 — every cost line carries a decision, and every declined line carries a reason and a rationale, before the settlement plan can be submitted.** The rule is stated here because L13 is where an assessor meets it; it is enforced at submission as check 1 of §5.10.2 (V-585) and it is the reason a line is never simply left alone.

#### 5.6.4 Correction in place — the raw is preserved and the difference is visible

This is §1.3 made concrete, and it is specified once here for the whole document.

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| **V-515** | **The extraction result is never overwritten** (BR-DATA-1). A correction writes a new value onto the **claim's copy**; the `I-09` result is immutable and re-fetchable for 90 days (D3 §I-09) |
| **V-516** | **A corrected field displays both values at all times** — the current value in the control, and beneath it, in a secondary line, *"Giá trị trích xuất: {rawValue} · độ tin cậy {confidence}"*. Not on hover, not behind a toggle. D1 §6.2's third presentation requirement: *"the interface must make that visible or assessors will treat the proposal as the answer"* |
| **V-517** | A corrected field carries a persistent **đã sửa** marker, and the tab and the claim header carry a count of corrected fields. The approver sees the same count (§5.11) |
| **V-518** | **Hoàn về giá trị trích xuất** restores the raw value. It is an action with an audit entry, not an undo |
| **V-519** | Every correction is audited actor · timestamp · old → new (BR-AUDIT-2), and the pair raw/corrected is what makes *"how often does the assessor overrule the machine"* answerable — which is what makes the auto-approval threshold tunable (D1 §7.1) |
| **V-715** | **A value the customer entered themselves is marked as theirs, and the two that anchor a measurement are read-only.** §2.4's `Source` vocabulary distinguishes `user` from `system` and `snapshot`, but not the assessor's keystroke from the customer's — so a console screen cannot show that the treatment type on this claim is what the customer chose rather than what an assessor decided. Every claim value captured in the app carries a **customer-declared marker** and renders the declared value beside the current one whenever they differ, in the same shape as V-516's raw-versus-corrected pair. **F3 (submission instant) and F8 (claimed amount as submitted) are read-only to every console role**: both are what a later measurement counts from, and a measurement whose start can be edited measures nothing. Everything else stays editable, because D1 requires the assessor to be able to correct a customer's mistake — §5.4.1 F7 and §5.7.2 F5 are the cases, and each already carries D2-74's confirmation. **Reduced from B-39**: a new `Source` value for *customer-declared* is **not** added; the marker is a per-field attribute on the claim record. **Part II has since settled the vocabulary question and settled it the same way** — §2.11 **UI-27** carries the convention, §2.4 stays the single list, and `D2-124`'s `Source` half is closed |
| **V-527** | Adding a cost line by hand is permitted and is marked `nguồn: cán bộ thẩm định`; **deleting an extracted line is not**. A line the assessor believes should not be paid is **declined with a reason**, not removed — otherwise the settlement letter loses the row that BR-LINE-4 requires it to show |

> **Why deletion is barred and decline is not.** A deleted line disappears from the letter and from the comparison set; a declined line appears in the same table as the paid lines, with a reason the customer can read (BR-LINE-4). The two look equivalent to an assessor in a hurry and are opposite in every property that matters afterwards.

#### 5.6.5 Confidence — what is shown, and what it does

| Level | What is shown | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Field | A band, with the numeric score available on inspection | `idp:I-09` |
| **Line** | **Green / amber / red per line**, with the reason — D1 §6.2's second presentation requirement, carried from the reference because it changes assessor behaviour: attention goes to the two lines that need it rather than to the whole claim | `idp:I-09` |
| Document | Classification confidence, plus any `competingType` | `idp:I-09` |
| Claim | The **minimum** across the mandatory field set — deliberately not the mean, so one badly-read amount cannot be averaged away (A4 §7) | `idp:I-09` |

**What confidence does: it routes work.** Below the configured threshold, the claim is flagged on the work list and the assessor is pointed at **the specific fields**, never at a generic "needs review" — `CLM-CONSOLE-001`, which carries `{fieldList}` for exactly this reason (A2 §8, A4 §7). The tab defaults to sorting the warning rail and the cost lines by ascending confidence.

**What confidence does not do: it is not a gate condition.** The auto-approval gate tests **four** conditions and confidence is not one of them (D1 §5.8, A5 §6.4, A4 §7). **A claim whose amounts were read with low confidence can auto-approve**, and the threshold limits the damage rather than preventing it — recorded in D1 §5.8 as a deliberate omission and as Framework RK-07, bounded by BC-3. This is stated on the screen specification because it looks like a defect to anyone who has not read D1 §5.8, and because a developer who "fixes" it by adding confidence to the gate has changed a business rule.

#### 5.6.6 Reconciliation disagreements — shown, never resolved

A4 §5's nine rules run inside IDP and arrive as `warnings[]`, each naming the document and the field it attaches to (A4 §8).

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| **V-521** | Every warning is rendered **at the field on every document it names**, and in the rail. R1 (patient name) fires on three documents and appears three times, not once |
| **V-522** | Where two documents disagree, **both values are shown side by side with their sources**, and the disagreement is flagged. **The screen never picks one** — D1 §5.4, §2.10. The system's job is to notice, not to resolve |
| **V-523** | A warning is **never a block**. It does not prevent a line decision, a calculation or a submission by itself |
| **V-524** | Every warning must be **acknowledged** — *đã xem*, recorded with actor and timestamp — before the settlement plan can be submitted (§5.10.2 check 7, V-591). Acknowledgement is not resolution: the disagreement stays on the claim, visible to the approver and in the trail |
| **V-525** | R6 (invoice against cost statement) is **skipped with a note** where no XML was supplied. The checklist item is *received-but-unverified* and the assessor may key the invoice header manually. **This is not a blocking error** (A4 §1.5) |
| **V-526** | Where IDP's determination and the document disagree, **IDP's determination is what was used and a warning was raised** (A4 §5). The console shows which was used; it does not silently correct either |

**V-524 is the one design decision in this subsection that no source settles**, and it is taken here because the alternative — a warning that can be submitted past without anyone having looked — makes §2.10's guarantee decorative. It is recorded as **D2-71** so the business can reject it if the friction is judged too high.

#### 5.6.7 Actions

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Sửa giá trị** | `ASSESSOR` | Claim not locked; field is `idp:I-09`-sourced | Writes to the claim copy; raw preserved and displayed (V-515, V-516); calculation marked stale | — |
| **Hoàn về giá trị trích xuất** | `ASSESSOR` | Field has been corrected | Restores the raw value; audited | — |
| **Chấp nhận dòng / Từ chối dòng** | `ASSESSOR` | Claim not locked | Sets L13; a decline demands L14 and L15 | L15 breaching B-14: *(new A2 item — **D2-59**)* |
| **Thêm dòng chi phí** | `ASSESSOR` | Claim not locked | New line, source `cán bộ thẩm định`, confidence n/a — V-527. **L17 must be chosen explicitly** — a hand-added line has no source document to allocate from | *(new A2 item — **D2-123**)* |
| **Gán sự kiện bảo hiểm cho dòng** | `ASSESSOR` | Claim not locked; at least one insured event exists | Sets or changes L17; audited old → new; **marks the calculation stale** — V-705 rule 4 | *(new A2 item — **D2-123**)* |
| **Ghi chú dòng chi phí** | `ASSESSOR` | Claim not locked | Writes L24. **Internal, never customer-facing** | — |
| **Xác nhận cảnh báo** | `ASSESSOR` | A warning is open | Acknowledged with actor and timestamp (V-524) | — |
| **Tính toán lại** | `ASSESSOR` | Every line has L13 **and L17**; every declined line has L14 and L15 | Runs the fourteen steps; posts provisionally; opens §5.9 | *(new A2 item — **D2-60**)* on a failed precondition |
| **Mở ảnh gốc** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER` | — | Viewer at the field's `page`/`bbox`. **The read is logged** (BR-AUDIT-4) | — |
| **Mở giao diện IDP** (F36) | `ASSESSOR` **C** | Assigned; 15-minute signed URL (A3 §4.10) | New tab, for looking only (AR-4) | — |

#### 5.6.8 Empty and error

| Condition | What the console shows |
|---|---|
| `DOC_PROCESSING`, result not yet pulled | The tab renders the document list and an explicit "đang trích xuất" state. **No empty cost table is drawn that could be mistaken for a claim with no costs** |
| `I-09` returns `409 NOT_READY` | Adapter retries on `Retry-After`; the screen keeps the processing state (D3 §1.3) |
| Package state `MISSING_FIELD` | The named fields are shown empty with the warning attached, and are editable — the assessor may key them from the image. `null` is *not known* and is never rendered as `0` or as an empty string (D3 §1.2) |
| Package state `ERROR` / `EXTRACTION_ERROR` | Operational: the operator queue on S-03 (§5.19), resubmission available, **never a decline** (D1 §4.3, G-3). Customer sees `SYS-ERR-001`. Console notice: *(new A2 item needed — **D2-57**)* |
| Claim is `PENDING_APPROVAL` or later | The whole tab is read-only, including document actions and resubmission (D1 §3.2.5, BR-DATA-3), with a banner naming who it is with — *(new A2 item — **D2-56**)* |
| The claim carries no `T1-04` XML | The invoice panel states that no e-invoice was supplied and that R6 was skipped. It is not an error and does not stop the settlement (A4 §1.5) |

---

### 5.7 Claim detail — Events & cover tab (F47)

**Purpose.** Decide, per insured event, whether the episode is covered — the diagnosis, its condition class, in or out of cover, the reason if out, and the assessor's own rationale — and settle the wording of every line-level decline before it reaches a customer.

**Entered from.** S-02, tab 4. Placed **before** the cost tab in the assessor's intended sequence, which is D1 §6.2's one deliberate change to the reference's order: deciding whether an episode is covered before arguing about individual line items saves the argument entirely when it is not.

**Who may open it.** `ASSESSOR` **F**, `APPROVER` **R**, scope `ASSIGNED` (A3 §2.1 F47). No `ADMIN` — every field on this tab is clinical detail under A3 §4.11.

#### 5.7.1 One tab, many events

**A claim carries many insured events** (D1 §5.1). Each is one provider, one date range, one diagnosis set, identified `CLM-26-000417/1`, `/2`, … (Framework §7.5). The tab is a list of events, each expanding to the field table below, and each rolling up to the settlement in §5.9.

**Every cost line belongs to exactly one of these events, and v0.3 is where that is stated.** §5.6.3 L17 carries the join and V-705 is the allocation rule; **this section owns the events the rule allocates to**. Three consequences follow and each is enforced somewhere else, so they are gathered here where an assessor first meets them:

| # | Consequence |
|---|---|
| 1 | **An event's cost total is the sum of the lines allocated to it**, and that is the base chain step 8's per-event cap works on (A5 §6.1). It is not a share of the claim total and it is not the source document's total |
| 2 | **The deduction condition is the event's**, not the claim's — F2 and F3 below are what A5 §4.3 reads. A claim with one in-network visit and one out-of-network visit produces two different step 11 outcomes on one claim, which is exactly the case v0.2 could not express |
| 3 | **An event with no lines allocated to it is legitimate and is not an error** — a visit the customer declared and produced no invoice for. It is assessed for cover, contributes a liability rationale, and prices at zero |

**Multi-diagnosis splitting** (D1 §5.2): where an episode carries several diagnoses, **each ICD-10 code produces its own assessment line**. The console splits on ICD codes and **does not split free text on punctuation** — that heuristic mis-splits Vietnamese medical prose. Where no ICD code is present, the event is flagged for the assessor to classify rather than guessed.

#### 5.7.2 Field table — per insured event

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Số sự kiện bảo hiểm | `text(20)` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F2 | Cơ sở y tế | `lookup(provider)` | `user` | M | From the provider master (F57), pre-filled from the extracted provider name. **The value the deduction condition is evaluated against** | *(new A2 item — **D2-58**)* |
| F3 | Trong danh mục liên kết | `bool` | `master` | M | **Read-only.** `in_network` at `providerMasterAsOf`. Absent from the master → *ngoài danh mục* (A5 §4.3) | *(new A2 item — **D2-58**)* |
| F4 | Ngày điều trị — từ / đến | `date` | `user` | M | The full chain of D1 §3.2.1, against the **member's** coverage period (F22 on S-02.1), not the policy's | `CLM-VAL-002` |

It is what A5 §8.1's benefit mapping reads**, unchanged. It is never captured and never edited: F18 is set and this follows, and code that lets the two disagree has a defect (A1 §4.2) | — |

A change is audited and marks the calculation stale | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-74**)* |

**Notes on the fields above.** **F1** is `claimNo/n` and is immutable; it is held at `text(20)` per §2.9, which is the claim number's canonical width with room for the event suffix. **F6** is the diagnosis of record for the event (A4 T1-03 field 12). **F15** carries `PROVIDER_OFF_NETWORK` where F3 is false and the benefit carries a deduction; it is **recorded on the claim** so the settlement letter can state the condition that applied (A5 §4.3, A2 §7.1).

**V-707 — the occurrence date, and why it is not the treatment date.** This is register row **S-08**, and it is the one change in this reissue where not making it produces a decision that is wrong **only in the direction that costs money**.

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| 1 | **F16 is the date the insured event occurred**, which is not in general the date it was treated. Both are on the event; neither is derived from the other |
| 2 | **Derivation where extraction returns nothing.** Where F8 is `ACC`, F16 defaults to the accident date if the package carries one and is otherwise **left empty for the assessor to enter**. For every other condition class F16 defaults to **F4's start date**, which is the ordinary case and is correct by definition for an illness first presented at treatment |
| 3 | **Constraint: F16 ≤ F4 start ≤ F4 end ≤ today**, tested as one chain on every save, per event row |
| 4 | **F16 is the date the waiting period counts to.** F10's arithmetic counts from the member's coverage start (BR-WAIT-1) to **F16**, not to F4 |
| 5 | **F16 is a third signal on the duplicate match key** — §5.2.6 V-503 |

> **What v0.2 got wrong, stated plainly because it is a live defect and not a missing nicety.** F10 counted the waiting period **to the treatment date**. Take a member whose cover began on 1 March with a thirty-day general wait, who is injured on 20 March and attends on 5 April. Counting to the treatment date gives thirty-five days, the wait is served, **and the claim is approved.** Counting to the occurrence date gives nineteen days, the wait is not served, and the claim declines. The second answer is the correct one, and every case where the two answers differ resolves the same way — **the error is one-sided, and the side it falls on is the expensive one**. `ACC` is one of A1 §4's six canonical condition classes and carries its own waiting period, so an accident treated later than it happened is an ordinary claim for this product, not an edge case.

**What is deliberately not added.** The reference's event also carries the **province where the loss occurred**, and together with the insured and the occurrence date it forms their identity of *one incident*. **We do not add it.** That identity exists in their system to accumulate approval authority across the claims of one incident, and **S-12 declares per-incident authority accumulation out of scope** (register **S-29**). A field with no rule reading it, on a screen an administrator may not open, is a redaction surface and nothing else.

**V-708 — the treatment-day count, and where ours comes from.** Register row **S-09**. F17 is the number of days the event consumed, counted **inclusive of both ends of F4**, so a single-day outpatient visit is **one day and not zero**. Without it, **chain step 9 — the count and day limit — has no input**, and every inpatient benefit in A5 that is limited in days is unpriceable. The pilot has not met this because its worked example (§5.9.4) is a one-day outpatient visit; it surfaces on the first inpatient claim.

> **One difference from the reference, and it is a choice rather than an accident.** In Reference System A this field is **returned by their extraction partner** and is not computed. **Ours is derived from F4 by the platform**, and is marked `derived` for that reason. The trade is stated so nobody later reads the difference as a gap: a derived count cannot disagree with the dates it is shown beside, which is the failure their arrangement is exposed to; what it cannot do is carry a count that differs from the dates for a reason the document states and the dates do not — a discharge on the morning of admission plus one, counted by the hospital as one day. **Where the two readings differ the dates win**, and an assessor who needs the other answer corrects F4. The counting unit is A1 §4's `countUnit`, which A5's schedule already names per benefit; **no new value set is introduced here** (§2.3).

**On F18, and on `D2-44` being closed here rather than carried again.** Register row **S-10** was applied to the app at §4.5 and **declined on the console**, with reasons: replacing `episodeType` reaches A1, A5 and D1. **The reasoning was correct and the decision has since been taken.** A1 **v1.2 §4.2** registers `lossType` and states the relationship the decline was missing — **`lossType` subsumes `episodeType`; it does not replace it.** With that, none of the three consequences the decline priced actually arrives:

| What the decline said it would cost | What it costs, given A1 §4.2 |
|---|---|
| An A1 change | **Made.** `lossType` is registered at A1 §4.2 and `episodeType` keeps its entry at A1 §5 |
| An A5 change | **None.** A5 §8.1 maps on `episodeType`'s five values and still does — F5 carries them, projected, with the same values |
| A D1 change | **None.** No `BR-` rule reads a loss type. The adjudication chain reads the condition class (F8), the setting, the benefit and the dates |

**The three fields and the direction they run, stated once because getting the direction wrong is the whole risk.** **F18 is set. F5 and the checklist follow.** Nothing reads F5 in order to compute F18, and nothing reads the documents on the claim in order to compute either.

| Field | What it is | Direction |
|---|---|---|
| **F18** `lossType` | The pathology-and-setting pair as one value, twelve on this surface | **The captured fact.** Pre-filled, correctable, audited |
| **F5** `episodeType` | Five values, A5 §8.1's mapping key | **Projected from F18**, read-only. `ILL_*` → `OUTPATIENT`/`INPATIENT`, `DEN_*` → `DENTAL`, `ACC_*` → `ACCIDENT`, `MAT_*` → `MATERNITY` |
| **F8** `conditionClass` | The canonical six, A1 §4, the waiting period's key | **Constrained by F18, not derived from it.** `ACC_*` admits only `ACC`; `MAT_*` admits `BIR` or `MAT`; `ILL_*` and `DEN_*` admit `PRE`, `SPE` or `GEN`. **The assessor still chooses within the admitted set** — that is a clinical judgement and F18 does not make it |

**F8's constraint is why the app can determine eight values and this screen twelve, and it is the same asymmetry A1 §4.2 records.** The app never asks a customer to separate childbirth from a maternity complication — 270 days of waiting period against 90 (A1 §4) — so it collects `MAT_OP` or `MAT_IP` and an assessor separates `BIR` from `MAT` here. The four values the app never offers at all are the death and permanent-disability variants (§4.5), which reach the console only through counter intake (§7.2).

> **The mapping is lossy in one direction and that is why `lossType` is the captured field rather than `episodeType`.** Eight values project onto five; five do not project back onto eight — *dental, inpatient* and *maternity, inpatient* have no five-value expression at all, which is the defect §4.5 named. **A platform that stored the five and derived the eight would be storing the answer it can compute from and deriving the one it cannot.** The old F18 derived the pair *for display only* and said *no rule reads it*; it is now the event's captured loss type, F5 is what is derived, and **the claim-level twin at §5.4.1 F7 is what A4 §6's checklist is keyed on** (§5.5.1). **The checklist stays per claim and not per event** — making it per event is Framework **S-38** and D2-135, and it is the same condition A1 §4.2 names for retiring `episodeType` altogether.

**On F19, F20 and F21, and the reduction they represent.** Register row **S-11**: the reference carries three free-text medical fields on the event — injury description, surgical or procedural method, and history related to the diagnosis — **all three optional**. All three are added, all three optional. **Two things are deliberately not done.** They are **not extraction targets** — A4 §4.1 carries no field for any of them, and making them so is an A4 change and an IDP change (**D2-134** asks the adjacent question about the cost-line fields). And they are **not carried into the clinical assessment request** on `I-15`, which would be a D3 contract change; the clinical track continues to reason over the diagnosis, the ICD code and the line, exactly as D1 §5.10 specifies. **They are evidence a person reads** — for F13's liability rationale, and for the second reader at §5.11.1. They are clinical detail under A3 §4.11 and are absent for `ADMIN` like everything else on this tab.

> **A correction to something the prototype asserts, recorded because it will be read.** The prototype marks F21 *"bắt buộc ở hệ tham chiếu"*. **It is not.** The reference makes none of the three mandatory, and the register raises the mis-statement as **X-2** — a prototype fix rather than a specification one. This document specifies all three as optional, which is both what the reference does and what our own use of them supports.

#### 5.7.3 Warning, not block — and what the assessor may override

D1 §5.4 settles the posture and this screen implements it exactly: **the engine computes the decline, the assessor can see and override it with a reason, and the override is audited.**

| Engine result | Screen behaviour |
|---|---|
| Waiting period not served **as at the occurrence date (F16)** | Pre-fills F11 = `NGOÀI_PHẠM_VI`, F12 = `WAIT`, and shows F10's arithmetic. `CLM-CONSOLE-004`. **Overridable with F14** — a hard block removes the assessor's ability to honour an endorsement the data does not carry |
| Cover period failed (`covered = false` at registration) | Pre-fills F12 = `PERIOD` with the `I-05` reasons. Overridable with F14 |
| Benefit not held | `NOBEN`. Overridable |
| Exclusion matched (A5 §7) | `EXCL`, naming the exclusion. Overridable |
| Limit exhausted | `LIMIT`, with `CLM-CONSOLE-003` naming the benefit, the remaining and the claimed. **Not overridable here** — a limit is arithmetic on the ledger, and the mechanism for paying more is not an override on this screen |

**There is no discretionary reduction anywhere on this tab.** An assessor who believes a line should be paid in part rather than in full has exactly one mechanism — **decline the line, with a reason** (D1 §5.6). No rate, no ratio and no amount on this screen is editable, and the deduction ratio is `master`/`snapshot` throughout.

#### 5.7.4 The AI-drafted decline text, and the B-14 wording rule enforced at the screen

Every declined cost line carries a rationale (BR-LINE-1). It may be AI-drafted (BR-LINE-2), the assessor may edit it, and **both the original drafted text and the final text are retained** (BR-LINE-3) — shown side by side on this tab, exactly as the raw and corrected extraction values are on §5.6.

The drafting patterns are A5 §8.2's; the customer-facing wording is A2 §4's `NOTREL` and `NOTCOV` templates. **B-14's rule — a clinical decline is a statement about cover, never an assertion that a prescription was wrong — is enforced here, at the screen, and not left to the assessor's judgement.** Four mechanisms, in order:

| # | Mechanism | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **V-530** | **The draft is generated from A2 §4's template only.** *"Khoản này không thuộc phạm vi chi trả cho chẩn đoán đã ghi nhận"* — the cover form. The clinical form, *"thuốc này không phù hợp với chẩn đoán"*, is not a template the system can produce | The default text is already compliant |
| **V-531** | **The final text must still name the item and the amount.** A2 §4's note: *"an edited message must still name the item and the amount, and the console enforces that."* Checked against `{itemName}` and `{itemAmount}` on save | Blocking validation |
| **V-532** | **A configurable prohibited-phrase list** — assertions about prescribing, about the treating doctor, or about clinical appropriateness — raises a **blocking** validation naming the phrase and offering the compliant form. The list is master data (F55), because the phrasings that need catching will be learned in UAT | Blocking validation |
| **V-533** | **The text is never attributed to a model.** No template, no draft and no editable field may contain an attribution, and the customer-facing rendering carries none. The attribution is recorded internally (BR-TRACK-6) and never externally (D1 §5.10.6) | Structural — there is no field to put it in |

**Why this is enforced by the software rather than by training.** The exposure is D1 §5.10.6's sharpest: a recommendation produced from unreviewed public material, confirmed by an assessor who is not a clinician, expressed to a customer as a reason their medicine was not paid for. The insurer can defend *"this is not covered for the recorded diagnosis"*. It cannot defend *"your doctor should not have prescribed this"*. That distinction cannot survive being left to a busy assessor with a free-text box, and RK-09's mitigation rests on it holding every time.

**The escalation route is the information request** (B-14, F29): the customer sends further medical information and the claim returns to an assessor. A2 §4's `NOTREL` template already carries the invitation — *"Nếu Quý khách có thông tin y tế bổ sung, vui lòng gửi để chúng tôi xem xét lại"* — and no new state or feature is required.

#### 5.7.5 Actions

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Thêm sự kiện bảo hiểm** | `ASSESSOR` | Claim not locked | A new event row, numbered `claimNo/n` at the next free `n`, with F2, F4, **F18**, F16 to be completed — **F5 is projected and is never keyed**. The date chain is tested **on that row alone** — **V-707 rule 3**, and both ends of F4 within the member's coverage period (F22 on S-02.1) | `CLM-VAL-002` |
| **Xóa sự kiện bảo hiểm** | `ASSESSOR` | Claim not locked; **the event has no cost line allocated to it** and has never been submitted in a frozen plan version (V-716) | The row is removed and the removal is audited. **An event that priced anything is never deleted** — it is assessed `NGOÀI_PHẠM_VI` with a reason, on the same argument V-527 makes for a cost line | inline; blocked: *(new A2 item — **D2-123**)* |
| **Lưu đánh giá sự kiện** | `ASSESSOR` | F7, F8, F11, F13, **F16** complete; F12 and F14 where conditional | Writes the event; marks the calculation stale | inline |
| **Tách sự kiện theo chẩn đoán** | `ASSESSOR` | More than one ICD-10 on the event | One assessment line per ICD (D1 §5.2) | — |
| **Ghi đè kết quả máy** | `ASSESSOR` | Engine produced a decline; F14 entered | Override recorded and audited | — |
| **Soạn lại diễn giải** | `ASSESSOR` | A declined line exists | Regenerates the draft from the template; the previous final text is retained | — |
| **Kiểm tra diễn giải** | `ASSESSOR` | On save of any L15 | Runs V-531 and V-532 | *(new A2 item — **D2-59**)* |

**Why the console adds events and the app does not — register row B-43, minimum version.** The commonest outpatient claim in this product is a customer who attends three times in a month, holds three sets of documents and submits once. **S11 in the app captures one treatment type, one date range and one provider**, and D2 §4.5 does not say who creates the second event. Reference System A answers it at the intake step, by a member of staff, before the claim reaches an assessor — and this is that answer, moved to the tab where our events already live.

**What it costs not to have it, and the cost is not presentational.** Without a way to merge, the customer opens three claims. Three claims for one member at one provider with overlapping dates trip **BR-DUP-1** against each other, so an assessor dismisses two false duplicate warnings before starting real work. Three chain runs post three provisional ledger entries where one belongs. And three claims each test the auto-approval threshold separately — which is exactly the hole **S-12** declared and accepted, except that without this control we would be **forcing** every multi-visit customer down it rather than merely tolerating it.

**The full version is not built and is declared rather than left silent.** Letting the customer declare several visits on S11 turns D2 §4.5's F3 to F8 into a repeating table and — the expensive part — makes A4 §6's checklist generate **per event** instead of per claim, which reaches A4, A2's information-request wording and the whole supplementary-document flow. That is a Part IV and annex change, not a Part V one. **It is recorded as an addition owed to Framework §7.4's simplification register — D2-135** — because today it is a silence rather than a decision.

#### 5.7.6 Empty and error

| Condition | What the console shows |
|---|---|
| No ICD-10 anywhere in the package | The event is flagged *"chưa xác định mã ICD-10"* and F7 is mandatory before the plan can be submitted. **Nothing is guessed** (D1 §5.2) |
| The ICD-10 master is unavailable | F7 accepts the code with a pattern check and flags it unvalidated; the claim is not blocked on a master-data outage |
| `waitingPeriodDays` is `null` for F8 × the benefit group | **Data error**, not a zero-day wait: the event is flagged, the claim routed to S-03 (§5.19), and no waiting-period result is computed (BR-WAIT-4) |
| The provider is not in the master | F3 shows *ngoài danh mục*, the work-list flag is raised, and the deduction ratio will apply. §5.17 states why this is the safe default and what its cost is |
| **F16 cannot be derived and extraction returned nothing** — an accident with no accident date in the package | The event is flagged *"chưa có ngày xảy ra sự kiện"* and F16 is mandatory before the event can be saved. **F4's start date is not silently used**: for `ACC` that is the assumption V-707 exists to prevent |
| **F16 is later than F4's start date** | Refused at the field with `CLM-VAL-002`, showing both dates. **Never reordered and never corrected** (§2.10) |
| **A claim carries cost lines and no event** | Stated on this tab with the count of unallocated lines and the *Thêm sự kiện* control. See §5.6.8 |
