### 5.8 Clinical recommendation review (F56)

**Purpose.** Show each clinical recommendation with the evidence it rests on, let the assessor confirm or reject it with a reason, and — on confirmation — re-run the rule chain and show exactly what moved and why.

**Entered from.** A panel on S-02.3, anchored at the cost line it applies to, plus a claim-level list reached from the tab header and from the work-list flag `CÓ_KHUYẾN_NGHỊ`. It is not a separate screen: a recommendation is about one cost line, and the line is on tab 3.

**Who may open it.** `ASSESSOR` **F**, `APPROVER` **R**, scope `ASSIGNED` (A3 §2.1 F56). Rejecting requires a reason, and **both outcomes are recorded against the recommendation** (BR-TRACK-6).

#### 5.8.1 Field table — one panel per recommendation

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Dòng chi phí | `derived` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F2 | Khoản mục | `text(300)` | `idp:I-09` | M | — | — |
| F3 | Mã lý do đề xuất | `enum(declineReason)` | `idp:I-16` | M | — | — |
| F4 | Diễn giải | `textarea(2000)` | `idp:I-16` | M | — | — |
| F5 | Độ tin cậy | `derived` | `idp:I-16` | M | — | — |
| F6 | **Bằng chứng** | `derived` | `idp:I-16` | **M** | — | — |
| F7 | Phiên bản cơ sở tri thức | `text(30)` | `idp:I-16` | M | — | — |
| F8 | Quyết định của cán bộ thẩm định | `enum(recDecision)` | `user` | M | `XÁC_NHẬN` · `BÁC_BỎ` | `CLM-CONSOLE-013` while any remains undecided |
| F9 | Lý do bác bỏ | `textarea(2000)` | `user` | C — **mandatory** when F8 = `BÁC_BỎ` | A3 §2.1 F56; the text is the knowledge base's feedback signal (BR-KB-3) | `CLM-CONSOLE-014` |
| F10 | Đồng thuận | `derived` | `system` | M | — | — |

**Notes on the fields above.** F1 to F7 and F10 are written by the platform or returned by IDP; the assessor enters only F8 and F9, so only those two carry a validation and an error path (§2.2).

- **F1** is `lineNo`, joined to the claim's own cost line. **A recommendation is never claim-level** (D1 §5.10.3).
- **F2** repeats the line's item name and amount so that the panel stands alone.
- **F3 is `NOTREL` or `NOTCOV` only.** Any other code is rejected at the adapter and never reaches this panel (D3 §I-16).
- **F4** is Vietnamese and patient-readable — it is the basis of what the customer will eventually be told (A2 §4).
- **F5** shows the score and the band `HIGH` / `MEDIUM` / `LOW`, both.
- **F6** is the cited knowledge-base entries with their summaries and the diagnosis relied on. **Empty evidence is a malformed response, not a low-confidence one** (BR-KB-2, D3 §I-16) — such a result never reaches this panel.
- **F7** is `knowledgeBaseVersion`, pinned on the claim (BR-KB-4) and displayed, because a claim assessed today must be explainable when the base has moved.
- **F10** records whether the decision agreed with the recommendation — **BR-TRACK-6**, and the input to the agreement rate (SC-09, B-16).

**F6 is not optional and not collapsible.** An assessor being asked to decline a customer's medication needs to see *why*, and *"the model said so"* is not a basis on which a person can take responsibility for a decision (D1 §5.10.3). With no clinical reviewer behind the knowledge base (B-13, RK-08), the evidence trail is the only thing standing between a recommendation and an unexplainable decline.

#### 5.8.2 Confirmation re-runs the chain — and what the assessor sees change

**BR-TRACK-4: the line's decline is applied and the rule chain is re-run in full — not patched.** Limits, ancestors, co-payment and the deduction ratio all recompute against the reduced base. Patching would leave the arithmetic dependent on the order the assessor clicked in.

**The failure mode this screen is written against is a total that moves without explanation.** A number that changes on screen with no account of why is how an assessor stops trusting the engine, and it is how an approver approves something nobody can reconstruct. So the re-run is not silent. On confirmation, the console shows, in this order:

| # | What is shown |
|---|---|
| 1 | A banner: **the chain is re-running**, naming the line just confirmed. NFR-3 bounds it at 2 seconds, so this is a state, not a progress bar to watch |
| 2 | The line's own change: `CHI_TRẢ` → `TỪ_CHỐI`, reason code `NOTREL`/`NOTCOV`, and the rationale carried from F4 into L15 — where it is then subject to V-531 and V-532 like any other decline text |
| 3 | **A before-and-after column on §5.9's step table**, for every benefit path whose base changed. Each step that produced a different number is highlighted, with both figures |
| 4 | **The total, old → new, with the delta and its cause stated in one line:** *"Giảm {delta} do dòng {lineNo} bị từ chối theo khuyến nghị đã được xác nhận."* |
| 5 | The ledger effect: the provisional posting is **reversed and re-posted**, never edited in place (BR-LEDGER-3) |
| 6 | Any warning the re-run newly raised — most often `CLM-CONSOLE-003` where a cap that was binding no longer binds, or the reverse |

> **One arithmetic consequence must be stated on the screen, because it surprises everybody the first time.** The total does **not** fall by the declined line's amount. The line is removed from the base *before* co-payment and the deduction ratio, so the insurer's share falls by less than the line — on the A5 §6.2 figures, declining a 400,000 line reduces the payable by 320,000 after a 20% co-payment, not by 400,000. The delta line in row 4 above therefore names the base it was computed on, and §5.9's step table shows the co-payment recomputed. An assessor who expects an exact subtraction and sees a smaller one will otherwise conclude the engine is wrong.

#### 5.8.3 The three outcomes from IDP

| Track 2 returned | What the console shows | What follows |
|---|---|---|
| **One or more recommendations** | The panels above; `CLM-CONSOLE-013` naming the count; the work-list flag `CÓ_KHUYẾN_NGHỊ`; submission blocked until each is confirmed or rejected (§5.10.2 check 5, V-589) | The chain re-runs on what was confirmed (BR-TRACK-4). **Auto-approval cannot fire** — condition 2 requires *no recommendation* |
| **Nothing, having assessed every line** — `state = COMPLETE` and `linesAssessed` covers them all | *"Đánh giá phù hợp y khoa đã hoàn tất, không có khuyến nghị."* No panel, no action, no block | **Nobody needs to decide anything.** The payable came from Track 1's deterministic chain alone — no AI judgement entered the number — so the claim may **auto-approve** if condition 1 also holds (D1 §5.8) |
| **Nothing, because it failed, timed out or skipped lines** | **`CLM-CONSOLE-015`** — *"The clinical assessment did not complete for this claim. It has **not** been assessed as clean."* Banner on the claim, flag on the work list, and lines outside `linesAssessed` marked **"chưa được đánh giá"** — visually distinct from "không có khuyến nghị" | Claim proceeds on **Track 1 alone**, with a human (BR-TRACK-5). **Auto-approval cannot fire** — BR-AUTO-3 |

**BR-AUTO-3 carries the weight and this screen is where it is visible.** An empty recommendation array and a failed assessment look identical to a naive check and mean opposite things. The console never renders them the same way: one says *hoàn tất, không có khuyến nghị*, the other says *chưa hoàn tất*, and the second is a flag.

| Failure | Console behaviour |
|---|---|
| `I-16` returns `409 NOT_READY` | Adapter retries on `Retry-After` (D3 §1.3, D3 §1.5). The panel shows *đang đánh giá*. **An adapter that treats this as an ordinary `4xx` loses Track 2 on every claim that took longer than one round trip** |
| `state = PARTIAL` | A result, not an error. Assessed lines show their outcome; unassessed lines are marked so, and `CLM-CONSOLE-015` is raised for the gap |
| `state = ERROR`, `503`, or the 30-minute ceiling in NFR-2a | Track 1 alone, `CLM-CONSOLE-015`, no auto-approval. **Never a decline** (G-3) |
| `422` — unknown `serviceCategory` or `knowledgeBaseVersion` | Rejected at the adapter; treated as a failed assessment, not as a clean one |

#### 5.8.4 Actions

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Xác nhận khuyến nghị** | `ASSESSOR` | Claim not locked; the panel is showing evidence | Line declined with F3's code and F4's rationale; **rule chain re-runs in full**; §5.8.2's sequence is shown; agreement recorded | — |
| **Bác bỏ khuyến nghị** | `ASSESSOR` | F9 entered | Recommendation rejected with the reason; **no amount changes**; disagreement recorded against the recommendation and against its knowledge-base entries (BR-KB-3) | `CLM-CONSOLE-014` prompts for the reason |
| **Xem bằng chứng** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER` | — | Expands the cited entries and the diagnosis relied on | — |
| **Đánh dấu đã xem cảnh báo đánh giá lâm sàng** | `ASSESSOR` | `CLM-CONSOLE-015` raised | Acknowledged; required before submission (§5.10.2 check 6, V-590) | `CLM-CONSOLE-015` |

#### 5.8.5 Advisory mode — what would change

D1 §5.11 records **advisory mode** as the reduction that costs least if delivery pressure arrives: recommendations shown to the assessor and recorded, but not wired into the settlement. It is a configuration switch, and this section states its effect precisely so that turning it on is not an improvisation.

| Aspect | Live | Advisory |
|---|---|---|
| Panels, evidence, confidence | Shown | **Shown, unchanged** |
| Confirm / reject with a reason | Recorded | **Recorded, unchanged** — BR-TRACK-6's agreement rate still measured, which is the point of keeping it |
| Effect of confirmation on the line | Line declined | **None.** The panel says so explicitly |
| Rule-chain re-run | Yes — §5.8.2 | **No.** Nothing in §5.8.2 fires |
| Reducing a line anyway | via confirmation | The assessor may still decline the line on §5.6 **as their own decision**, recorded as such and not as an agreement |
| Submission blocked until each is decided | Yes | **Yes** — the decision is still the measurement |
| **Auto-approval** | Condition 2 satisfiable | **Condition 2 is unsatisfiable, so the gate never fires** (Framework RK-13) — and condition 3 is independent of it. Every claim reaches an assessor and SC-04 rests on assessor throughput alone |

**Everything in D1 §5.10.6 defers with it**, and nothing about the screen's shape changes — which is what makes advisory mode a switch rather than a rebuild.

---

### 5.9 Benefit calculation and the limit ledger (F48)

**Purpose.** Show the settlement as a calculation rather than as a number: every step of the chain, the base it worked on, the parameter it used and what it did — so that the payable amount can be explained rather than merely reported.

**Entered from.** S-02, tab 5. The views below are also refreshed automatically after the **system-triggered first chain run** (§5.11.4), after *Tính toán lại* on §5.6, and after a confirmation on §5.8.

**Who may open it.** `ASSESSOR` **F**, `APPROVER` **R**, scope `ASSIGNED` (A3 §2.1 F48). **There is no permission to apply a deduction ratio** — A3 §2.1 states it as a struck row, and the console has no control for it (D1 B-09).

**This is BO-3 made visible.** A system that extracts perfectly and then asks a human what to pay has automated the typing and left the work; a system that computes a number nobody can reproduce has done something worse. The screen's job is to make the arithmetic legible.

#### 5.9.1 The step view — fourteen steps, per cost line

One block per cost line, each block one row per step. The steps, their applicability and their base amounts are A5 §6.1 and D1 §5.3; **the console renders them and configures nothing.**

| Column | Type | Source | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bước | `int` | `system` | 1 … 14, always in order, **always all fourteen** |
| Tên bước | `text(100)` | `system` | A5 §6.1's names |
| Kết quả | `enum(stepOutcome)` | `system` | **A1 §4.10's four values** — `ÁP_DỤNG` · `BỎ_QUA` (switched off) · `KHÔNG_ÁP_DỤNG` (the benefit carries nothing for this step to act on) · `KHÔNG_ĐẠT` (the step declined or reduced). **Until A1 v1.5 this document defined the four here, inside a screen table, which §2.3 forbids** — A1 has taken the set and this row cites it (`D2-174`, closed). **None of the four means *could not be evaluated***, which `V-754` needs and which is asked of A1 as `D2-181` |
| Cơ sở tính | `derived` | `system` | **The amount entering the step**, in integer dong. Stated for every step, because ambiguity about the base is the commonest defect in health claim specifications (A5 §6.2) |
| Tham số | `derived` | `snapshot` / `config` | The rate, limit, count or list the step applied, with its origin — the benefit node, the ledger, or configuration |
| Tác động | `derived` | `system` | The reduction, in integer dong, signed, or "—" |
| Còn lại | `derived` | `system` | The amount leaving the step, in integer dong, **rounded to the nearest whole dong, half away from zero, at this step** (D1 §5.3, A5 §6.2) |
| Diễn giải | `text(300)` | `system` | One sentence naming what happened, in the same terms the settlement letter will use |

**Two amounts this table produces are named, because the rest of Part V now refers to them.**

| Name | Definition | Where it appears |
|---|---|---|
| **Số tiền thuộc phạm vi bảo hiểm** | **The amount leaving step 6** — after the line-by-line pay/decline decision and before any cap, co-payment or deduction touches it. It is the amount the policy accepts as a claim, distinct from the amount it pays on it | §5.9.2 per benefit, §5.10.1's grid, and the frozen plan (V-716) |
| **Khách hàng tự trả** | Claimed less payable, per benefit and per claim — what the customer is left carrying after every declined line, every cap, the co-payment and the deduction | The same three places, on the same rows |

**On the first of the two — register row S-22, applied in a reduced form.** The reference gives this number a name and shows it on both its event grid and its settlement grid, and it is the figure their limit check runs against. **We name it and show it on the settlement side only.** It exists in this document today as *"còn lại sau bước 6"* in a fourteen-row table, which is a coordinate rather than a name, and a number that only has a coordinate cannot be quoted in a conversation, a letter or a defect report. **What is omitted is the per-cost-line rendering**: §5.6.3 L25 already carries the line's payable, the step table already shows step 6 per line, and a second per-line money column that differs from the first only before step 8 invites the reading that one of them is the answer.

**Step 8's basis is the count the insured event consumed, and until v0.3 it had none.** Step 8 applies `maxCount` and `countUnit` from the benefit node (A5 §6.1, BR-TREE-4). The quantity it compares against is **§5.7.2 F17**, the event's treatment-day count where the unit is days, and the sum of the allocated lines' L3 where the unit is occurrences. **Both readings need §5.6.3 L17**: a count is per event, and a line that belongs to no event contributes to no count. The row therefore states which unit it applied and which event's count it read.

**Three display rules that are not cosmetic:**

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| **V-540** | **Every step is shown, including the ones that did nothing.** A step that is skipped is evidence: step 11 absent from the display is indistinguishable from step 11 applied at 0%, and A5 §4.3 is explicit that a met-nothing condition means *no deduction*, not a zero-rate deduction |
| **V-541** | **Rounding is shown at each step.** The chain rounds at every money-producing step, not once at the end, because BR-TRACK-4 re-runs it and a chain that rounded only at the end could return a different total on the same inputs |
| **V-542** | **A bound cap is explained, always** — BR-TREE-5. Where a limit reduced the payable, the row states the benefit, the remaining limit and the reduction, and that same text flows into `CLM-LETTER-001`. **Capping is allowed; capping silently is not**. **From v0.6 this covers a term `CAP` as well** — `BR-TERM-12` makes a term-stated ceiling a limit bound like any other (§5.28.3 F11, `V-755`) |
| **V-754** | **A step the chain cannot evaluate is never rendered as a pass** — D1 v0.5 **`BR-CHAIN-1`**. Where a fact the step requires is unavailable — a treatment-day count extraction did not return (`Q-IDP-06`), a line-level ICD that is not there (`Q-IDP-02`) — **the line is held, a checkpoint is raised at §5.29 naming the missing fact, and the claim is outside the auto-approval gate by condition 3.** It is **not** a decline: an absent fact is a data problem, and §2.10's distinction between failing to *find* something and failing to *satisfy* it applies to a fact exactly as it applies to a policy. **The step row states the missing fact in its *Diễn giải* cell** rather than leaving the *Tác động* column at zero, because a step that quietly passed and a step that could not run look identical in a total. **A1 §4.10's `stepOutcome` carries four values and none of them means *could not be evaluated*** — the row renders `KHÔNG_ĐẠT`, which is the nearest of the four and is not the right one, and **a fifth value is owed to A1 as `D2-181`** |

#### 5.9.1a The terms tested — every one of them, fired or not (F66)

*(New at v0.5. D1 §5.3.1 **BR-TERM-1**; *Solution Paper* §4.1; decisions **D-2** and **D-3**, 24 August 2026.)*

**Steps 4 and 7 are the two steps whose parameter is data rather than code.** Until v0.5 the step table rendered each of them as one row whose *Tham số* cell read *"A5 §7"* — a pointer to ten sentences of prose. That cell said what the engine **consulted**. It did not say what the engine **found**, and it could not, because there was nothing structured for it to find (D1 §5.3.1). With the term register there is, and this panel is where it is shown.

**Every term in scope is evaluated and the result of every term is recorded, whether it fired or not.** The panel opens with one line, and that line is what an assessor reads first:

> **n điều khoản trong sổ · m đã xét · x từ chối · y điểm kiểm · z đạt · k không thuộc phạm vi**

**Six figures, and the identity between them is stated because a header line that does not add up is worse than no header line.**

| Figure | What it counts |
|---|---|
| **n** — *trong sổ* | Every term registered against the claim's `ruleSetRef`, **whatever its status**. It is the denominator an auditor asks about |
| **m** — *đã xét* | Every term **actually evaluated**: `ACTIVE`, inside its effective window, bound to the claim's `ruleSetRef`. **`n − m` is the drafts and the withdrawn versions**, and the panel says so rather than leaving a reader to subtract |
| **x** — *từ chối* | `TỪ_CHỐI` — the term declined the line or the event |
| **y** — *điểm kiểm* | `ĐIỂM_KIỂM` — a checkpoint was raised |
| **z** — *đạt* | `ĐẠT` — in play, tested, did not fire |
| **k** — *không thuộc phạm vi* | `KHÔNG_THUỘC_PHẠM_VI` — the selector did not match, so the term was never in play |

**The identity is `x + y + z + k = m`, and `m ≤ n`.** v0.5's header read *"14 điều khoản đã xét · 1 từ chối · 2 điểm kiểm · 11 đạt"* — three outcomes summing to the total, **with nowhere for `KHÔNG_THUỘC_PHẠM_VI` to go**, which is the fourth value of `termOutcome` (A1 §4.10) and on a typical claim the largest of the four. A term whose selector did not match was being counted as though it had passed, and *"considered and not applicable"* is a different answer from *"tested and satisfied"* — an auditor is owed the difference (A5 §7.5).

**The `KHÔNG_THUỘC_PHẠM_VI` group is collapsed by default and the other three are expanded.** It is the group that grows with the register and the one that carries no work; collapsing it is what keeps the panel legible on a product with forty terms, and the count is on the header line whether the group is open or not.

**Why the passes are shown and not only the hits.** Two readers need them and neither is served by a list of hits. **An assessor who sees only the first hit cannot tell whether the case was close** — a claim that failed one term of fourteen and a claim that failed one term of one are different claims and look identical on a hit list. **And an auditor asking *"was clause 5.2 considered?"* must get an answer**, and the answer must not be *"we stopped before we got there."* This is BR-TERM-1, and it is the reason the engine evaluates all rather than stopping at first match.

**The panel — one row per term, under the step it was evaluated at.**

| Column | Type | Source | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bước | `int` | `system` | **4** or **7** — the step the term was evaluated at. The panel groups on it, so a product exclusion and a benefit proviso are never read as one list |
| Mã điều khoản | `text(20)` | `snapshot` | `termId`, **with the version that was evaluated** — not the version in force today (BR-TERM-4, P-02). Opens the term read-only at §5.28 |
| Điều khoản | `text(20)` | `snapshot` | `clauseRef` — the clause number in the wording the customer is holding, e.g. *Art. 5.2(c)* |
| Tiêu đề | `text(200)` | `snapshot` | `titleVi`. The full clause text is one click away and is quoted verbatim (§5.29.2) |
| Loại | `enum(termClass)` | `snapshot` | `D` · `J` · `E`. **Rendered as a class, not as a colour** — an assessor must be able to see that a term *could not* have declined |
| Phạm vi | `enum(termScope)` | `snapshot` | `PRODUCT` · `BENEFIT` · `BENEFIT_SUBTREE`, with the code. Says which line or event the term was tested against |
| Căn cứ chọn | `derived` | `system` | **The facts the `selector` matched on**, named and valued — `serviceCategory = SUPPLEMENT`, `benefitCode = 200.2`. This is what makes the row checkable rather than assertable |
| Kết quả | `enum(termOutcome)` | `system` | `ĐẠT` (tested, did not fire) · `TỪ_CHỐI` (the term declined — only ever a class-`D` term whose effect is `DECLINE_EVENT` or `DECLINE_LINE`) · `ĐIỂM_KIỂM` (a checkpoint was raised — §5.29; **any class may produce it**, §5.28.1a) · `KHÔNG_THUỘC_PHẠM_VI` (the selector did not match, so the term was never in play) |
| Tác động | `derived` | `system` | The line or the event the result attached to, and the money effect where there is one, signed. `—` where there is none |

**Note on the columns above.** Every cell is written by the platform from the evaluation record retained under D1 §5.3.1, so no row on this panel carries a *Req* or an *On error* — it is a rendering of a record, exactly as §5.9.1's step table is, and §5.9.1's four-column shape is the one it follows. **The panel is read-only for every role.** Nothing on it is a control: a checkpoint is worked at §5.29 and a term is authored at §5.28, and putting either action here would put a master-data edit inside a claim.

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| **V-752** | **The *đã xét* count excludes every `DRAFT` and every `WITHDRAWN` term.** A `DRAFT` term is invisible to the engine (`V-735`, A1 §4.10 `termStatus`): it is not evaluated, it produces no `termOutcome`, and it is not counted. **On the pilot product four of the ten registered terms are `DRAFT`** — two waiting on `Q-IDP-02`, one on `Q-IDP-05`, one on a document type A4 does not carry — **so `n` is ten and `m` is six** (A5 §7.5). A panel that counted ten would be telling an assessor that four terms had been considered when the engine had never looked at them, which is the same class of untruth as counting only the hits. **The rule is stated in one place and cited from two** — here and at §5.9.7 requirement 1 — because two documents that count differently produce two different answers to *"was clause `TBC-06` considered?"* |
| **V-729** | **Every term in scope is displayed, including every term that passed and every term whose selector did not match** — and the header line carries all **six** counts, never only the hits (**BR-TERM-1**). A panel that lists hits alone is indistinguishable from a panel on a claim where nothing was tested, which is the failure this rule exists to prevent. **And every hit carries its `clauseRef` into the decline message — all of them, not only the first** (BR-TERM-2): a line declined on two clauses is declined on two clauses, and a letter citing one of them is a letter the customer can answer by disproving the wrong clause. **A2 cannot carry this today and the gap is named rather than assumed away** — `EXCL` binds a single `{exclusionRef}` and `CLM-LETTER-002`'s *Basis* section is written in the singular — **`D2-178`** |

> **What this panel costs and what it buys, because the cost is real.** A claim touching a product with forty terms renders forty rows on a screen an assessor is reading under time pressure, and the grouping, the default collapse of the `KHÔNG_THUỘC_PHẠM_VI` group and UI-19's truncation rules are what keep it legible. **What it buys is the only defensible answer to the question a disputed decline always asks**, which is not *"why did you decline"* — the letter says that — but *"what else did you look at."*

> **Step 7 has no instance on the pilot product, and an empty step-7 group is the expected state.** All ten terms in A5 §7.2's register are `PRODUCT` scope, so **the term engine is called at step 7 and evaluates an empty set on every claim of this product** (D1 v0.5 §5.3, `B-23`). The panel therefore renders the step-7 group with UI-25's *nothing exists yet* sentence — *"không có điều khoản riêng của quyền lợi trên sản phẩm này"* — **and not as an absent group**, because an absent group and an empty one look identical and mean opposite things. **No proviso is invented here to give the step something to do**: D1 asks the business for a real one as **`B-23`**, and until it lands the step is a mechanism with nothing to run, exactly as step 13 is.

#### 5.9.2 The roll-up view

| Level | Columns |
|---|---|
| Per cost line | **Insured event (L17)**, item, billed, claimed (`L5 − L6`), decision, payable (L25), **and the assessor's note (L24)** |
| **Per benefit** | **Insured event**; benefit code and name, indented by `depth`; **annual sum insured**; **remaining in the year before this claim**; **remaining in the year after this claim**; **remaining per occurrence**; **remaining days**; **co-payment rate**; claimed; **in-scope amount**; capped; co-payment; **deduction rate**; deduction; payable; **customer-borne**; and the ancestor path each amount consumed |
| Per insured event | Event number, provider, in/out of network, **occurrence date, treatment range and day count**, event total, and the deduction condition where one was met |
| Claim | Total claimed, **total in-scope**, total payable, **total customer-borne**, and the count of declined lines |

**Every grid on this screen that carries a money column carries a total row**, rendered under the body and excluded from sorting. Stated because it was absent and because a settlement grid without a total is the one table a reader will add up by hand.

**The sources, since the row mixes three.** *Annual sum insured*, *remaining per occurrence*, *co-payment rate* and *deduction rate* are `snapshot` — the schedule as at the service date, never re-read (§5.2.4). *Remaining before* and *remaining after* are `system`, read from the ledger, and they **keep V-543's labelling**: *before* is the sum insured less **final** consumption, and *after* subtracts this claim's provisional posting and is labelled as provisional. The two are never blended into one figure, here or anywhere (§5.9.3). *Remaining days* is `system` and exists only because **S-09** gave the ledger a count to hold.

**Why the limits belong beside the arithmetic — register row S-26, with S-22 and G-V-07 folded into the same pass because all three touch this grid.** The three facts an assessor needs to price a benefit — the limit, what is left of it, and what this claim did to it — were in three places: the pinned tree at §5.4.3, the ledger at §5.9.3 behind a click, and this roll-up, **which carried no limit column at all**. The roll-up is the only grid that shows what a benefit produced, and it did not show the headroom that production was measured against. §5.9.4's own worked example makes the case better than an argument does: **three of the four things the screen "says out loud" on that claim are about a limit that bound**, and the grid that says them carried no limit. **The ledger at §5.9.3 is unchanged and stays the full record**; what is added here is the summary beside the number it explains. This also closes **X-1** — the prototype's settlement grid has carried these columns since 23 August 2026.

**BR-TREE-2 is visible here.** Where a composite and one of its own sub-limits both apply to the same line, the composite consumption is counted **once**, and the roll-up shows the single posting against each ancestor rather than one per level.

#### 5.9.3 The limit ledger panel (S-11)

**Register row `S-11`, and it gains a dimension at v0.5.** The panel listed, for a member, the sum insured, the count limit, the total paid, the days paid, the remaining amount and the remaining days — **six figures with no period against any of them**. Nothing in D1 or D2 had defined what *"annual"* meant operationally, so the panel was displaying a number whose window was undefined. D1 §5.9.1's **`L-1` … `L-4`** define it, and the panel carries it: **the counter period is the policy year**, derived from the policy inception date on the snapshot and **not** the calendar year (`L-1`); a cost line posts to the period containing its **treatment date**, never its submission date (`L-2`); and **a claim whose lines span a period boundary posts to two periods, line by line** (`L-3`).

| Column | Type | Source | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Kỳ hạn mức** | **`text(20)`** | **`system`** | **`periodKey` — the policy year the row's figures belong to**, rendered as its two dates, e.g. *01/04/2026 – 31/03/2027*. **Derived from the policy inception date on the snapshot, never from the calendar year** (`L-1`). **New at v0.5** |
| Mã quyền lợi | `text(20)` | `snapshot` | The tree, indented |
| Tên quyền lợi | `text(200)` | `snapshot` | |
| Số tiền bảo hiểm năm | `money` | `snapshot` | Blank where capped by the parent |
| Đã sử dụng (chính thức) | `money` | `system` | Final consumption — approved claims only |
| Đang giữ (tạm) | `money` | `system` | **This claim's provisional posting**, labelled separately and never merged into the line above |
| Hạn mức còn lại | `derived` | `system` | Sum insured − final consumption, in integer dong. **Provisional consumption is invisible to other in-flight claims** (BR-LEDGER-2) |
| Số lần / số ngày: giới hạn · đã dùng · còn lại | `derived` | `system` | Whole counts. `0` renders **"Không giới hạn"** (BR-TREE-4) |
| **Số lần / số ngày đang giữ (tạm)** | `int` | `system` | **The count this claim is holding provisionally** — the sum of §5.7.2 F17 over the claim's events where the unit is days, and of the allocated lines' quantities where it is occurrences. Labelled separately from the row above and **never merged into it**, on exactly the reasoning V-543 applies to money. **New in v0.3 — S-09** |
| Phiên bản | `int` | `system` | The counter's optimistic-concurrency version — **per counter and therefore per `counterType`**, so an `AMOUNT` counter and a `DAY` counter on one benefit version independently (BR-LEDGER-5) |

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| **V-543** | **Provisional at calculation, final at approval** (BR-LEDGER-1, G-2). The panel labels the two separately and never shows a single blended figure, because the difference is what a concurrent claim can and cannot see |
| **V-544** | **Consumption is never deleted — only reversed or offset** (BR-LEDGER-3). No action on any screen in Part V deletes a consumption record |
| **V-545** | A single payment posts to **every counter on the ancestor path**, with BR-TREE-2 applied (BR-LEDGER-6) |
| **V-723** | **The ledger counter is keyed on `(memberId, policyId, benefitCode, periodKey, counterType)`, where `counterType ∈ {AMOUNT, OCCURRENCE, DAY}`** — five parts, and it was three until v0.3 and four until v0.5. **`periodKey` and `counterType` are added at v0.5** (D1 §5.9.2, `L-4`, decisions **D-7** and **D-8**): without `periodKey` the counter is not unique across policy years and a member's second-year claims consume their first-year allowance; without `counterType` the `count_limit` and `per_day_cap` that sit on all 51 benefit rows, and that **chain step 9 tests**, are counted against a money counter that cannot express them — which is how the panel came to display *"remaining days"* that no rule produced. `OCCURRENCE` increments by one per qualifying event; `DAY` increments by the treatment-day count of the line (§5.7.2 F17), **which extraction does not return today — `Q-IDP-06`**, so a benefit limited in days is not fully enforceable until it does. **BR-LEDGER-1 … 6 apply to all three counter types, not to money alone.** The earlier reasoning stands unchanged and is kept: v0.2 keyed the counter on the member and the benefit alone (D1 §7.4), which is correct for one policy per member and silently wrong for two: a member covered under an employer group policy and a personal policy would consume one annual sum insured across both, and neither insurer's limit would be the one enforced. **The policy number is on the claim's snapshot already** (§5.4.2 F17) and adding it to the key costs nothing at MVP 1 volumes. **Reduced from S-27**: the reference adds a **second** key to its *remaining per occurrence* counter — provider plus treatment-date range, its reconstructed identity of one visit. **We do not**, because after **S-07** a cost line carries its insured event explicitly (§5.6.3 L17), and a remaining-per-occurrence figure computed from the event we recorded is better than one computed from an identity inferred from two attributes. **What is not adopted is the inference, not the figure** |
| **V-546** | On a version clash — two claims for the same member adjudicating at once — the calculation is **re-run against the current counters** and the assessor is told the figures moved and why. **It is never silently merged** *(new A2 item needed — **D2-67**)*. **BR-LEDGER-8 states the half that is easiest to implement wrongly**: the retry must **re-run adjudication**, not re-post the figure the first pass computed. The figure is a function of the counter the write collided with, so replaying it breaches the limit by a race |
| **V-730** | **The panel is keyed on the period and a claim that spans a boundary shows a figure per period, never one number** (`L-1`, `L-3`). Where the claim's lines fall in two policy years the tree renders **twice, once per `periodKey`**, each with its own sum insured, consumption and remaining, and the two are **never summed into a single remaining figure**. There is no such number: the member has one allowance in each year and adding them describes an allowance nobody has. On a policy-year basis every member's boundary falls on a different day, so this is an ordinary case rather than a December edge case |
| **V-731** | **The remaining figure is labelled *final consumption only*, on the figure and not in a footnote** (BR-LEDGER-2). *"Hạn mức còn lại — chỉ tính các hồ sơ đã duyệt"*. An assessor who reads it as *available* will be surprised when a concurrent claim approves first, and the surprise arrives as a settlement that moved between assessment and approval. **The provisional hold of this claim is shown beside it and is never blended into it** (V-543), and provisional holds of *other* in-flight claims are not shown at all, because they are not visible to this claim |

> **What the two-phase ledger costs, stated here because §5.9.3 states the rule and not the consequence.** Provisional consumption is invisible to other in-flight claims (V-543, BR-LEDGER-2), so **two claims for the same member assessed at the same moment both see the full remaining limit and both compute a full payable.** When the first is approved, the second's figures move, and **V-546** is the mechanism: the chain re-runs against the current counters and the assessor is told what changed and why. The second assessor has by then done work against a number that was going to move. That is the price, and it buys something more expensive than it costs — **two claims can never both be approved into a total that exceeds the annual limit**, which is what a model where provisional holds are visible cannot guarantee without a hold-expiry mechanism MVP 1 does not have. Reference System A takes the other side of this trade and deducts every non-cancelled claim including the unapproved ones; the register records the comparison as **S-28** and the decision as unchanged. A reader who knows the other model would otherwise read V-543 as an omission.

**Why final at approval and not at payment.** An approved claim has committed the limit. A second claim adjudicating at the same moment must see that commitment, not a provisional figure that might evaporate — otherwise two legitimately approved claims jointly exceed an annual limit (D1 §5.9, D3 G-2).

| `200.2` Thuốc kê đơn và thực phẩm chức năng | 1.300.000 | 1.000.000 | −200.000 | **800.000** | *(theo `200`)* | 800.000 | — |
| **`200` Điều trị ngoại trú** | 3.000.000 | 2.500.000 | −500.000 | **2.000.000** | 20.000.000 | 2.000.000 | **18.000.000** |

**Four things this screen says out loud on this claim**, each with its own banner:

1. **Both children were capped.** *"Hạn mức 1.500.000 đ mỗi lần khám của quyền lợi 200.1 đã áp dụng; giảm 200.000 đ."* and the same sentence for `200.2` at 1.000.000 đ, giảm 300.000 đ. BR-TREE-5 — a bound cap is explained here and in `CLM-LETTER-001`, every time.
2. **The cap is per benefit, not on the claim total.** `200.1` and `200.2` each breach their own per-visit cap by a different amount. An engine that capped 3.000.000 at 1.500.000 would under-pay by 1.000.000 and look, from the outside, exactly like one that got it right (A5 §6.2).
3. **This claim does not auto-approve, and it fails two conditions rather than one.** The payable is **exactly at** the 2.000.000 threshold, so the arithmetic half of condition 1 passes — **and its second clause fails, because a limit bound at step 8**. **Condition 3 fails as well**: `TERM-HC-003` raised a checkpoint on line 4 and nobody has answered it. The claim reaches an assessor — *(new A2 item needed — **D2-61**)*, naming **both** failing conditions rather than the first. **A cheap claim is not automatically a clean one.**
4. **Six terms of ten were tested, one raised a checkpoint, and five were never in play** — and the screen says all of that rather than saying nothing (§5.9.1a, **V-729**, **V-752**, BR-TERM-1). *"Was clause `TBC-06` considered?"* is answerable on this claim without opening anything: it was, and it did not select. **Four terms were not tested and the header says so too** — `n − m` is four `DRAFT` rows, not four passes.

> **Re-cut at v0.6 against A5 v1.5, and `D2-157` closes with it.** The example above was A5 v1.3's and diverged from the product in three ways, each of which changed a number a reader would have taken as demonstrated. **(a)** It showed *"10 điều khoản đã xét"* when four of the ten seed rows are `DRAFT` and a draft term is invisible to the engine — the true count is **six** (A5 §7.5, `V-752`). **(b)** It showed *"2 điều khoản đã xét"* at step 7 when **there are no `BENEFIT`-scope terms on this product at all**, so the honest figure is zero and the group is empty. **(c)** Its note 4 concluded that the claim satisfied the gate, when `TERM-HC-003` selects on line 4's `SUPPLEMENT` and raises a checkpoint — so condition 3 fails and the claim was never a candidate. **`SUPPLEMENT` also left §8.1's decline column at A5 v1.4**: line 4 now maps to `200.2`, is not declined at step 6, and is priced into `200.2`'s per-visit cap, which is why the payable moves from 1.920.000 to 2.000.000.
>
> **One thing the re-cut does *not* change, and it is worth naming.** `TERM-HC-002` — health checks, screening and vaccination — selects on `serviceCategory in [SCREENING, VACCINATION]` and **not** on `SUPPLEMENT`, so on this claim it reports `KHÔNG_THUỘC_PHẠM_VI` rather than raising a second checkpoint. It is recorded here as a checked fact rather than an assumed one, because the two terms are neighbours in the register and reading one for the other is the easiest mistake available on this page.
>
> **And no term on this register could have declined line 4 in any case — `BR-TERM-10`.** Every `clauseRef` in A5 §7.2 is a provisional `TBC-nn`, and a term whose clause reference is provisional raises a checkpoint instead of declining, whatever its class and whatever its effect (§5.28.3 F3, `V-743`). On the pilot product as it stands, **step 4's auto-decline branch cannot fire at all**, and this example is what that looks like on a screen.

**The same claim off network.** Had the provider been outside the listed network, step 11 would read `ÁP_DỤNG`, base 2.000.000, parameter *20% — điều kiện `PROVIDER_OFF_NETWORK`*, impact **−400.000**, remaining **1.600.000** — and 1.600.000, not 2.000.000, is what steps 12 and 14 carry (`200.1` 960.000, `200.2` 640.000). The condition either held or it did not; nothing about it is a judgement, and no control on this screen can change it.

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Tính toán lại** | `ASSESSOR` | Every cost line decided; every event assessed; claim not locked | Runs all fourteen steps; posts provisionally; refreshes both views | *(new A2 item — **D2-60**)* on a failed precondition |
| **Xem sổ hạn mức** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER` | — | Opens S-11 for the member | — |
| **Xem chi tiết bước** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER` | — | Expands a step to the per-line arithmetic and the parameter's origin | — |
| **Xuất bảng tính** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER` | — | The step table as CSV, for the claim file. Contains clinical detail, so the export is logged (BR-AUDIT-4) | — |

#### 5.9.6 Empty and error

| Condition | What the console shows |
|---|---|
| No calculation yet | The step table renders empty with *"Chưa tính toán"* and the action. **No zero total is displayed**, because zero is a meaningful answer and an absent answer is not |
| Inputs changed since the last run | The whole tab is marked **stale**, the total is greyed with *"cần tính toán lại"*, and submission is blocked (§5.10.2 check 8, **V-592**) |
| Ledger version clash | V-546 — re-run, told, never merged *(new A2 item — **D2-67**)* |
| A benefit node in the snapshot has no `waitingPeriodDays` entry for the event's condition class | Data error, not a zero wait: the calculation halts for that line and the claim is flagged (BR-WAIT-4) |
| The snapshot is absent | `CLM-CONSOLE-007` — escalate, do not proceed. No calculation is offered against a live read |

#### 5.9.7 The term evaluation service — what these two screens require of it (F66)

*(New at v0.5. **F66**, Priority 1. D1 §5.3.1; *Solution Paper* §3–§4; decision **D-3**.)*

**F66 has no screen of its own, on the same reasoning §5.1 gives for F52.** It is the engine behind steps 4 and 7 of the chain, and it surfaces in exactly three places: **§5.9.1a**, which renders what it did; **§5.29**, which works the checkpoints it raised; and **§5.11.4**, whose third gate condition it decides. Specifying it here rather than inventing an S-nn identifier for a thing with no user keeps §5.1's promise that a screen exists for every feature and no screen exists without one.

**What this document requires of it, and each line is a requirement a screen above cannot be built without.**

| # | Requirement | Why the console needs it |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Evaluate every term in scope, never first-match**, and return a result for each — `ĐẠT`, `TỪ_CHỐI`, `ĐIỂM_KIỂM`, `KHÔNG_THUỘC_PHẠM_VI` (BR-TERM-1, A1 §4.10 `termOutcome`). **In scope means `ACTIVE`, inside its effective window, bound to the claim's `ruleSetRef`: a `DRAFT` or `WITHDRAWN` term is not evaluated and produces no outcome** — `V-752`, `V-735` | §5.9.1a's six counts have no source otherwise, and V-729 and V-752 are both unenforceable. **The count must also return `n`, every term registered against the rule set** — without it `n − m` cannot be shown and the panel cannot say how many terms were *not* looked at |
| 2 | **Return the facts the `selector` matched on**, named and valued, per term | §5.9.1a's *Căn cứ chọn* column, and §5.29.2's *what it matched on* panel. A checkpoint an assessor cannot see the basis of is a task with no brief |
| 3 | **Return every `clauseRef` that fired on a line, in order**, not the first — **and the `textVi` of each, as it stood on the version evaluated** | BR-TERM-2, and `CLM-LETTER-002`'s citation list. A decline letter citing one of two clauses is answerable by disproving the wrong one. **A2 v1.1 cannot render a list**: `EXCL` binds one `{exclusionRef}` and `CLM-LETTER-002`'s *Basis* section says *"the clause … quoted"*, singular. The engine returns the list regardless — the gap is A2's and is **`D2-178`** |
| 4 | **Evaluate against the claim and the policy snapshot, never against live data**, and against the term versions **pinned onto the snapshot at registration** — `ruleSetRef` plus the register's own version identifier (P-02, BR-TERM-4, §5.2.4) | §5.9.1a renders *the version evaluated*, not the version in force today. A panel that re-read the register would show an approver a different claim from the one the assessor submitted. **v0.5 said *submission* here and *registration* at §5.4.2 F39, and the two are not the same instant** — D1 v0.5 settles it at **registration** and §5.2.4 now carries the row |
| 5 | **Be deterministic and order-independent** — same claim, same snapshot, same `ruleSetRef`, same result, always (BR-TERM-3) | BR-TRACK-4 re-runs the whole chain when a clinical recommendation is confirmed, and §5.8.2 shows the assessor a before-and-after. A non-deterministic engine makes that comparison meaningless |
| 6 | **Never auto-decline on a class-J or class-E term** (D1 §5.3.1) | It is the whole of the class model, and §5.29 exists because of it |
| 7 | **Retain every evaluation with the term version that produced it, for the life of the claim** | §5.14's trail, §5.21's frozen plan versions and §5.11.1 rows 4 and 9 all read it. An evaluation retained without its version answers *what happened* and not *against what* |
| **8** | **Never decline on a term whose `clauseRef` is provisional** — raise a checkpoint instead, whatever the term's class and whatever its effect (**`BR-TERM-10`**, `V-743`) | **On the pilot product this is every term**, so step 4's auto-decline branch does not fire at all today. An engine that ignored it would produce a decline letter quoting `TBC-03`, which is not a clause number — it is a placeholder somebody typed to fill a column |
| **9** | **Add the A4 document type of a `REQUIRE_DOC` term to the claim's checklist at `REQUIRED`, and raise a checkpoint that stays open until the document arrives or the requirement is waived** (**`BR-TERM-11`**, `V-756`) | §5.5.1's checklist has one key today and no mechanism by which a term can add a row — §5.29.2 F7 renders the requirement and the checklist does not carry it until A4 lands (**`D2-179`**) |
| **10** | **Hold, never pass, a step it cannot evaluate** (**`BR-CHAIN-1`**, `V-754`) | Passing is the path of least resistance and it favours the claimant silently: the line survives, nothing is cut, condition 1 of the gate is satisfied, and the claim settles unreviewed against a limit nobody enforced |

> **What F66 does not do, stated because a reader will look for it.** It does not author, version or approve a term — that is F65 at §5.28. It does not decide a checkpoint — that is a person at §5.29. And **it does not run against historical claims**: that is F68, which is Priority 2 and is not specified in this pass (**D2-158**). The consequence is named at §5.28.4 rather than left as an absence.
