### 5.10 Settlement plan (F49)

**Purpose.** Assemble everything the claim has become into one reviewable object, check that it is complete enough to be approved, and hand it over — after which the claim locks.

**Entered from.** S-02, tab 5, below §5.9's views.

**Who may open it.** `ASSESSOR` **F**, scope `ASSIGNED`. **The approver has no permission here at all** (A3 §2.1 F49) — assembling and submitting is the assessor's act, approving is the approver's, and that separation is the only control on the amount paid.

#### 5.10.1 What the plan contains

Assembled, not entered. Every row is `derived` from work already done, which is why the plan has no field table of its own beyond the two rows below.

| Section | Contents |
|---|---|
| Header | Claim, member, policy, plan, period, episode types, assessor, date, **the submission round number (V-716)**, and **the policy rule-set reference where one is recorded** (§5.4.2 F39) |
| **Parties** | **The insured member, the claimant — name, identity number, legal capacity and family relationship (§5.4.2 F34 to F37) — and the beneficiary.** Three rows, because the plan is the document a second reader checks the payment against, and *who is asking* and *who is paid* are different questions from *whose cover is used* |
| Per insured event | Event number, provider and network status, **occurrence date**, treatment dates, **day count**, ICD-10, condition class, cover decision, decline reason, **the liability rationale in the assessor's words**, and the deduction condition where one was met |
| Per benefit | §5.9.2's roll-up **in full**: the insured event, annual sum insured, remaining before and after, remaining per occurrence, remaining days, co-payment rate, claimed, **in-scope amount**, capped, co-payment, deduction rate, deduction, payable, **customer-borne**, and the ancestor path. **A total row under the grid** |
| Per cost line | **Insured event**, item, amount, decision, reason code, **the `clauseRef` of every term that fired on the line, in order** (BR-TERM-2), the final rationale **and the assessor's note (L24)** — **paid and declined lines in one table**, never an appendix (BR-LINE-4) |
| **Điều khoản đã xét** — the terms tested | **§5.9.1a's rows in full**, under the step each was evaluated at: `termId` with the version evaluated, `clauseRef`, title, class, scope, the facts the selector matched on, the outcome and the money effect — **and the six counts of §5.9.1a's header line, with `n − m` shown** (`V-729`, `V-752`). **Every checkpoint appears here with its outcome, its reason and who recorded it** (§5.29.2 F8 to F11), including one closed as moot. **New in v0.6 — `V-753`** |
| Clinical track | Each recommendation, its decision, the reason where rejected, the agreement flag, and the knowledge-base version (BR-TRACK-6, BR-KB-4) |
| Totals | Total claimed, **total in-scope**, total payable, **total customer-borne**, in figures and in words |
| Ledger effect | Provisional postings and the remaining limit per benefit group after this claim |
| Payee | Beneficiary, **the beneficiary's identity number and relationship**, masked account, `accountNameVerified`, **and against whom the verified name was compared (V-710)** |

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Ghi chú trình duyệt | `textarea(2000)` | `user` | O | — | — |
| F2 | Trạng thái trước khi trình | `enum(claimState)` | `system` | M | — | — |

**Notes on the two fields above.** F1 is the assessor's note to the approver: it is internal and is **never rendered to a customer**. F2 is **stored at submission and restored on return** (D1 §4.4) and is read-only on every screen. Neither carries a validation, so neither carries an error path (§2.2).

**V-753 — the plan carries the contractual basis of the settlement, and until v0.6 it did not.** The nine sections above were eight, and none of them held a term result. **`V-716` calls the frozen copy *"the only durable statement about a claim that has closed"*** — and it was freezing a settlement whose *arithmetic* was complete and whose *contractual basis* was somewhere else, in a panel on a live screen that reads the evaluation record. Six months after closure the panel is still there and the claim is not: it renders whatever the register says then. **Three consequences follow and all three are in this version:** §5.10.1 gains the **Điều khoản đã xét** section above; *Per cost line* gains a clause column, so a declined line names the clause on the same row as the money; and **§5.11.1 gains a ninth row** so the approver sees the term results as evidence rather than having to open a tab. **All of it flows into `V-716`'s frozen copy and `V-717`'s export unchanged** — the frozen version is the data and the export is one way of reading it, and neither needed a new mechanism, only a section it was missing.

#### 5.10.2 Validate — the thirteen checks

*Kiểm tra phương án* runs server-side and lists **every** failure at once, never the first one. Submission is refused until all **thirteen** pass. **Each check carries its own identifier** — they are cited from several screens and from Part VIII, and a set of rules referred to only as "the submission checks" cannot be traced.

| # | Rule | Check | Source of the rule | Message on failure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **V-585** | Every cost line carries a decision; every declined line a reason **and** a rationale naming the item and the amount | BR-LINE-1, A2 §4, V-520 | inline per line |
| 2 | **V-586** | The rationale on every declined line passes the B-14 wording rule | V-531, V-532 — **and see §5.29.3: `V-531` is not applied to an `EXCL` rationale produced by a term uphold while `D2-178` is open** | *(new A2 item — **D2-59**)* |
| 3 | **V-587** | Every insured event has ICD-10, condition class, a cover decision and a **liability rationale** | D1 §6.2 step 3 | inline per event |
| 4 | **V-588** | Every `REQUIRED` document is received; every `EXPECTED` one is received or waived with a reason | BR-DOC-1, V-510 | `DOC-NOTIF-001` |
| 5 | **V-589** | Every clinical recommendation is confirmed or rejected, with a reason where rejected | A3 §2.1 F56, BR-TRACK-6 | `CLM-CONSOLE-013` · `CLM-CONSOLE-014` |
| 6 | **V-590** | Where the clinical assessment did not complete, the warning is acknowledged | BR-TRACK-5 | `CLM-CONSOLE-015` |
| 7 | **V-591** | Every reconciliation warning is acknowledged | V-524 | `CLM-CONSOLE-002` |
| 8 | **V-592** | **The calculation is current** — no input has changed since the last chain run | §5.9.6 | *(new A2 item — **D2-60**)* |
| 9 | **V-593** | **The payout account name is verified** | BR-PAY-3 | `CLM-CONSOLE-006` |
| 10 | **V-594** | No conflict of interest: no ID-number match, and any declared relationship has already returned the claim to the queue | A3 §4.12 | `CLM-CONSOLE-011` · `CLM-CONSOLE-012` |
| 11 | **V-595** | A snapshot exists and a schedule was effective at the service date | D3 §I-05, G-1 | `CLM-CONSOLE-007` |
| **12** | **V-706** | **Every cost line is allocated to an insured event**, and every insured event that carries a line has an occurrence date, a treatment-day count and a cover decision | **S-07**, V-705, V-707, V-708 | *(new A2 item — **D2-123**)*, listed line by line |
| **13** | **V-732** | **No term checkpoint on this claim is open** — every one raised at chain step 4 or 7 has been upheld or cleared at §5.29, or has closed as moot behind a decline | **`BR-TERM-13`**, **BR-TERM-2**, **F67**. **Ratified by D1 v0.5 and `D2-177` closes** | *(new A2 item — **D2-156**)*, listing each open checkpoint and the clause it quotes |

**`V-585 … V-595`, `V-706` and `V-732` are the settlement-submission check set** and are cited by that range wherever Part V or Part VIII refers to "the submission checks". **The twelfth is allocated from the `V-701 … V-799` overflow** (§8.1) rather than continued at `V-596`, because `V-596` … `V-599` are §5.19.4's operator-queue rules and were allocated before this reissue. They are **not** `V-550`, which is §5.14.3's append-only audit rule and nothing else.

**Check 13 was v0.5's, and it was the one place in this document where a rule was specified ahead of D1 rather than behind it. D1 v0.5 has ratified it and it is now an ordinary check.** A class-J term is by definition one no engine may decide (D1 §5.3.1), and **a settlement plan submitted with that judgement still unmade is a plan whose reasoning is incomplete** — the approver reviewing it cannot supply the judgement either, because they may not edit (§5.11.1). v0.5 observed that D1 stated the checkpoint rule for the **auto-approval gate** and not for **submission**, so the two routes to an approval were governed differently for no reason anybody chose; it specified the check, cited it to `BR-TERM-2`, and **raised `D2-177` for D1 to ratify or refuse**. **D1 v0.5 `BR-TERM-13` ratifies it in exactly those terms** — *an open checkpoint blocks the submission of a settlement plan, not only the automatic route* — **and `D2-177` closes.** The posture is worth keeping on the record: this is what V-591 is still doing under **D2-71**, and it is the mechanism by which a downstream document raises a rule without inventing one.

**Check 12 is v0.3's, and it is a hard block rather than a warning for a stated reason.** Every other check on this list guards a piece of reasoning that a person could in principle supply later. Check 12 guards **arithmetic that cannot run at all**: chain step 8's per-event cap, step 11's deduction condition and §5.9.2's per-event roll-up each take the event as their unit, and a line outside every event is outside all three. A plan submitted with an unallocated line does not carry a defensible number — it carries a number computed as though the line were not there, which is a different claim.

**A duplicate flag does not block submission** — it must have been *reviewed*, and review is an acknowledgement, not a resolution (BR-DUP-2: the signal belongs to the assessor, and a genuine second claim for the same episode is common).

**Check 8 is the one that catches the subtle failure.** An assessor who corrects an amount and submits without recalculating would otherwise hand the approver a plan whose totals do not follow from its lines. The check is on input change, not on elapsed time.

#### 5.10.3 Submit — and the lock

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Kiểm tra phương án** | `ASSESSOR` | Claim in `UNDER_ASSESSMENT` or `PENDING_INFO` | Runs **V-585 … V-595**, **V-706** and **V-732**; lists every failure | *(new A2 item — **D2-60**)* |
| **Xem điều khoản đã xét** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER` | A chain run exists | Opens §5.9.1a's panel from the plan, at the section `V-753` adds | — |
| **Trình phương án** | `ASSESSOR` | All thirteen pass | State → `PENDING_APPROVAL`; **prior state stored in F2**; **the claim locks**; the approver's queue is updated | — |
| **Xem trước thông báo** | `ASSESSOR` | A calculation exists | Renders `CLM-LETTER-001` or `CLM-LETTER-002` with every placeholder filled, so the wording is seen before it is sent | — |
| **Xuất phương án bồi thường** | `ASSESSOR` **R**, `APPROVER` **R** | A frozen version exists — that is, the plan has been submitted at least once (V-716) | **PDF of the plan exactly as it was assembled at that submission**, stamped with the round number, the submitter, the approver where one has acted, and both timestamps. Stored against the claim and re-openable from §5.14. **Contains clinical detail, so the export is logged** — V-554, V-717 | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-131**)* |

**V-716 — every submission freezes a numbered version of the plan, and this is what an audit asks for first.** Register row **S-30**.

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| 1 | **Each *Trình phương án* writes a complete, immutable copy of §5.10.1** — every section above, as assembled at that instant — numbered from 1 for the claim, carrying the submitter and the submission timestamp |
| 2 | **Each approval, return or decline stamps the same version** with the decider, the decision, the timestamp and the reason where one was given. One version, two acts, one record |
| 3 | **A returned claim that is resubmitted writes version *n+1*. It never overwrites version *n*** |
| 4 | **Versions are readable from §5.14** by anyone who may open the claim, and each is exportable under V-717 |
| 5 | **A frozen version is never edited and never deleted**, by any role including `ADMIN` — the same standing as an audit entry (V-550, BR-AUDIT-1) |

**What v0.2 had, and why it was not enough.** §5.14.2 recorded *that* a claim was submitted, *that* it was approved and *that* it was returned with a reason. It did not keep **what was submitted**. A claim returned once and resubmitted overwrote its own plan, so the approver in round two had no way to see what round one contained, and six months later nobody could reconstruct how a closed claim came to be settled the way it was — the trail held the pieces and nothing held the assembly. **With S-13 in force — no re-opening a closed claim — the frozen version is the only durable statement about a claim that has closed.**

**V-717 — the export, and the one thing it is not.** Register row **S-42**, and it is the visible half of **S-30** — the frozen version is the data, the export is one way of reading it. Until v0.3 the only printable artefacts in Part V were the two customer letters and a CSV of the step table (§5.9.5); **the plan itself, the thing an approver actually decided on, could not be printed at all**, while the prototype has carried an *Xuất phương án (PDF)* control since 23 August 2026. *Xuất phương án bồi thường* renders a frozen version as a PDF for the claim file. Two constraints. **It is logged**, because it carries diagnosis, ICD-10 codes and cost-line item names, and V-554 already requires that of any export that does (BR-AUDIT-4). And **it is not signed and the document says so on its face** — Framework §7.2 excludes digital signature from MVP 1 (register row **S-33**), and a rendered internal document that looks like an instrument is worse than one that plainly is not. The statement is on the export itself and not only in this paragraph, because the person who needs it is holding the paper.

**On submission the entire claim becomes read-only** — amounts, coverage decisions, document actions and the ability to submit a fresh extraction request alike — until an approver acts (D1 §3.2.5). The lock is enforced server-side on every action and reflected as a banner naming the state and the queue *(new A2 item — **D2-56**)*.

**Why the lock covers documents and not only amounts.** Without it, an assessor can alter amounts or swap attachments while the claim sits in the approver's queue, and **the approver signs a different claim from the one they reviewed**. A re-run of extraction can produce a newer proposal under an older settlement, which is why BR-DATA-3 forbids the request outright rather than reconciling the result.

**The lock releases on rejection or on approval. It is never released by the assessor** — there is no control for it on any screen in Part V.

#### 5.10.4 Empty and error

| Condition | What the console shows |
|---|---|
| Nothing to assemble — no calculation | The plan renders its header and states that a calculation is required |
| A fully declined claim | The plan assembles normally with a payable of zero and every line declined. **A decline is a decision that needs approving, not an absence of one** (D1 §4.5) — it goes through the same submission and the same approval |
| Submission raced another action | Optimistic concurrency on the claim version; the assessor is told what changed and the checks re-run |

---

### 5.11 Approval and rejection (F50), including auto-approval

**Purpose.** Let an approver review a settlement plan and approve it, return it, or approve a decline — without being able to alter it; and let small, clean claims settle without an approver at all.

**Entered from.** S-01 filtered to `PENDING_APPROVAL`, S-08's tile, or a link. S-05.

**Who may open it.** `APPROVER` **F**, scope `QUEUE` (A3 §2.1 F50). **The assessor has no permission on this screen** and does not see the controls — an unavailable function is absent, not disabled (A3 §0.1).

#### 5.11.1 What the approver sees that the assessor did not

The plan itself is §5.10.1's, read-only. **Nine things are added** — six in v0.2, two in v0.3 and one in v0.6 — and each exists because it is evidence about the assessment rather than part of it:

| # | Shown to the approver | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **The raw-versus-corrected summary** — how many extracted fields the assessor changed, which ones, and both values | The approver is reviewing a settlement computed partly from human corrections. Which ones, and how far they moved, is the first question worth asking |
| 2 | **The agreement flags on every clinical recommendation** — confirmed or rejected, and the rejection reasons | BR-TRACK-6. The assessor records their decision; the approver sees the pattern of it, which the assessor has no view of |
| 3 | **Every override of an engine result**, with the assessor's F14 reason | A waiting-period or cover override is the assessor exercising judgement against the chain, and it is the thing most worth a second pair of eyes |
| 4 | **The auto-approval evaluation record** — **all four conditions** and the values they were tested against, whether it fired, failed, or **could not be evaluated because the first chain run was abandoned** (§5.11.4) | BR-AUTO-5. On a claim that reached them, it says *why* it reached them — and "no chain ever ran" is a different answer from "the payable was too high" |
| 5 | **The segregation check result** | A3 §4.1, evaluated against the processing trail rather than the session |
| 6 | **Every acknowledged warning** — reconciliation, duplicate, clinical-failure — with who acknowledged it and when | An acknowledgement that nobody can see is not a control |
| **7** | **Every earlier frozen version of this plan** (V-716), and what changed between the last one and this one — §5.21 | An approver reviewing a resubmitted claim was previously reviewing it as though for the first time. The question worth asking on round two is *what did they change*, and until v0.3 the screen could not answer it |
| **8** | **Every cost line the assessor re-allocated to a different insured event** (§5.6.3 L17, V-705 rule 4), with both events named | Moving a line between events changes which per-event cap prices it. It is a judgement with a money effect and it looks like data entry |
| **9** | **Every term result on this claim** — §5.9.1a's rows in full with the version evaluated, and **every checkpoint with its outcome, the reason recorded against it and who recorded it** (§5.29.2 F8 to F11), a moot closure included | **New in v0.6.** Row 4 shows the approver the gate's conditions and until now nothing showed them the term layer's own output. **The approver is the second reader of a decline that quotes a clause**, and on a claim where a checkpoint was upheld the whole of what they are approving is a judgement one person made against one clause — the reason for it is the evidence, and it was not on this screen. It is **read-only**, like everything else here: an approver who disagrees with a checkpoint outcome returns the claim (§5.11.3), because re-deciding it would put the judgement on the person who may not edit |

**The approver cannot edit.** A3 §2.1 gives `APPROVER` **R** on F46, F47 and F48, and the console has no editable control on any of them for that role. **An approver who disagrees sends the claim back — they do not edit it** — so the assessment trail always shows who decided what.

#### 5.11.2 Field table — S-05

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Phương án bồi thường | `derived` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F2 | Số tiền được duyệt | `derived` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F3 | Kết quả kiểm tra tách bạch nhiệm vụ | `derived` | `system` | M | Fails where this user appears in the claim's processing trail as the assessor | `CLM-CONSOLE-005` |
| F4 | Quyết định | `enum(approvalDecision)` | `user` | M | `PHÊ_DUYỆT` · `TRẢ_LẠI` · `TỪ_CHỐI_TOÀN_BỘ` | inline |
| F5 | Lý do trả lại | `textarea(2000)` | `user` | C — **mandatory** when F4 = `TRẢ_LẠI` | Recorded and shown to the assessor | *(new A2 item — **D2-62**)* |
| F6 | Trạng thái sẽ khôi phục | `derived` | `system` | M | — | — |

**Notes on the fields above.** F1 is a read-only rendering of §5.10.1. **F2 is the plan's total and is not editable** — an approver who wants a different number returns the claim; there is no control on this screen that changes an amount, which is why the row carries no validation and no error path. F6 is §5.10.1 F2's stored value, **displayed before the return is confirmed** so the approver knows where the claim is going.

#### 5.11.3 Actions

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Phê duyệt** | `APPROVER` | State `PENDING_APPROVAL`; F3 passes; no ID-number conflict (A3 §4.12) | State → `APPROVED`; **ledger consumption becomes final** (BR-LEDGER-1, G-2); lock releases; `CLM-LETTER-001` generated | `CLM-NOTIF-005`, or `CLM-NOTIF-008` where the settlement is partial. Blocked: `CLM-CONSOLE-005` |
| **Trả lại** | `APPROVER` | F5 entered | State → **the stored prior state** (D1 §4.4), never a fixed state; lock releases; claim returns to the assessor with the reason | *(new A2 item — **D2-62**)* |
| **Từ chối toàn bộ** | `APPROVER` | The plan's payable is zero and every line is declined | State → `DECLINED`; `CLM-LETTER-002` generated; the claim **closes on this approval**, since there is no cash to wait for (D1 §4.5) | `CLM-NOTIF-006` |
| **Hủy phê duyệt tự động** | `APPROVER` | Claim was **auto-approved**, and **no payment instruction has been issued** | State → `UNDER_ASSESSMENT`; the final ledger posting is reversed to provisional; recorded as an override (BR-AUTO-4) | — |
| **Xuất phương án bồi thường** | `APPROVER` **R** | A frozen version exists (V-716) | As §5.10.3's action: the PDF of the version, stamped and logged — V-717. **Unsigned, and the export says so** | *(new A2 item — **D2-131**)* |
| **Xem các lần trình duyệt trước** | `APPROVER` | More than one frozen version exists | Opens **§5.21** — every round of this claim side by side, with what changed between them. **This is what a second round of approval was previously blind to** | — |

**Returning restores the previous state, and that is the whole point.** A claim that was waiting on customer documents when it was submitted must go back to waiting on customer documents — not jump into the assessor's active worklist ahead of claims that are genuinely ready (D1 §4.4). `PENDING_INFO` → `PENDING_APPROVAL` → `PENDING_INFO` is a legal cycle and the console implements it.

**`CLM-CONSOLE-005` is a real control, not a warning.** *"You assessed this claim and cannot approve it. Reassign to another approver."* It is checked against the claim's **processing trail**, not the session — a user who holds both roles and assessed the claim yesterday is blocked today (A3 §4.1, §0.2). In a pilot team of three this looks like friction; it is the only control on the amount paid, and the correct relief valve is the auto-approval threshold, not weakening segregation.

**BR-AUTO-4's override is not a re-open.** It is available only on a claim that was auto-approved and only before a payment instruction has been issued. A claim an approver approved by hand cannot be walked back this way — S-13 still holds.

#### 5.11.4 Auto-approval — the four-condition gate

Evaluated **once**, by `SYSTEM`, after Track 1's chain and Track 2's assessment have both resolved (J2-14). A claim that passes **never enters `UNDER_ASSESSMENT`**: the transition is `DOC_PROCESSING → APPROVED` (D1 §4.1).

> **Once means once, and v0.5 said two things about it. This version says one.** v0.5 opened with *evaluated once* and closed with a note that a claim whose checkpoints had all been cleared *"auto-approves on the next evaluation"*. **There is no next evaluation.** A claim that raised a checkpoint has already left `DOC_PROCESSING` for `UNDER_ASSESSMENT`, and Part VII §7.2 carries no `UNDER_ASSESSMENT → APPROVED` row for `SYSTEM` — which, by §7.2's own rule that *an action not listed for a state does not exist in that state*, means the transition does not exist. **The first reading is the one that is kept: the gate is evaluated once, clearing a checkpoint does not re-open it, and a claim that raised one always reaches a person.** The closing note is deleted rather than reconciled, because the alternative — adding a `SYSTEM` re-gate out of `UNDER_ASSESSMENT` — is a new transition and therefore a change to D1, not to a screen.

| # | Condition | Value | Evaluated from |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | Total payable **at or below the threshold**, **and nothing was cut** — no cost line declined, no limit bound | **2.000.000 đ** (D1 B-03), `config`, changeable without a release (BR-AUTO-1). **The value read is the one pinned onto the claim at registration — `autoApprovalThresholdAsOf`, V-722** | The chain's own output: the payable, the line decisions, and whether any cap bound at steps 8, 9 or 12 |
| **2** | The clinical appropriateness assessment **completed and returned no recommendation** | — | `state = COMPLETE` **and** `linesAssessed` covers every line **and** `recommendations` is empty — BR-AUTO-3 |
| **3** | **No term checkpoint is open — whichever class raised it** *(new at v0.5; re-cut at v0.6)* | — | **F66's evaluation record**: no term evaluated at chain step 4 or step 7 returned `ĐIỂM_KIỂM` with an outcome still unrecorded at §5.29. **A checkpoint closed as moot behind a decline does not block** — it is closed. **The condition names no class** (D1 v0.5 §5.8): two of the pilot's four `CHECKPOINT` terms are class `D`, so a condition worded *"class J or class E"* would let half of them through. **A step held under `BR-CHAIN-1` raises a checkpoint and blocks here like any other** — V-754 |
| **4** | **No duplicate signal is outstanding** *(new at v0.6)* | — | **`BR-DUP-1` or `BR-DUP-3` matched and the signal has not been reviewed** — §5.2.6 V-503, §5.4.1 F10. **V-750** |

**V-750 — the fourth condition, and it closes a control that was inert on exactly the population that needed it.** `BR-DUP-2` makes a duplicate signal *a warning to the assessor*, which is the right control only where a claim reaches an assessor. **An auto-approved claim never does**, so on the one population that settles unreviewed the whole duplicate mechanism fired into an empty room: BR-DUP-1 matched, BR-DUP-3 matched, and the claim settled with the warning addressed to nobody. D1 v0.5 §5.8 adds the condition and this screen carries it. **The signal must be *reviewed*, not resolved** (BR-DUP-2) — a genuine second claim for the same episode is common, and review is an acknowledgement; what the gate refuses is a claim on which nobody has looked at the signal at all.

**V-733 — the third condition, and why it follows from the class model rather than from caution.** A **class-J** term is one no engine may decide and a **class-E** term is one no engine may decide without a document that is not there (D1 §5.3.1). **If an open checkpoint did not block the gate, the platform would auto-approve a claim on which a judgement was required and never made** — which is precisely the failure the three-class model exists to prevent, arriving through the one door the model did not have a lock on. Decision **D-5**, approved 24 August 2026.

**The cost is real and is stated rather than absorbed: any claim touching a term that ends at a person leaves the straight-through path.** **Four of A5 §7's ten terms carry `CHECKPOINT`** — two class `J`, cosmetic treatment among them, and **two class `D`**, health checks and supplements (§5.28.1a) — and a fifth, class `E`, raises one whenever its document is absent. So **a measurable share of dental and dermatology claims will now reach an assessor that would previously have settled without one**, and **every supplement line does too, because `TERM-HC-003` raises a checkpoint rather than declining** (A5 §7.4). **Framework SC-04 rests on the gate firing**, so this is a reduction in the straight-through rate that somebody has accepted rather than a side effect nobody costed. **§5.15's dashboard must count it**: the auto-approval rate broken down by failing condition is what tells the business whether the threshold, the clinical track or the term layer is the constraint, and until v0.5 there were only two answers it could give.

> **What condition 3 does not do.** It does not make a checkpoint a decline, and it does not make a checkpoint a block on the *claim*. The claim proceeds normally to an assessor with the settlement already computed; what it does not do is settle without one. **And clearing every checkpoint does not bring the claim back to the gate**: the gate ran once, in `DOC_PROCESSING`, and the claim is now with a person who submits a settlement plan in the ordinary way (§5.10).

**Anything else routes to an assessor with the failing condition named** *(new A2 item needed — **D2-61**)*. Naming it matters: *"payable 2.400.000 exceeds the threshold 2.000.000"*, *"line 4 was declined"*, *"clause 5.2(c) raised a checkpoint that nobody has answered"* and *"a duplicate signal on claim CLM-26-000318 has not been reviewed"* are four different pieces of work, and only the first is work on the number. **`D2-61`'s message gains the third and fourth conditions**; it is not a new code.

**V-751 — an auto-approved claim whose payout account is not verified routes to the operator queue** (D1 `BR-AUTO-6`). `BR-PAY-3` blocks a settlement plan and a payment instruction while `accountNameVerified` is `false`, and **auto-approval bypasses the settlement plan** — so without this rule the claim reaches `APPROVED` and stops there with nothing naming why. **It is a routing rule and not a fifth gate condition, deliberately**: the gate is about adjudication, and whether we know where to send the money is an operations question. The claim still auto-approves, still records that it did, and appears on §5.19's queue as a `CHI_TRẢ_TREO` row. **`APPROVED` with an unverified account is not an error state and is never expressed to the customer as one** (§2.10). It matters practically as well as tidily: `D2-106` means the verification call has no contract yet, so `accountNameVerified` may be `false` on every claim in the pilot, and as a gate condition that would switch auto-approval off entirely and the measurement of SC-04 with it.

**Every auto-approved claim records all four conditions and the values they were evaluated against** — including the count of terms tested and checkpoints raised (BR-AUTO-5, BR-TERM-1), **the term register version it was evaluated against** (BR-TERM-4, §5.2.4) and **any duplicate signal considered and found not outstanding**, and S-02.1 displays that record. *"Why was this approved without a human"* is answerable from the claim alone — **and from v0.3 the record names the threshold version that answered it**, not merely the number.

**V-722 — the gate is evaluated against the threshold pinned at registration, and this closes a live hole.** Register row **B-41**.

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| 1 | **`autoApprovalThresholdAsOf` is written onto the claim's snapshot at registration** (§5.2.4), alongside `providerMasterAsOf`, and every gate evaluation on that claim resolves against the version in force at that instant |
| 2 | **Including the evaluations that follow a re-run.** BR-TRACK-4 re-runs the whole chain when a clinical recommendation is confirmed, and the gate is evaluated on the output. Without the pin, a claim registered under a threshold of 2.000.000 could be gated on a re-run against a threshold an administrator changed in between |
| 3 | **The evaluation record names the version, the value and its effective date**, not only the value. *"Approved automatically at or below 2.000.000"* is not an answer if nobody can say which 2.000.000 |
| 4 | **§5.16.2 gains an effective-to date and a reference to the instrument that authorised the change** — the approval note, the minute, the memo. `text(200)`, optional, retained on the version. A threshold is a delegation of authority and a delegation has a source |

**What the reference does that we do not, and why the difference is smaller than it looks.** Their approval authority is granted by a numbered management instrument with an issue date, an effective window and an issuing unit, and a claim carries a flag saying whether it is within or beyond the authority that instrument confers. **We have one threshold and one approval level** — declared at **S-12** and unchanged here. **What was missing was not the hierarchy, it was the effective dating**: V-571 already said a threshold change is not retrospective, and nothing on the claim recorded which threshold had actually applied, so the rule was true and unverifiable. Rows 1 to 3 make it checkable; row 4 records who authorised it. Neither adds a level of approval (**G-B-09**).

**The chain that produces condition 1's input is system-triggered, and this is where that is specified.** Condition 1 tests a **total payable**, and a total payable exists only after the fourteen-step chain has run. Everywhere else in Part V the chain is started by an assessor pressing *Tính toán lại* (§5.6.7, §5.9.5), whose precondition is that every line is already decided and every event already assessed — which cannot be true of a claim no human has opened. **Without a system-triggered first run there is no claim the gate can ever fire on, and Framework SC-04 rests on the gate firing.** So the first run is the platform's, not the assessor's.

**The first chain run.**

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | The **extraction result and the clinical assessment have both returned** for the claim — `I-09` has produced a package state, and `I-16` has resolved to `COMPLETE`, `PARTIAL`, `ERROR`, or the 30-minute ceiling in NFR-2a has been reached. The ceiling **is** a resolution: the run never waits indefinitely for Track 2 |
| **Actor** | `SYSTEM`. The run happens **before any assessor opens the claim**, while the claim is in `DOC_PROCESSING`, and is logged with the system as the actor, never the last human (BR-AUDIT-3, V-551) |
| **Idempotency** | Keyed on the claim and its input version. A repeated `I-08` or `I-16` webhook resolves to the run that already exists — **no second run, and no second provisional posting** (D3 §1.3, BR-LEDGER-3) |
| **Relation to *Tính toán lại*** | Unchanged. The assessor's action is the **second and subsequent** runs, and its precondition in §5.6.7 and §5.9.5 stands exactly as written |

**Preconditions — all seven, and a failure of any one means the run does not happen at all.**

| # | Precondition |
|---|---|
| 1 | **A snapshot exists.** Registration resolved to exactly one member and calls 2 and 3 were written atomically (§5.2.4). A claim on the multi-match or no-match path has no snapshot and no chain to run |
| 2 | **The package state is not `ERROR`.** An extraction that failed is an operational fact, not an input (§5.6.8, G-3) |
| 3 | **The clinical assessment has resolved** in one of the four senses above |
| 4 | **Every cost line maps to a benefit automatically** — L10 is present, is one of the canonical **twenty** (A5 §8.1, §5.6.3 L10), and A5 §8.1 yields a benefit for L10 × treatment setting |
| 5 | **Every insured event can be assessed automatically** — provider resolved against the master at `providerMasterAsOf`, treatment dates present, an ICD-10 code present, a condition class derivable, and a cover decision computable from the snapshot alone |
| 6 | **No assessor has taken the claim** and the claim is not locked. A claim already assigned belongs to a person, and the platform does not compute underneath them |
| **7** | **Every cost line is allocated to an insured event** — V-705 resolved each line to exactly one event, with no line ambiguous and no line unmatched. **New in v0.3, S-07.** Chain step 8's per-event cap and step 11's deduction condition both take the event as their unit; a claim carrying a line outside every event has no base for either |

**What the run does when all six hold.** It sets each line's L13 from the engine — `CHI_TRẢ`, or `TỪ_CHỐI` with the engine's own reason code where a step declined it — marks those decisions as the engine's rather than an assessor's, runs all fourteen steps, posts **provisionally** to the ledger (BR-LEDGER-1), and writes the step table §5.9.1 renders. The gate is then evaluated on that output. **Every one of those line decisions remains fully overridable** by an assessor if the claim routes to one; none of them is a human's decision and none is presented as one.

**What happens to the claim in each case.**

| Case | What happens |
|---|---|
| **All six preconditions hold, the chain completes, both gate conditions pass** | `DOC_PROCESSING → APPROVED` by `SYSTEM`. Ledger consumption becomes final (G-2), `CLM-LETTER-001` is generated, `CLM-NOTIF-005` is sent, and the evaluation record is written (BR-AUTO-5) |
| **The chain completes and a gate condition fails** | Claim → `UNDER_ASSESSMENT`, **unassigned**, on the work list with a computed settlement already on it. The failing condition and its values are named — *(new A2 item needed — **D2-61**)* |
| **A cost line cannot be mapped** — L10 empty, outside the **twenty**, or A5 §8.1 yields no benefit for L10 × setting | **No chain run.** Claim → `UNDER_ASSESSMENT`, unassigned, the line flagged *"chưa ánh xạ được quyền lợi"* on §5.6, and the gate recorded as **not evaluated** rather than as failed — the two are different facts and an approver reading §5.11.1 row 4 needs to see which one happened. *(new A2 item needed — **D2-77**)* |
| **Some lines map and some do not** | **The run is abandoned whole.** It is never run on the mappable subset: a payable computed from part of a claim is a wrong number, not a partial one. Claim → `UNDER_ASSESSMENT` as above |
| **A cost line could not be allocated to an insured event** — V-705 matched none, or matched more than one | **No chain run**, and the run is abandoned **whole** on the same reasoning as the row above. Claim → `UNDER_ASSESSMENT`, unassigned, the lines flagged on §5.6 and the count on the tab header, and the gate recorded as **not evaluated** rather than as failed. *(new A2 item — **D2-123**)* |
| **An insured event has no occurrence date** — V-707 could not derive one and extraction returned none | **No chain run.** The waiting-period arithmetic at chain step 2 counts to the occurrence date and has nothing to count to. Claim → `UNDER_ASSESSMENT` with the event flagged. **F4's start date is not substituted** |
| **An insured event cannot be assessed automatically** — no ICD-10, no derivable condition class, provider unresolved, or a cover decision the snapshot cannot settle | **No chain run.** Claim → `UNDER_ASSESSMENT`, unassigned, the event flagged for the assessor to classify. **Nothing is guessed** (D1 §5.2) — *(new A2 item needed — **D2-77**)* |
| **`waitingPeriodDays` is `null` for the event's condition class × benefit group** | A **data error**, not a zero-day wait (BR-WAIT-4). No chain run, claim → `UNDER_ASSESSMENT`, **and** the claim appears on the operator queue (§5.19), because the schedule itself is wrong and no assessor can fix it on the claim |
| **The clinical assessment did not complete** — `PARTIAL`, `ERROR`, or the NFR-2a ceiling | **The chain still runs**, on Track 1 alone (BR-TRACK-5), so that the assessor arrives at a computed settlement rather than an empty tab. Condition 2 fails by BR-AUTO-3, so the claim → `UNDER_ASSESSMENT` with `CLM-CONSOLE-015` and the acknowledgement required at §5.10.2 check 6 |
| **The ledger version clashes during the run** | Re-run once against the current counters (V-546). A second clash abandons the run; the claim → `UNDER_ASSESSMENT` and the assessor recalculates. **It is never silently merged** |

**In every one of those cases the claim is `UNDER_ASSESSMENT` and unassigned, never `DECLINED` and never stalled** (G-3, D1 §4.3). The gate not firing is the ordinary outcome; the gate not being *evaluable* is recorded as such, and neither is a decision about the customer's claim.

#### 5.11.5 What the gate deliberately does not test

Recorded on the screen specification because a developer or a reviewer will otherwise read each as a defect and fix it — which would change a business rule (D1 §5.8).

| Not tested | Consequence | Where it is recorded |
|---|---|---|
| **Extraction confidence** | A claim whose amounts were read with low confidence can auto-approve. The threshold limits the damage; it does not prevent it. **Confidence stays a routing signal** (A4 §7) and §5.6.5 says so at the field | D1 §5.8, Framework RK-07 |
| **Post-hoc sampling** | No proportion of auto-approved claims is re-reviewed. A systematic false negative in Track 2 surfaces as a complaint, not as a measurement. The dashboard counts auto-approved claims and their amounts (§5.15) but nothing samples them | D1 §5.8 |

**Two omissions that were closed on 17/08/2026 and must not be re-opened by a UI change.** *(They are omissions of condition 1 and are untouched by condition 3, which closed a different hole at v0.5.)* Condition 1's second clause means a **coverage or waiting-period failure** (which produces a decline or a reduction) and a **bound limit** (which produces a cut) both keep a claim outside the gate. What remains is the narrow case the gate was meant for: **small, clinically clean, and nothing cut.** The A5 §6.2 worked example is the canonical demonstration — 1.920.000 đ, under the threshold, and still routed to a human.

**Both remaining omissions are bounded by BC-3 — no real money moves in MVP 1** — and they stop being acceptable at the same moment S-17 does.

#### 5.11.6 Empty and error

| Condition | What the console shows |
|---|---|
| The approver assessed this claim | The approve control is **absent**; `CLM-CONSOLE-005` states why and what to do |
| The approver is named on the claim (ID match) | Every control is absent; `CLM-CONSOLE-011`; the claim returns to the queue |
| Approval races a concurrent ledger change | Optimistic concurrency: the approval is refused, the chain re-runs, and the approver reviews the new figures — an approval is never applied to a total that has since moved *(new A2 item — **D2-67**)* |
| Track 2 never completed | The claim is here **with** `CLM-CONSOLE-015` and the acknowledgement from §5.10.2 check 6 (V-590). It cannot have arrived by auto-approval |

---

### 5.12 Payment instruction and status (F51)

**Purpose.** Instruct the payment of an approved settlement, and show what the finance system did with it.

**Entered from.** S-02's settlement tab and S-01, on a claim in `APPROVED` or `PAYMENT_IN_PROGRESS`. S-06.

**Who may open it.** `APPROVER` **C** under A3 §4.6, scope `ASSIGNED`. **The assessor has no permission** (A3 §2.1 F51) — the person who computed the amount does not release the money.

> **The account, the payee and the verified flag are **F58**'s, and **§5.20** is their specification.** This section states what the payment does with them and what it refuses without them; it does not restate the records, the verification flow or who may run it. **Where this section and §5.20 appear to disagree, §5.20 wins** — §5.20.5 maps the four preconditions below onto what F58 supplies for each.

#### 5.12.1 The three preconditions

A3 §4.6, and all three are checked server-side before the adapter is called:

| # | Precondition | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The claim is in **`APPROVED`** | Follows from D3 G-2 — finalisation happens at approval and `I-11` happens after it — and is enforced by the claim service |
| 2 | The amount is **exactly the approved settlement total** | The adapter re-checks against the claim before sending. **An instruction that disagrees with its claim is refused, not corrected** (D3 §I-11) |
| 3 | The payee account is **verified** — `accountNameVerified = true` | `422 ACCOUNT_NOT_VERIFIED` from `I-11`; refused before that by the console. **The flag is set on §5.20 by an assessor or an administrator, never by the customer and never by an approver** (A3 §3.2, §5.20.4) |

**And a fourth condition that is not in A3 §4.6 but is in A3 §4.5.** If the payout account changed after approval, the payment is **held until an approver re-releases it** — `CLM-CONSOLE-010`. Changing the account also clears the verified name and re-triggers verification (BR-PAY-2). This closes the classic redirection fraud: submit clean, change the account after approval.

#### 5.12.2 Field table — S-06

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Mã lệnh chi trả | `text(24)` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F2 | Số tiền chi trả | `derived` | `system` | M | Equals the approved total exactly. **Read-only**, and the adapter re-checks it against the claim before sending | inline |
| F3 | Người thụ hưởng | `text(200)` | `snapshot` | M | — | — |
| F4 | Ngân hàng · Số tài khoản | `text(60)` | `snapshot` | M | — | — |
| F5 | Đã xác thực tên chủ tài khoản | `bool` | `snapshot` | M | Must be `true`. **Re-read live against F58's record at instruction time as well as read from the snapshot** — an account verified at registration and changed since is not a verified account (§5.20.5, BR-PAY-2) | `CLM-CONSOLE-006` |
| F6 | Nội dung chuyển khoản | `text(140)` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F7 | Ngày giá trị | `date` | `user` | M | ≥ today | inline |
| F8 | Trạng thái lệnh | `enum(instructionState)` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F9 | Ngày chi trả | `datetime` | `system` | O | — | — |
| F10 | Mã giao dịch ngân hàng | `text(40)` | `system` | O | — | — |
| F11 | Lý do thất bại | `text(300)` | `system` | C — where `I-12` returned `REJECTED` or `RETURNED` | `failureReason`, shown to the operator, **never to the customer verbatim** | *(new A2 item — **D2-63**)* |

**Notes on the fields above.** **F1** is `instructionRef`, e.g. `PAY-26-000417-1`, generated by the claim system and used as **the business idempotency key** (D3 §I-11). **F3** is the beneficiary, not necessarily the insured (A1 §5), at the canonical name width of §2.9. **F4** renders the bank name with the account masked to the last four digits (A2 §5). **F6** is `BT {claimNo}`. **F8**'s `ACCEPTED` moves the claim to `PAYMENT_IN_PROGRESS` and **`ACCEPTED` is not `PAID`** (D3 §I-11). **F9 and F10** arrive on the `I-12` callback and are recorded as `system` per convention **V-d**; F10 is rendered to the customer in `PAY-NOTIF-002`.

#### 5.12.3 Actions

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Lập lệnh chi trả** | `APPROVER` | The three preconditions, plus A3 §4.5's hold cleared | `POST /v1/payment-instructions` with `Idempotency-Key`; claim → `PAYMENT_IN_PROGRESS` | `PAY-NOTIF-001` to the customer. Blocked: `CLM-CONSOLE-006` · `CLM-CONSOLE-010` |
| **Phát hành lại** | `APPROVER` | Only after `RETURNED`, with a corrected and re-verified account | **A new `instructionRef`.** The original is never reused (D3 §I-12) | `PAY-NOTIF-001` |
| **Xem trạng thái** | `APPROVER`, `ASSESSOR` | — | The instruction and its callbacks | — |

**The control is issued once.** After a `202 ACCEPTED` the create action is gone from the screen, and a repeat of the same `instructionRef` returns the original state rather than creating a second instruction (D3 §1.3). **This is the one place in the system where a duplicate costs real money**, which is why the idempotency key is mandatory on the wire and the control is removed in the UI as well.

#### 5.12.4 What happens when the finance stub reports failure

| `I-12` outcome | Claim | Ledger | Console | Customer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PAID` | → `PAID` | Unchanged — already final at approval | Instruction shows `paidAt` and `bankReference` | `PAY-NOTIF-002` |
| **`REJECTED`** | **Back to the assessor** with the reason; **not** `DECLINED` | **A reversal is posted** (BR-LEDGER-4, G-2a) | *(new A2 item — **D2-63**)*, and the claim appears on S-03 (§5.19) | `PAY-NOTIF-003` — which does **not** ask the customer to fix anything, because the cause is as often our data as theirs |
| **`RETURNED`** | An operational state requiring a corrected account, re-verification (BR-PAY-2) and an approver's re-release (A3 §4.5) | **A reversal is posted** | As above, plus the re-issue path | `PAY-NOTIF-003` |
| No callback at all | Stays `PAYMENT_IN_PROGRESS`, appears on S-03 (§5.19) with the elapsed time | Unchanged | Operator queue | Nothing new — the last message stands |

> **The ledger is already final by the time any of this happens.** Consumption is finalised at **approval**, not at payment (BR-LEDGER-1, G-2). A failed payment therefore posts a **reversal** — it does not un-finalise, and **nothing is ever deleted** (BR-LEDGER-3, G-2a). The consumption record carries the reversal information, so the history stays reconstructable. Un-finalising would be the easier implementation and it would make the ledger's history unrecoverable; it is also unsafe, because an approved claim has committed the member's limit and a concurrent claim must see that commitment.

**A rejected or returned payment does not close the claim** (D1 §4.5). It returns to the assessor with the reason, and the claim is settled again or corrected.

#### 5.12.5 Empty and error

| Condition | What the console shows |
|---|---|
| Claim not `APPROVED` | The instruction control is **absent** (A3 §4.6, §0.1) |
| `422 ACCOUNT_NOT_VERIFIED` | `CLM-CONSOLE-006`; the account verification path is offered — **it opens §5.20** (A3 §3.2 — an assessor or an administrator may verify a payout account; an approver may not) |
| Amount mismatch detected by the adapter | Refused with the two figures shown. **Never corrected to match** |
| `503` from finance, or the circuit is open | Retried on the standard backoff, then an operational alert. The claim holds in `PAYMENT_IN_PROGRESS` on S-03 (§5.19) — **never `DECLINED`** (G-3) |

### 5.13 Claim closure and final posting (F52)

**Purpose.** Close a claim once the money has moved — or once a decline has been approved — and record the terminal state.

**Entered from.** S-05 and S-06. F52 has no screen of its own (§5.1).

**Who may open it.** `APPROVER` **F**, scope `ASSIGNED` (A3 §2.1 F52).

> **A naming correction that matters.** Framework §7.1 titles F52 *"Claim closure and final ledger posting"*. **The ledger was already finalised at approval** — A3 §2.1's own note on F52 says so, and BR-LEDGER-1, A1 §5.1, A5 §6.1 step 14 and D3 G-2 all agree. **Closure posts nothing to the ledger.** It records a terminal state and nothing else. This document follows D1 and the annexes; the Framework's feature title is the outlier, and it is raised as **D2-68** so Framework §7.1's wording can be corrected rather than implemented.

#### 5.13.1 When a claim closes

| Case | Gate | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Fully declined** | **On approval of the decline** | There is no cash to wait for. A decline is a decision that needs approving, not an absence of one — and closing declined claims without approval leaves the most disputable decisions the least audited (D1 §4.5) |
| **Paid in full or in part** | **On confirmation of payment** — `I-12` returned `PAID` | Reference System A gates closure on a payment date supplied by the accounting system. Treating "approved" as "closed" produces a reported claim population that diverges from the cash ledger |
| **Payment rejected or returned** | **Does not close** | Returns to the assessor with the reason; a reversal is posted (§5.12.4) |
| **Cancelled** | Terminal on cancellation | `CANCELLED` is reachable only before approval (D1 §4.6) |

#### 5.13.2 Field table

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Ngày đóng hồ sơ | `datetime` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F2 | Người đóng hồ sơ | `lookup(user)` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F3 | Hình thức kết thúc | `enum(closureType)` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F4 | Số tiền chi trả cuối cùng | `derived` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F5 | Tham chiếu ghi nhận hạn mức | `derived` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F6 | Thông báo đã gửi | `derived` | `system` | M | — | — |

**Notes on the fields above.** Every row is written by the platform at the moment of closure, so no row carries a validation and none carries an error path (§2.2). **F1** is set on closure and is immutable. **F2** is the `APPROVER`, or **`SYSTEM`** where closure follows a confirmed payment automatically — logged with the system as the actor, never the last human (BR-AUDIT-3, V-551). **F3** is `ĐÃ_CHI_TRẢ` · `CHI_TRẢ_MỘT_PHẦN` · `TỪ_CHỐI` · `ĐÃ_HỦY`. **F4** is zero on a decline. **F5** references the final consumption records and any reversals — **a reference, not a new posting**. **F6** names `CLM-LETTER-001` or `CLM-LETTER-002` with the dispatch timestamp.

#### 5.13.3 Actions and errors

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Đóng hồ sơ** | `APPROVER` | `PAID`, or `DECLINED` with the decline approved | State → `CLOSED`; F1–F6 written; **no ledger movement** | Blocked where payment is unconfirmed: *(new A2 item needed — **D2-64**)* |

| Condition | What the console shows |
|---|---|
| Claim is `APPROVED` but not `PAID` | The close control is absent, with the reason: closure waits on cash (D1 §4.5) *(new A2 item — **D2-64**)* |
| Claim is `CLOSED` | Everything is read-only. **There is no re-open in MVP 1** (S-13) — the control does not exist, for any role. A supplementary invoice on a settled claim cannot be paid (S-10), and that is a known cost, not a defect |

### 5.14 Claim history, processing trail and audit (F53)

**Purpose.** Answer three different questions from one record: *where is this claim*, *what happened to it and who did it*, and *what does the system say happened*.

**Entered from.** A drawer on every tab of S-02, and a full screen at S-07.

**Who may open it.** `ASSESSOR` **R** and `APPROVER` **R** over `ASSIGNED`; `ADMIN` **C** over `ALL_CLAIMS` under A3 §4.11 (A3 §2.1 F53, A3 §3.1 F63).

#### 5.14.1 Four views

**Three in v0.2, four in v0.3.** The fourth answers a question the console could not answer at all: *the customer says they never received the letter.*

| View | Audience | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| **Diễn tiến hồ sơ** — state timeline | Everyone, including what the customer sees in the app | State, Vietnamese label from A1 §5.1, entered-at, actor. **Operational states are shown as processing, never as outcomes** (D1 §4.3) |
| **Nhật ký xử lý** — processing trail | Assessor and approver | **One row per action**, with actor, timestamp, the action in Vietnamese, **a note carrying the reason where the action had one**, and a link opening the field-level detail — **V-720** |
| **Nhật ký hệ thống** — audit log | Assessor and approver in scope; `ADMIN` for configuration and access events only | The JSON entries (F63), filterable, exportable |
| **Thư từ & thông báo** — correspondence | **Anyone who may open the claim** | Every message sent about this claim: when, by whom or by what, the A2 code and template version, the address, the rendered body, and whether delivery succeeded — **§5.22**, V-718 |
| **Phương án theo lần trình duyệt** — submission rounds | Assessor and approver | Every frozen version of the settlement plan (V-716), with what changed between rounds — **§5.21** |

**V-720 — the unit of the processing trail is an action, not a field.** Register row **B-37**, console side.

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| 1 | **One user action produces one row.** A save that changed seven fields is one row, not seven |
| 2 | **The row carries the reason.** A return, a cancellation, a waiver, a rejected recommendation, a dismissal, an override — the text the person typed sits on the action row, in its own column, and is not buried in the `valueAfter` of whichever field happened to be written last |
| 3 | **The row opens a detail table** — one line per field changed, with the field's Vietnamese label, the old value and the new value. That is §5.14.4's *Xem chi tiết mục*, and the values shown are exactly what BR-AUDIT-2 already records |
| 4 | **Nothing is recorded less than before.** Every old and new value is still written, the clinical partition still applies (V-552), and the log is still append-only (V-550). **The change is the grouping, not the coverage** |
| 5 | **A machine-performed action is one row too**, attributed to `SYSTEM`, `IDP` or `IMO` (V-551) |

**Why this is a defect and not a preference.** §5.14.1 promises the assessor and approver *"every action, with actor, timestamp, and old → new"*. Against v0.2's schema — one audit entry per field (§6.3.3) — one pass over a cost grid renders as several dozen consecutive rows, same second, same actor, different field, with nothing joining them, and §5.14.5 forbids showing an empty panel so the reader gets a wall instead. **And the reason has nowhere to live.** This document makes a reason mandatory in six places and the entry schema has no field called *reason*; it would have to be written into the `valueAfter` of some field, and *"why was this claim returned"* would be answered by joining two entries that nothing binds together.

> **Half of this change was Part VI's and the second pass has made it.** **§6.3.3 is now a parent action** carrying `action`, `actorId`, `occurredAt`, `correlationId`, `changeCount` and **an explicit `reason` column**, with the field changes as a nested `changes[]` list, and **V-630** and **V-631** hold the invariants a nested structure needs. What §5.14.4's *Xem chi tiết mục* opens is A14's array. **What is still owed is D1's rule** — `BR-AUDIT-2` reads one-entry-per-field and must be restated as grouped by action, which is **D2-117**, the remaining half of **D2-128**. **The timing mattered more than the content**: an append-only store is by definition the hardest table in the system to migrate, so the schema was cheap to decide before code exists and expensive after, and it has now been decided.

#### 5.14.2 What is recorded

Every row below is an entry, and the list is the specification — an action in Part V that is not here is a defect in Part V.

| Category | Entries |
|---|---|
| Lifecycle | Every state change, with the actor — `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER`, `ADMIN`, **`SYSTEM`**, `IDP`, `IMO` (§1.2) |
| Registration | Number allocation, the `I-05` calls, the snapshot, the four outcomes of §5.2.3, the duplicate check result |
| Documents | Checklist transitions old → new (BR-DOC-3), information requests with the exact items, waivers with reasons, uploads, extraction resubmissions with the new `requestId` |
| Extraction | Every field correction, **raw → corrected**, and every reversion (V-519); every warning acknowledgement |
| Cover | Every event assessment, every engine override with its reason, every condition-class determination |
| Cost lines | Every pay/decline decision, reason code, drafted rationale and final rationale (BR-LINE-3) |
| Clinical | Every recommendation received, its evidence and confidence, the assessor's decision, the reason where rejected, **the agreement flag**, and the `knowledgeBaseVersion` in force (BR-TRACK-6, BR-KB-4) |
| Calculation | Every chain run: the trigger, the fourteen steps' inputs and outputs, **every term tested and its result** (BR-TERM-1), and the configuration in force |
| Ledger | Every provisional posting, finalisation, and **reversal** — never a deletion (BR-LEDGER-3) |
| Gate | The auto-approval evaluation, **all four conditions** and their values, whether it fired (BR-AUTO-5), **the terms-tested counts behind condition 3** (BR-TERM-1) and **the duplicate signal behind condition 4** (BR-DUP-1, BR-DUP-3) |
| Approval | Submission, approval, return with reason and restored state, decline approval, auto-approval override |
| Payment | Instruction, callbacks, failures, reversals, re-issues |
| Access | **Every read of clinical detail** (BR-AUDIT-4) and **every denied permission attempt** (BR-AUDIT-5, A3 §6) |
| **Insured events** | **Every event created and removed (B-43), every occurrence date entered or corrected, and every cost line allocated or re-allocated to an event, old → new** (V-705, V-707) |
| **Settlement rounds** | **Every frozen plan version** — its number, its submitter, its decider, both timestamps and the reason (V-716). The version itself is the record, not a description of it |
| **Correspondence** | **Every message sent about the claim**, its A2 code and template version, its address, its delivery outcome, and every manual re-send with the addresses it went to (V-718, V-719) |
| **Claimant** | **Every change to the claimant's name, identity number, legal capacity or family relationship** (§5.4.2 F34 to F37), and every V-709 refusal |

#### 5.14.3 Rules

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| **V-550** | **The audit log is append-only.** No role, including `ADMIN`, may edit or delete an entry (BR-AUDIT-1). No screen offers a control |
| **V-551** | A machine-performed step is logged with **the system as the actor**, not the last human (BR-AUDIT-3). The auto-approval, the ledger posting and the closure that follows a confirmed payment all show `SYSTEM` |
| **V-552** | For `ADMIN`, the trail shows **operational rows only**: states, timestamps, who did what, configuration in force. Diagnosis, ICD-10, condition class, cost-line item names and document images are **absent, and the access is logged** (A3 §4.11) |
| **V-553** | **A cross-user report — "what did person X do" — does not exist in MVP 1.** That is an audit function and no `AUDITOR` role exists (A3 §5). The trail is per claim, and the absence is deliberate |
| **V-554** | Export is per claim, scope-filtered, and the export is itself logged where it contains clinical detail |

**Retention is unset and unowned.** NFR-8 says so plainly: no retention period for claim data exists anywhere in the document set, and A3-05 covers audit entries and access logs only. This screen implements no purge and no archive, and the gap is a business and legal decision that needs a B-item opened in D1 §11 before release. Recorded here as **D2-69** because it is this screen that would implement whatever is decided.

#### 5.14.4 Actions

There is no action on this screen that changes a claim. Everything here reads, filters or exports — which is what makes V-550 enforceable rather than aspirational.

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Mở nhật ký hồ sơ** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER`, `ADMIN` | The claim is in scope | Opens S-07, or the drawer on S-02. For `ADMIN` it opens **redacted** (V-552) and **the read is logged** (BR-AUDIT-4) | — |
| **Lọc nhật ký** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER`, `ADMIN` | — | Filters the trail by category (§5.14.2), actor, and date range. A filter that matches nothing shows the filter, never a blank panel (§5.14.5) | — |
| **Xem chi tiết mục** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER` | An entry is selected | Expands the action row to its **field-change table — one line per field, with the Vietnamese label, the old value and the new value** — plus the actor, the timestamp, the reason and the `correlationId` (V-720, D3 §1.2) | — |
| **Mở lịch sử thư từ** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER`, and any role that may open the claim | — | Opens §5.22's view for this claim | — |
| **Mở phương án theo lần trình duyệt** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER` | At least one frozen version exists | Opens §5.21 | — |
| **Xuất nhật ký hồ sơ** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER` | **One claim**, in scope — never a cross-claim export (V-553) | CSV or JSON of the filtered entries for that claim, scope-filtered. **The export is itself logged where it contains clinical detail** (V-554, BR-AUDIT-4) | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-78**)* on refusal |
| **Xuất nhật ký hệ thống** | `ADMIN` | Configuration and access events only | JSON export of F63's entries. **No clinical row is included**, and the redaction is applied at the query, not at the render (V-552, A3 §6) | *(new A2 item — **D2-78**)* |
| **Sửa hoặc xóa một mục** | — | — | **Does not exist.** No role, including `ADMIN`, has this control on any screen in Part V — V-550, BR-AUDIT-1 | — |

#### 5.14.5 Empty and error

| Condition | What the console shows |
|---|---|
| A claim with no activity beyond registration | The three entries that exist. **Never an empty panel** |
| `ADMIN` viewing | The redacted trail, with a visible note that clinical rows are withheld — **withheld, not silently absent**, so an administrator diagnosing a stuck claim knows there is more and does not conclude the claim is broken |
| The audit store is unavailable | The timeline and trail render from the claim record; the JSON view shows the outage. **No entry is dropped** — writes are not best-effort |

### 5.15 Dashboard (F54)

**Purpose.** Show the shape of the work: what is waiting, what is late, what is stuck, and what settled without a human.

**Entered from.** Login, and the console's navigation. S-08.

**Who may open it.** `ASSESSOR` **R**, `APPROVER` **R**, `ADMIN` **R**, scope `QUEUE` (A3 §2.1 F54). Every tile is scope-filtered **as a predicate at the query layer** — a claim outside scope is not counted, not merely hidden (A3 §6).

#### 5.15.1 Tiles

| # | Tile | Type | Source | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | Hồ sơ theo trạng thái | `int` | `system` | One counter per live state, Vietnamese labels from A1 §5.1. Links to S-01 pre-filtered |
| T2 | Hàng đợi của tôi | `int` | `system` | Assigned to the user, split by ageing bucket |
| T3 | Chưa giao | `int` | `system` | The queue's backlog — the single number the pilot's one-queue model (S-11) lives or dies on |
| T4 | Nhóm quá hạn | `derived` | `system` | `TRONG_HẠN` / `ĐẾN_HẠN` / `QUÁ_HẠN` on the **internal** clock from submission (§5.3.2) |
| T5 | Chờ phê duyệt | `int` | `system` | Approver-facing; also shows the oldest |
| T6 | Có khuyến nghị lâm sàng chưa xử lý | `int` | `system` | Recommendations outstanding — `CLM-CONSOLE-013`'s population |
| T7 | Đánh giá lâm sàng không hoàn tất | `int` | `system` | `CLM-CONSOLE-015`'s population. **Distinct from T6** — a failed assessment and an empty one mean opposite things (BR-AUTO-3) |
| T8 | Lỗi xử lý tài liệu | `int` | `system` | `EXTRACTION_ERROR` and stalled `DOC_PROCESSING`. **An operational queue, never an outcome** (D1 §4.3). Opens S-03 — §5.19 |
| T9 | Chi trả bị treo | `int` | `system` | Stalled `PAYMENT_IN_PROGRESS`, plus `REJECTED` and `RETURNED` awaiting an operator. Opens S-03 — §5.19 |
| T10 | Duyệt tự động hôm nay — số hồ sơ | `int` | `system` | How many claims settled without a human today |
| T11 | Duyệt tự động hôm nay — tổng số tiền | `money` | `system` | The number that says **how much money** moved without a human today. Split from T10 because a count and an amount are two measurements, not one |
| T12 | Tỷ lệ đồng thuận | `derived` | `system` | Confirmed ÷ total recommendations, rolling, as a percentage (BR-TRACK-6, SC-09). **No target line is drawn** — B-16 is deliberately unset until the first benchmark, and drawing an invented target would be worse than drawing none |
| T13 | Cơ sở y tế chưa có trong danh mục | `int` | `system` | Claims whose provider is absent from the master, and therefore priced as off-network (§5.17) |

#### 5.15.2 Rules

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| **V-560** | **No tile measures a statutory clock.** Ageing is the internal SLA only, from submission — D1 B-04, S-19. The complete-and-valid-file timestamp is captured (V-504) and is not counted against here |
| **V-561** | **No tile is broken down by diagnosis, ICD-10 or condition class.** For `ADMIN` that would breach A3 §4.11; for everyone else it is clinical detail on a shared screen, and the claim is where it belongs |
| **V-562** | T10, T11 and T12 are the measurements the pilot is judged on that exist nowhere else. All three are read from the audit record, not recomputed from live claims, so they stay stable as claims close |
| **V-563** | Tiles refresh on load and on demand. **No auto-refresh** — a counter that changes while an assessor is reading it is how work gets double-taken in a one-queue model |

#### 5.15.3 Actions

Nothing on this screen changes a claim. Every control either narrows what is counted or hands the user to the screen where the work is done.

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Mở ô đếm** (drill through a tile) | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER`, `ADMIN` | The tile has a non-zero count | Opens S-01 pre-filtered to that tile's population, **scope-filtered as a predicate at the query layer** (A3 §6). For `ADMIN` the list opens redacted and the read is logged | — |
| **Mở hàng đợi vận hành** | `ASSESSOR`, `ADMIN` | T8 or T9 is non-zero | Opens S-03 (§5.19) filtered to that tile — T8 to the extraction failures, T9 to the payment failures | — |
| **Chọn khoảng thời gian** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER`, `ADMIN` | — | T10, T11 and T12 render for today, the current week or the current month. The state and ageing tiles are always live and carry no period | — |
| **Làm mới** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER`, `ADMIN` | — | Re-reads every tile on demand. **There is no auto-refresh** — V-563 | — |
| **Xuất số liệu bảng điều khiển** | `APPROVER`, `ADMIN` | — | CSV of the tile values **as displayed**, with the scope and the period stated in the file. **No claim-level rows and no clinical breakdown** (V-561) | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-78**)* on refusal |

#### 5.15.4 Empty and error

| Condition | What the console shows |
|---|---|
| Nothing in a bucket | `0`, not a hidden tile. An empty operator queue is information |
| A tile's source is unavailable | That tile shows an outage marker; the rest render. **A dashboard that fails whole because one counter failed is worse than a partial one** — the opposite of the work list's rule in §5.3.4, and deliberately so: the work list is where work is taken, the dashboard is where it is looked at |

### 5.16 Administration (F55)

**Purpose.** Hold the four things the console configures — people, the threshold, the document checklist, and general master data — without a release.

> **Three masters are not F55's, and each has its own section for a stated reason.** The **provider master** is F57 (§5.17) because one boolean on it moves money. The **payee and payout-account master** is F58 (§5.20) because it is claim-time data with a claim-time verification control on it. The **group policy and member bulk load** is F59 (§3.6) because it is where policy and member data enters the solution. F55 holds what is left, and what is left is genuinely ordinary reference data.

**Entered from.** The console's navigation. S-09.

**Who may open it.** `ADMIN` only, scope `MASTER`, and **`ADMIN` performs no claim operations at all** (A3 §4.11). One item is visible to `APPROVER` as **R** — the auto-approval threshold (A3 §3.1).

#### 5.16.1 Users and roles

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Tên đăng nhập | `text(40)` | `user` | M | Unique across all users; immutable after creation | inline |
| F2 | Họ tên | `text(200)` | `user` | M | Present; §2.9's canonical name width | inline |
| F3 | Email | `text(200)` | `user` | M | One address, syntactically valid. A hard bounce marks it `UNDELIVERABLE` and no further mail is attempted until an administrator clears the flag (Part VI §6.1.5) | inline |
| F4 | Vai trò | `enum(role)` multi | `user` | M | `ASSESSOR` · `APPROVER` · `ADMIN`. **A user may hold more than one**, and A3 §4.1 then binds per claim, not per user (A3 §0.2). **Never on the acting user's own record** — V-570 | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-79**)* |
| F5 | Trạng thái | `enum(userState)` | `user` | M | `ĐANG_HOẠT_ĐỘNG` · `NGỪNG_HOẠT_ĐỘNG` | inline |
| F6 | Quyền `clinical` | `bool` | `user` | O | Required to edit the clinical knowledge base (A3 §4.13). **Never on the acting user's own record** — V-570 | *(new A2 item — **D2-79**)* |

**Note on F6.** F38 is IDP's feature, so this grant governs **our** side of any proposal route only. It does not confer anything inside IDP.

**V-570 — no user may modify their own roles or their own `clinical` grant** (A3 §4.8). The controls are absent on the acting user's own record, and the API refuses independently. Privilege escalation is otherwise a single click.

**Actions — users and roles**

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Tạo người dùng** | `ADMIN` | F1 to F5 complete; F1 not already in use | User created and audited with the acting administrator's identity. **Inactive until F5 is set active** | inline on a duplicate login |
| **Sửa người dùng** | `ADMIN` | Not F4 or F6 on the acting administrator's own record — V-570 | Change written and audited **old value → new value** (BR-AUDIT-2) | *(new A2 item — **D2-79**)* |
| **Ngừng hoạt động** | `ADMIN` | F5 is active; the target is not the acting administrator | F5 → `NGỪNG_HOẠT_ĐỘNG` and open sessions end. **Claims already assigned are not reassigned automatically** — they are listed so an approver can reassign them through §5.3.3, because silently moving a person's work is how a claim goes missing | inline |
| **Đặt lại mật khẩu** | `ADMIN` | — | A reset is issued to F3. The password is **never displayed and never mailed in clear**, and the reset is audited | — |
| **Xóa người dùng** | — | — | **Does not exist.** A user who has touched a claim must stay resolvable in the processing trail forever (BR-AUDIT-1, V-550); deactivation is the mechanism and there is no control for deletion on any screen | — |

#### 5.16.2 The auto-approval threshold — the second-administrator rule

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F7 | Ngưỡng duyệt tự động | `money` | `config` | M | Integer dong, > 0. Default **2.000.000 đ** (D1 B-03) | inline |
| F8 | Người đề nghị · thời điểm | `derived` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F9 | Người xác nhận · thời điểm | `derived` | `system` | M | **A different administrator** | `CLM-CONSOLE-009` |
| F10 | Hiệu lực từ | `datetime` | `system` | M | — | — |
| **F11a** | **Hiệu lực đến** | `datetime` | `system` | O | — | — |
| **F11b** | **Căn cứ thay đổi** | `text(200)` | `user` | O | A reference to the instrument that authorised the change — the approval note, the minute, the memo. Retained on the version | — |

**Notes on the fields above.** F8 is recorded when the change is requested and F10 is set to the moment of confirmation; both are written by the platform, so neither carries a validation. The field numbering continues from §5.16.1 because S-09 is one screen.

**On F11a, and why its *Validation* column is now empty.** F11a is **set by the platform when a later version supersedes this one**; **every version is retained**, and a claim resolves against the version its `autoApprovalThresholdAsOf` names. That is `V-722`, it is defined at **§5.11.4** and enforced there, and restating it in a *Validation* cell on a read-only field put a rule in a column with no error path — which §2.2 defines as a defect and §10.4 now counts. The behaviour is unchanged. *(One of the four rows §10.4 names — v0.6.)*

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Đề nghị thay đổi ngưỡng** | `ADMIN` | New value entered | Change requested, **not applied**; the old value stays in force | `CLM-CONSOLE-008` |
| **Xác nhận thay đổi** | `ADMIN` | The confirming user is **not** the requester | Applied; audited **with both identities** (A3 §4.7, BR-AUTO-2) | `CLM-CONSOLE-009` where the requester tries to confirm |

**This is the most sensitive number in the Claim Platform**, and it is a single field edit: raising it silently approves larger claims with no human involved. It is one of exactly two places where the pilot's deliberate two-level model is exceeded on purpose — the other is import commit (A3 §4.9) — and both guard an action with a blast radius far wider than one claim.

**V-571 — a threshold change is not retrospective.** It applies to the gate evaluation of claims registered after F10, and never re-evaluates a claim already decided. A3 does not state this (A3 §4.14 states the analogous rule for the provider master), so it is specified here and raised as **D2-73**: without it, BR-TRACK-4's re-run of the chain could evaluate a gate against a threshold that did not exist when the claim was registered.

| Service category → benefit mapping | Yes | A5 §8.1 | Per category × treatment setting |
