### 5.17 Provider master (F57)

**Purpose.** Hold the list of medical providers and, on each, the `in_network` flag that the deduction-ratio condition is evaluated against.

**Entered from.** The console's navigation. S-10.

**Who may open it.** `ADMIN` **C** under A3 §4.14, scope `MASTER`. Assessors and approvers **read** it through the lookups on §5.4 and §5.7 and cannot change it.

> **This is not ordinary reference data.** A3 §3.1 says so in the matrix itself: *"It is the data source for a money-moving rule (A5 §4.3), not ordinary reference data."* One boolean on this screen decides whether a 20% deduction applies to an outpatient or dental claim — and since B-09 removed the assessor's discretion, **nobody downstream can correct it.**

#### 5.17.1 Field table

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Mã cơ sở y tế | `text(20)` | `user` | M | Unique, immutable after creation | inline |
| F2 | Tên cơ sở y tế | `text(200)` | `user` | M | Vietnamese, with diacritics as printed. Matched against the extracted provider name (A4 §4.1) | inline |
| F3 | Tên viết tắt / tên khác | `text(200)` multi | `user` | O | — | — |
| F4 | Mã số thuế | `text(13)` | `user` | O | 10 or 13 digits, and **unique across the master** — a shared tax code makes A4 R3's strongest match key ambiguous | inline |
| F5 | Địa chỉ | `text(300)` | `user` | O | — | — |
| F6 | Loại hình | `enum(providerType)` | `user` | O | — | — |
| F7 | **Trong danh mục liên kết** | `bool` | `user` | **M** | `in_network` — **the value A5 §4.3's `PROVIDER_OFF_NETWORK` condition reads.** Setting or clearing it changes what every claim registered from F8 onward is paid, by 20% on benefit groups `200` and `300`. The change is refused unless F12 carries a reason, and the console states the money consequence before it is written | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-75**)* |
| F8 | Hiệu lực từ | `date` | `user` | M | ≥ today on a change — **a change may not be back-dated** (V-584) | inline |
| F9 | Hiệu lực đến | `date` | `user` | O | — | — |
| F10 | Phiên bản | `int` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F11 | Người tạo · Người sửa · thời điểm | `derived` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F12 | Ghi chú | `textarea(500)` | `user` | C — **mandatory whenever F7 is set or cleared** | The reason the flag was set as it was — the contract reference, where there is one. Retained on the version (V-581) | *(new A2 item — **D2-75**)* |
| F13 | Tỉnh/Thành phố | `lookup(province)` | `user` | O | — | — |

**Notes on the fields above.** **F3 is the practical determinant of whether the extracted provider name matches**, and it is maintained from the first extraction mismatches rather than guessed up front. **F6** is `BỆNH_VIỆN` · `PHÒNG_KHÁM` · `NHA_KHOA` · `KHÁC`. **F9** is set when a version is superseded or the provider is retired. **F10** is incremented on every change and **every version is retained** (V-580). **F11** is the attribution A3 §4.14 requires. **F5 and F13** are descriptive and are never read by a rule.

> **Why F7 is the one row on this screen that carries an error path.** It is the single most money-sensitive field in the product: it is mandatory, it is a boolean, it has no downstream corrector since B-09 removed the assessor's discretion, and it is not re-readable once a claim is registered (V-583). A rule with no way to tell the person that it fired is a defect anywhere (§2.2); here it is the difference between a 20% deduction applied deliberately and one applied by a mis-click nobody was told about.

#### 5.17.2 Versioned, attributed, and effective-dated

A3 §4.14, implemented exactly:

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| **V-580** | **A change creates a new version.** The previous version is end-dated, never overwritten, and both stay readable |
| **V-581** | **Every change is attributed** — who, when, and F12's reason |
| **V-582** | **A change takes effect only for claims registered after it.** It **never re-prices a claim already assessed** |
| **V-583** | **The mechanism: `providerMasterAsOf` is pinned onto the claim at registration** (§5.2.4) and every `in_network` read on that claim resolves against the version in force at that instant — including the reads performed when **BR-TRACK-4 re-runs the whole chain** after a clinical confirmation |
| **V-584** | F8 may not be back-dated. A retrospective effective date would defeat V-582 by another route |

**Why the pin, and why registration rather than the service date.** A5 §4.3 says the condition is evaluated from *the provider recorded on the insured event* — and that provider is not known until extraction, which happens after registration and can be corrected by the assessor afterwards. A3 §4.14 says the flag is effective-dated at *registration*. Both hold only if the two are separated: **which provider** is a fact about the claim that may change during assessment; **which version of the master answers the question** is fixed at registration. Without the pin, the same claim re-run after a master edit would settle differently — and BR-TRACK-4 re-runs the chain, so that is not hypothetical. **Effective-dating is what keeps the settlement reproducible**, and the pin is what makes effective-dating work on a value discovered late.

#### 5.17.3 The absent-provider default

**A provider absent from the master is treated as off-network** (A5 §4.3). The deduction applies.

**Why that default and not the other one.** The safe default is the one that does not silently pay at the higher rate: an unknown provider treated as in-network would over-pay quietly and invisibly, while an unknown provider treated as off-network under-pays visibly, on a settlement letter that states the condition it applied. One of those is discoverable and the other is not.

**And the cost of it, stated plainly, because it is severe.** If the provider master is not loaded, **every claim the deduction reaches is cut by 20%** — benefit groups `200` and `300`, outpatient and dental (Framework §7.1's note on F57). Inpatient, maternity and accident carry no deduction ratio and are untouched. Since B-09, **no assessor can correct it on the claim**, and since V-582 a corrective edit to the master does not reach a claim already registered.

Three mitigations, all on this screen or reachable from it:

| # | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| 1 | **The unmatched-provider flag** on the work list (§5.3.1 F10) and the dashboard tile T13 (§5.15.1) make an unloaded or incomplete master visible **before** assessment rather than after a settlement letter |
| 2 | Every event whose provider is unmatched shows the warning at the field on §5.7 (F3), naming the consequence, not merely the absence *(new A2 item needed — **D2-58**)* |
| 3 | The master is a **pilot prerequisite**, loaded before the first claim, and F3's alternate names are maintained from the first extraction mismatches |

**The residual case, and it has no clean answer today.** A provider that *was* in-network but was missing from the master when a claim was registered cannot be corrected on that claim: the flag is pinned, the assessor has no discretion, and the master edit is not retrospective. The only exit the current rules leave is to **cancel the claim and have it re-submitted** — which allocates a new claim number and a new registration date (Framework §7.5, A3 §2.1) — and that is only available before `PENDING_APPROVAL`. Raised as **D2-72**: either the business accepts the exit, or A3 §4.14 needs a narrow, audited correction path, and inventing one here would be exactly the kind of quiet discretion B-09 removed.

#### 5.17.4 Actions

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Thêm cơ sở y tế** | `ADMIN` | F1, F2, F7, F8 complete | Version 1, effective from F8 | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-70**)* |
| **Sửa cơ sở y tế** | `ADMIN` | F8 ≥ today | **New version**; previous end-dated; both retained; attributed | *(new A2 item — **D2-70**)*, stating that the change is effective for claims registered from F8 |
| **Ngừng sử dụng** | `ADMIN` | — | F9 set. **No deletion** — past claims must stay explainable | *(new A2 item — **D2-70**)* |
| **Nhập danh mục** | `ADMIN` | CSV, validated before commit | Same two-phase shape as I-14: validate, review, commit; **no partial import** | — |
| **Xem lịch sử phiên bản** | `ADMIN` | — | Every version with its dates, its author and its reason | — |

**A3 does not require a second administrator here**, and this document does not invent one. The control on this screen is **effective-dating plus attribution**: a change cannot reach a claim that has already been priced, and every change has a name against it. That is a different control from A3 §4.7's, aimed at a different failure — the threshold's danger is a silent change taking effect immediately, and the provider flag's danger is a change taking effect *retrospectively*.

#### 5.17.5 Empty and error

| Condition | What the console shows |
|---|---|
| The master is empty | A prominent warning on S-09 and on the dashboard: **every claim will price as off-network**. Not a quiet empty list |
| A provider name from extraction matches nothing | The claim carries the flag; the assessor may select the right provider on §5.7 F2 if one exists, and the `in_network` value then resolves at `providerMasterAsOf` |
| Two providers share a tax code | Blocked at save. A duplicate tax code makes A4 R3's strongest match key ambiguous |
| A change is attempted with a past effective date | Refused — V-584 |

### 5.19 Operator queue (S-03)

**Purpose.** Give every operational failure in Part V one place to land, one person who can see it, and one action that clears it — so that the guarantee repeated throughout this part, *the claim is never declined, it goes to the operator queue*, terminates on a specified screen rather than on a name.

**Entered from.** S-08's tiles T8 and T9; the console's navigation; and directly from the banner on any claim that is held. Ten places in Part V route here: §5.2.7 (registration held on `I-05` or `I-07`), §5.5.6 (package state `ERROR`), §5.6.8 (extraction error), §5.7.6 (`waitingPeriodDays` is `null`), §5.11.4 (a data error that abandoned the first chain run), §5.12.4 and §5.12.5 (payment rejected, returned, stalled or unreachable).

**Who may open it.** `ASSESSOR` **F** and `ADMIN` **R** (§5.1). The two see different things and that separation is deliberate: **claim-processing failures are the assessor's**, because clearing one means looking at a claim; **notification-dispatch failures are the administrator's** (Part VI §6.1.6, A3 §3.1), because F61 is an administration function and carries no claim data beyond a reference. An administrator opening the claim-processing section sees it **redacted** under A3 §4.11 and the read is logged. `APPROVER` sees the payment rows only, over `ASSIGNED`, because re-releasing a payment is theirs (A3 §4.5).

**This screen is the reason no operational failure in Part V is a claim outcome.** §2.10 and D1 §4.3 forbid expressing a stalled interface as a decision about a customer's claim. That prohibition only holds if the failure goes somewhere a person looks; a rule that says "never decline" and nothing else produces claims that sit in `SUBMITTED` for a week. **The queue is where the platform admits it is stuck.**

#### 5.19.1 What appears in it

**Four populations**, in one list, distinguishable by their `Loại sự cố` and filterable to one at a time. **The fourth is new at v0.6**: §5.28.7 routed a term-register defect here and §5.19.1 defined three populations, none of which it was — so the route terminated on a section that did not accept it. **It is added as a population rather than made a banner on S-13**, because a broken term is not visible from any claim it silently failed to evaluate and nobody opens the register to check. **`ADMIN` holds **R** over it and `ASSESSOR` **F**, on the same split the other three use**: the row names a term and a rule-set reference and carries **no claim data at all**, so it is the one population an administrator can work end to end.

| Population | Rows | Source of the row |
|---|---|---|
| **Operational states** — a claim held in a live state longer than its interface should take | Registration retrying on `I-05` (`503`, timeout, circuit open); registration held on `422 NO_SCHEDULE_AT_DATE`; a package refused by `I-07`; `DOC_PROCESSING` stalled or returned `ERROR`; an `I-16` result that never resolved before the NFR-2a ceiling; a chain run abandoned on a data error (§5.11.4); `PAYMENT_IN_PROGRESS` with no `I-12` callback; `REJECTED` and `RETURNED` payments awaiting a corrected account | The claim's own state plus the elapsed time on the internal clock |
| **Failed notifications** | An outbox row that exhausted its retries, and an address marked `UNDELIVERABLE` after a hard bounce — **Part VI §6.1.6**, whose columns are the ones rendered here | The notification outbox |
| **Stalled interfaces** | An adapter whose circuit is open, or whose backlog has not drained — `I-05`, `I-07`, `I-09`, `I-11`, `I-16` (D3 §1.3) | The adapter's own health, not a claim |
| **Term-register defects** — **the fourth population, new at v0.6, `V-757`** | An `ACTIVE` term that **cannot be evaluated**: a `scopeCode` absent from the rule set's benefit tree (§5.28.7), a fact that is no longer available at the step the term's scope runs at (§5.28.3a, `BR-TERM-9`), or a term whose expression will not parse. **Not a claim failure and not an interface failure** — the claim is unaffected and no outcome moves | **The term register itself**, checked on save and again on every evaluation |

**A row exists because something needs doing, not because something went wrong once.** A call that failed and succeeded on the standard backoff never appears here; the retry schedule in D3 §1.3 runs first, and the queue is what is left after it.

#### 5.19.2 Field table — S-03

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Loại sự cố | `enum(operationalIssueType)` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F2 | Số hồ sơ | `text(20)` | `system` | C — absent on an interface-level row | — | — |
| F3 | Giao diện | `enum(interfaceCode)` | `system` | C — absent on a notification row | — | — |
| F4 | Trạng thái hồ sơ | `enum(claimState)` | `system` | C — where F2 is present | — | — |
| F5 | Thời điểm phát sinh | `datetime` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F6 | Thời gian chờ | `derived` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F7 | Số lần thử lại | `int` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F8 | Lần thử gần nhất | `datetime` | `system` | O | — | — |
| F9 | Lỗi | `text(300)` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F10 | Mã tương quan | `text(40)` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F11 | Người xử lý | `lookup(user)` | `system` | O | — | — |
| F12 | Trạng thái mục | `enum(queueItemState)` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F13 | Hành động đã thực hiện | `derived` | `system` | O | — | — |
| F14 | Lý do bỏ qua | `textarea(2000)` | `user` | C — **mandatory when the item is dismissed** | Recorded on the item and in the trail (BR-AUDIT-2). **A dismissal without a reason is how a stuck claim becomes invisible** | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-76**)* |
| F15 | Giá trị nhập tay | `text(300)` | `user` | C — mandatory when an item is cleared by keying a value | The value the assessor keyed in place of the one the interface did not return, marked `nguồn: cán bộ thẩm định` and audited old → new (V-519) | *(new A2 item — **D2-76**)* |

**Notes on the fields above.** Every row except F14 and F15 is written by the platform, so none of them carries a validation (§2.2). **F1** is `ĐĂNG_KÝ_TREO` · `TRÍCH_XUẤT_LỖI` · `ĐÁNH_GIÁ_LÂM_SÀNG_TREO` · `DỮ_LIỆU_SAI` · `CHI_TRẢ_TREO` · `THÔNG_BÁO_LỖI` · `GIAO_DIỆN_TREO` · **`ĐIỀU_KHOẢN_LỖI`**, the fourth population's code, new at v0.6. **F3** names the D3 interface, `I-05` … `I-16`. **F6** is the elapsed time since F5 and is what the list sorts on by default, descending — the oldest stuck thing first, because in a one-queue model nothing else prioritises it. **F9** is the adapter's last RFC 7807 `title` (D3 §1.5), never a stack trace. **F10** is the `correlationId` that traces the same work across every interface (D3 §1.2). **F12** is `MỚI` · `ĐANG_XỬ_LÝ` · `ĐÃ_XỬ_LÝ` · `ĐÃ_BỎ_QUA`. **F13** lists what has already been tried, so two people do not retry the same thing twice.

**No clinical detail appears on this screen at all** — no diagnosis, no ICD-10, no item name, no amount. A row names a claim and a failure; the work is done on the claim. That is what lets an administrator hold **R** over the whole queue without breaching A3 §4.11.

**Three enumerations this screen introduces need a home** — `operationalIssueType`, `interfaceCode` and `queueItemState` — as does `province` on §5.17.1 F13. §2.3 requires that an `enum(X)` names a set living in A1 §4 or in the annex that owns the concept, and none of these has one yet. They are added to the registration request Part VI §6.5.2 already raises, rather than being defined here, because a set defined in a screen specification is a set nobody else can find.

#### 5.19.3 Actions

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Nhận xử lý sự cố** | `ASSESSOR`, `ADMIN` (own population) | F12 = `MỚI` | F11 = the user, F12 → `ĐANG_XỬ_LÝ`. Prevents two people working the same failure | — |
| **Thử lại** | `ASSESSOR` (claim rows), `ADMIN` (notification rows) | F12 is `MỚI` or `ĐANG_XỬ_LÝ`; the interface's circuit is not open | Re-issues the call **on the same business idempotency key** — `requestId` for `I-07`, `instructionRef` for `I-11`, the outbox key for a notification (D3 §1.3, Part VI §6.1.7). **A retry never creates a second instruction or a second notification.** On success F12 → `ĐÃ_XỬ_LÝ` | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-76**)* on success and on a repeated failure |
| **Nhập tay giá trị** | `ASSESSOR` | The failure is a value the interface did not return and a person can supply — an unreadable field, a provider the master did not match, an invoice header where no XML was supplied (V-525) | F15 written onto the **claim's copy**, marked `nguồn: cán bộ thẩm định`, raw preserved (V-515, V-516). F12 → `ĐÃ_XỬ_LÝ` | *(new A2 item — **D2-76**)* |
| **Giao lại** | `APPROVER`, `ADMIN` | The item is assigned | F11 → the target user; both names in the trail. **Same rule as §5.3.3**: an assessor may take and give back, only an approver may hand work to somebody else (A3 §4.2) | — |
| **Bỏ qua** | `ASSESSOR`, `ADMIN` | F14 entered | F12 → `ĐÃ_BỎ_QUA`, with the reason, the actor and the timestamp. **The claim's own state does not change** — dismissing a queue row admits that nothing more will be done about the failure, and never asserts anything about the claim | *(new A2 item — **D2-76**)*; reason missing → the same item |
| **Mở hồ sơ** | `ASSESSOR` | F2 present; the claim is in scope | Opens S-02. For `ADMIN` the control is **absent** — an administrator performs no claim operations (A3 §4.11) | — |
| **Phát hành lại lệnh chi trả** | `APPROVER` | The row is a `RETURNED` payment with a corrected and re-verified account (BR-PAY-2, A3 §4.5) | Hands over to §5.12.3's *Phát hành lại*, which allocates **a new `instructionRef`** | `PAY-NOTIF-001` |
| **Xóa mục** | — | — | **Does not exist.** A queue row is closed or dismissed, never deleted; the history of what was stuck is part of the claim's trail (BR-AUDIT-1, V-550) | — |

**Retry is idempotent or it is not offered.** The one place in the system where a duplicate costs real money is a payment instruction (§5.12.3), and this screen is the one place where a person is invited to press *try again* on one. The control therefore re-issues the original `instructionRef` and never creates a second instruction; where an operator genuinely needs a new one — a returned payment to a corrected account — that is a different control, with a different name, on a different precondition.

#### 5.19.4 Rules

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| **V-596** | **A row on this screen never changes a claim's state by itself.** Clearing, retrying or dismissing an operational failure resolves the failure; the claim moves only through the transitions in Part VII. **No operational failure is ever expressed as a claim outcome** (§2.10, D1 §4.3, G-3) |
| **V-597** | **Every row carries an elapsed time and the list is sorted by it.** A queue that does not show age is a list, and a list is how a stalled claim survives a week (D1 §8.1) |
| **V-598** | **Every action on this screen is audited** — actor, timestamp, the action, and old value → new value where a value was keyed (BR-AUDIT-2), and it appears on the claim's own trail (§5.14.2) as well as on the item |
| **V-757** | **A term-register defect is an operator-queue population and not a banner.** An `ACTIVE` term that cannot be evaluated — an absent `scopeCode`, a fact its scope can no longer see, an expression that will not parse — **is not evaluated, does not affect any claim, and is invisible from every claim it failed to evaluate**. That is the whole problem: **a term that silently matched nothing is indistinguishable from a term that passed** (§5.28.7), and on §5.9.1a it does not even appear, because it produced no `termOutcome`. **The row carries no claim reference, no personal data and no clinical detail** — a `termId`, a version, a `ruleSetRef` and the reason — which is what lets `ADMIN` hold **R** over it under A3 §4.11 without a redaction. **It is cleared by fixing the term** at §5.28, never by dismissing it: a dismissal here would leave a contractual term in force and unevaluated, which is `V-599`'s point applied to the register |
| **V-599** | **A dismissal is not a resolution.** `ĐÃ_BỎ_QUA` is retained, is visible on the claim, and is reported separately from `ĐÃ_XỬ_LÝ` on the dashboard. A queue that can be emptied without doing anything is worse than no queue |

#### 5.19.5 Empty and error

| Condition | What the console shows |
|---|---|
| The queue is empty | *"Không có sự cố đang chờ xử lý."* — with the filter that produced it, and the counts by `Loại sự cố` all at `0`. **An empty operator queue is information and is displayed as such**, exactly as the dashboard shows `0` rather than hiding a tile (§5.15.4) |
| A row's underlying claim is outside the user's scope | The row does not appear and no count includes it (A3 §6). It is not shown as a redacted placeholder — a row a person cannot act on is noise |
| `ADMIN` is viewing | The claim-processing rows render **without any clinical field**, and the *Mở hồ sơ* control is absent. The notification rows render in full, because they carry no clinical data (Part VI §6.1.6) |
| The queue's own source is unavailable | The screen states the outage and **does not render a partial queue**. A short queue that is short because a query failed is the one thing this screen must never show — the same rule as the work list's in §5.3.4, and for the same reason |
| A retry fails again | F7 increments, F9 carries the new error, and the row stays open. **It is never auto-dismissed after n attempts** — a failure that stops being visible has not stopped happening |

### 5.20 Payee and payout-account master (F58)

**F58 is new in Framework v2.0** and it is one of the three things the deleted Policy Data Store held that came to the Claim Platform rather than going to InsureMO. The reason is the same for all three and it is worth stating once: **a payout account exists to reimburse a claim.** It is created at claim time, verified at claim time by a person holding a claim-side permission, and it is not a term of the contract of insurance. The payee is a party to a **settlement**, not to a policy — and it differs from the insured precisely in the cases a claim raises.

**Purpose.** Hold the payee and the payout account for each insured member, verify the account name against the bank, and be the one place the payment preconditions at A3 §4.6 read from.

**Entered from.** S-02.1's insured panel, one click; S-04 after a member is resolved; the console's navigation. **S-12.**

**Who may open it.** `ASSESSOR` **F** at scope `ASSIGNED`, `APPROVER` **R**, `ADMIN` **F** at scope `MASTER` — A3 §3.2. **The customer never opens it**: they capture the account in the app (Part IV §4.5) and hold exactly one grant over it, *change it*.

> **Three fragments of F58 already exist elsewhere in this document and this section is the single specification they defer to.** Part IV §4.5 is the customer's capture of the account and the four `BR-PAY-*` rules as the app experiences them. Part V §5.12 is the payment instruction and the three preconditions it checks. **Neither restates what is below, and where either appears to, this section wins.** §3.2.8 and §3.2.9 carry the two record schemas; this section carries the screen, the verification flow and the permissions.

#### 5.20.1 The two records

Schemas at §3.2.8 (`payout_account`) and §3.2.9 (`beneficiary`), both **mastered by the Claim Platform**. Restated here only as the shape of the screen:

| Panel | Holds | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **Tài khoản nhận tiền** | Bank, account number, account name, verified flag | A member may hold **more than one**. The account used by a claim is the one the payee points at, pinned onto the claim's snapshot at registration (§5.2.4) |
| **Người thụ hưởng** | Payee name, relationship to the insured, the payee's identity number, and the payout account used | **One row per member, created automatically, defaulting to the insured.** The default is the common case and the entity exists for the case that is not |

**Three parties, not one.** A claim references the **insured member** (whose cover is being used), the **claimant** (who submitted it), and the **beneficiary/payee** (who is paid). They usually coincide in MVP 1 reimbursement and the app defaults all three to the signed-in member — but they are modelled separately, because the payee determines where money goes and reconciling that after the fact is the failure mode that matters most.

> **In v0.2 that paragraph was a claim this document did not keep, and v0.3 keeps it.** It asserted three parties and specified two: the insured is InsureMO's record, the beneficiary has the field table below, **and the claimant had no fields anywhere in Part V** — appearing only as `claim.claimantUserId` inside §6.2.3's `SELF` scope predicate. **The claimant's field table is at §5.4.2 F34 to F37**, on the general tab rather than here, because a claimant is a party to *a claim* while the payee and the account are master data that outlive one. The legal capacity — self, guardian, heir, authorised representative — is the dimension that makes the sentence above true, and it is separate from the family relationship at F9 below (register **S-47**, **B-07**, **G-V-13**).

#### 5.20.2 Field table — S-12

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Người được bảo hiểm | `text(200)` | `imo:I-05` | M | **Read-only.** The insured whose cover is used; not the payee | — |
| F2 | Số thẻ bảo hiểm | `text(20)` | `imo:I-05` | M | **Read-only** | — |
| F3 | Ngân hàng | `lookup(bank)` | `user` | M | V-110 — F3…F5 supplied together or not at all | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-121**)* |
| F4 | Số tài khoản | `text(30)` | `user` | M | V-110. Digits only. **Masked except on focus**, and masked on every list (A2 §5) | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-121**)* |
| F5 | Tên chủ tài khoản | `text(140)` | `system` | M | **Never typed on any surface — BR-PAY-1.** Written only by the verify action; read-only thereafter. **The control has no keyboard, so the screen cannot produce the failure — but a payload can**, and a request carrying a value for this field is **refused server-side rather than ignored**, because a client that sends one is a client that believes it may set it | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-121**)* on the server-side refusal |
| F6 | Đã xác thực tên chủ tài khoản | `bool` | `system` | M | **Set by the verify action only.** Resets to `false` on any change to F3 or F4, **on edit and not on save** — BR-PAY-2 | `CLM-CONSOLE-006` where a settlement or a payment is attempted |
| F7 | Người xác thực · thời điểm | `derived` | `system` | C — where F6 is `true` | Actor and timestamp of the successful verification | — |
| F8 | Người thụ hưởng — họ và tên | `text(200)` | `user` | M | Defaults to F1 | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-121**)* |
| F9 | Người thụ hưởng — quan hệ với người được BH | `enum(relationship)` | `user` | M | Defaults to `SELF` | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-121**)* |
| F10 | Người thụ hưởng — số giấy tờ tùy thân | `text(20)` | `user` | M | **The payee's**, not the insured's. Mandatory **even where the insured has none** — a minor has no CCCD and the payment is still made against an identity | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-121**)* |
| F11 | Người thụ hưởng — tài khoản nhận tiền | `lookup(payout_account)` | `user` | M | **V-701** — may be an account belonging to a different member | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-122**)* |
| F12 | Hồ sơ đang dùng tài khoản này | `derived` | `system` | — | Claim numbers and states of every non-terminal claim whose snapshot pins this account | — |

**Notes on the fields above.** **F1 and F2 are read from I-05 and are read-only here** — the insured is InsureMO's record and this screen does not edit it (§3.5). Widths follow §2.9: name `text(200)`, card and identity numbers `text(20)`, bank account number `text(30)`. **F5 has no keyboard on any surface**, which is BR-PAY-1 stated as a control rather than a rule. **F12 exists because a change on this screen reaches claims that are already in flight** and the person making it is entitled to see which ones before they make it — §5.20.5.

#### 5.20.3 Actions

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Lưu** | `ASSESSOR` (scope `ASSIGNED`), `ADMIN` (scope `MASTER`) | Validations pass | Writes the account and beneficiary rows; **clears F5 and F6 where F3 or F4 changed** (BR-PAY-2), on every claim referencing the account; audit entry per field (F63) | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-121**)* on failure |
| **Xác thực tên chủ tài khoản** | `ASSESSOR` (scope `ASSIGNED`), `ADMIN` | F3 and F4 complete; a claim exists and is assigned to the acting assessor | Calls the verification service; on success writes F5 from the **bank's** answer and sets F6 `true` with actor and timestamp | Success: none. Service says no match: `CLM-VAL-005` to the customer (Part IV §4.5). Service unreachable: **operator queue, never the customer** (§2.10) |
| **Đổi tài khoản** | `ASSESSOR`, `ADMIN` | The claim is before `PENDING_APPROVAL`, **or** an approver's re-release is accepted (A3 §4.5) | Replaces F3 and F4; BR-PAY-2 clearing; where a settlement is already approved the payment is **held** | `CLM-CONSOLE-010` |
| **Xem** | `APPROVER` | — | Read-only. **An approver does not verify** — see below | — |

#### 5.20.4 Who may verify, and why it is not the customer and not the approver

**A3 §3.2 assigns *verify a payout account* to `ASSESSOR` and `ADMIN`, at scope `ASSIGNED`, and to no one else.** Three exclusions follow, and each is deliberate:

| Excluded | Why |
|---|---|
| **`CUST`** | A3 §1 gives the customer exactly one grant over the payout account — **change it**, `C`, scope `SELF`. A customer who could assert their own account name verified would defeat the only control standing between a mis-keyed digit and a payment to a stranger. **The app captures the account unverified and says so as a progress line, not an error** (Part IV §4.5) |
| **`APPROVER`** | An approver releases the money (A3 §4.6, F51). The person who releases a payment does not also attest the account it goes to; that is the same separation as F49/F50 applied to the payee rather than to the amount |
| **Anyone, on an unassigned claim** | Scope `ASSIGNED` means verification happens on a claim someone is working. It is also why verification **cannot** happen on a `DRAFT`: a `DRAFT` has no claim number and no assignee, so no assessor holds the scope. Part IV §4.5 works through the deadlock this would otherwise create |

**The timing follows from the scope, and it is the whole reason submission is not gated on verification.** Verification is possible from the first moment a claim exists that an assessor can be assigned to — registration. Before that there is no holder of the permission. **So a claim is submitted on an unverified account, deliberately, and the money is held behind A3 §4.6 until verification succeeds.** What is blocked is the payment, never the customer's ability to ask.

> **The verification service has no contract, and this section cannot invent one.** A3 §3.2 lists it as a function and I-05 returns `accountNameVerified`, but **D3 carries no verify operation** — there is no request, no response, no error set and no timeout behaviour. BR-PAY-1 says F5 is populated *only* by that call, and the call does not exist. This was raised in v0.1 as **D2-106** against a store that at least held the flag; **F58 makes it sharper, because the flag is now ours and the service behind it is still nobody's.** It is the one open item that blocks a screen in this section rather than a detail on it.

#### 5.20.5 The relationship to the payment preconditions (A3 §4.6, §5.12)

**§5.12.1 states three preconditions on a payment instruction. The third is this screen's, and the fourth condition — the one that is not in A3 §4.6 — is this screen's too.**

| # | Precondition | What F58 supplies | Where it is checked |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The claim is in `APPROVED` | Nothing | Claim service |
| 2 | The amount is exactly the approved settlement total | Nothing | The adapter, re-checked against the claim |
| **3** | **The payee account is verified** — `accountNameVerified = true` | **F6**, pinned onto the claim's snapshot at registration and re-read live at instruction time | Refused by the console; `422 ACCOUNT_NOT_VERIFIED` at I-11 (D3 §I-11) |
| **4** | **A3 §4.5's hold** — where the account changed after approval, the payment waits for an approver to re-release it | **The change itself.** A save on F3 or F4 against a claim in `APPROVED` sets the hold | `CLM-CONSOLE-010` |

> **Precondition 4 closes one specific attack and it is worth naming it.** Submit a clean claim, let it be approved, then change the payout account. Every check that mattered has already passed. **This is why BR-PAY-2's clearing runs on every claim referencing the account and not only on the one being edited**, why F12 shows which those are, and why the re-release sits with an approver rather than with whoever made the change. D1 §3.2.2 names the failure mode: a misdirected payment is the most expensive and least recoverable error a claim system makes.

**V-710 — the verified account name is compared against the beneficiary, and until v0.3 it was compared against nothing.** BR-PAY-3 and §5.10.2's check 9 require `accountNameVerified = true`. **No document said whose name the verified name had to be.** A `true` with no comparand is a boolean about a bank's own record, and the gap between a clean claim and a payment into an unrelated account is exactly the size of that missing comparand.

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| 1 | **F5, the verified account name, is compared against F8, the beneficiary's name.** Not the insured's, and not the claimant's |
| 2 | **Where the beneficiary is not the insured, the family relationship recorded at §5.4.2 F37 is the relationship of record**, and the beneficiary's identity number at F10 is what A3 §4.12 tests |
| 3 | **A mismatch is shown with both values and is not corrected** (§2.10). It does not silently clear F6; it is a warning that the settlement checks then read |
| 4 | **The comparison is diacritic-insensitive and case-insensitive**, and nothing else — no fuzzy matching and no initials. A bank's answer and a payee record differing by more than diacritics is a fact a person should see |
| 5 | **The plan records what was compared against what** (§5.10.1's payee row), so an approver reviewing a payment can see the anchor and not only the flag |

**V-709 — where the claimant says they are the insured, they must be.** Where §5.4.2 F36 is `BẢN_THÂN`, F34 and F35 must equal the insured's name and identity number from the snapshot. **A mismatch is blocking on save**, not a warning — this is the one place in Part V where a mismatch stops a person, and it is deliberate: a claimant who declares themselves the insured while carrying a different identity is either a data-entry error that will misroute a payment or a fact that needs a different legal capacity chosen. Reference System A blocks in the same place, and it is the strongest single control on this screen. *(new A2 item — **D2-125**)*.

> **What these two rules unlock, stated because it is the whole argument for S-47.** **A3 §4.12** — the conflict-of-interest check — compares the acting user's identity number against the insured, **the claimant** and the beneficiary. Until v0.3 the claimant's identity number existed nowhere in this document, so that third comparison ran against nothing and returned *no match* on every claim, every time, silently. **G-B-02** raised it in the previous round and it survived v0.2 untouched. It is closed at §5.4.2 F35.

**An earlier gate, and it is not the same gate.** BR-PAY-3 — no settlement on an unverified account — is enforced when the settlement plan is submitted, at §5.10.2's check **V-593**, with `CLM-CONSOLE-006`. It exists so that the failure is found while an assessor is still holding the claim, rather than at the payment instruction when an approver is. **Two checks, one condition, two different people's screens** — and neither is redundant, because a plan submitted on a verified account can still be paid against one that was changed afterwards.

#### 5.20.6 Rules

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| **V-701** | **The payee's payout account may belong to a different member.** F11 is a lookup across the platform's accounts, not across this member's, and restricting it would make the case the entity exists for unrepresentable — a minor's settlement paid to a parent's account. **What it may not be is an account with no owner**: the referenced account must exist and carry a `member_id` |
| **V-702** | **F5 is written only by the verification service.** No screen, no import, no API and no administrator writes it. An import supplies F3 and F4 and creates the account with F6 `false`, without exception (§3.6.1) |
| **V-703** | **A change to F3 or F4 clears F5 and F6 on every claim that references the account**, immediately, on edit rather than on save, so that no screen anywhere briefly shows a verified name against a different account |
| **V-704** | **A payout account is never deleted while any claim references it.** The claim snapshot pins the account used, the payment instruction quotes it, and a deleted account makes a settled claim unexplainable. It is deactivated instead |

> **`V-701` … `V-704` are allocated from a new range, and §8.1 records why.** Part V's `V-5nn` block is exhausted at `V-599`; F58 arrives after it was full. The block is extended into **`V-701 … V-799`** rather than reusing a retired number, because a reused identifier is how a document starts meaning two things at once.

#### 5.20.7 Empty and error

| Condition | What the console shows |
|---|---|
| No account captured yet — the customer submitted without one | The panel is empty with a prompt to capture it, **not an error**. It is a normal state on a claim that arrived from an information request path |
| Verification service unreachable, times out, or returns an unusable answer | **The account stays unverified, the claim keeps moving, and the failure goes to the operator queue on S-03** (§5.19). **Nothing is shown to the customer** — a verification the service could not perform at all is not the customer's error to fix (A2 rule M-7, §2.10) |
| Verification returns a name that does not match | `CLM-VAL-005` to the customer against the app's F13 (Part IV §4.5), whose remedy is their single grant — a different account. **The console shows the outcome and not the name the bank returned**: naming it teaches an attacker which digit was wrong |
| `I-05` unavailable, so F1 and F2 cannot be read | The account and payee panels still render from **our** records — they are ours (§3.2.8, §3.2.9). The insured's name and card number show the values on the claim's snapshot, marked as such. **This is one of the few places where the split model degrades better than the store did** |
| A claim in `PENDING_APPROVAL` or later | Every control is **absent** (V-005). The account is changed by an approver's re-release path or not at all |

| # | Item | Category | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| **D2-121** | Console messages for a failed save on the payee and payout-account panels — mandatory field, V-110's three-together rule, and the account-name width | **A2** | BA |
| **D2-122** | Console message for **V-701**: the selected payout account does not exist or has no owner | **A2** | BA |
| **D2-106** | **The payout-account verification service has no contract in D3** — no request, no response, no error set, no timeout behaviour. Raised in v0.1; **F58 makes it the item that blocks a screen** rather than a detail on one | **D3** | BA + dev lead |

### 5.21 Settlement plan versions (F49, F53)

**Appended rather than inserted, by the convention §5.18 already states.** §5.19 and §5.20 took the next free number rather than renumbering every citation of §5.18; §5.21 to §5.26 do the same. **A section number is an address, not a position.**

**Purpose.** Show every round of submission this claim has been through, what the plan contained at each, who decided it and why — so that a returned-and-resubmitted claim can be reviewed as a sequence rather than as a single current state.

**Entered from.** §5.14.1's fifth view; §5.11.3's *Xem các lần trình duyệt trước*; the claim header where more than one version exists. **A surface of S-02 and S-07 — not a new screen** (§5.1).

**Who may open it.** `ASSESSOR` **R**, `APPROVER` **R**, scope `ASSIGNED`. **No `ADMIN`** — a frozen plan carries diagnosis, ICD-10 codes and cost-line item names, which is A3 §4.11's whole subject.

#### 5.21.1 Field table — one row per submission round

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Lần trình duyệt | `int` | `system` | M | From 1, per claim, never reused — V-716 | — |
| F2 | Người trình | `lookup(user)` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F3 | Thời điểm trình | `datetime` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F4 | Ghi chú trình duyệt | `textarea(2000)` | `system` | O | §5.10.1 F1 as it stood at that submission | — |
| F5 | Người quyết định | `lookup(user)` | `system` | C — where the round has been decided | `SYSTEM` on an auto-approval (V-551) | — |
| F6 | Quyết định | `enum(approvalDecision)` | `system` | C — as F5 | `PHÊ_DUYỆT` · `TRẢ_LẠI` · `TỪ_CHỐI_TOÀN_BỘ` | — |
| F7 | Thời điểm quyết định | `datetime` | `system` | C — as F5 | — | — |
| F8 | Lý do | `textarea(2000)` | `system` | C — mandatory on a return | §5.11.2 F5 as entered | — |
| F9 | Tổng số tiền chi trả của lần này | `money` | `system` | M | The payable **as frozen**, not as it stands now | — |
| F10 | Phương án đã đóng băng | `derived` | `system` | M | **Immutable — V-716 rule 5.** No role including `ADMIN` may edit or delete a frozen version, **there is no control for it on any screen** (§5.21.3), and a write reaching the server is refused rather than applied | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-131**)* on a refused write |
| F11 | Khác biệt so với lần trước | `derived` | `system` | O | See §5.21.2 | — |

**Notes on the fields above.** Every row is written by the platform at submission or at decision, so none carries a validation or an error path (§2.2). **F9 is the frozen figure and is deliberately not recomputed** — a version whose total moved after it was decided is not a record of anything. **F10 is opened, not summarised**: the point of the version is that the reader sees what the decider saw.

#### 5.21.2 What changed between rounds

Computed on demand between any two versions, and between the latest version and the claim's current state.

| Compared | Shown |
|---|---|
| Cost lines | Lines added, lines removed, and per line: a changed decision, a changed reason code, a changed rationale, a changed amount, **a changed insured event (V-705 rule 4)** and a changed note |
| Insured events | Events added or removed (B-43), and per event: a changed cover decision, a changed condition class, a changed occurrence date, a changed liability rationale |
| Clinical | Recommendations decided differently between rounds, with both reasons |
| Amounts | Total claimed, total in-scope, total payable and total customer-borne, both figures with the delta |
| Documents | Items that changed state between the two submissions |

**This is what a second round of approval was blind to.** An approver returning a claim asks for something to change; on resubmission they were shown the plan afresh, with nothing marking what had moved. The comparison is derived from two immutable snapshots, so it cannot disagree with either.

#### 5.21.3 Actions

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Mở phương án của một lần trình** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER` | The version exists | Renders F10 read-only. **The read is logged** (BR-AUDIT-4) | — |
| **So sánh hai lần trình** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER` | Two versions exist | §5.21.2's comparison | — |
| **Xuất phương án bồi thường** | `ASSESSOR` **R**, `APPROVER` **R** | The version exists | §5.10.3's export of that version — stamped, logged, **unsigned and saying so** (V-717) | *(new A2 item — **D2-131**)* |
| **Sửa hoặc xóa một lần trình** | — | — | **Does not exist.** No role, including `ADMIN`, has this control — V-716 rule 5 | — |

#### 5.21.4 Empty and error

| Condition | What the console shows |
|---|---|
| The claim has never been submitted | The view states so and names what submission requires — §5.10.2's thirteen checks. **Not an empty list** |
| Exactly one version, undecided | The version, with F5 to F8 empty and marked *đang chờ phê duyệt*. The comparison control is absent, not disabled |
| A version's rendering fails | The header row still renders from F1 to F9, with the body marked unavailable and the correlation id. **A version whose figures are readable and whose body is not is still evidence** |

### 5.22 Correspondence history on the claim (F53, F61)

**Purpose.** Answer, from the claim, the question the console could not answer at all: *what have we actually sent this customer, what did it say, and did it arrive.*

**Register rows S-43 and B-35**, which are the same finding seen from the settlement side and the intake side. **G-B-11** raised it in the previous round and v0.2 did not close it.

**Entered from.** §5.14.1's fourth view, and §5.14.4's *Mở lịch sử thư từ*. **A surface of S-07** (§5.1).

**Who may open it.** **Anyone who may open the claim** — `ASSESSOR` **R**, `APPROVER` **R**, and `ADMIN` **R** with the body redacted where a message quotes clinical detail (A3 §4.11). This is wider than v0.2's arrangement on purpose: the outbox at Part VI §6.1 is an administrator's screen and shows **failed** dispatches only, so the person a customer telephones — the assessor holding the claim — had nowhere to look.

#### 5.22.1 Field table — one row per message sent

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Thời điểm gửi | `datetime` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F2 | Người gửi | `derived` | `system` | M | A named user, or `SYSTEM` where the message followed an event (V-551) | — |
| F3 | Mã thông điệp | `text(20)` | `system` | M | The A2 code — `CLM-NOTIF-005`, `DOC-NOTIF-001` | — |
| F4 | Phiên bản mẫu | `text(20)` | `system` | M | The template version in force when it was rendered (Part VI §6.1.3) | — |
| F5 | Loại thư | `derived` | `master` | M | A2's Vietnamese name for F3 — **never the code**, to anyone (A2 rule M-3) | — |
| F6 | Kênh | `enum(channel)` | `system` | M | A2 §0.3 | — |
| F7 | Địa chỉ nhận | `text(200)` | `system` | M | Masked per A2 §5 on a list; full on the row | — |
| F8 | Nội dung đã gửi | `derived` | `system` | M | **The rendered body, as sent** — every placeholder resolved. Opened, not summarised | — |
| F9 | Kết quả gửi | `enum(deliveryOutcome)` | `system` | M | Sent, delivered, failed after retries, or the address marked `UNDELIVERABLE` (Part VI §6.1.5) | — |
| F10 | Số lần thử | `int` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F11 | Gửi lại tới | `derived` | `system` | O | Where the message was re-sent under V-719: the addresses, the actor and the timestamp | — |

**Notes on the fields above.** Every row is written by the notification engine, so none carries a validation (§2.2) — the exception §2.2 grants Part VI does **not** apply here, and no row needs it. **F8 is the body as rendered**, not the template plus parameters: a template that has since been versioned would otherwise render a message the customer never received, which is the one thing this view exists to prevent.

**V-718 — every message about a claim writes a row here, without exception.** Customer-facing or staff-facing (§5.23), automatic or re-sent, delivered or failed. **A message that failed is not hidden from the claim and shown only on the administrator's outbox**: the person who has to explain it to the customer is the one holding the claim.

#### 5.22.2 Actions

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Xem nội dung đã gửi** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER` | — | Renders F8. **Logged where the body carries clinical detail** (V-554) | — |
| **Gửi lại thông báo** | `ASSESSOR` | The row exists and its A2 message is customer-facing; claim in scope; one or more addresses entered | **Re-sends the message already generated**, unchanged, to the addresses keyed. Writes a new row with F11 populated and the original referenced. **The addresses are recorded** — V-719 | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-132**)* |
| **Xuất lịch sử thư từ** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER` | One claim, in scope | CSV of F1 to F11 for the claim. **Logged where any body carries clinical detail** (V-554) | *(new A2 item — **D2-78**)* |
| **Soạn thư mới** | — | — | **Does not exist.** See below | — |

**V-719 — a manual send re-sends an existing message; it never originates one.** Register rows **S-44** and **B-34**, applied in a reduced form and stated as one rule because they are one mechanism.

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| 1 | **What may be sent is a message this claim has already generated.** The body is exactly what was rendered at F1; nothing is re-rendered and no placeholder is re-resolved |
| 2 | **What the assessor supplies is the address, and only the address.** One or more, keyed |
| 3 | **Every re-send is a row** (V-718) carrying the addresses, the actor and the timestamp |
| 4 | **The claim's state does not change**, and no rule reads a re-send. It is a delivery act, not a claim act |

**The reduction, and it is the whole of what makes this cheap.** The reference lets a member of staff pick from a menu of about ten letter types, filtered by the claim's current state, and send one. **We do not**, for a reason that is §0.5 rather than effort: **A2 owns which message fires on which event**, and a console control that originates a letter makes that ownership unenforceable — the catalogue would describe the messages the platform sends and the console would send others. §6.1.9's exclusion of staff-composed correspondence stands untouched by this section. **What the register itself observed is that the reference's mechanism is not free composition either** — it is re-sending a template to a different address, which is the half that carries the value and none of the cost (**G-B-30** was priced against the wrong assumption).

**And what B-36 asked for, reduced to what Part V can hold.** Each message row carries **F3 and F4 — the A2 code and the template version in force when it rendered** — which is what makes a sent message reconstructable and a template change traceable to the claims sent before and after it. **What is not adopted here** is the reference's *official form code with a year of issue* and its *machine-checkable applicability condition beside each template*: both are the structure of the message catalogue, **A2 owns it (§0.5)**, and a screen specification that invented a form-code register would be describing a document it does not own. Recorded as a correction owed to A2 — **D2-132**.

#### 5.22.3 Empty and error

| Condition | What the console shows |
|---|---|
| Nothing has been sent yet | *"Chưa gửi thông báo nào cho hồ sơ này."* — with the claim's state, since a claim in `DOC_PROCESSING` has legitimately generated exactly one. **Never a blank panel** (§5.14.5) |
| A body was not retained | The row renders from F1 to F7 and F9, with F8 marked unavailable and the reason. **The row is never suppressed** — that it was sent is the fact being asked about |
| `ADMIN` viewing | Rows in full; **bodies quoting clinical detail are withheld with a visible note**, not silently absent (V-552, A3 §4.11) |
| The notification store is unavailable | The view states the outage. **No partial history is rendered** — a correspondence list that is short because a query failed is the one answer this view must never give |

### 5.23 Staff notification (F53, F61)

**Purpose.** Tell a member of staff that something happened to their work, at the moment it happens, instead of at the moment they next happen to look.

**Register row B-33**, console side. The reference carries fifteen staff email templates and seven in-system notifications; **what is specified below is the surface and eight events, not twenty-two templates**. **The channel is `STAFF_INBOX`** (§6.1.2, §6.1.2b) and **the eight sentences are A2 §8.1's** — `STAFF-NOTIF-001` … `-008`, with the two that also go by `EMAIL` named there and not here.

**Entered from.** A bell on the console shell, on every screen. It is a panel on the shell rather than a screen: **S-07** carries the per-claim history and this is the cross-claim inbox.

**Who may open it.** Every console role, over **their own** notifications only. A notification is addressed to a user, and no role reads another user's — **V-553's prohibition on a cross-user report applies here exactly as it does to the trail.**

#### 5.23.1 What raises one

Eight events, all of which already exist in this document and none of which reaches a person today.

| # | Event | Recipient |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | A claim is assigned to you (§5.3.3) | The assignee |
| 2 | A claim is reassigned away from you, or to you | **The former assessor, the new assessor and the approver who did it** — three, because a hand-over nobody confirms is a claim in limbo |
| 3 | An approver returned your claim, with the reason (§5.11.3) | The assessor |
| 4 | The customer supplied the documents you asked for (§5.5.4) | The assessor holding the claim |
| 5 | Extraction failed or stalled on your claim (§5.6.8) | The assessor holding the claim |
| 6 | Extraction completed on your claim | The assessor holding the claim |
| 7 | Your claim crossed into `QUÁ_HẠN` (§5.3.2) | The assessor, **before** the bucket changes rather than after |
| 8 | A settlement plan is waiting for you (§5.10.3) | The approver queue |

#### 5.23.2 Field table

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Thời điểm | `datetime` | `system` | M | — | — |
| F2 | Số hồ sơ | `text(20)` | `system` | M | Links to S-02, **scope-checked at the link** (A3 §6) | — |
| F3 | Sự việc | `enum(staffNotificationType)` | `system` | M | §5.23.1's eight | — |
| F4 | Nội dung | `derived` | `master` | M | The A2 sentence for F3 — **`STAFF-NOTIF-001` … `-008`, A2 §8.1**. Rendered from the template record (§6.1.3) with named parameters; **this screen displays it and never composes it** | — |
| F5 | Người gây ra | `lookup(user)` | `system` | O | The acting user, or `SYSTEM` | — |
| F6 | Đã đọc | `bool` | `user` | M | Set by opening it. **Never auto-cleared by age** | — |

#### 5.23.3 Rules

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| **V-721** | **The bell is the channel and it is `STAFF_INBOX`, a real one.** §6.1.2 carries it and §6.1.2b specifies how a recipient is resolved, how the record is read and marked read, and what happens when the addressee has left. **`EMAIL` reaches a member of staff on exactly two of the eight events** — the returned claim and the overdue claim — and **which two is A2 §8.1's rule S-4, not this screen's.** **No browser push and no digest**, which §6.1.9 excludes and A2 §9 gives the reason for. **`D2-127` is closed**; what Part V specifies is the surface and the event set, and what A2 §8.1 specifies is the eight sentences and the seven rules they obey |
| **V-721a** | **A notification is never a claim outcome.** It reports that something happened; the claim moved through Part VII or it did not move (§2.10, D1 §4.3, G-3) |
| **V-721b** | **A notification carries no clinical detail** — no diagnosis, no ICD-10, no item name, no amount. It names a claim and an event, on exactly the reasoning §5.19.2 applies to the operator queue |
| **V-721c** | **Scope is applied at the link and at the query.** A user who lost scope over a claim after the notification was raised sees the row and cannot open it (A3 §6) |
| **V-721d** | **A notification is never deleted.** It is read or unread, and it is retained with the claim's correspondence record (V-718) |

**Why this is worth the two screens it costs.** The console measures a claim's age and sorts three overdue buckets from it, **and has no mechanism to tell anyone before a claim falls into one**. A claim assigned to somebody on leave is discovered by the `QUÁ_HẠN` bucket — that is, after it is late. `CLM-CONSOLE-015` was written to reach an assessor about a failed clinical assessment and reaches nobody who has not opened that claim. A returned claim goes back to the queue and waits until somebody's filter happens to catch it. **A measurement with no alerting channel is a number to read in a report after the work has already gone wrong** (**G-B-18**).

> **The machine already existed and this was a catalogue, not a build.** §6.1.5 to §6.1.7 carry the outbox, the versioned templates, the immutability constraint, the retry schedule and the operator queue on failure. **None of it was rewritten.** What was missing was a recipient group and eight sentences. **Both have since arrived**: A2 v1.1 §8.1 wrote the eight sentences and their seven rules — **`D2-126` is closed** — and §6.1.2b carries the recipient group and the channel, which closes **`D2-127`**. **What the engine gained is a resolver and a read state, and nothing else.**

#### 5.23.4 Empty and error

| Condition | What the console shows |
|---|---|
| Nothing unread | The bell carries no count and the panel states so. **Not hidden** |
| A claim referenced has left the user's scope | The row renders and the link is inert, with the reason. **Never a broken link and never a silent removal** |
| The notification store is unavailable | The bell shows an outage marker. **The console is fully usable** — a notification channel that can block work has become a dependency, which is what §6.1.6 forbids for the customer channel and forbids here for the same reason |

### 5.24 Prior claims of the insured member (F53)

**Purpose.** Show every previous claim of the same insured member on one screen, so that *"has this been claimed before"* and *"what happened last time"* are answerable without leaving the claim.

**Entered from.** §5.4.3's *Xem lịch sử bồi thường của người được bảo hiểm*; §5.9.3's ledger panel. **A second panel on S-11**, alongside the ledger it complements.

**Who may open it.** `ASSESSOR` **R**, `APPROVER` **R**, scope `ASSIGNED` on the claim they came from. **No `ADMIN`** — the rows carry diagnosis and provider (A3 §4.11).

#### 5.24.1 The list

**One row per insured event, across every prior claim of the member** — not one row per claim, because the question is about episodes of treatment and a claim may carry several (§5.7.1).

| Column | Type | Source | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Số hồ sơ · số sự kiện | `text(20)` | `system` | `claimNo/n`. Links to that claim, **scope-checked at the link** |
| Ngày mở hồ sơ | `date` | `system` | |
| Loại hình tổn thất | `enum(lossType)` | `system` | The prior claim's F7 (§5.4.1), rendered as its A1 §4.2 label |
| Ngày xảy ra sự kiện | `date` | `system` | §5.7.2 F16 |
| Điều trị từ / đến · số ngày | `date` · `int` | `system` | F4 and F17 |
| Cơ sở khám chữa bệnh | `text(200)` | `system` | And its network status as it was pinned on that claim |
| Chẩn đoán · mã ICD-10 | `text(500)` · `text(20)` | `system` | |
| Số tiền yêu cầu · số tiền đã chi trả | `money` | `system` | The final figures, not provisional |
| Trạng thái | `enum(claimState)` | `system` | A1 §5.1's Vietnamese label |

**The match key is `memberId`** — §5.4.2 F15, the same key the limit ledger uses (D1 §7.4). The reference matches on name plus date of birth plus identity number because it has no member identifier to hand; **ours is stronger and no name matching is performed**, which also means a member whose name was recorded differently on two claims still resolves to one history.

#### 5.24.2 Actions

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Mở hồ sơ trước** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER` | The prior claim is in the user's scope | Opens S-02 on it, read-only where it is terminal. **The read is logged** (BR-AUDIT-4) | — |
| **Mở chứng từ của hồ sơ trước** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER` | As above | Opens that claim's §5.5 documents tab. **Every image opened is logged** (BR-AUDIT-4, A3 §3.3) | — |
| **Lọc theo cơ sở y tế hoặc mã ICD-10** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER` | — | Narrows the list. **A filter that matches nothing shows the filter** (§5.3.4) | — |

**Register rows B-38 and S-21, and the second is the reduced one.** **B-38** is the list itself: the data has existed since the first claim closed and no screen showed it, so an assessor asking whether a course of treatment has been claimed before had the limit ledger — which shows money consumed and not what it was consumed on. **S-21** asked additionally for the prior claims' **attachments** to be reachable, and that is the second action above: reached **from this list**, under the same scope check and the same read logging. **What is omitted is the reference's arrangement** — an inline block of prior-claim attachments on the documents tab of the current claim. It duplicates this list, and it doubles the surface on which a clinical document is opened without the reader having navigated to the claim it belongs to. **One route, logged, is better than two.**

#### 5.24.3 Empty and error

| Condition | What the console shows |
|---|---|
| The member has no prior claim | *"Người được bảo hiểm chưa có hồ sơ bồi thường nào trước đây."* — **which is information**, and is the answer to the question that was asked |
| A prior claim is outside the user's scope | It does not appear and no count includes it (A3 §6) |
| The claim store is unavailable | The panel states the outage. **No partial history** — a prior-claims list that is short because a query failed answers *"has this been claimed before"* with a wrong *no* |

### 5.27 Policy and cover enquiry from the claim (F60)

> **§5.25 and §5.26 are registers, not screens.** The screen sections of Part V are §5.1 to §5.24 and this one. It is numbered §5.27 rather than inserted at §5.25 so that no existing cross-reference moves.

**Purpose.** From an open claim, answer three questions without leaving it: **what does this policy say**, **what do the terms say**, and **what has this member got left**. All three are things an assessor asks on almost every claim, and v0.4 could answer none of them.

**Why this is a gap and not a wish.** §3.3.2 already specifies the data — *"the policy row, its benefit levels, and its members with their coverage periods and benefit-level pointers"* — as a requirement on `I-05`. **We ask InsureMO for it and then render none of it.** §5.4.2 shows the snapshot fields of *this member on this policy*; §5.9.3 shows the counters of *the benefits this claim touches*; §5.4.2 F39 shows the rule set as **a reference string that opens nothing.**

**Feature.** New — **F60, Priority 1, Group E.** The catalogue moves 48 → 49 and Priority 1 44 → 45 (Framework §7.1). This is a real scope addition and it is stated as one rather than folded into F45.

#### 5.27.1 Two readings of the same policy, and the screen must always say which

This is the design decision the section turns on, and getting it wrong is the P-02 failure mode.

| Reading | Answers | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Như đã chụp** — as snapshotted | *What did the contract say when this claim was assessed?* | **Yes.** Every figure the settlement rests on comes from here |
| **Hiện tại** — live from InsureMO | *What does the policy say now?* — the endorsement landed, the member left, the level changed | No. Explicit, labelled, logged |

**The two are never shown blended and never shown without a label.** The snapshot view carries the service date it was taken at; the live view carries the timestamp of the read and a standing banner that **nothing on it feeds a calculation**. An assessor comparing the two is doing exactly the right thing — noticing that the policy has moved since the claim was registered — and that is a reason to raise a correction, not a reason to re-price silently.

**The live read is read-only and marks nothing stale.** Contrast §5.4.2's renewal re-read (A3 §4.21), which *writes* to the claim and therefore does mark the calculation stale. This one changes nothing on the claim, so it needs no such control — it is a window, not an edit.

#### 5.27.2 Chi tiết hợp đồng — the policy panel

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Số hợp đồng | `text(20)` | `snapshot` | M | — | `inline` |
| F2 | Chủ hợp đồng | `text(200)` | `snapshot` | M | — | `inline` |
| F3 | Loại hợp đồng | `enum(policyType)` | `snapshot` | M | Cá nhân · Nhóm | `inline` |
| F4 | Thời hạn hợp đồng | `date` | `snapshot` | M | Từ / đến, two cells | `inline` |
| F5 | Trạng thái hợp đồng | `enum(policyStatus)` | `snapshot` | M | — | `inline` |
| F6 | Phí đã đóng | `bool` | `snapshot` | M | — | `inline` |
| F7 | Bộ quy tắc bảo hiểm | `lookup(ruleSet)` | `snapshot` | M | Opens §5.27.4 | `inline` |
| F8 | Kênh khai thác · mã khách hàng | `text(100)` | `snapshot` | O | Decision `B6` | `inline` |
| F9 | Ngày chụp ảnh | `datetime` | `system` | M | **Derived** — the registration instant, and the service date the schedule was read at | `inline` |

**Các mức quyền lợi trên hợp đồng** — a list, because a policy may carry several and the claim's member points at one:

| Column | Type | Source | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Số mức | `int` | `snapshot` | |
| Chương trình | `text(20)` | `snapshot` | Plan code and name |
| Hiệu lực | `date` | `snapshot` | From / to |
| Số thành viên | `derived` | `system` | |
| **Mức của hồ sơ này** | `bool` | `derived` | The row the claim's member points at is marked, not merely sorted first |

**Thành viên trên hợp đồng** — every member, not only the claimant's:

| Column | Type | Source | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Họ và tên | `text(200)` | `snapshot` | |
| Ngày sinh · giới tính | `date` · `enum(sex)` | `snapshot` | |
| Số thẻ | `text(20)` | `snapshot` | |
| Quan hệ với chủ hợp đồng | `enum(claimantRelationship)` | `snapshot` | A1 §4.3 |
| Mức quyền lợi | `int` | `snapshot` | |
| Hiệu lực bảo hiểm | `date` | `snapshot` | From / to. **A member end-dated mid-year shows the end date, not a blank** |
| Tình trạng | `enum(memberStatus)` | `snapshot` | |
| Tình trạng tái tục | `enum(renewalStatus)` | `snapshot` | A1 §4.6 |

> **The identity number is not on this list, and that is deliberate.** §6.4.3 forbids rendering an identity number on a list screen. A member's identity is visible on the claim that concerns them (§5.4.2) and on the payee record (§5.20), both of which are single-subject screens with a reason to show it. **A roster of everyone on a policy is not.** `V-728`.

**Cây quyền lợi đầy đủ của mức này** — the whole tree, not the extract §5.4.2 renders. Columns as §5.9.3's snapshot columns: code indented by depth, name, annual sum insured, per-event and per-day caps, count limit and unit, co-payment, **deduction ratio and its triggering condition**, waiting period **by condition class** (six columns or one expandable cell — presentation, per §2.11).

#### 5.27.3 The live read

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Xem trạng thái hợp đồng hiện tại** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER` | Assigned or in scope on the claim | Calls `I-05` afresh. Renders a **second, labelled panel** beside the snapshot with the differences highlighted. **Writes nothing to the claim.** Logged as an access event (F63) | `*(new A2 item needed — D2-151)*` on failure |
| **Báo cáo lệch dữ liệu hợp đồng** | `ASSESSOR` | The live read differs from the snapshot on a field that affects cover | Raises an operator-queue item (§5.19) naming the field, both values and the claim. **Does not change the claim** | `*(new A2 item needed — D2-152)*` |

**`V-726` — a live read never becomes an input.** No value from the live panel may be copied into a claim field, and the chain has no access to it. The only outputs of a live read are *a person now knows* and, optionally, an operator-queue item.

#### 5.27.4 Điều kiện điều khoản — reading the wording

**This is the sharpest of the three gaps.** `ruleSetRef` is a `text(200)` reference. A decline under `EXCL` must, per D1 `BR-MSG-3`, state the clause relied on — and the clause lives in a document nobody can open from the console.

**Where the wording lives is an open question with three answers**, and the recommendation is the buildable one:

| Option | What it means | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| **A — InsureMO holds it** and exposes a document reference or URL on `I-05` | We deep-link, versioned by `ruleSetRef` | **Preferred if available.** One source of truth, and it is the document the policy was issued against. **New confirmation `C-IMO-12`** |
| **B — we hold a wording store** keyed on `ruleSetRef` | An administrator uploads a PDF per rule set under F55 master data; the console links to it | **The buildable default.** Cheap, and it works whatever InsureMO answers |
| **C — nothing** | The reference renders as a string and the assessor opens a shared drive | **Not acceptable.** It is what v0.4 does today, and it puts the defensibility of every `EXCL` decline outside the system |

**Specified: option B, with A superseding it if `C-IMO-12` comes back yes.** Concretely — a `rule_set` master record under F55 with the reference, a title, an effective window, and one attached document; §5.4.2 F39 and §5.27.2 F7 become links that open it in a new tab; the version opened is **the one named on the claim's snapshot**, never the newest.

**`V-727` — a decline citing a clause requires the wording to be present.** Where the rule set named on the snapshot has no document loaded, `EXCL` remains selectable but the settlement plan cannot be submitted until either the document is loaded or the rationale states the clause in full. **A decline that cites a clause nobody can read is a decline we cannot defend**, and this is the one place in the section where a missing document blocks rather than degrades.

#### 5.27.5 Hạn mức toàn hợp đồng — the member's every counter

§5.9.3's panel is scoped to the benefits **this claim touches**, because that is what the calculation needs. This one is scoped to **every benefit on the member's level**, because that is what the question *"what has this member got left"* needs.

Same columns as §5.9.3, minus the provisional-holding columns — this view is about what is settled, and mixing in another claim's provisional posting is exactly what `BR-LEDGER-2` forbids showing. Rows for benefits with no consumption render with the sum insured and a zero, **not** suppressed: a nil counter is the answer to a real question.

**Two totals below the tree**: consumption across the policy year, and the member's remaining aggregate where the product has one. **This product has none** (A5 §6.1 step 13), so the second renders *"Sản phẩm không có hạn mức tổng"* rather than a blank.

#### 5.27.6 Who may open it

| | `ASSESSOR` | `APPROVER` | `ADMIN` | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| §5.27.2 policy and members | **R** | **R** | **R** | `ASSIGNED` for the first two; `ALL_POLICIES` for `ADMIN` |
| §5.27.3 live read | **R** | **R** | — | `ASSIGNED` |
| §5.27.4 wording | **R** | **R** | **F** on the master record | — |
| §5.27.5 policy-wide limits | **R** | **R** | — | `ASSIGNED`. **No `ADMIN`** — a limit is a claim fact (A3 §4.11) |

**`ADMIN` sees the policy roster and not the limits**, which looks inconsistent until you say why: the roster is administrative data an administrator maintains master data against, and a limit is the residue of claim decisions. A3 §4.11 draws that line and this screen respects it.

#### 5.27.7 Empty and error

| Situation | What the screen shows |
|---|---|
| The claim has no snapshot yet (`DRAFT`, `SUBMITTED`) | The section is **absent**, not empty. There is nothing to render and an empty policy panel reads as *a policy with nothing on it* |
| `I-05` unavailable on a live read | The snapshot panel stands; the live panel shows that the read failed and offers a retry. **The claim is unaffected** — an outage here cannot touch a settlement, which is the point of the snapshot |
| The rule set has no document loaded | F7 renders the reference with *"chưa tải văn bản quy tắc"* and a link to the master record for an administrator. `V-727` governs what that blocks |
| A member on the roster has been end-dated since the snapshot | Only visible on the live panel, and it is exactly the kind of difference §5.27.3's second action exists to report |
