### 5.28 Term register administration (F65)

*(New at v0.5. **F65**, Priority 1, **Group G**. D1 §5.3.1; *Solution Paper* §2, §5 and §6; decisions **D-1**, **D-2**, **D-6**, 24 August 2026. Screen **S-13**.)*

**Purpose.** Author, version and approve the policy's terms as **evaluable objects** rather than as prose, so that chain steps 4 and 7 have something to evaluate and every decline can cite the clause it rests on.

**Entered from.** The console's navigation, under administration. **S-13** — a screen in its own right and not a tab of S-09, because S-09 is F55's ordinary reference data and this is contractual text with a four-eyes lifecycle on it.

**Who may open it.** `TERM_AUTHOR` **F** and `TERM_APPROVE` **F** on their own halves; `ASSESSOR` and `APPROVER` **R**, so that §5.9.1a's term rows and §5.29's clause quotations open something. **`ADMIN` is not granted authorship by holding `ADMIN`** — the two grants are separate and **A3 v1.5 now carries both, together with the four-eyes rule, the back-dating override and the correction declaration; `D2-175` closes**. Read access is deliberately wide: a decline nobody can look up is a decline nobody can answer.

**Why this is claim-side master data and not InsureMO's.** InsureMO returns `ruleSetRef` on `I-05` — **which** terms apply. What they **mean operationally** is a predicate, and a predicate arriving from a vendor is a decision-in-waiting, which breaches **P-01**. Option B of the *Solution Paper* §2.6, approved as **D-1**. §5.4.2 **F39** already renders the rule-set reference on the claim; until v0.5 it was a string that opened nothing, and this is what it opens.

#### 5.28.1 The three classes, and what each may do

Restated from D1 §5.3.1 because every field and every control below is shaped by it. **D1 owns the rule; this table is the version a developer reads beside the screen.**

| Class | Meaning | The engine **may** | The engine **may never** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **D — Deterministic** | Decidable from facts the claim already holds | **Auto-decline**, reason code `EXCL`, the term's `clauseRef` carried into the decline | — |
| **J — Judgemental** | Requires a person, or a clinical opinion — *cosmetic*, *under the influence* | Raise a **checkpoint** with the clause quoted, routed to §5.29 | **Auto-decline** |
| **E — Evidential** | Decidable only if a specific named document says so — a police or hospital statement | **Require the document**; raise a checkpoint where it is absent | **Auto-decline** |

**A class-J term auto-declined is a decline citing a clause on a judgement no human made.** That is the whole reason the class exists, and it is why `predicate` is constrained below rather than merely documented.

#### 5.28.1a `termClass` and `effect` are two axes, and this document read them as one

**Corrected on 24 August 2026, the same day this version was issued, and stated here rather than in a changelog because it changes what a screen refuses.** As first issued, §5.29.2 F5 read that *a class-D term never raises a checkpoint* and that a row showing `D` in the queue must be **refused rather than rendered**. **A5 §7.1 says the opposite and A5 is right; this document yields** (§0.5 — A5 owns the pilot product, and the rule it rests on is D1's `BR-TERM-7`).

**The two are not the same axis.**

| Field | The question it answers | What it governs |
|---|---|---|
| **`termClass`** | ***Can the system decide this?*** | Whether an **auto-decline** is permitted — and nothing else |
| **`effect`** | ***What happens when the term is in play?*** | `DECLINE_EVENT` · `DECLINE_LINE` · `REQUIRE_DOC` · `CHECKPOINT` · `CAP` |

**A class-D term is one whose `selector` fires deterministically. That does not oblige it to decline.** Exclusion #3 is the clearest case and it is on the pilot product today: `serviceCategory = SUPPLEMENT` selects deterministically, and the wording's proviso — *"not prescribed as treatment for the diagnosed condition"* — means **a supplement that was prescribed for the condition is covered**. Declining it automatically would be wrong. **So it selects as class `D` and resolves as a `CHECKPOINT`** (A5 §7.2, `TERM-HC-003`; the same is true of `TERM-HC-002`, health checks and screening).

**The rule that survives is one-directional, and it must be read in one direction only:**

> **A class `J` or class `E` term may never carry `DECLINE_EVENT` or `DECLINE_LINE`. A class `D` term may carry any effect, including `CHECKPOINT`.**

Read the other way — *"class D declines, class J and E checkpoint"* — the model forces an auto-decline wherever a fact happens to exist, which is the outcome the three classes were introduced to prevent. **`V-742` states the surviving half; `V-734` states the field rule and is untouched by this correction.** The checkpoint queue at §5.29 therefore receives class `D`, `J` and `E` rows alike, and F5 there renders whichever class raised it.

#### 5.28.2 The correction this document makes to the model it was given, and why it could not be avoided

**This is the one place where v0.5 does not simply apply the *Solution Paper*, and it is stated at the point of change rather than buried in a changelog.**

The paper's §2.3 gives `policy_term` a single `predicate` field and states that it is *"null and not permitted for class J"*. Applied literally, that is unbuildable — and it fails in the direction that produces the worst outcome rather than the safest one.

**A term needs two different decisions and the paper's model has one field for them:**

| Question | What answers it |
|---|---|
| **Is this term in play for this claim, this event or this line at all?** | A predicate |
| **Given that it is in play, does it fire?** | A predicate |

For a class-D term the two can be the same expression — *"the service category is `OPTICAL` or `HEARING`"* both selects and decides. **For a class-J term they cannot be**, because the second question is the one a human is there to answer. With one field, forbidden to be non-null on class J, **there is nothing left to answer the first question** — and a term with no way to say which claims it concerns concerns all of them. **Evaluated literally, every class-J term would raise a checkpoint on every claim**, and a queue that receives every claim is a queue nobody works.

**The split, and it is two fields rather than one:**

| Field | Decides | Required | Permitted |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`selector`** | Whether the term is **in play** for this claim, event or line | **Mandatory and non-null for every class — `D`, `J` and `E` alike** | Always |
| **`predicate`** | Whether the term **fires** — the auto-decline | **Mandatory where the class is `D` and the effect is a decline** | **Class `D` only. Null for `J`, for `E`, and for a class-`D` term carrying `CHECKPOINT`** |

**For a class D declining term the two may be the same expression**, and the screen offers a control that copies one into the other so that the ordinary case costs one entry rather than two. **Where they differ, the difference is the point**: A5's exclusion #6 is in play on every dental line and declines only those the mapping did not put under `300`, and a term that selected on the whole condition would report nine non-selections where the assessor needed to see nine tests that passed.

**Both halves are one validation — `V-734` — because a term failing either half is unevaluable in the same way.** A class-J term with a null selector fires on everything; a class-J term with a non-null predicate can auto-decline, which is the prohibition the class model exists to state.

**A null selector is not *"not selected"* — it is *"in play for every claim"*, and that is why `V-734` has no exception.** A5 §7.3 takes the two irreducibly judgemental terms — cosmetic treatment and alcohol or drug dependency, which have no fact that decides them — and gives each a **deliberately narrow selector from the closed vocabulary** rather than leaving the field empty, with everything the selector does not reach coming to a person through the clinical track as it did before. That is a product judgement and A5 owns it; what this screen requires is only that the field is present and validated.

> **This was owed upstream, and it has been paid — `D2-173` is closed, 24 August 2026.** D1 §5.3.1 and A5 §7 carried the paper's single-field model, and a downstream document silently correcting an upstream one is how a set stops agreeing with itself (§10.3), so the split was specified here and raised rather than applied outwards. **On the same day D1 adopted it as `BR-TERM-7`, A5 §7.1 and §7.2 gave every one of the ten terms both fields, and the seed carries a non-null `selector` on all ten rows — `A5_seed_v1.4.json` then, `A5_seed_v1.5.json` now.** The three documents now say the same thing, and this section is an application of D1 rather than a correction to it. **What §5.28.2 records from here on is why the field is split**, which is worth keeping: the argument is the reason the rule is the shape it is.
>
> **One clarification the upstream adoption carries back into this screen.** `predicate` is **mandatory only where a class-`D` term's effect is `DECLINE_EVENT` or `DECLINE_LINE`**. A class-`D` term carrying `CHECKPOINT` — two of the pilot's ten do (§5.28.1a) — has **no predicate**, because nothing is auto-declined and there is nothing for one to decide. F14 and `V-734` are worded to that.

#### 5.28.3a The expression builder — the control F13 and F14 are entered through

**New at v0.6, and it is the largest hole v0.5 left.** F13 and F14 both said *"entered through the expression builder, never as free text, validated against the vocabulary on save"* — **and no expression builder was specified anywhere in this document.** No field table, no fact list, no operators, no nesting rule, no empty state, no error state, and both fields typed `textarea(2000)`. A developer handed that builds a free-text box and a regular expression, which is precisely what §5.28.2 argues against: **an author who can type a predicate can invent a fact, and a term written against a fact the engine cannot supply silently never fires.**

**Everything the builder needs already exists in an annex; nothing below is a new vocabulary.**

| What the builder offers | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| **The facts** | **A1 §4.11's closed fact vocabulary** — twelve facts, each with a level, a source, a status and an **available from step** column. **An author cannot invent a fact**, and a fact whose status is *Missing* is offered greyed with its open question named (`Q-IDP-02`, `Q-IDP-05`) so that a term written against it is authored deliberately and left `DRAFT` |
| **The operators** | **A1 §4.10's `termOperator`** — `eq` · `ne` · `in` · `notIn` · `gt` · `gte` · `lt` · `lte` · `startsWith` · `between`, and the three grouping keywords **`all`**, **`any`** and **`not`**. There is no `and` and no `or`: `all` and `any` are those operators under names that cannot be confused with a screen label |
| **The values** | The domain of the chosen fact — `enum(serviceCategory)`'s twenty codes, `enum(lossType)`'s twelve, an ICD-10 prefix, a date, an integer. **Typed against the fact, never free text**, except where the fact's own domain is open (an ICD prefix), and there the control validates the shape |
| **The stored form** | **The JSON of `A5_seed_v1.5.json`'s `policy_term.selector` and `.predicate`** — a leaf is `{"fact": …, "op": …, "value": …}` and a group is `{"all": […]}`, `{"any": […]}` or `{"not": {…}}`. **The seed is the contract**: what the builder writes is what the engine reads and what the seed already holds for all ten pilot terms |

**One level of nesting, and no more.** A group may contain leaves; **a group may not contain another group**. `TERM-HC-005`'s selector — five `startsWith` leaves under one `any` — and `TERM-HC-006`'s predicate — two leaves under one `all` — are the two shapes the pilot register actually uses, and both are one level. **The limit is deliberate and it is stated as a decision rather than a phase-1 shortcut**: a nested expression is one an author cannot check by reading, a reviewer cannot four-eyes by reading, and an assessor at §5.29.2 F6 cannot reconstruct from the facts it matched on. An exclusion that genuinely needs two levels is two terms, and two terms is what the assessor's *tested* count should say anyway.

**Field table — the builder, opened from F13 or from F14 on S-13**

*(The numbering continues S-13's, on the convention §5.4.1 states: a field number is an identifier, not a position. F20 to F24 render inside the builder that F13 and F14 open, and F13 and F14 render its result.)*

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F20 | Cách kết hợp | `enum(termOperator)` — the three grouping keywords only | `master` | C — **mandatory where more than one condition is present; absent where there is exactly one** | `all` · `any` · `not` — A1 §4.10 `termOperator`. **`not` takes exactly one condition** and the control refuses a second rather than dropping it. Defaults to `all`, because a term with two conditions and no chosen combinator almost always means both | inline |
| F21 | Dữ kiện | `lookup(fact)` | `master` | M | **A1 §4.11's closed vocabulary and nothing else.** The list is **filtered to the facts available at the step F9's scope runs at** — `PRODUCT` runs at step 4, `BENEFIT` and `BENEFIT_SUBTREE` at step 7 — so `benefitCode` is **absent from the list on a `PRODUCT`-scope term** rather than offered and refused on save (`BR-TERM-9`, **V-744**). Changing F9 re-filters the list and **flags every condition the new scope can no longer see** | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-153**)* |
| F22 | Phép so sánh | `enum(termOperator)` | `master` | M | **Filtered to the operators legal for F21's type** (A1 §4.10): `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte` and `between` on numeric and date facts only; `startsWith` on string facts only; `eq`, `ne`, `in` and `notIn` on any scalar. **An illegal pairing is not offered** — V-744 | inline |

F13 and F14 are this field's two instances | inline |

**Notes on the fields above.** **F24 is the value F13 and F14 hold** and is the only one of the five that is persisted as such; F20 to F23 are the controls that build it, repeated once per condition. **F21 and F23 carry an error path and F20, F22 and F24 do not**, because the first two can fail against data the screen cannot enumerate in advance — a fact that has become unavailable under a changed scope, a value outside a domain that master data owns — while the other three are prevented by their controls (§2.2).

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| **V-744** | **Four checks on save, all four server-side, and a failure lists every breach at once rather than the first.** **(1) The fact exists** in A1 §4.11's vocabulary. **(2) The operator is legal for the fact's type**, per A1 §4.10. **(3) The value is legal for the fact's domain** — a `serviceCategory` outside the twenty, a `lossType` outside the twelve, a malformed ICD prefix, an empty list under `in`. **(4) The fact is available at the step the term's scope runs at** — `BR-TERM-9`, checked against A1 §4.11's *available from step* column, which is **the data this rule exists to be checked against**. **Check 4 is the one that was missing and the one that had already bitten**: `TERM-HC-006` was authored as a `PRODUCT`-scope term testing `benefitCode`, which step 5 produces and step 4 cannot see, so the expression evaluated against a null on every claim — on the one row A5 §7.3 relied on as proof that step 4 works. **The check runs at save, not at evaluation**, because a term that cannot be evaluated must not reach the register at all. **The save is refused, never corrected** (V-734) |

**Empty and error**

| Condition | What the builder shows |
|---|---|
| **No condition entered yet** (a new `DRAFT`, F13 opened for the first time) | One empty condition row with F21 open and F22, F23 and F24 disabled, and UI-25's sentence: *"chưa có điều kiện nào — điều khoản sẽ áp dụng cho mọi hồ sơ"*. **The sentence is the point**: `V-734` refuses an empty selector precisely because an empty selector does not mean *not selected*, it means *in play for every claim*, and an author is told that here rather than at the save |
| **F14 on a term with no predicate** — class `J`, class `E`, or class `D` carrying `CHECKPOINT` | The builder is **absent**, not empty and not disabled, with one sentence naming which of the three cases applies (§5.28.2). Changing F11 to `CHECKPOINT` **empties and closes it** rather than retaining a hidden predicate |
| **A fact the term already uses is no longer available** — F9's scope changed, or A1 retired a fact in a release | The condition renders **flagged, with the fact named and the reason**, the term is **not saved** until it is corrected, and **an already-`ACTIVE` term in this state is not evaluated and raises an operator-queue item** (§5.28.7). It is never silently dropped: a condition that disappears changes what the term means |
| **A fact whose A1 status is *Missing* or *Open*** — `lineDiagnosisCode`, `facilityCountry`, `facilityType` | Offered, greyed, with the open question named. **The term can be authored and cannot leave `DRAFT`** — which is exactly the state four of A5 §7.2's ten terms are in, and it is a deliberate holding position rather than a defect |
| **The vocabulary itself cannot be read** | The builder does not open and the save control is absent. **A builder that falls back to a text box is a builder that does not exist** |

#### 5.28.4 Lifecycle, four eyes and effective dating

**Four rules, and each of them is the reason a term is different from the reference data at §5.16.3.** A term is a contractual statement. Getting one wrong does not mis-sort a document; it declines a claim on a clause the customer can read for themselves.

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| **V-735** | **The lifecycle is `DRAFT → PENDING_ACTIVE → ACTIVE → WITHDRAWN` and there is no other edge.** No return from `ACTIVE` to `DRAFT`, no jump from `DRAFT` to `ACTIVE`, no revival of a `WITHDRAWN` term — a term that must come back is a **new version** of it (§5.28.5). **`PENDING_ACTIVE` is a real state and not a formality**: it is a term that has been authored and approved and whose effective date has not arrived, which is a thing an insurer needs and would otherwise have discovered late. **A `DRAFT` term is invisible to the engine** — F66 evaluates only `ACTIVE` terms inside their effective window, so a half-written predicate can never decide a claim |
| **V-736** | **Four eyes: F18 and F19 must be different people, and the approve control is absent on a version the acting user authored.** No self-approval, checked server-side against the version record and not against the session, on exactly the reasoning `CLM-CONSOLE-005` applies to a claim (§5.11.3). **`TERM_AUTHOR` and `TERM_APPROVE` are carried by A3 v1.5, with the four eyes stated there rather than only here — `D2-175` closed**, and `V-736` is enforceable from the day A3 v1.5 is in force |
| **V-737** | **No back-dating past the earliest open claim bound to that rule set, without an explicit recorded override.** An `effectiveFrom` earlier than the oldest non-terminal claim on F2's rule set changes the terms a live claim is being assessed against, retrospectively and invisibly. The screen shows **the count of blocking claims and the earliest date that bound the check** before it refuses — **not the claim numbers, unless the acting user also holds a claims scope: V-759**. The override, where the business takes it, is recorded with a reason, the acting user and both dates, and is listed on every affected claim's trail (F63). **The binding instant is the claim's registration** (§5.2.4), because that is when the claim acquired the register |
| **V-734** | **`selector` is mandatory and non-null on every class; `predicate` is permitted on class `D` alone, is null on `J` and on `E`, and is mandatory on class `D` only where the effect is `DECLINE_EVENT` or `DECLINE_LINE`.** Both halves, in one rule, because a term failing either is unevaluable in the same way — §5.28.2. **The rule has no exception, and the reason is that a null selector does not mean *not selected* — it means *in play for every claim*.** **The save is refused, never corrected**: a platform that supplied a missing selector would be authoring a contractual term |
| **V-743** | **A term whose `clauseRef` is provisional may not decline — D1 v0.5 `BR-TERM-10`.** Where F3 begins `TBC-`, the term is marked **unciteable**: it is saved, it is approved, it is evaluated, and **whatever its class and whatever its effect it raises a checkpoint instead of declining**, and the checkpoint names the missing citation. **The save is not refused** — a term authored before the wording is filed is a legitimate thing to hold, and refusing it would leave the register empty and step 4 with nothing to test. **What is refused is the decline**, at evaluation and again at §5.29.5, where the *Giữ nguyên* control is **absent rather than disabled**. **On the pilot product this is every one of the ten terms** (A5 §7.2), so **step 4's auto-decline branch cannot fire at all today**, and that is a business blocker on the whole term-decline path rather than a screen defect — **`D2-159`**. The marker is shown wherever the term is: on this screen, on §5.9.1a's row and on §5.29's queue |
| **V-755** | **`CAP` is a real effect from v0.6 — D1 v0.5 `BR-TERM-12`.** A term whose effect is `CAP` applies a **monetary ceiling at chain step 7**, to the amount as at the end of **step 6**, and **it counts as a limit bound**: a claim it reduces fails §5.11.4's condition 1 exactly as a schedule limit does, and `V-542`'s obligation to explain a binding cap applies to it unchanged. **F11's fifth value now has a home** — until v0.6 it was on the control with no behaviour behind it anywhere. **No term in the pilot product uses it**, and **A1 §4.10 deliberately did not register it**, on the ground that registering a value nothing produces puts an option on a screen with no meaning behind it. **D1 has since given it a meaning, so the alignment runs the other way and A1 is asked to register it — `D2-181`** |
| **V-758** | **A term may cite `EXCL` and no other decline reason.** F12 offers one of A5 §6.3's seven codes and the other six are produced by other steps of the chain — a term that cited `LIMIT` would be a contractual exclusion wearing a limit's clothes, and the customer would receive a letter saying their annual limit was exhausted when it was not. **The control offers one value and the save refuses any other**, which is a narrowing of what v0.5 allowed rather than a new rule: A5 §7.2 gives all ten pilot terms `EXCL` already, and nothing in D1 or A5 contemplates a term citing anything else |
| **V-742** | **A class `J` or class `E` term may never carry `DECLINE_EVENT` or `DECLINE_LINE`, and the save is refused where it does.** **The rule runs in one direction and only one**: it says nothing about what a class `D` term may carry, and **a class-`D` term carrying `CHECKPOINT` is valid, is saved, and raises a checkpoint at §5.29** — §5.28.1a, D1 `BR-TERM-7`, A5 §7.1. **New at the same-day correction of 24 August 2026**, allocated from the `V-701 … V-799` overflow and indexed at §8.1. It carries the half of the old F11 constraint that survives; the half that did not — *"a class `J` or `E` term may carry only `CHECKPOINT` or `REQUIRE_DOC`"* — was read on this screen as though it constrained class `D` too, and it never should have been written as a two-sided rule |

> **What is missing from this screen, named because §6 of the *Solution Paper* argues it should not be.** **F68 — the test mode** — runs a candidate term set against a sample of historical claims and shows what would have changed. It is **Priority 2** (decision **D-10**) and **is not built in this pass**. **So an approver pressing *Phê duyệt điều khoản* is signing something whose effect on real claims nobody has been able to see** — they can read the predicate and they cannot see what it does. That is survivable at one product and roughly ten terms and it stops being survivable as the register grows. **`D2-158`** carries it, and the Framework's own note says it moves to Priority 1 if the term count grows materially before go-live.

#### 5.28.5 Correction versus new version — the author must declare which

*(D1 **BR-TERM-5** and **BR-TERM-6**; decision **D-6**; simplification **S-40**.)*

**`P-02` solves the ordinary case and does not solve this one.** A claim binds `ruleSetRef` at submission and is evaluated against that version for its whole life (BR-TERM-4), so a term changed tomorrow does not disturb a claim submitted today. **But if a term was authored *wrongly* — the predicate tests the wrong field, the clause reference is wrong — then in-flight claims have been evaluated against something that was never the intent, and leaving them alone is the wrong answer.**

**So the author declares which of two operations they are performing, and the screen will not save without the declaration.**

| Operation | Meaning | In-flight claims | What the screen requires first |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Phiên bản mới** — new version | The terms have genuinely changed | **Untouched.** Every claim already submitted stays on the version it bound | Approval; an effective date |
| **Sửa lỗi** — correction | The term never expressed the intent | **Re-evaluated.** Every claim whose result changes is routed to a **named human queue** — §5.29's, with the before and the after both recorded. **Never an automatic re-decision** | Approval; **a written reason**; and **an impact count shown before confirmation** |

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| **V-759** | **A term-register screen may not show claim numbers to a grant whose data scope is `MASTER`.** A3 describes `MASTER` as *"configuration and master data — contains no personal data"*, and `V-737` and `V-738` were both written to show claim numbers on it: the back-dating refusal named the blocking claim, and the correction's impact analysis listed every affected claim. **A claim number is not master data.** It resolves to one person's medical claim, it is the key every other screen in Part V opens a clinical record with, and rendering it here would give a term author a claim-side read that A3 never granted — through a screen A3 classified as carrying no personal data. **What is shown by default is counts and dates**: how many claims block the back-dating and the earliest date among them; how many in-flight claims are bound to the rule set, how many change result, and how many were excluded as `PAID` or `CLOSED`. **The numbers themselves sit behind an explicit control, available only to a user who also holds a claims scope** (`ASSIGNED`, `QUEUE` or `ALL_CLAIMS`), and **the reveal is logged like any other clinical-adjacent read** (BR-AUDIT-4, V-554). **The grant question is A3's — `D2-182`**: either `TERM_AUTHOR` gains a narrow claim-reference read, or the control is available only to the subset of authors who hold an assessor or approver role as well, and A3 owns which |
| **V-738** | **The declaration is mandatory and the two behave differently, so a default would be a decision.** On **Sửa lỗi** the screen runs the impact analysis **before** the confirmation is offered and shows the count of in-flight claims bound to that rule set, the count whose result changes and **— behind `V-759`'s control — the claim numbers**; the reason is `textarea(2000)` and mandatory (§2.9); and **no claim is re-decided automatically** — each is routed to a person with both results visible. **A correction never silently changes a claim's outcome**, for exactly the reason class J may never auto-decline: it would be the engine settling a question the engine got wrong once already |
| **V-747** | **A correction landing on a claim that already carries an open checkpoint on the same term supersedes it, and records both.** The re-evaluation a correction runs (V-738) produces a fresh result for every in-flight claim, and on a claim whose checkpoint from the **old** version is still open there are then two questions about one clause. **The old checkpoint is closed as `KHÔNG_CÒN_HIỆU_LỰC` — superseded — by the platform** (V-741's mechanism, V-551's actor), **a new one is raised against the corrected version**, and **both are retained and both are visible on §5.9.1a**, each with the term version that produced it (V-740). **The new row's *Nguồn* column reads *raised by a term correction*** (§5.29.4) and carries a link to the superseded one, because an assessor arriving at it needs to know that the claim already had a question and that the question moved. **The old checkpoint is never silently re-pointed at the new version**: an assessor's half-formed judgement about one wording is not a judgement about another, and re-pointing would attach a person's name to a clause they never read. **Where the old checkpoint had already been answered**, the answer stands on the version that produced it and the new checkpoint is raised beside it — which is `V-738`'s whole posture, that a correction never re-decides anything automatically |
| **V-739** | **Neither operation may touch a claim in `PAID` or `CLOSED`** (BR-TERM-6, **S-40**). The impact count excludes them and states that it has, naming how many were excluded — a count that silently omits a population is a count that will be quoted as though it were complete. Correcting a settled claim means recovering money from a customer or paying them more, and MVP 1 has neither mechanism; it is a business matter, not a system operation |

#### 5.28.6 Actions

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Tạo điều khoản** | `TERM_AUTHOR` | F2 selected | A `DRAFT` version is created, F1 allocated, F18 written | inline on a duplicate `clauseRef` within F2 |
| **Lưu bản nháp** | `TERM_AUTHOR` | F17 is `DRAFT`; **V-734 and V-742 pass** | The draft is written and audited field by field (F63). **Invisible to the engine** — V-735 | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-153**)* on a failed validation |
| **Trình phê duyệt** | `TERM_AUTHOR` | Every mandatory field present; **V-734**, **V-742** and **V-737** pass; F17 is `DRAFT`; **the correction-versus-new-version declaration is made — V-738** | F17 → `PENDING_ACTIVE`; the approver's queue is updated (§5.23's staff notification) | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-153**)* listing every failure at once, never the first |
| **Phê duyệt điều khoản** | `TERM_APPROVE` | F17 is `PENDING_ACTIVE`; **the acting user is not F18 — V-736**; **on a correction, the impact count has been displayed and acknowledged — V-738, V-739** | F19 written; F17 → `ACTIVE` at F15. **On a correction, the re-evaluation runs and every claim whose result changed is routed to §5.29** | *(new A2 item — **D2-154**)*, carrying the impact count and the written reason. Self-approval: *(new A2 item — **D2-153**)* |
| **Trả lại bản nháp** | `TERM_APPROVE` | F17 is `PENDING_ACTIVE`; a reason entered | F17 → `DRAFT`; the reason is shown to the author. **The same shape as an approver returning a settlement plan** (§5.11.3) | *(new A2 item — **D2-153**)* |
| **Thu hồi điều khoản** | `TERM_APPROVE` | F17 is `ACTIVE` | F17 → `WITHDRAWN`, F16 set. **Claims already bound to the version are unaffected** (BR-TERM-4); the version is retained and stays readable from §5.9.1a forever | *(new A2 item — **D2-153**)* |
| **Sao chép làm phiên bản mới** | `TERM_AUTHOR` | An `ACTIVE` or `WITHDRAWN` version exists | A new `DRAFT` version of the **same `termId`**, pre-filled, with F15 blank and the declaration unset | — |
| **Xem lịch sử phiên bản** | any role with **R** | — | Every version of the term with its author, approver, dates, the declaration made and **the claims evaluated under it** | — |
| **Kiểm thử trên hồ sơ lịch sử** | — | — | **Does not exist in MVP 1.** F68, Priority 2 — **D2-158**. The control is absent rather than disabled, per §2.5 | — |
| **Xóa điều khoản** | — | — | **Does not exist.** A term that has evaluated a claim must stay resolvable forever, on exactly the rule V-550 applies to a user who has touched a claim. **Withdrawal is the mechanism** | — |

#### 5.28.7 Empty and error

| Condition | What the console shows |
|---|---|
| No term is registered against the selected rule set | UI-25's *nothing exists yet* sentence, naming what causes a row to appear, **and a standing banner: chain step 4 will test nothing on every claim bound to this rule set.** This is a real operational state at the start of the pilot and it must not read as a clean one |
| A term references a benefit code absent from F2's rule set | The row renders with the code flagged and **the term is not evaluated**; the claim is not affected and the register raises an **operator-queue item of the fourth population — §5.19.1, V-757**. **A term that silently matched nothing would be indistinguishable from a term that passed** |
| A correction's impact analysis cannot complete | The confirmation is **not offered**. An approval with an unknown impact count is the one thing V-738 exists to prevent |
| A pending version exists when a second author opens the term | The screen is read-only with a banner naming the author and the moment, exactly as §5.16.4 does for a pending threshold change |
| **Two authors save the same `DRAFT` version** | **Optimistic concurrency on the version record — V-746**, the same shape as §5.10.4's on the claim. The second save is **refused, never merged**: the author is told which fields moved, by whom and when, and re-opens the version at its current state. **A term is not a form, it is a contractual statement**, and a merge that silently combined one author's `selector` with another author's `predicate` would produce a term neither of them wrote and both of them would sign off. The version record carries an integer version, incremented on every save, and the check is server-side |
| **A term-register defect is raised** — a scope code absent from the tree, a fact no longer available, a `TBC-` reference on a term whose effect is a decline | **The operator queue's fourth population — V-757, §5.19.1.** The banner on this screen names the count; the work is done here, and the queue is what makes sure somebody looks |

---

### 5.29 Term checkpoint queue (F67)

*(New at v0.5. **F67**, Priority 1, **Group G**. D1 §5.3.1 **BR-TERM-2**; *Solution Paper* §2.1 and §4.2; decision **D-2**. Screen **S-14**.)*

**Purpose.** Put the clause in front of a person, with the case, and record what they decided — so that a term whose effect is `CHECKPOINT`, or a class-E term whose document is absent, reaches a judgement instead of reaching an auto-decline or nothing at all. **That is not the same population as *class J and class E***: a class-`D` term may carry `CHECKPOINT` and two of the pilot's ten do (§5.28.1a), so this queue receives all three classes.

**Entered from.** The console's navigation; the banner on any claim carrying an open checkpoint; §5.9.1a's `ĐIỂM_KIỂM` rows; and the routing a term **correction** performs (§5.28.5). **S-14.**

**Who may open it.** `ASSESSOR` **F**, scope `ASSIGNED`; `APPROVER` **R**. **`ADMIN` has no access at all** — a checkpoint is a claim decision and A3 §4.11 keeps `ADMIN` out of every one of them. **A3 v1.5 carries the queue grant and states the `ADMIN` exclusion explicitly — `D2-175` closed.**

**Why this screen is the other half of the class model.** §5.28.1 says a class-J term may never auto-decline. **That is a prohibition and not a design until there is somewhere for the term to go instead** — otherwise the engine's only options are to decline it anyway or to ignore it, and the second is worse than the first because it is silent. This queue is that somewhere.

#### 5.29.1 What a checkpoint is, and what it is not

| It is | It is not |
|---|---|
| A **question about a claim, raised by a term**, with the clause quoted and the facts the selector matched on beside it | A decline. A checkpoint that nobody answers is not an outcome and never becomes one |
| **Attached to the claim, and to the line or the event the term's scope named** | A claim state. No state in §7.1 is added and none is needed: the claim sits in `UNDER_ASSESSMENT` exactly as it would otherwise |
| **A block on the auto-approval gate while it is open** — condition 3, §5.11.4 | A block on the claim. An assessor works the claim normally; what they cannot do is submit the plan with it open (§5.10.2 check 13) |

#### 5.29.2 Field table — S-14, one checkpoint

| # | Label (VI) | Type | Source | Req | Validation | On error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Số hồ sơ | `text(20)` | `system` | M | The claim, with its `/n` event suffix where the term's scope was an event. **Never truncated** (UI-19) — a clipped suffix attributes a judgement to the wrong event. The column is sized to §2.9's width, so the constraint is met by the control | inline |
| F2 | Dòng chi phí / sự kiện | `derived` | `system` | M | **What the checkpoint attaches to, keyed on the level of the fact the selector matched — V-745**, not on the term's scope and not on its effect. Opens the line on §5.6 or the event on §5.7. **A checkpoint whose line or event no longer exists is not rendered as an orphan** — it is flagged and routed to the operator queue (§5.19) | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-155**)* |
| F3 | Điều khoản | `text(20)` | `snapshot` | M | The `clauseRef` of the term that raised it, opening the term read-only at §5.28 **at the version evaluated**, never the version in force today | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-155**)* where the version cannot be resolved |
| F4 | Nội dung điều khoản | `textarea(4000)` | `snapshot` | M | **The clause text quoted verbatim** from F6 of the term version — §5.28.3. **Rendered in full and never truncated to a summary**: the person deciding must read what the contract says, not what a screen thought it said. Read-only for every role, so the panel expands rather than clipping (UI-19 does not apply to it) | inline |
| F5 | Loại điều khoản | `enum(termClass)` | `snapshot` | M | `D`, `J` or `E` — **all three reach this queue and the row is rendered whichever it is.** **Corrected 24/08/2026**: this row read *"`J` or `E`; a class-D term never raises a checkpoint, so a row showing `D` is a defect in F66 and is refused rather than rendered"*, which was wrong and would have refused to render a checkpoint the product actually raises. `termClass` governs the **auto-decline**, not the effect (§5.28.1a): **a class-`D` term whose effect is `CHECKPOINT` selects deterministically and then asks a person**, and two of A5 §7.2's ten do — `TERM-HC-002` and `TERM-HC-003`. **What is refused is the other direction**, and it is refused at authoring by `V-742` rather than at rendering here: a class `J` or `E` term carrying a decline effect. **The class is shown because it tells the assessor what kind of question they are being asked** — on `D` the facts matched and a proviso is open; on `J` the whole question is a judgement; on `E` a document decides it | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-155**)* where the class cannot be resolved from the evaluated version |
| F6 | Căn cứ chọn | `derived` | `system` | M | **The facts the `selector` matched on, named and valued** — `serviceCategory = SUPPLEMENT`, `benefitCode = 200.2`, `lossType = ILL_OP`. This is the brief for the task. **A checkpoint with no visible basis is a question with no context**, and the assessor's only recourse would be to re-derive it from the claim. **At least one fact is always present**, because V-734 makes the selector non-null | inline |
| F7 | Tài liệu yêu cầu | `enum(documentType)` | `snapshot` | C — **mandatory where the term's effect is `REQUIRE_DOC`** | The A4 document type the term requires, and whether the checklist already carries it (§5.5). **A checkpoint whose document has since arrived is still answered by a person** — arrival is not a judgement. **The type A5 §7.2's one class-E term names — a police or hospital statement — is not in A4's catalogue, so today this field renders a type that does not exist**; until A4 carries it (**`D2-179`**) **F7 renders the term's own stated requirement as text and the checklist does not carry a row for it** — `V-756` | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-155**)* |
| F8 | Kết luận | `enum(checkpointOutcome)` | `user` | M | `GIỮ_NGUYÊN` — uphold, decline the line or the event citing the clause · `BỎ_QUA` — clear · `KHÔNG_CÒN_HIỆU_LỰC` — closed as moot, **written by the platform and never chosen by a person** (V-741, V-749). **Registered by A1 v1.5 §4.10 — `D2-174` closed** | inline |
| F9 | Lý do | `textarea(2000)` | `user` | **M on every outcome, including an uphold** | §2.9's free-text reason width. **A clear needs a reason because it is a decision not to apply a contractual term**, and an uphold needs one because B-14 governs the wording that reaches the customer (V-531, V-532). **Never empty** | *(new A2 item needed — **D2-155**)* |
| F10 | Phiên bản điều khoản đã áp dụng | `derived` | `system` | M | **The term version that produced this checkpoint**, recorded on the outcome — V-740. Resolved from the claim's evaluation record, never from the register's current state | inline |
| F11 | Người quyết định · thời điểm | `derived` | `system` | C — **mandatory once F8 is set** | Written on the outcome and carried into the processing trail (§5.14) and the audit log (§6.3). **`SYSTEM` on a moot closure** (V-741, V-551), never the last human who touched the claim | inline |

**V-745 — what a checkpoint attaches to, and v0.5's rule covered nothing the pilot actually raises.** As issued, F2 read *"the cost line where the term's scope was `BENEFIT` or `BENEFIT_SUBTREE`, the insured event where it was `PRODUCT` **with `DECLINE_EVENT`**"*. **Both halves miss.** A checkpoint is raised by an effect of `CHECKPOINT` or by an unmet `REQUIRE_DOC` — **never by `DECLINE_EVENT`**, which declines rather than asking — and **all ten of the pilot's terms are `PRODUCT` scope**, so the first half never fires either. The rule as written attached nothing to anything on the one product we have.

**The right key is the fact the selector matched on**, which F6 already renders and which is the only thing that says *what the question is about*:

| The selector matched on | Level | The checkpoint attaches to |
|---|---|---|
| `serviceCategory` · `benefitCode` · `lineDiagnosisCode` · `treatmentDate` · `memberAge` | **Line** (A1 §4.11) | **That cost line**, and F2 opens it on §5.6. One checkpoint per matching line, not one per term |
| `diagnosisCode` · `lossType` · `facilityCountry` · `facilityType` · `conditionClass` · `continuousCoverDays` | **Event** (A1 §4.11) | **That insured event**, and F2 opens it on §5.7 |
| `claimantCapacity` | **Claim** (A1 §4.11) | **The claim**, with no line and no event named. F2 renders the claim number alone and opens S-02's general tab |
| **A `REQUIRE_DOC` checkpoint** | — | **The insured event whose loss type selected the term.** The document is evidence about an event, not about a line — A5 §7.2's one class-E term selects on `lossType in [ACC_OP, ACC_IP]` and the police or hospital statement it wants describes the accident |

**Where a selector matches at both levels, the checkpoint attaches at the line level, once per matching line.** A selector written as `all(lossType = ACC_OP, serviceCategory = DENTAL)` is in play on an event *and* on the lines within it, and attaching it to the event would ask the assessor a question about four lines when it concerns one. **The event is named on the row beside the line** so nothing is lost, and F6 shows both facts with their values. **The reverse never happens**: a purely event-level selector is never fanned out across the event's lines, because that would put the same judgement in front of a person four times and record four answers to one question.

**Notes on the fields above.** **F8 and F9 are the only two fields a person enters**, which is the whole of the screen: everything else exists to make those two answerable. **The other nine are written or resolved by the platform and every one of them still carries an error path**, because each carries a rule and §2.2 does not allow a rule with no way to report it — seven of the nine are `inline`, where the control or the render prevents the failure rather than reporting it, and two are not: F2, where the line or event a checkpoint attaches to has gone, and F3, where the term version cannot be resolved. **Those two are the only ways this screen can fail in a manner a person must be told about**, and both route to the operator queue rather than to a claim outcome (§2.10).

#### 5.29.3 The two outcomes, and the third that is not chosen

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| **V-740** | **Every outcome is recorded with the term version that produced it** (F10), for the life of the claim. Not the `termId`, and not the version in force when the outcome was recorded — **the version the claim was evaluated against** (BR-TERM-4, P-02). A checkpoint answered against version 3 and re-read after version 4 is `ACTIVE` would otherwise show a person's judgement beside a clause they never saw. **On an uphold, the line or the event is declined citing that version's `clauseRef` and quoting that version's `textVi`**, and both flow into `CLM-LETTER-002` — **unless that version's `clauseRef` is provisional, in which case there is no uphold to record**: `V-743` and `BR-TERM-10` remove the control rather than letting a decline quote a placeholder |
| **V-748** | **A `WITHDRAWN` term's open checkpoints stay open and stay answerable.** Withdrawing a term takes it out of future evaluations (`V-735`, BR-TERM-4); **it does not retract a question already asked about a claim that is still being assessed**, and closing those checkpoints automatically would either decide them by default or leave the claim with a gap where a judgement should be. **F3 opens the withdrawn version read-only**, at the version evaluated, exactly as it does for an `ACTIVE` one — §5.28.6's *Thu hồi điều khoản* already retains every version forever for this reason. **The queue row carries a marker saying the term has since been withdrawn**, because it changes what the assessor should think about, and it is a fact they have no other way to see |
| **V-749** | **A `CANCELLED` claim closes every open checkpoint on it as `KHÔNG_CÒN_HIỆU_LỰC` — moot — written by the platform** (V-551, `SYSTEM`), extending `V-741`'s mechanism from *overtaken by a decline* to *overtaken by the claim ending*. A cancelled claim will never settle, so a judgement about what it should pay is a question with no consumer, and leaving the checkpoint open leaves an item on somebody's queue that can never be cleared honestly. **The reason recorded is the cancellation, with its `cancellationReason` (V-725) and the claim's own trail entry**, so the closure says *which* ending overtook it. It is not an outcome a person may choose from F8, for exactly V-741's reason: nobody decided it |
| **V-741** | **A declined line with an open checkpoint is still declined, and the checkpoint closes as `KHÔNG_CÒN_HIỆU_LỰC` — moot — with that reason recorded** (BR-TERM-2). **A `CHECKPOINT` never overrides a decline.** The closure is written by the platform and is not an outcome a person may choose from F8: nobody decided it, the claim decided it, and recording it as a human judgement would put a name against a decision nobody made. **A moot checkpoint does not block the gate** (§5.11.4 condition 3) and does not block submission (§5.10.2 check 13) — it is closed. **It stays visible on §5.9.1a with its closure reason**, because *"this clause was raised and then overtaken"* is a different fact from *"this clause was never raised"* |

**Uphold and clear are not symmetrical, and the screen should not draw them as though they were.** An **uphold** produces a decline and is therefore subject to every rule that governs a decline — the reason code from A5 §6.3 (`EXCL` for an exclusion), the B-14 wording rule on the rationale, and the item and the amount named (V-531, V-532, §5.10.2 check 2). A **clear** produces nothing visible to the customer at all; its whole audience is the auditor asking why a contractual term was not applied. **So the uphold path is longer, and it is longer because it is the one that reaches a person outside the company.**

**And the uphold path cannot be submitted today, because the message it produces cannot carry what the term layer hands it.** Three requirements meet here and A2 v1.1 satisfies none of them for `EXCL`:

| Required by | The requirement | What A2 v1.1 §4 has |
|---|---|---|
| `V-740` above, and §5.10.2 check 1 (`V-585`) | **The item and the amount named** in the decline the uphold produces | **`EXCL` binds neither.** It is *"Khoản chi phí này thuộc điểm loại trừ {exclusionRef}…"* — one placeholder, and it is the clause. `NOTREL` and `NOTCOV` bind `{itemName}` and `{itemAmount}`; `EXCL` does not |
| §5.9.7 requirement 3 and `V-729` | **Every `clauseRef` that fired, in order** | **A single `{exclusionRef}`**, and `CLM-LETTER-002`'s *Basis* section reads *"**The clause** of the policy terms relied on — article and clause number, quoted"* — singular in both places |
| `V-740` | **The clause's `textVi` quoted verbatim**, from the version evaluated | The *Basis* section quotes *a* clause number. Nothing binds the text |

**`D2-178` asks A2 for all three**: `EXCL` to bind `{itemName}`, `{itemAmount}` and a **list** of `{clauseRef}`, and `CLM-LETTER-002`'s *Basis* section to accept **one or many** clauses with each `textVi` quoted verbatim. **Until it lands, `V-531` is not applied to an `EXCL` rationale produced by a term uphold** — stated here rather than left to a developer, because `V-531` requires the item and the amount to be named in the rationale and the template has nowhere to put them, so **the check would refuse every uphold and the path could not be submitted at all** (§5.10.2 checks 1 and 2). The carve-out is narrow and it is temporary: it applies to an `EXCL` rationale and to nothing else, `V-532` and the B-14 wording rule are untouched, and it is deleted the day `D2-178` closes. **It is recorded as a defect being tolerated, not as a design.**

#### 5.29.4 The queue itself

**The list is a grid and obeys §2.11's grid conventions without exception.** Default sort is **descending on the moment the checkpoint was raised** (UI-14), page size 25 (UI-18), and it carries no money column and therefore no totals row (UI-20).

| Column | Note |
|---|---|
| Số hồ sơ | F1, with the event suffix |
| Điều khoản | F3, and F4's first line |
| Loại | F5 |
| Người được bảo hiểm | From the claim's snapshot |
| Nguồn | **Raised by evaluation** or **raised by a term correction** (§5.28.5) — two different pieces of work, and an assessor arriving at a correction-routed item needs to know that the claim already had an answer and that the answer moved |
| Tuổi | The ageing clock from the moment it was raised, in §5.3.2's buckets |
| Trạng thái | Open · upheld · cleared · moot |

#### 5.29.5 Actions

| Action | Who | Precondition | Effect | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Giữ nguyên điều khoản** | `ASSESSOR` | Assigned; F9 entered; claim not locked; **the term version's `clauseRef` is not provisional — `V-743`** | F8 → `GIỮ_NGUYÊN`; **the line or the event is declined citing F3 and quoting F4**, with F12's reason code from the term; the chain re-runs in full; the checkpoint closes; V-740 written | *(new A2 item — **D2-155**)*. Rationale breaching B-14: *(D2-59)*. **`V-531` is not applied to the `EXCL` rationale while `D2-178` is open** — §5.29.3 |
| **Bỏ qua điểm kiểm** | `ASSESSOR` | Assigned; F9 entered; claim not locked | F8 → `BỎ_QUA`; **nothing on the claim changes except the record**; the checkpoint closes; V-740 written | *(new A2 item — **D2-155**)* |
| **Mở hồ sơ** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER` | — | Opens S-02 at the tab F2 names | — |
| **Xem điều khoản** | `ASSESSOR`, `APPROVER` | — | Opens §5.28 read-only at the evaluated version | — |
| **Đóng vì đã bị từ chối** | — | — | **Does not exist as a control.** V-741 and V-749 — the platform writes a moot closure; no role may choose it | — |

**`V-743` on this screen: the *Giữ nguyên* control is absent, not disabled.** Every one of A5 §7.2's ten terms carries a provisional `TBC-nn` clause reference, because the filed wording does not exist. **D1 v0.5 `BR-TERM-10` forbids a decline that cites one**, and a decline is exactly what an uphold produces. So on the pilot product as it stands **the uphold control does not appear on any checkpoint in this queue** — §2.5's rule applies unchanged: a control a role may not use is absent, not disabled, because a disabled control the user cannot explain is a support call. **The banner says why in one sentence** — *"điều khoản này chưa có số điều khoản chính thức; chưa thể giữ nguyên"* — and names `D2-159`, which is the business item that unblocks it.

**What is left on the screen is the clear, and that is the honest state rather than a degraded one.** An assessor can still read the clause, see the facts it matched on, and record that it does not bite with a reason. What they cannot do is decline a customer's line by quoting a clause number that was invented to fill a column. **The whole term-decline path is blocked on filed wording** and it is recorded as a business blocker rather than as a screen defect — `D2-159`, §5.31.

#### 5.29.6 Empty and error

| Condition | What the console shows |
|---|---|
| No open checkpoint | UI-25's *nothing exists yet* sentence, saying what causes a row to appear. **Not an error colour and not a congratulation** — an empty queue on a portfolio whose register carries four `CHECKPOINT` terms — two class `J` and two class `D` (A5 §7.2) — is an ordinary morning, and it is also what a broken selector looks like |
| A checkpoint whose term version cannot be resolved | The row renders with F3 and F4 flagged and **no outcome control at all**. A person may not decide a checkpoint whose clause the screen cannot show them. Operator queue (§5.19) |
| The claim has since been locked at `PENDING_APPROVAL` | The outcome controls are absent, the checkpoint is read-only, and the banner says which claim and which state. **Check 13 means this cannot ordinarily arise**; where it does, it is a defect and is visible as one |
| The claim reached `PAID` or `CLOSED` with a checkpoint still open | Read-only, and flagged. **S-40** — nothing may touch it, and the fact that it exists is worth reporting rather than hiding |
| **The claim was cancelled** | Every open checkpoint on it is **closed as moot by the platform** with the cancellation named — `V-749`. The rows leave the open queue and stay readable on §5.9.1a and on the claim's trail, because *"raised and overtaken by a cancellation"* is a different fact from *"never raised"* |
| **The term that raised the checkpoint has since been withdrawn** | **The row stays open and stays answerable** — `V-748`. F3 opens the **withdrawn version** read-only, at the version evaluated, and the row carries a marker saying the term is no longer in force. **The outcome controls are not removed**: a question asked of a live claim is still a question, and withdrawing the term does not answer it |
| **Every open checkpoint on the claim has been answered** | The claim leaves this queue and §5.10.2's check 13 stops refusing. **It does not return to the auto-approval gate** — the gate was evaluated once, in `DOC_PROCESSING`, and §5.11.4 says why |
