### 10.2b For the vendor — BnK IDP

> **The identifier scheme for IDP questions changed on 24 August 2026, and every reference written so far still tracks.** The vendor register identified IDP's questions as **`I-9` … `I-12`**. **D3 uses `I-01` … `I-16` for interface contracts**, so `I-10`, `I-11` and `I-12` each meant two different things across the live set — an IDP question in one file and an integration contract in another. **The four existing questions keep their numbers and become `Q-IDP-01` … `Q-IDP-04`**, a prefix of their own. **`C-IDP-nn` is reserved for the ten closed IDP capability confirmations and is not extended.** **`I-nn` now means an interface and nothing else.** *Solution Paper* §12, applied here.
>
> **An earlier form of the rename collided, and the collision is now resolved.** Reusing `C-IDP-09` … `C-IDP-12` would have clashed with Framework §7.5's vendor register, where `C-IDP-01` … `C-IDP-10` are **closed IDP capability confirmations** — `C-IDP-09` the clinical-appropriateness capability and `C-IDP-10` the curated knowledge base. Questions and capability confirmations are different things and must not share a series. The settled scheme, recorded in `_Cau_hoi_Vendor_v1.3.md` §2.0, gives IDP questions their own prefix: **`I-9` → `Q-IDP-01`, `I-10` → `Q-IDP-02`, `I-11` → `Q-IDP-03`, `I-12` → `Q-IDP-04`**, with `Q-IDP-05` and `Q-IDP-06` new here. `I-nn` now means an interface, `C-IDP-nn` a closed capability confirmation, and `Q-IDP-nn` an open question — three series, three meanings, no overlap.

| # | Question to IDP | What waits on it here |
|---|---|---|
| **Q-IDP-05** | **Can extraction return the country of the treating facility?** | **§5.28** — A5 §7's exclusion 10, *treatment received outside Vietnam*, is class **D** and unevaluable in practice, because `facilityCountry` is in A1 §4.11's vocabulary and **not yet held**. **The term is authored with its selector and predicate written and its status left `DRAFT`** (A5 §7.2, `TERM-HC-010`), and a draft term is invisible to the engine — **so nothing is evaluated and no checkpoint is raised**, rather than a checkpoint being raised on a fact nobody has. Every foreign-treatment claim is therefore settled today as though the exclusion did not exist |
| **Q-IDP-06** | **Can extraction return a treatment-day count per line?** | **§5.9.3 and §5.7.2 F17.** The `DAY` counter added to `V-723` increments by the treatment-day count of the line. Today §5.7.2 F17 derives a count **per event** from the treatment date range; **per line there is nothing**, so a benefit limited in days is enforceable only where the range makes the count derivable. **`V-708` is the workaround and it is not the answer** |

> **`Q-IDP-02` — line-level ICD, under the settled scheme — rises in priority and is not new.** It already blocked the line-level diagnosis column (`D2-134`); it now also blocks two of A5 §7's exclusions from reaching class D — **#5** (infertility and assisted reproduction) and **#9** (congenital conditions). **Two exclusions that a fact would decide are decided by a person instead**, and each of those claims leaves the straight-through path under §5.11.4's third condition.

> **`D2-05` is retired.** It asked whether an administrator might override the `premium_paid` flag manually. The flag is InsureMO's, on a record we do not edit, and we have no administrator here to grant the override to (§3.5). **The exposure it named is not retired with it**: A5 §6.1 step 1 tests a value we no longer govern, and a policy paid outside the mocked flow is now corrected in InsureMO or not at all.

### 10.4 For A2 — messages that must be written

**Fifty-eight open items are cited as missing A2 messages, at 199 points of use across the document, and they stand behind something closer to a hundred sentences than to fifty.** Each is marked at the point of use as `*(new A2 item needed — D2-nn)*`, so a reader of any field table can see immediately that the message behind it has still to be written. Parts V and VI additionally collect theirs — §5.18 and §6.5.1. **From v0.6 none of them proposes a `CLM-CONSOLE` number above `-015`** — `D2-88`, §5.18. The summary:

| Group | Count | The one that matters most |
|---|---|---|
| **Group import** (`D2-09`) | 1 group, ~11 messages | The eleven import validation codes need Vietnamese text a non-technical administrator can act on. **`D2-06`, `D2-07` and `D2-08` are retired** with the administration screens they belonged to (§3.5) |
| **Payee and payout-account master** (`D2-121`, `D2-122`) | 2 | New with F58 (§5.20.8). `D2-121` is the save-failure family; `D2-122` is V-701, a payout account that does not exist or has no owner |
| Mobile (`D2-21…34`) | 14 | **`D2-25` — there is no generic mandatory-field message in A2 at all.** Roughly a dozen rows in Part IV have a rule with no way to tell the customer it fired, which §2.2 defines as a defect. This is the single most consequential gap in the list, and **§2.11 UI-3 now makes it general** — it is the message every screen in the document falls back to. `D2-25` is cited by three more field rows after this pass and by the loss-type control |
| **Mobile — the claimant block** (`D2-39…42`) | **4** | Four messages the app cannot show without: standing and relationship validation (`V-116`), a claimant identity that does not match the insured where standing is *bản thân* (`V-117`), the accident narrative (`V-403`), and the claimant's email (`V-404`). **`D2-40`'s wording must not teach the attack** — it says the details do not match, not that a mismatch is treated as suspicious |

**A rule enforced with a generic "permission denied" gets worked around rather than understood.** That is A2's own reasoning, and it is why these are listed as work rather than left to the implementer.

#### 10.4.1 The number this section used to give, and the number that can actually be checked

**v0.5 opened this section with *"roughly fifty messages"*, and *roughly* was doing more work than it looked.** Fifty was neither the count of items — there are **58** — nor the count of points of use — there are **199** — nor the count of sentences A2 must write, which nobody has counted because several items carry a family behind one identifier (`D2-153` is eight, `D2-123` is five, `D2-09` is eleven). **A number that is not the count of anything cannot be reconciled against anything**, which is the objection §8.1 makes to a range with no count beside it, arriving in Part X instead.

**There is a number here that *can* be checked, and it is a different and more useful one: the count of field-table rows carrying a `Validation` with an empty `On error`.** §2.2 defines that as a defect — *"it means a rule exists with no way to tell the user it fired"* — so the count is a direct measure of how far this document is from its own convention. **Recomputed from the merged file at v0.6: 54 such rows before this pass, 50 after.**

**And the composition matters more than the total, because it is mostly not what §2.2 is worried about:**

| Group | Rows | What they are |
|---|---|---|
| **Part VI record schemas** — §6.1.4's template, §6.2.6's user and grant records, §6.3.2's audit entry | **9** | **The declared exception.** §2.2 and §6.0 both state it: these fields are written by the platform and never validated against a person, so *On error* is empty by nature. **Not defects** |
| **Descriptions written into the wrong column** | **~41** | A *Validation* cell holding a derivation, a provenance note or a cross-reference rather than a rule — *"set when the claim is first assigned"*, *"§5.10.1 F1 as it stood at that submission"*, *"the ageing clock from the moment it was raised"*. **§2.2 separately prohibits this**: *"the Validation column is not a place to put a description."* They are not missing messages; they are misfiled sentences, and the fix is to move them to the section's notes rather than to ask A2 for anything |
| **Genuine rules with no way to report them firing** | **4** | The real defects, and they are the only ones §10.4 should ever have been counting |

**The four, named rather than left as a total, and all four are fixed in v0.6:**

| Row | The rule that had no message | What v0.6 does |
|---|---|---|
| **§5.20.2 F5** — *Tên chủ tài khoản* | **BR-PAY-1**: the account name is never typed on any surface. The control has no keyboard, so the *screen* cannot produce the failure — **but a payload can**, and a request carrying a value must be refused rather than ignored | **Gains a message** — *(new A2 item needed — `D2-121`)* on the server-side refusal. It is the one of the four that is genuinely a missing message |
| **§5.21.1 F10** — *Phương án đã đóng băng* | **V-716 rule 5**: a frozen plan version is never edited and never deleted, by any role including `ADMIN`. A write reaching the server is refused | **Gains a message** — *(new A2 item needed — `D2-131`)* on a refused write |
| **§5.4.1 F31** — *Ngày giao việc* | *"Set when the claim is first assigned and re-set on every reassignment"* — a **derivation**, not a validation, and a platform-written date has no way to fail in front of a person | **The rule moves to §5.4.1's notes** and the cell is emptied. Nothing about the behaviour changes; the sentence is now where §2.2 says it belongs |
| **§5.16.2 F11a** — *Hiệu lực đến* | `V-722`, which is **defined at §5.11.4 and enforced there**. Restating it on a read-only field put a rule in a column with no error path | **The rule moves to §5.16.2's notes** and the cell is emptied |

**Two of the four gain a message and two are re-filed, which is the honest split rather than the tidy one.** A missing message is A2's work; a misfiled sentence is this document's, and pretending the second is the first would put two more rows on A2's list for no benefit to anybody reading a screen. **The remaining ~41 are the same shape as the two re-filed here** and should be swept in one pass rather than one at a time — it is a legibility defect rather than a functional one, and it is recorded as **`D2-160`** rather than done here, because forty-one edits scattered across five parts in a reissue that already changes this much is how a regression enters a document nobody diffed.

### 10.5 Where every open item is defined

**Two of v0.5's items are worth naming here rather than leaving in §5.30.** **`D2-173`** was the only place in this reissue where this document was knowingly ahead of D1 on a data model, and it was ahead because the model as written could not be built. **It is closed the same day** — D1, A5 and the seed adopted the split, and the interesting part of the closure is that the split immediately produced a question none of the three had asked: *what selects a term whose whole substance is a judgement?* A5 §7.3 answers it rather than leaving `V-734` with an exception. **`D2-158`** is the only feature in the catalogue that we build and this document does not specify, and §0.3 says so on the first page rather than letting Part IX's arithmetic imply it.

Both are in §10.2, with the business. **D2-13** joins them as the one item that reopens a settled principle rather than filling a gap. **D2-10** blocks neither a screen nor a decision, and is nonetheless the item most worth answering first, because it decides whether five reason codes are a contract term or an internal enum.

### 10.7 The vendor-answer exposure

**v0.1 said this document does not depend on the InsureMO and IDP confirmations. Half of that is no longer true, and the half that failed is the one that mattered.**

The confirmations came in on 21 August 2026. IDP confirmed every capability, including the two that were open — the clinical appropriateness assessment and the versioned knowledge base — so the rows below that concern IDP are now history rather than exposure. **InsureMO confirmed more than we asked**, and the consequence was that a system was deleted: the schedule and the register moved to InsureMO, and **the fallback moved nowhere, because there is no longer anywhere for it to go.**

| **InsureMO is used for the policy side only; the claim platform is built entirely by us** — C-BUS-09 | Parts IV to VIII are unaffected in substance. **Framework D-B closes as *none*** and C-IMO-02 is moot: the limit ledger at §5.9 is exclusively ours by decision, not by discovery |
| **IDP can do the clinical appropriateness assessment** — *the clinical-assessment capability item*, **C-IDP-09** in Framework §7.5's numbering *(and see `D2-176` — the identifier is now overloaded)* | §5.8 is buildable and auto-approval's condition 2 is satisfiable. **Framework RK-13 closes.** The fail-safe stays in the design: an assessment that did not run is never a clean result, so advisory mode makes the gate **inactive**, not open (§5.11.4) |
| **IDP will build a curated, versioned knowledge base with named provenance** — *the knowledge-base capability item*, **C-IDP-10** in Framework §7.5's numbering *(and see `D2-176`)* | §5.8's evidence column stands, and B-14's defensibility argument stands with it. **What is not settled is clinical sign-off, and none was offered** — Framework RK-08, High/High, survives its own confirmation |

| If it turns out otherwise | What changes here |
|---|---|
| **The benefit tree as demonstrated does not survive our full Product Data Sheet** — a depth of nesting, a count limit, a waiting period across the six classes, an inherited co-payment or a deduction-ratio condition that the product model turns out not to express | **This is RK-14, and it is the one that has no answer in this document.** v0.1's row read: *"Nothing in Parts IV, V, VI. The schedule is mastered in the Policy Data Store instead — which Part III already specifies, because the store holds it either way. P-06 was designed for this."* **That sentence is withdrawn in full.** The schedule has nowhere else to live. §3.2.3 is unbuildable as specified, §5.2.2's third call has nothing to return, §5.9's chain has no tree to run against, and **SC-03 and SC-08 both fail**. The remedy is a build, not a swap. **Mitigation: C-IMO-06 — evaluate the sandbox against A5 v1.2, benefit by benefit, early. §3.4 Cases A to E are written to be that test** |
| **InsureMO returns the coverage facts rather than a coverage verdict**, or returns a verdict with different boundary semantics | **D2-10.** §3.3.3 is built to survive both: the console implements the five tests against the snapshot and compares rather than replaces where a verdict arrives. What it costs is that five reason codes are a contract term under one reading and an internal enum under the other, and D3's I-05 cannot be finalised until it is known |
| **InsureMO pages the benefit tree, or pages a member search instead of refusing it** | §3.3.4 property 3 and §3.3.1 are the two places a general-purpose platform is most likely to do the ordinary thing and be wrong. A partially loaded tree is a **corrupt snapshot**; a truncated member list **silently hides the right member**. Both are caught at the adapter and both hold the claim rather than settling it — §5.2.7, **V-501** |
| **InsureMO's effective dating does not answer as at a date**, or silently falls back to current | **C-IMO-05, and it is the contract-detail item where a surprise costs design rather than a mock.** An as-at-a-date query that quietly returns current is indistinguishable from a correct one until a claim is disputed. §3.4 Case E is the test |
| **InsureMO exposes no bulk member load** — C-IMO-10 answers no | **§3.6.7 path B.** F59's validator, report and two-phase commit are unchanged; what changes is a member extension on our side, **two member lists**, a precedence rule at registration, and `cardNo` uniqueness ceasing to be an invariant. The build is bounded and the reconciliation obligation is permanent |
| **`I-05` does not expose renewal status or a continuous-participation start at member-on-policy level** — **D2-129**, register **B-15**/**S-50** | §5.4.2 F38 and §5.7.2 F10's continuity basis are specified and unbuildable. **The fallback is not neutral in either direction.** Treat every member as first-time and a member who has been covered for five years and renewed last month **is blocked by a thirty-day wait** — which, on an annually renewing group policy, is the commonest claim in the month after renewal. Treat every member as renewed and the two-hundred-and-seventy-day maternity wait never applies to anyone. **A5 §5's waiting-period accumulation rule has no input either way** (**G-B-01**). If InsureMO holds the predecessor policy, continuity is derivable and the question becomes a query rather than a field |
| **`I-05` does not expose the policy's rule-set or wording reference** — **D2-130**, register **S-45** | §5.4.2 F39 is specified and unbuildable. **Nothing miscalculates** — no step of the chain reads it. What is lost is that a decline cites a benefit and a rule step and cannot cite the clause in the document the customer is holding, which is the first thing a disputed decline is answered with |
| **InsureMO's quote or issuance schema differs** — C-IMO-03 | §4.3's field tables for the quote and application screens, and D3 §I-02/§I-03. **Still bounded to two screens** — this is the half of P-06 that held |
| **InsureMO cannot record claim registration** — I-06 | Part VII §7.2's registration effect line. Nothing else — registration is a notification, not a dependency (V-505) |
| **IDP's extraction payload differs from A4** | §5.6's field table and A4. The *behaviour* — editable, attributed, raw preserved — does not change, because it follows from AR-1, not from the payload |

> **The one that would hurt is no longer C-IDP-09 — it is confirmed. It is RK-14.** Everything else on this page is a payload change to a screen already specified, or a bounded build behind an interface that already exists. RK-14 is different in kind: it does not remove a feature or disable another, it removes **the data every claim reads**, and there is no second source. **Contract-first (P-06) still keeps the build moving and still bounds interface rework to six contracts. It no longer bounds the outcome.** That distinction is the whole of what changed between v0.1 and v0.2, and it is why §0.3's "this document does not depend on the confirmations" had to be withdrawn rather than edited.

## Part XI — Change control

This document changes by change request against **D1**. A rule stated here and contradicted in D1 is a defect *here*; a rule stated here and absent from D1 is a rule that should not exist — it is added to D1 first, with an identifier, and only then to this document.

**Where an annex owns the fact, the annex wins over both** (§0.5). A label that disagrees with A1, a sentence that disagrees with A2, a permission that disagrees with A3, a document type that disagrees with A4, a benefit that disagrees with A5 or a payload that disagrees with D3 is a defect in this document in every case.

**The one addition this part carried while the set was out of step is spent, and it is recorded as spent rather than quietly dropped.** Framework v2.0 was baselined on 21 August 2026 while D1, A1, A3, A5 and D3 still described four systems, and until that pass landed the Framework won over all of them on system boundary, feature codes, interface targets and data mastership (§0.5a). **It landed the same day**, and **the whole set is now issued against Framework v2.5**: D1 v0.5, A1 v1.5, A5 v1.5, D3 v2.3 and this document, with A2 v1.2, A3 v1.5 and A4 v1.3 in the same pass. **§0.5's precedence table holds without qualification**, and §0.5a stays only as the record that it once did not — *"a temporary exception that acquires a second version has stopped being temporary"*, and this one did not acquire one.

**What v0.3 applied, and what it deliberately did not.** *D2 Bảng đánh giá khác biệt v1.0* carries ninety-five differences against Reference System A and the client approved every recommendation in it. **v0.3 applies it in two passes and both are in** — the Part V rows with X-1 and X-3 first, then the Part II, III, IV, VI and VII rows (§0.6b rows 17 to 28). **The register is now applied across the whole document rather than across one part of it.** Three of the four dependencies §5.26 named have been met: **D2-124**'s `Source`-vocabulary half is answered at §2.11 UI-27, **D2-128**'s schema half is made at §6.3.3, and **D2-127** — narrowed to `EMAIL` alone by the second pass — **is closed outright by the third**. **D2-133** is not, and stayed open through a pass that edited Part VII, because it arises from a Part V observation and belongs to the register row that raised it.

**What the two passes left standing, and what a third pass has since closed.** The two passes left **`D2-44`** — Part IV replaced `episodeType` with an eight-value `lossType` on register row **S-10** and Part V, on the same row, declined to — and **`D2-127`**, register row **B-33**'s staff-channel half. **Both are now closed**, in the third pass recorded at §0.6a rows 29 to 31, and in both cases by the same mechanism: **the annex that owns the fact settled it and this document yielded** (§0.5). A1 v1.2 §4.2 settled the loss type; A2 v1.1 §8.1 settled the staff channel. **`D2-117`** carries D1's `BR-AUDIT-2` and is still owed. **A change applied to half of a document set in one pass is how the set stops agreeing with itself**, and naming the other half is the only honest way to stop half-way — but naming it is not closing it, and both halves have now been closed by the document that owned them.

**What v0.5 applied, and the one place it went further than its source.** The ten decisions of the *Solution Paper — Policy Terms, Rule Engine and Limit Management v1.1*, approved on 24 August 2026, reach this document as **§5.28** (the term register, F65), **§5.29** (the checkpoint queue, F67), **§5.9.1a** and **§5.9.7** (the evaluation service, F66), the **fourteen-step chain**, the **third auto-approval condition**, the **period dimension** on `S-11`, and `V-723` extended with `periodKey` and `counterType`. **Every one of those is an application of a decision taken elsewhere.**

**One is not, and it is named rather than absorbed.** §5.28.2 **splits `predicate` into `selector` and `predicate`**, because the single-field model D1, A5 and the paper all carry is unbuildable for class J: with the one field forbidden, nothing decides which claims a judgemental term concerns, and evaluated literally every claim raises a checkpoint. **This document did not fix D1 or A5** — a downstream document silently correcting an upstream one is how a set stops agreeing with itself — so the split was specified here, enforced by `V-734`, and **owed upstream as `D2-173`**. A second, smaller instance is **`D2-177`**: check 13 blocks submission on an open checkpoint, D1 states the rule for the gate alone, and D1 is asked to ratify or refuse.

**Two corrections applied on 24 August 2026, the day of issue, and recorded here rather than held for v0.6.** Both were found while the prototype was built against v0.5 and both were real disagreements between live documents.

| # | The conflict | Direction | What moved |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **May a class-D term raise a checkpoint?** §5.29.2 F5 said never, and refused the row rather than rendering it; A5 §7.1 says a class-D term may carry `CHECKPOINT` and two of the ten do | **This document yields.** A5 owns the pilot product (§0.5) and the underlying rule is D1's | **§5.28.1a** is new and carries the reasoning; **§5.28.3 F11 and F14**, **`V-734`**, **§5.29** and **§5.29.2 F5** are rewritten; **`V-742`** is allocated for the half of the old constraint that survives — a class `J` or `E` term may never carry a decline effect. §8.1's count moves from 152 to **153** |
| 2 | **The `selector` / `predicate` split** — specified here at v0.5 and owed upstream as **`D2-173`** | **Upstream adopts.** D1 `BR-TERM-7`, A5 §7.1/§7.2, `A5_seed_v1.4.json` | **`D2-173` closes** (§10.3). §5.28.2's *"owed upstream"* note becomes a record of the adoption, and A5 §7.3 answers the question the split exposed — what selects an irreducibly judgemental term — so **`V-734` needs no exception** |

**Neither is a new business rule invented here**, which is the test Part XI applies: the first is this document being corrected by the annex that owns the fact, and the second is D1 ratifying a rule this document had already flagged as owed. `D2-177` remains open on the same posture.

**What v0.6 applied, and the one thing it declined to.** The substantive review of 25 August 2026 — twenty-two findings, seven at severity 1 — reaches this document as §0.6's table. **Sixteen of the twenty-two are applications of a decision or a rule taken elsewhere**: D1 v0.5's `BR-CHAIN-1`, `BR-TERM-8` … `BR-TERM-13`, `BR-AUTO-6` and the gate's fourth condition; A1 v1.5's ten value sets, its fact vocabulary with an *available from step* column, and its re-cut of `lossType`; A5 v1.5's twenty service categories and its six live terms; A3 v1.5's two grants. **Four are internal defects** — a gate that promised a re-evaluation Part VII forbids, an attachment rule that covered nothing the pilot raises, a control specified nowhere, and a `CLM-CONSOLE` number space this document had been writing in without owning. **Two are counts that were wrong**, and both are now recomputed from the merged file rather than carried.

**Nothing in v0.6 is a business rule this document invented**, which is the test this part applies — and the one place v0.5 was ahead of D1 has been ratified rather than kept: **`BR-TERM-13` closes `D2-177`**, and §5.10.2's check 13 is an ordinary check citing an ordinary rule. **The posture that produced it is worth keeping**: a downstream document that finds a rule missing specifies it, cites what it can, flags it at the point of change and raises it upstream. It worked twice — `D2-173` and `D2-177` — and both closed within a day.

**What it declined to do is invent a benefit-level proviso.** Chain step 7 exists, its scope model is right (`BR-TERM-8`), and **it evaluates an empty set on every claim of the pilot product**, because all ten terms are `PRODUCT` scope. Inventing a proviso to give the mechanism something to do would be a contractual term no wording supports — which is exactly what Part XI forbids. **D1 asks the business for a real one as `B-23`**, and §5.9.1a records the empty group as the expected state.

**Three changes remain queued against this document**: the **`V-4nn` allocation for Part IV's *remaining* inline mobile rules** (**D2-91**, §8.3), which waits for D4; **`D2-160`**, the sweep of the ~41 *Validation* cells holding a description rather than a rule (§10.4.1), which waits for nothing and should be taken as a pass of its own; and **`D2-158`**, F68, which is the only feature we build and this document does not specify.

**The next document is D4** — the product backlog with acceptance criteria, traceable to the features here and the rules in D1.

*End of D2 v0.6.*
